general_translation: Is able to, Can, Possible
formation: Verb［stem］+ える(1)Exceptions:Verb［stem］+ えない(*)Verb［stem］+ えた(*)Verb［stem］+ えなかった(*)(1) うる(*) For negative, past and negative past forms, only conjugations of える are used
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ える(1)Exceptions:Verb［stem］+ えない(*)Verb［stem］+ えた(*)Verb［stem］+ えなかった(*)(1) うる(*) For negative, past and negative past forms, only conjugations of える are used
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ えます(1)Exceptions:Verb［stem］+ えません(1)Verb［stem］+ えました(1)Verb［stem］+ えませんでした(1)(1) For polite forms, only conjugations of える are used
explanation: A formal expression which focuses on having or gaining the possibility to do (A).

example_sentences.japanese: それはありえる。
example_sentences.english: That can be possible!

example_sentences.japanese: 順調にいけば、二年後に会社を立ち上げることもありえる。
example_sentences.english: It's possible that I'll set up my own company if everything goes well after two years.

example_sentences.japanese: いくら気をつけていても、交通事故は起こりえるものだ。
example_sentences.english: No matter how careful you are, it's possible for a car accident to occur.

example_sentences.japanese: その対策はかんがえうる。
example_sentences.english: It is possible to consider that countermeasure.

example_sentences.japanese: 災害はいつだっておこりえる。
example_sentences.english: Disaster can occur at anytime. (there is a possibility that it can occur)

example_sentences.japanese: 対応次第でストライキはかいひしえる。
example_sentences.english: A strike can be avoided depending on how it is dealt with.

example_sentences.japanese: たがやしうる土地を持っている方は田植えができます。
example_sentences.english: People who own arable land can plant rice. (can be farmed)

example_sentences.japanese: 消防士である彼は、信頼しうる人です。
example_sentences.english: Being a firefighter, he is a person you can trust. (there is a possibility it can be done)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼なら、もっと大きなことをなしうるだけの力がある。
example_sentences.english: In his case, he has the power to be able to accomplish even greater things. (there is a possibility that it can be accomplished)

example_sentences.japanese: この仕事でしりえた情報は、誰にも話してはいけません。
example_sentences.english: I can't talk to anyone about the information I was able to obtain through this job.

example_sentences.japanese: しょうじうるあらゆる事態を想定するのは不可能です。
example_sentences.english: It is not possible to predict every circumstance that can arise. (there is a possibility that it can arise)

example_sentences.japanese: その言い方は恐喝にもなりえるから、やめた方がいい。
example_sentences.english: It would be better if you stopped, since saying it in that way can become a threat/blackmail.

example_sentences.japanese: 我が社にできえるだけの努力はいたします。
example_sentences.english: I will put in as much effort as our company is capable of. (there is a possibility it can be done)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は群衆の目にもたえうる精神力の持ち主だ。
example_sentences.english: He possesses the force of will to be able to endure the piercing eyes of the crowd. (there is a possibility that it can be endured)

example_sentences.japanese: そういう事はセクハラにもなりえるので、そういう事はやらない方がいい。
example_sentences.english: Things like that can be considered as sexual harassment, so you shouldn't do that.

example_sentences.japanese: 考えうる事は、すべてこの企画書に書いておきました！
example_sentences.english: I wrote everything I can think of on this proposal!

example_sentences.japanese: うん、それもあり得るね...
example_sentences.english: Yeah, that is also a possibility...

example_sentences.japanese: 電気代がまた値上がりするみたいだよ。マジあり得ない。
example_sentences.english: It looks like the electricity bill is going to go up again. There's no way.

general_translation: Unable to, Cannot
formation: Verb［stem］+ えない
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ えない
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ えません
explanation: A formal phrase which focuses on not having, or not gaining the possibility to do (A).

example_sentences.japanese: そこまで大きな地震はおこりえない。
example_sentences.english: An earthquake of that magnitude cannot occur.

example_sentences.japanese: この個人情報は、本人以外は知り得ない情報だ。
example_sentences.english: This personal information is something that nobody apart from the person in question can know.

example_sentences.japanese: １０年後の自分なんて、想像し得ません。
example_sentences.english: Something like me 10 years in the future, I cannot imagine it.

example_sentences.japanese: 本来、水と油はまざりえない。
example_sentences.english: Naturally, you cannot mix water and oil.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなことはほとんどおこりえないと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that there is a good chance that such a thing cannot happen.

example_sentences.japanese: 私がその夢を叶えることはありえない。
example_sentences.english: It is not possible for me to achieve that dream.

example_sentences.japanese: 君の話術を持ってしても、説得しえないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if I had your skill in conversation, I probably couldn't persuade them.

example_sentences.japanese: 過去に犯罪を犯した人は、信頼しえない。
example_sentences.english: A person that has committed a crime in the past is unable to be trusted.

example_sentences.japanese: 無知な彼女が選挙で勝つことなど、ありえない。
example_sentences.english: That she, who is ignorant, would do something like win in the election is unbelievable.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は専門家だから、偽物を買うなんてということは、絶対ありえない。
example_sentences.english: Since he is an expert, that means that it is impossible that he would do something like buy a fake.

example_sentences.japanese: 太陽がなければ地球の生命は存在しえない。
example_sentences.english: If there was no sun, life on Earth could not exist.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の失礼な態度を見て、人としてありえないと思った。
example_sentences.english: Seeing his rude attitude, I thought that it was unbelievable as a person.

example_sentences.japanese: 健康な父が脳梗塞になることは、予測しえなかった。
example_sentences.english: I was unable to predict that my healthy father would suffer from a stroke.

example_sentences.japanese: 二次元のキャラクターは実際に存在しえないからこそ、人々の目に魅力的に映るのだ。
example_sentences.english: It is precisely because two dimensional characters cannot exist in reality, that they fascinate people.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな大きな災害は起こりえないと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that it's impossible for a disaster that big to happen. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: そんな大きな災害は起こりうないと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that it's impossible for a disaster that big to happen. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: まあ、それもあり得るかもしれないけど...
example_sentences.english: Well, that is possible, but…

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんはすごく頭がいいから、不合格になるなんて絶対あり得ない。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-san is very smart, so it is absolutely impossible for him to fail.

general_translation: Can't help doing, Have no choice but
formation: Verb［ない］+ ざるを得ない
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ ざるを得ない
polite_structure: Verb［ない］+ ざるを得ません
explanation: A formal, old-fashioned structure which indicates that not needing to do (A) cannot be gained, or is unavoidable.

example_sentences.japanese: サプライズのプレゼントに、おどろかざるをえなかった。
example_sentences.english: I couldn't help but be surprised at the surprise present.

example_sentences.japanese: 山の頂上まで登りたかったが、天候が悪くなって来たから諦めざるをえない。
example_sentences.english: I wanted to hike to the peak of the mountain, but the weather was getting worse so we had no choice but to give up.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩に指示されたので従わざるをえません。
example_sentences.english: Because my senpai told me to do it, I had no choice but to obey.

example_sentences.japanese: 思い掛けない出会いに、感動せざるをえなかった。
example_sentences.english: I couldn't help but be moved at the chance meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんはとても忙しかったのでゴルフの誘いをことわらざるをえなかった。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Tanaka was so busy he had no choice but to turn down an invitation to play golf.

example_sentences.japanese: 古い家屋は倒壊する恐れがあるから、こわさざるをえません。
example_sentences.english: The old building is at risk of collapsing, so I have no choice but to tear it down.

example_sentences.japanese: 今まで使った顕微鏡が壊れたから、新しいのをかわざるをえない。
example_sentences.english: The microscope I have been using until now broke, so I have no choice but to buy a new one.

example_sentences.japanese: 環境保護のために、工場の排気量を規制せざるをえない。
example_sentences.english: In order to protect the environment, we have no choice but to regulate the amount of emission from the factory.

example_sentences.japanese: 地元のチームではないが、甥っ子が入団したから応援せざるをえない。
example_sentences.english: The team isn't from my home town, but my nephew joined the team so I can't help but cheer for them.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度の上司は外部からの出向だから、きをつかわざるをえない。
example_sentences.english: This superior is being transferred from outside of the company, so I have no choice but to be mindful of his needs.

example_sentences.japanese: 話し合いが終わらない。会議室を借りる時間を延長せざるをえない。
example_sentences.english: The discussion is not coming to an end. We have no choice but to extend the amount of time allotted to use this meeting room.

example_sentences.japanese: 前の選手が序盤からかなりのスピードで走っているから、今はリードをゆるさざるをえない。
example_sentences.english: The last athlete had quite a bit of speed from the outset, so now I have no choice but to give up the lead.

example_sentences.japanese: 学会への出席は必須だから、元々予定していた旅行をあきらめざるをえない。
example_sentences.english: Because attendance at the academic meeting is compulsory, I have no choice but to give up on the trip that I had originally planned.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車のダイヤの改正があり、出勤時間を変更せざるをえない状況です。
example_sentences.english: The train timetables were revised. Now I am in a situation where I have no choice but to change my commute time.

example_sentences.japanese: フランスの大学へ行くため、フランス語を勉強しざるを得ない。
example_sentences.english: In order to go to a college in France, I have no choice but to study French. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: フランスの大学へ行くため、フランス語を勉強せざるを得ない。
example_sentences.english: In order to go to a college in France, I have no choice but to study French. (Natural Japanese)

general_translation: With the intention of doing, Instead of..., Act as if or pretend, Believing that..., Thinking that...
formation: Verb + つもりで［な］Adjective + な + つもりでNoun + の + つもりでAct as if・pretend・be convinced:Verb［た］+ つもりで
casual_structure: Verb + つもりで［な］Adjective + な + つもりでNoun + の + つもりでAct as if・pretend・be convinced:Verb［た］+ つもりで
explanation: A phrase that expresses the intention of doing (A), or doing something pretending that (A) were true.

example_sentences.japanese: ご馳走するつもりで行ったのに、おごってもらうことになった。
example_sentences.english: Despite going with the intention of treating everyone, they treated me.

example_sentences.japanese: 何も買わないつもりで新しく出来たショッピングモールへ行ったが、色々買ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: I went to the newly built shopping mall without any intention of buying anything, but I ended up purchasing various things.

example_sentences.japanese: 新鮮な魚を選んだつもりで買ったのに、パックから出したらものすごいにおいがした。
example_sentences.english: I chose this believing that it would be fresh fish, but when I took it out of the package, it smelled incredibly bad.

example_sentences.japanese: 冗談のつもりで言っただけなのに、相手を傷付けてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Despite saying it with the intention of making a joke, I ended up hurting their feelings.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度は、主人公になったつもりで読んでみてください。
example_sentences.english: Next, try reading it as if you were the main character.

example_sentences.japanese: パーティーでダンサーになったつもりで、みんなの前で踊った。
example_sentences.english: At a party, I danced in front of everybody, as if I was a dancer.

example_sentences.japanese: 本にするつもりで執筆していたが、これはボツだな。
example_sentences.english: I wrote with the intention of publishing a book, but this will surely be rejected.

example_sentences.japanese: お土産のつもりで買ったが、食べてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I bought it with the intention of giving it as a gift, but I ended up eating it.

example_sentences.japanese: 車掌になったつもりで、毎日電車に乗っている。
example_sentences.english: I ride the train every day acting like/pretending I have become a conductor.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に行ったつもりで、日本語を勉強しています。
example_sentences.english: I am studying Japanese as if I went to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月末までに完成させるつもりで、毎日努力をした。
example_sentences.english: With the intention of finishing by the end of the month, I worked on it every day.

example_sentences.japanese: こっそり返すつもりでペンを借りたのに、返すところを見られてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Despite borrowing the pen with the intention of returning it secretly, just as I was returning it, I was seen.

example_sentences.japanese: 趣味のつもりで始めた歌でしたが、コンサートを開くまでに成長できました。
example_sentences.english: I started singing with the intention of it being a hobby, but it's grown to the point where I have concerts.

example_sentences.japanese: カレーを作るつもりで買い物をしたのに、結局シチューを作った。
example_sentences.english: Despite going shopping with the intention of making curry, I ended up making a stew.

example_sentences.japanese: 祭日にやるつもりで宿題を残しておいたのですが、全然できませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I set aside my homework with the intention of doing it over the holiday, but I didn't do any of it.

example_sentences.japanese: 再来週旅行に行くつもりで準備していたのに、仕事の都合で行けなくなってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Despite getting ready with the intention of going on a trip the week after next, due to circumstances at work, I unfortunately cannot go.

example_sentences.japanese: 受験するつもりで勉強すると、集中力が湧いてくる。
example_sentences.english: If you study with the intention of taking an exam, the ability to concentrate will come to you.

general_translation: Anyhow, At any rate, In any case, I have no doubt that, Probably
formation: どうせ + Phrase
casual_structure: どうせ + Phrase
explanation: A common exclamation of frustration used when one feels that in any case, the result or situation of (A) cannot be avoided.

example_sentences.japanese: どうせダイアモンドなんて買ってもらえない。
example_sentences.english: I have no doubt I won't be able to get them to buy me diamonds.

example_sentences.japanese: どうせまたパチンコに行くんでしょ。
example_sentences.english: In any case, you are going to the pachinko parlor again, aren't you?

example_sentences.japanese: どうせ私のことなんて好きじゃないんでしょ。
example_sentences.english: In any case, you probably don't even like me.

example_sentences.japanese: どうせ新しいスマホを買うならもうちょっといい奴買いなよ。
example_sentences.english: If you're going to buy a new smartphone, you might as well buy something a little better.

example_sentences.japanese: どうせまた負けるんだから頑張っても時間と体力の無駄だよ。
example_sentences.english: We're going to lose again anyway, so trying our best would be a waste of time and energy.

example_sentences.japanese: どうせ「ウドの大木だ」と悪口を言われるのがオチだ。
example_sentences.english: I have no doubt that it will just end with me being called 'big and useless'.

example_sentences.japanese: どうせ通訳はつけてもらえない。自力で頑張るしかない。
example_sentences.english: In any case, I can't have it interpreted. I have no choice but to try my best.

example_sentences.japanese: 私がどう謝っても、どうせ彼は許すつもりはないだろう。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much I apologize, I have no doubt that he won't forgive me.

example_sentences.japanese: どうせご飯を炊かないといけないのだから、あなたの分も炊きますよ。
example_sentences.english: In any case, since I have to cook rice, I will cook your share too.

example_sentences.japanese: どうせもう蓄えがないのだから、最後のチャンスに賭けてみよう。
example_sentences.english: In any case, since there is no reserve left, I will try to bet it on my last chance.

example_sentences.japanese: またどうせ散らかすんでしょ。せっかく片付けたのに。
example_sentences.english: You will no doubt make a mess again, won't you? Even though I went through the trouble of straightening everything up.

example_sentences.japanese: どうせ付き合わないといけないのだから、楽しんだ方がいい。
example_sentences.english: In any case, since I must accompany you, it would be better to enjoy it.

example_sentences.japanese: どうせ車を買うのなら、ヒーターシートが付いているのを買おう！
example_sentences.english: If we are buying a car anyway, let's buy one with heated seats.

example_sentences.japanese: 君の話は聞きたくない。どうせだますつもりなんでしょ。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to listen to what you have to say. I have no doubt that you plan to deceive me, right?

example_sentences.japanese: この試験の難しさから考えると、どうせ失敗するに決まっている。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the difficulty of the exam, I have no doubt that my failure has been decided.

example_sentences.japanese: どうせ短期のバイトだと思って適当にやっているんじゃないですか？
example_sentences.english: At any rate, you are thinking that this is a short-term, part time job and are halfheartedly working, aren't you?

general_translation: At least
formation: せめて + Phrase
casual_structure: せめて + Phrase
explanation: A grammar point which highlights that something cannot be done to an acceptable degree, but at least (A) can be done.

example_sentences.japanese: せめてドアくらい閉めて欲しかった...。
example_sentences.english: I would have liked them to at least close the door...

example_sentences.japanese: ご飯は残しても良いから、せめて刺身だけは全部たべて。
example_sentences.english: You can leave the rice, but at least finish the sashimi please.

example_sentences.japanese: せめて国語の宿題はやっておきなさい。
example_sentences.english: At least finish your Japanese homework in advance.

example_sentences.japanese: せめてこの曲だけでも弾けるようになりたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to be able to play this song, at least.

example_sentences.japanese: えっ... たったの５千円だけ？せめて１万は欲しいよ。
example_sentences.english: What…only five-thousand yen? I want at least ten-thousand yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 別に毎日洗濯をしろっては言わないけど、せめて晩御飯だけは毎日作ってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I'm not telling you to do laundry everyday, but I want you to at least make dinner every night.

example_sentences.japanese: １日にせめて１リットルの水を飲むべきだ。
example_sentences.english: You should drink at least 1 liter of water a day.

example_sentences.japanese: 親：「せめておかずだけでも食べて。」
example_sentences.english: Mother: 'At least eat your sides or something.'

example_sentences.japanese: せめて着替えさせてもらえませんか？びしょ濡れなんです。
example_sentences.english: Would you at least let me change? I am soaked.

example_sentences.japanese: いい案ではなくてもいいので、せめてアイデアだけでも出してください。
example_sentences.english: Since it is okay even if it isn't a good idea, please at least submit an idea.

example_sentences.japanese: 楽器を寄贈させてください。せめてもの恩返しです。
example_sentences.english: Please let me give you an instrument. It is at least a repayment of the favor.

example_sentences.japanese: 買わなくてもいいので、せめて感想を教えてください！
example_sentences.english: Since it is okay even if you don't buy it, please at least tell me your impression!

example_sentences.japanese: せめて観測結果を教えてください。この通りです！
example_sentences.english: Please at least tell me the results of the observation. Like this!

example_sentences.japanese: せめて角度だけでも教えてもらえれば、その形を再現できるのに。
example_sentences.english: If you would at least tell me the angle, I would be able to reproduce that shape...

example_sentences.japanese: 泊まらなくてもいいので、せめて温泉だけでも入っていってください。
example_sentences.english: Since it is okay even if you don't stay overnight, please at least go to the onsen.

example_sentences.japanese: マラソンで勝つのは無理だけど、せめて、完走したい...
example_sentences.english: I realize it is not possible to win the marathon, but I want to finish it at least...

example_sentences.japanese: かつてのような強さが取り戻せなくても、せめて半分くらい取り戻せれば...。
example_sentences.english: Even if I cannot take back my former strength, if I can at least get back half of it...

example_sentences.japanese: ライトノベルの主人公：「君は居候だから、せめて自分の料理は自分でするべきだよ。」
example_sentences.english: The protagonist of a light novel: 'You are a freeloader, so at least you should cook your own food!'

general_translation: Apparently, Looks Like, Seems like
formation: どうやら + Phrase + みたいだ(1)(1) ようだ、そうだ 、らしい、って 感じだ
casual_structure: どうやら + Phrase + みたいだ(1)(1) ようだ、そうだ 、らしい、って 感じだ
explanation: An expression indicating that how (A) seems or appears is creating feelings of uncertainty or confusion in the speaker.

example_sentences.japanese: あの二人、どうやら結婚してる感じだよ。
example_sentences.english: It seems like those two are married.

example_sentences.japanese: 鈴木くんはいるか？居ないのかな？どうやら今日も休んでいるみたいだね。
example_sentences.english: Is Suzuki-kun present? Maybe he's not here? It seems like he's taking today off as well.

example_sentences.japanese: どうやら私は彼女には必要がないようだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems like I am not needed by her.

example_sentences.japanese: どうやら彼は結婚しているらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that he is apparently married.

example_sentences.japanese: あの動画、どうやら削除されたみたいだ。
example_sentences.english: It looks like that video was deleted.

example_sentences.japanese: どうやら今年の紅葉は遅れているらしい。
example_sentences.english: It looks like fall colors are late this year.

example_sentences.japanese: どうやら「心当たりがない」というのは本当らしい。
example_sentences.english: Apparently it is true that he 'has no clue.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はどうやらお小遣いをもらったことがないようです。
example_sentences.english: It seems like he has never received an allowance.

example_sentences.japanese: どうやら、俺は電気をつけっぱなしにしたらしい。すみません。
example_sentences.english: It looks like I left the light on. I'm sorry.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はどうやら本気でコンクールに出品したいらしい。
example_sentences.english: It looks like she is serious in wanting to enter an exhibit in the contest.

example_sentences.japanese: どうやら祭日はあのお店やってないみたいだよ。
example_sentences.english: Apparently that store isn't open on national holidays.

example_sentences.japanese: あの施設の完成は、どうやら再来年になるらしいです。
example_sentences.english: It looks like that facility will be finished the year after next.

example_sentences.japanese: ＮＨＫ集金人：「どうやら、私はこの辺りでは歓迎されないようだ...」
example_sentences.english: NHK Collector: 'Apparently, I am not welcome here.'

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚式の客１：「あれは誰？」結婚式の客２：「どうやら花嫁の兄みたいだな。」
example_sentences.english: Wedding Guest 1: 'Who is that?' Wedding Guest 2: 'Apparently, it is the bride's elder brother.'

example_sentences.japanese: 知ってた？ どうやら 田中さんは彼氏と別れて、今はフリーらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: Did you know? Apparently, Tanaka broke up with her boyfriend. She is free now!

example_sentences.japanese: お隣の鈴木さんがどうやら来月からイギリスに行くらしいですよ。
example_sentences.english: Our neighbor, Suzuki-san, is apparently going to England next month, or something.

general_translation: Something (or other), Some kind of
formation: 何（なに）やら + Phrase
casual_structure: 何（なに）やら + Phrase
explanation: An adverb used to express that there is something unknown.

example_sentences.japanese: なにやらいいにおいがします。
example_sentences.english: I smell something or other nice.

example_sentences.japanese: 外はなにやらにぎやかですね。
example_sentences.english: For some reason, it’s lively outside, isn’t it?

example_sentences.japanese: なにやら、今週の会議は、空気が重かったよね。
example_sentences.english: For some reason, the atmosphere at this week’s meeting was a bit heavy, don’t you think?

example_sentences.japanese: あの人、なにやら困っているようです。
example_sentences.english: That person seems to be bothered by something or other.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんの様子が、なにやら変わったように思いませんか？
example_sentences.english: Don’t you think something or other is different about Tanaka?

example_sentences.japanese: この場所には、なにやら懐かしい空気が流れている。
example_sentences.english: For some reason, this place has a nostalgic air to it.

example_sentences.japanese: なにやら胸がざわついて、落ち着かないのであった。
example_sentences.english: For some reason, my chest felt uneasy and I couldn’t calm down.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の言葉には、なにやら裏があるように感じた。
example_sentences.english: I felt his words had a hidden meaning or something.

example_sentences.japanese: なにやら急に天候が悪くなったらしく、すぐに帰ってきたよ。
example_sentences.english: For some reason, the weather seemed to have suddenly taken a turn for the worse, so I came right back home.

example_sentences.japanese: 二人の関係は、なにやら、どうにもこうにも上手くいかなくなったらしい。
example_sentences.english: For some reason, their relationship seemed to not go well no matter what they did.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日のプレゼン、なにやら皆の反応がいつもと違った気がするが、君はどう見たかね？
example_sentences.english: For some reason, I feel like everyone’s reaction was different at today’s presentation. How’d it seem to you?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のまなざしには、なにやら言葉にならない想いが隠されていた。
example_sentences.english: In her gaze, some kind of ineffable sentiment had been concealed.

example_sentences.japanese: なにやら母は、宝くじの一等を当てたことを、家族全員に黙っていたらしい。
example_sentences.english: For some reason, it seems my mother kept quiet to the entire family that she’d won the first prize in the lottery.

example_sentences.japanese: なにやら社長に隠し子がいたらしく、その噂がオフィスの他社にも広まっているよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard like the boss might have a secret kid or something... The rumor's even spreading to other companies.

example_sentences.japanese: なにやら私が不在の間に、子供達がパーティーをしていて、それが騒音被害として通報されたらしい。
example_sentences.english: For some reason, it seems that my children had a party while I wasn’t around, and they were reported for noise pollution.

example_sentences.japanese: 洗濯やら何やらをしない奴は文句言うな！
example_sentences.english: As a person who doesn't do things such as cleaning and other things, don’t complain! (As someone who doesn't do chores, you have no right to complain)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人に何やら言われても何にも感じない。
example_sentences.english: I don't feel anything when that person says something to me.

example_sentences.japanese: やっと子供が落ち着いたと思ったら、何やら歌い出した。
example_sentences.english: When I thought my kid finally settled down, he started to sing some kind of song.

example_sentences.japanese: 家に帰ってカバンを開けたら何やら見覚えのないレシートが入ってた。
example_sentences.english: When I opened my bag when I got home, there was a receipt in there that I have no recollection of for some reason.

example_sentences.japanese: あの二人の間で何やらあったらしい。
example_sentences.english: Apparently something happened between those two. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: お茶か何やら飲みますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you want tea or something? (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 何やらお隣の家が空き巣にあったみたい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that our next door neighbour got burglarized or something.

example_sentences.japanese: どうやら昨日この付近で事故があったようだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that there was an accident around here or something.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はどこやら怪しいんだよな。
example_sentences.english: Something about him is suspicious.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が帰ってくるのはいつやら…
example_sentences.english: I wonder when he will come home…

general_translation: To have no choice but, No other way than, Have to
formation: Verb + より + ほか + （は(1)）+ ない(1) に、には
casual_structure: Verb + より + ほか + （は(1)）+ ない(1) に、には
explanation: A construction highlighting that apart from doing (A), there is no other choice.

example_sentences.japanese: ゴルフの解説者：「このコースレイアウトだと、刻むよりほかないですね。」
example_sentences.english: Golf commentator: 'If it is this course layout, there is no choice but to lay up the ball.'

example_sentences.japanese: 人身事故のせいで電車が止まったので、会社までタクシーで行くよりほかはなかった。
example_sentences.english: Because the train stopped due to an accident, I had no choice but to take a taxi to work.

example_sentences.japanese: 靴に穴が空いたので、新しいのを買うよりほかない。
example_sentences.english: I have no choice but to buy a new pair of shoes because there's a hole in mine.

example_sentences.japanese: 被害者が無事であることを祈るよりほかにない。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing we can do other than pray that the victims are safe.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰もお婆さんを助けようとしなかったので、私が助けるよりほかはなかった。
example_sentences.english: No one was trying to help the old lady, so I had no choice but to help her.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事をクビになったので新しい仕事を探すよりほかにはない。
example_sentences.english: I got fired from my job, so I have no choice but to look for a new one.

example_sentences.japanese: 給与が悪すぎる。仕事を代えるよりほかない。
example_sentences.english: The salary is too poor. I have no choice but to change jobs.

example_sentences.japanese: 教養がなさすぎる。勉強するよりほかありません。
example_sentences.english: They lack education. There is no choice but to study.

example_sentences.japanese: 車を出せなかったので、自転車で行くよりほかはなかった。
example_sentences.english: Because I couldn't get my car out, I had no choice but to ride my bike.

example_sentences.japanese: 材料が入手できない。休業するよりほかない。
example_sentences.english: I can't obtain the material. There is no choice but to suspend business.

example_sentences.japanese: 急に田中さんがキスをしてきたので、驚くよりほかはなかった。
example_sentences.english: Because Tanaka-san suddenly came and kissed me, I had no choice but to be surprised.

example_sentences.japanese: 泥棒の攻撃から守るためだったため、相手を撃つよりほかなかった。
example_sentences.english: Since it was in order to defend myself against the thief, I had no choice but to shoot him.

example_sentences.japanese: ここまでびしょ濡れになったら、服を買って着替えるよりほかない。
example_sentences.english: If you become drenched to this extent, there is no choice but to buy clothes and change.

example_sentences.japanese: きっかけがつかめるまで、忍耐強く努力するよりほかありません。
example_sentences.english: Until you grasp the chance, there is no choice but to persevere.

example_sentences.japanese: ご近所トラブルが続いている。境界線を決めるよりほかない。
example_sentences.english: Neighborhood trouble is continuing. There is no choice but to decide boundary lines.

example_sentences.japanese: 部長：「そのプロジェクトは時間とお金の無駄だったので、融資を諦めるよりほかない。」
example_sentences.english: Department Head: 'Because the project was a waste of time and money, there is no choice but to give up on financing it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 漁業を営みたいのなら、早起きするよりほかない。
example_sentences.english: If you want to run a fishing business, there is no choice but to wake up early.

general_translation: Just in case, Just to be sure
formation: 一応（いちおう） + Phrase
casual_structure: 一応（いちおう） + Phrase
explanation: An expression implying that (A) is just in case. While (B) is not bound to happen, the application of (A) should prevent the negative (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 「いちおう夜道だから、気をつけてね。それじゃまた明日。」
example_sentences.english: 'Just in case, be careful since you are walking at night. Alright, I'll see you tomorrow.'

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はずっと晴れって天気予報で言ってたけど曇ってきたから いちおう傘を持って行ったほうがいいかも。
example_sentences.english: They said it was going to be sunny all day today on the forecast, but it's starting to get cloudy so it might be better to bring an umbrella just in case.

example_sentences.japanese: これで大丈夫だと思うけど、 いちおうチェックしておいてくれない？
example_sentences.english: I think this is fine, but just to be sure, can you please double check it for me?

example_sentences.japanese: 田中：「仕事慣れてきた？」鈴木：「はい、 いちおう...」
example_sentences.english: Tanaka: 'Have you gotten used to work?' Suzuki: 'Yes, more or less…'

example_sentences.japanese: 一応はよくなってるみたいですけど、また来週病院まで来てください。
example_sentences.english: For the time being, it seems like you're getting better, but please come to the hospital again next week.

example_sentences.japanese: ルームメイトの間での話：「Ｆａｃｅｂｏｏｋアカウントはいちおう持ってるけど、あまり使ってない。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between roommates: 'I have a facebook account just in case, but I don't use it much.'

example_sentences.japanese: 教師が生徒に：「ハサミが必要になるかは分かりませんが、いちおう持ってきてください。」
example_sentences.english: Teacher to students: 'I do not know if scissors will be necessary, but just in case, please bring some.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達は助言する：「引越ししたら、いちおう、隣近所に挨拶しないとね。」
example_sentences.english: A friend is giving advice: 'If you move, just in case, greet the neighbors.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の間での話：「このスマホは充電してあるけど、いちおうモバイルバッテリーも持ってきた。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'This phone is already charged, but just in case, I also brought a power bank.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達とのＳＮＳメッセージ：「隣の人の騒音がうるさいから、いちおう、大家さんに通報しておいた¯\__/¯」
example_sentences.english: SNS message between friends: 'My neighbor is loud, so just in case, I have notified the landlady.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「（君の要望はたぶん叶えられないとは思うが）いちおう担当者には伝えておくよ。」
example_sentences.english: '(I don't think that your request will be fulfilled, but) just in case I will tell that to the person in charge (in advance).'

example_sentences.japanese: 部長、部下に：「（それを後で使うかどうか）よく分からないけどいちおうやっといて。」
example_sentences.english: Department chief to an employee: 'I don't really know (if it will be used later or not), but just in case, get it done.'

example_sentences.japanese: ルームメイトの間での話：「戸締まりいちおうチェックしたけど、念のためもう一度確認しよう。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between roommates: 'I checked if the doors were closed just in case, but to be really sure, let's check again.'

example_sentences.japanese: 初めてカラオケで歌う日の、友達との会話：「いちおう言っとくけど...ちょーオンチだから。」
example_sentences.english: Conversation between friends, before singing for the first time at Karaoke: 'I am letting you know in advance, just in case... I am totally tone-deaf.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の間での話：「手紙には私服でいいって書いてあったけど、いちおうスーツを着ることにしたんだ。」
example_sentences.english: Conversation between friends: 'It said that plain clothes are okay in the letter, but just in case, I decided to wear a suit.'

example_sentences.japanese: 何かをテストする前の、従業員の間での話：「（そんなことには気にしないと思うが）いちおう伝えておきます。」
example_sentences.english: Before testing something, a conversation between employees: '(I don't think they really care, but) Just in case, I will tell them in advance.'

general_translation: Surely, Certainly
formation: 確（たし）かに  + Phrase
casual_structure: 確（たし）かに  + Phrase
explanation: A phrase that indicates (A) as certainly, or indeed being the case.

example_sentences.japanese: たしかに彼は信頼できます。
example_sentences.english: He certainly is reliable.

example_sentences.japanese: たしかに彼はイケメンですが、マナーが悪いです。
example_sentences.english: He is certainly handsome, but he has bad manners.

example_sentences.japanese: たしかにさっきのは言い過ぎだった。ごめん。
example_sentences.english: What I said earlier was certainly out of line. I'm sorry.

example_sentences.japanese: たしかにその服はあなたに似合う。
example_sentences.english: Those clothes certainly look good on you.

example_sentences.japanese: みんな焦っているようだ。たしかに期限が迫っている。
example_sentences.english: It appears that everyone is in a hurry. The deadline is certainly approaching.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校の規則上、たしかに生徒は先生に従うべきだ。
example_sentences.english: From the standpoint of the school's rules, students should certainly obey their teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のうちは音楽一家らしいが、たしかに楽器がうまい。
example_sentences.english: I heard he is from a musical household, but he is certainly skilled with an instrument.

example_sentences.japanese: 移籍金はかなりの額だったが、たしかに活躍している。
example_sentences.english: The fee for transferring (to another team) was a considerable amount, but (he) is certainly actively participating.

example_sentences.japanese: 脂は控えるよう言われています。たしかにカロリーが高いですからね。
example_sentences.english: It is said that you should avoid fat. Since it is certainly high in calories.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼には愛嬌があって、たしかに可愛がられている。
example_sentences.english: He has charm, surely he is loved.

example_sentences.japanese: 驚きすぎてキョトンとしてしまったが、たしかに感激しました。
example_sentences.english: It was such a surprise that he blanked, but surely he was impressed.

example_sentences.japanese: みんな「目が乾く」と言っていましたが、たしかに乾燥していますね。
example_sentences.english: Everyone said, 'your eyes will get dry,' but they certainly are, aren't they.

example_sentences.japanese: この箱は重たい。何が入っているかは分からないが、たしかにぎっしり詰まっている。
example_sentences.english: This box is heavy. I don't know what is in it, but it certainly is tightly packed.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事は山積みだが、たしかに休息は重要だ。
example_sentences.english: I have heaps of work, but relaxation certainly is important.

example_sentences.japanese: 確かに結構難しいね。ちょっと甘く見てたわ。
example_sentences.english: This is certainly difficult. I underestimated it. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 確かに！宿題が終わってるならゲームをしてもいいよ。
example_sentences.english: Certainly! You may play video games if you finish your homework. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は確かたくやくんのおじさんだったような気がする。
example_sentences.english: If I recall correctly, I feel like that person was Takuya-kun's uncle.

example_sentences.japanese: そう言えば、前いくら借りたっけ？確か３千円だったよね？
example_sentences.english: By the way, how much money did I borrow the other day? If I remember correctly, it was three-thousand yen, correct?

general_translation: more or less, for the time being, tentatively, roughly
formation: 一応 + Phrase
casual_structure: 一応 + Phrase
explanation: An expression implying that (A) is tentative. While not complete, one application of (A) should meet some minimum needs.

example_sentences.japanese: 「もうコンピュータを直したの？」「いちおうね。時間がかかったけど。」
example_sentences.english: 'Have you repaired the computer?''More or less. It took a while though.'

example_sentences.japanese: いちおう私が店長ですが、どうかなさいましたか。
example_sentences.english: I'm more or less the manager. Did something happen?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はいちおうここまでにしておきましょう。
example_sentences.english: For the time being, let's call it a day for today.

example_sentences.japanese: 周りの人たちが立ち始めたので、僕もいちおう立った。
example_sentences.english: People around me started to stand up, so tentatively, I also stood up.

example_sentences.japanese: 今夜は寒くなるかも知れないから、いちおうジャケットかなんか持ってきな。
example_sentences.english: Why don't you take a jacket or something, just in case, since it might get cold tonight.

example_sentences.japanese: 一応言っておくけど私は踊るのが下手だからね。
example_sentences.english: Just to be sure, I want to let you know that I am not a good dancer.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者、患者について：「ふう…いちおう、容態は安定化できました。」
example_sentences.english: Doctor, about a patient: '*sighing* We were able to stabilize her condition, for the time being.'

example_sentences.japanese: 若く見えるメリオダズさん：「これでもいちおう、僕は大人なんです。」
example_sentences.english: Young looking Meliodaz: 'Despite this (the way I look), I am more or less an adult.'

example_sentences.japanese: 部長：「残念ながらもう時間がありませんので、これでいちおう会議は終わりです。」
example_sentences.english: Head of the department: 'Unfortunately, we have run out of time, so with that, the meeting is finished for the time being.'

example_sentences.japanese: 転んだ友達１に話しかける友達２：「大丈夫？」友達１：「いちおう。」
example_sentences.english: Friend2 talks to Friend1 who has fallen: 'Are you ok?'Friend1: 'More or less.'

example_sentences.japanese: レストランの客：「さすがソウマさん！」鼻が高いソウマさん：「いちおう、プロの料理人ですから。」
example_sentences.english: Restaurant Customer: 'As expected from Mr. Souma.'Proud Souma: 'Pretty much, I am a pro chef after all.'

example_sentences.japanese: 会社、先輩：「書類はもう読んできたの？」後輩：「はい、いちおう目を通しました。」
example_sentences.english: Company, senpai: 'Have you already read the documents?'kouhai: 'Yes, I have more or less looked over them.'

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官：「こんにちは、警察署から来ました。オーナーと話をしたいです。」エリアスさん：「いちおう私がオーナーのエリアスです。」
example_sentences.english: Policeman: 'Hello, I have come from the police station. I would like to speak with the owner.'Elias: 'I am Elias, more or less the owner.'

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の人、せきさん：「娘さんは、いかがですか。」誇りに思う親：「大学卒業して、いちおう検察官になりました。」
example_sentences.english: Neighbor, Mr. Seki: 'And how is your daughter doing?'Proud parent: 'She graduated from the university, and became, more or less THE public prosecutor.'

example_sentences.japanese: お母さん：「グリーンピースが嫌いって言うから、お弁当にたくさん入れてあげたよ。たくさん食べて、食べられるようになった方がいいでしょ？」娘さん：「...いちおう感謝しておくわ...」
example_sentences.english: Mother: 'Since you said that you dislike green peas, I put a lot of them in your bento. It would be better to eat a lot of them and grow accustomed to them, don't you think?'Daughter:'...I am thankful, more or less.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達１：「田中といえば…ちょっと驚いた。勉強嫌いなのに、漢字が思ったより書けるのね。」友達２：「まぁ、日本人ならどんなに勉強嫌いでも漢字は書けるよね。いちおうは。」
example_sentences.english: Friend1: 'Speaking of Tanaka, I was a bit surprised. Even though he hates studying, he can write kanji better than I thought!'Friend2: 'Well, no matter how much they hate studying, if they are Japanese they can write kanji. More or less.'

example_sentences.japanese: 就職の面接、面接官：「英語ができますか？田中さん。」田中さん：「私は日常的な会話ぐらいならいちおうできますが、ビジネスで英語を使うのは自信がありません。」
example_sentences.english: Job interview, the interviewer: 'Can you speak English, Mr. Tanaka?'Mr. Tanaka: 'I am more or less able to do day-to-day conversations, but I don't feel confident in using English in business.'

general_translation: Without a doubt, Certainly, Surely, Not mistaken
formation: Verb + （から）+ に相違（そうい）ない［い］Adjective + （から）+ に相違（そうい）ない［な］Adjective + （である(1)）+ に相違（そうい）ないNoun + （である(1)）+ に相違（そうい）ない(1) であるから
casual_structure: Verb + （から）+ に相違（そうい）ない［い］Adjective + （から）+ に相違（そうい）ない［な］Adjective + （である(1)）+ に相違（そうい）ないNoun + （である(1)）+ に相違（そうい）ない(1) であるから
explanation: A formal phrase expressing that there is no mistaking (A). Literally there are no mutual discrepancies in (A).

example_sentences.japanese: この下駄は彼の物にそういない。
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that these geta are his.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は小学生の頃から一生懸命勉強をし続けたので、いい大学に行けるにそういない。
example_sentences.english: Since he's been studying hard since he was in elementary school, there's no doubt that he can go to a good university.

example_sentences.japanese: このコースはあの世界的に有名なシェフによって作られたものなので美味しいにそういない。
example_sentences.english: This course has been prepared by a world famous chef, so there is no doubt that it will be delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: この街には電車が３分に１本来るので便利にそういない。
example_sentences.english: In this city, a train comes every 3 minutes, so there is no doubt that it is convenient.

example_sentences.japanese: あの事件の犯人はあの人にそういない。
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that that person is the culprit.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼がキョロキョロしているのは、嘘をついているからにそういない。
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that he's being restless because he's lying.

example_sentences.japanese: この技が全国の大会で禁止されているのは危ないからにそういない。
example_sentences.english: There's no doubt that the reason why this move is forbidden in all competitions across the nation is because it's dangerous.

example_sentences.japanese: これは県庁からの指示ということにそういないか？
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that these are instructions from the prefectural office?

example_sentences.japanese: これは我が社の公式の見解ということにそういない。
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that this is our company's official view.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしの意見は妻の意見ということにそういない。
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that my opinion is my wife's opinion.

example_sentences.japanese: これはゴッホの絵のコレクションにそういない。
example_sentences.english: This is without a doubt Gogh's collection of paintings.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼こそこの作品の本当の作者にそういない。
example_sentences.english: He is, without a doubt, the real creator of this work.

example_sentences.japanese: 撮影した日は１０月１９日にそういない。
example_sentences.english: I am certain that the (photo) shoot took place on October 19th. (without a doubt)

example_sentences.japanese: 課長：「競合他社は何か魂胆があるにそういない。」
example_sentences.english: Section manager: 'Competitors are surely plotting something.' (without a doubt)

example_sentences.japanese: 報告によると、この新しいウイルスは空気を介して広がるにそういない。
example_sentences.english: According to the report, this new virus is, without a doubt, spreading through the air.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中先生は一流の外科医だから、手術は成功するにそういない。
example_sentences.english: Doctor Tanaka is a first-class surgeon, so the surgery will be successful without a doubt.

example_sentences.japanese: 検察官：「被害者の死因は鉄パイプのようなもので殴りつけられたからにそういない。」
example_sentences.english: Public prosecutor: 'It is certain that the cause of the victim's death was a blow from something like an iron pipe.' (without a doubt)

example_sentences.japanese: 記者：「首相は来年減税をすると言ったから、グレーゾーンを減らそうとするにそういない。」
example_sentences.english: Reporter: 'The prime minister said that he will reduce taxes next year, so he will without a doubt attempt to reduce the gray zone.'

general_translation: Just in case, In the worst-case scenario, In the unlikely event, By any chance
formation: 万（まん）（が）一（いち） + Phrase
casual_structure: 万（まん）（が）一（いち） + Phrase
explanation: A grammar point which expresses that in the unlikely event of (A), (B). Literally on the one in 10,000 chance.

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいちのために、消火器を買うことにした。
example_sentences.english: I decided to buy a fire extinguisher, just in case.(in the unlikely event...)

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいちの時のために防災セットを買っておきましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's buy a disaster kit (in advance) just in case.

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいち来れなくなった場合は、連絡をください。
example_sentences.english: In the unlikely event that you are unable to come, please contact us.

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいち思いついたら、アイデアを教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Just in case you think of something, please tell me your idea.(in the unlikely event...)

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいち嫌がられても、次の手は打ってある。
example_sentences.english: Even in the worst case scenario that they hate it, I will take alternative measures.

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいち裁判で争うことになっても、受けて立ちますよ。
example_sentences.english: Even in the unlikely event that we dispute it in court, I will accept that challenge.

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいち入れ物がないと困るから、袋を持って行こう。
example_sentences.english: Since we will run into trouble not having a bag, let's take a bag along just in case.(in the unlikely event...)

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいち、宝くじが当たったら、世界一周旅行をしようと思う。
example_sentences.english: By any chance, if I win the lottery, I shall go on a round-the-world trip.

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいち熊の足跡を見つけた場合は、連絡してください。
example_sentences.english: Just in case you should find bear tracks, please let me know. (in the unlikely event...)

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいち鹿が暴れた場合は、麻酔銃で撃ちます。
example_sentences.english: In the unlikely event the deer should get violent, I will shoot it with a tranquilizer gun.

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいち台風が来たら大変なので、雨戸を閉めておこう。
example_sentences.english: Since it would be terrible if a typhoon comes, just in case let's close our storm shutters.(in the unlikely event...)

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいちあらすじがばれても、この結末は誰も予想できないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even in the worst case scenario that our outline gets leaked, nobody would be able to guess this ending.

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいち移転することになったら、僕の仕事は君にお願いしたい。
example_sentences.english: In the unlikely event that it is decided that I will transfer, I want to entrust my work with you.

example_sentences.japanese: まんがいちのことがあったら、お祖母さんの家に子どもを預けることになっている。
example_sentences.english: If an unlikely event happens, it has been decided that the children will be entrusted to grandmother.

example_sentences.japanese: 万が一の時のためにメールアドレスも教えていただいてもよろしいでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: Can I possibly have your email address too just in case.

example_sentences.japanese: 万一分からないことがあれば、何でも私に聞いてください。
example_sentences.english: If by chance, there is something you don't understand, you can ask me anything.

general_translation: There's no way to, It's impossible to
formation: Verb［stem］+ よう + が(1) + ない.［する］Verb + （の）+ しよう + が(1) + ない(1)  も
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ よう + が(1) + ない.［する］Verb + （の）+ しよう + が(1) + ない(1)  も
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ よう + が(1) + ありません.［する］Verb + （の）+ しよう + が(1) + ありません(1)  も
explanation: An expression that highlights when the speaker wants to do (A), but there is no possible manner in which to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 何ともいいようがない味だ。
example_sentences.english: There is no way to put this taste/flavor into words.

example_sentences.japanese: 車も自転車も壊れているので買い物に行きようがない。
example_sentences.english: Because my car and bicycle are broken, there is no way for me to go shopping.

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンが車にひかれて粉々になったため直しようがない。
example_sentences.english: It's impossible to fix my computer because it was run over by a car and smashed to pieces.

example_sentences.japanese: 電話番号もメールアドレスも分からないので、連絡のしようがありません。
example_sentences.english: I have no way to contact them because I don't know their phone number nor their email address.

example_sentences.japanese: 弁解のしようがない。
example_sentences.english: It is impossible to explain.

example_sentences.japanese: これはどうにもしようがない。
example_sentences.english: There is no way to do this.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は速すぎておいこしようがない。
example_sentences.english: He is too fast, there is no way to overtake him.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなバレバレのサプライズ、おどろきようがない。
example_sentences.english: It is impossible to be surprised by such an obvious surprise.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな無理な要求をされても、おうじようがない。
example_sentences.english: Even if such an impossible demand is made, it is impossible to comply.

example_sentences.japanese: 確率が低すぎて、投資のしようがない。
example_sentences.english: The chances are too low, it is impossible to invest in it.

example_sentences.japanese: あまりにも雑すぎて、カバーのしようもない。
example_sentences.english: Being exceedingly messy, it is impossible to cover it up.

example_sentences.japanese: あまりにも固い態度で、親しくなりようがない。
example_sentences.english: With an exceedingly hard attitude, it is impossible to become close.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな支離滅裂な質問、回答のしようもない。
example_sentences.english: It is impossible to answer such an incoherent question.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな架空の話をされても、反応のしようもない。
example_sentences.english: Even if such a fictitious story is told, it is impossible to react to it.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなにやる気のない選手なら、応援のしようもない。
example_sentences.english: It is impossible to cheer for an athlete if they have so little motivation.

general_translation: Nothing but, None other than, Simply
formation: Noun + にほかならない(1)(1) にほかならぬ
casual_structure: Noun + にほかならない(1)(1) にほかならぬ
polite_structure: Noun + にほかなりません
explanation: A construction expressing that (A) is nothing but (A), and can become no other. Simply (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 第一にすべきは人命にほかなりません。
example_sentences.english: The first priority is nothing other than human life.

example_sentences.japanese: かすみさんがみんなに好かれるのはお人よしだからにほかならない。
example_sentences.english: The reason why Kasumi-san is liked by everyone is simply because she is a good person.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな夜遅くに訪問してくるなんて迷惑にほかならない。
example_sentences.english: Visiting me at such a late time is nothing but a nuisance.

example_sentences.japanese: 三位という結果は彼の実力にほかならない。
example_sentences.english: Getting (the result of) 3rd was simply due to his skill.

example_sentences.japanese: 結局「笑い」というのは好き嫌いにほかならない。
example_sentences.english: In the end, 'laughing' is simply up to your likes and dislikes. （好き嫌い = noun)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼があの番組に出たのは、宣伝にほかならない。
example_sentences.english: Him going on that show was simply for publicity.

example_sentences.japanese: 通常の事故の原因はスピード違反にほかならない。
example_sentences.english: The common cause of the accidents is simply people going too fast.

example_sentences.japanese: 人の話を聞かないのは、彼の短所にほかなりません。
example_sentences.english: His weak point is simply not listening to other people's conversations.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回の成績は、地味な努力の積み重ねによるものにほかならない。
example_sentences.english: This result is nothing but the accumulation of calm, collected effort.

example_sentences.japanese: 何事においても大切なのは、素質と努力にほかならない。
example_sentences.english: With anything and everything, the most important thing is none other than one's qualities and effort.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社がここまで成長したのは、彼との出会いがあったからにほかならない。
example_sentences.english: Being able to get this far at this company is thanks to none other than meeting him.

example_sentences.japanese: わが社の今年度の多大な利益は顧客のおかげにほかなりません。
example_sentences.english: Our company's tremendous profit for this fiscal year is thanks to none other than our customers.

example_sentences.japanese: タイタニック号の沈没は低品質なリベットに因ったものにほかならない。
example_sentences.english: The sinking of the Titanic was caused by nothing but low quality rivets.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校校長の生徒に対した演説：「みなさんの未来に責任を持つのは誰でしょうか。それはみなさん自身にほかならないのです。」
example_sentences.english: School director's speech to students: 'Who is responsible for your future? That is none other than yourself.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａチームがこの大会で優勝できたのは岡村コーチのおかげにほかならぬ。
example_sentences.english: The reason why team A was able to win this tournament is simply because of coach Okamura.

example_sentences.japanese: 我が社の商品が人気なのは広告が印象的だからにほかならぬ。
example_sentences.english: The reason our company's products are popular is simply because our advertisements leave a lasting impression.

general_translation: There is no chance of, There is no way of, Impossible
formation: Verb［stem］+ っこない
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ っこない
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ っこない + です(1)(1) However if you really have to be polite, then it is better to not use っこない.
explanation: A strong structure which implies that there is almost no chance of doing (A), or that it's impossible. Often following potential verbs.

example_sentences.japanese: 「今持っているスキルでリングは何もほろぼせっこありません。」
example_sentences.english: With the skills we possess right now, we can’t destroy anything with this ring.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年中に３０万円貯めたいの？お前の給料じゃできっこないよ。
example_sentences.english: You want to save up three hundred thousand yen this year? There's no chance you can with your salary.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに鍛えてもあの人だけには勝てっこないよ。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much I train, there's no chance that I can beat him.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなデカい家、どんなに貯金しても買えっこないよ。
example_sentences.english: I will not be able to buy a house that big, no matter how much I save.

example_sentences.japanese: 練習をたくさんしなくては、楽器の演奏なんかできっこない。
example_sentences.english: If you do not practice a lot, there is no way you will be able to do a musical performance.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語で書く練習をしないと、日本語で書けるようにはなりっこない。
example_sentences.english: If you do not practice writing in Japanese, there is no way you will become able to write it.

example_sentences.japanese: 怒ったお母さん：「ひきこもりのように、一日中家でゲームしてばかりでは、何もなしとげっこない。」
example_sentences.english: Angry mother: 'There is no way you are going to accomplish anything if you are just sitting at home, playing games like a hikikomori.'

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに勉強したって「は」と「が」の違いなんてわかりっこない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much I study, there is no way for me to understand the difference between 'は' and 'が'.

example_sentences.japanese: すべてのケースに備えることはできっこないけど、そうしようとすることは価値がある。
example_sentences.english: It is impossible to prepare for every case, but there is worth in attempting to do so.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「試験は明日だよ！」Ｂ：「明日？明日までに資料全部なんてよめっこない。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'The exam is tomorrow!'B: 'Tomorrow? There is no chance of me reading all of the material by tomorrow.'

example_sentences.japanese: 昨年の優勝者と戦ってもどうせかてっこないけど、私は最後まで頑張りぬく。
example_sentences.english: Even if I fight with last year's champion there is no chance I can win, but… I… will give my best till the bitter end.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「Ｂさん、日本語はもう読める？」Ｂ：「大分前から読めることは読めるけど、漢字はわかりっこない。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'B-san, are you already able to read Japanese?'B: 'I have been able to read for quite a while, but there is no chance of me understanding kanji.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「熱があるなら、休暇を取った方がいい！」Ｂ：「休暇なんてとれっこないよ！期限が明日までの仕事があるから！」
example_sentences.english: A: 'If you have a fever, you should take the day off! 'B: 'There is no way that I can take a day off! There is work that needs to be finished by tomorrow.'

example_sentences.japanese: 初めて漢字を見て「こんなに書きにくい文字はおぼえられっこない」と思ったけど、とにかく勉強し始めた。
example_sentences.english: When I first saw kanji, I thought 'there is no way I can remember such complicated characters,' but I started learning anyway.

example_sentences.japanese: 宝くじって、当たる運のよい数を予測できっこないのに、ある人は毎日わざわざ予測しようとしている。
example_sentences.english: Despite there being no way to guess the winning lottery ticket numbers, some people go out of their way to try and do so every single day. (no chance of being able to)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日までに５ページのレポートとか、絶対書けっ子ないよ。
example_sentences.english: There is no way that I can write a 5 page essay by tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな漢字だらけの新聞なんて読めっ子ない。
example_sentences.english: There is no way I can read this newspaper that is filled with kanji.

general_translation: Then, If that's the case
formation: それなら + Phrase
casual_structure: それなら + Phrase
explanation: A hypothetical expression that assumes that if the previous statement is the case, then (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 遠藤さん：「アプリをもっと使いやすくしました。」土井さん：「それなら普及すると思います。」
example_sentences.english: Endo-san: 'They made the application easier to use.' Doi-san: 'If that is the case, I think it will spread.'

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の近くにあるスーパーに行くの？それならついでに私を駅まで送ってくれない？
example_sentences.english: You're going to the supermarket near the station? If that's the case, can you drop me off at the station?

example_sentences.japanese: カメラの画質がいいスマホをお探しなんですか？それならこのスマホをお勧めします。
example_sentences.english: You are looking for a smartphone with a good camera? If that's the case, I recommend this one.

example_sentences.japanese: それなら彼でもできるようだ。
example_sentences.english: If that's the case, it seems like even he will be able to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: それなら早く警察に電話したほうがいいよ！
example_sentences.english: If that's the case, you should call the cops as soon as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: それなら先生に聞いたほうがいいと思います。
example_sentences.english: If that's the case, you should ask the teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で食べに行くの？だったら僕も一緒に行ってもいい？
example_sentences.english: You're going to go eat alone? If that's the case, can I come with you?

example_sentences.japanese: 田中君もコストコに行くの？それだったら一緒に行こうよ。そのほうがガソリン代も節約できるし。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-kun, are you also going to Costco? If that's the case, let's go together. That way, we can save money on gas.

example_sentences.japanese: 岩村さん：「もう誰も食べないんだね。」山崎さん：「それなら蓋をした方がいい。」
example_sentences.english: Iwamura-san: 'No one else is going to eat anymore.' Yamasaki-san: 'If that is the case, it would be good to put the lid on.'

example_sentences.japanese: 藤本さん：「この戸は鍵が壊れてかからない。」横山さん：「それならあまりにも物騒だ。」
example_sentences.english: Fujimoto-san: 'The lock on this door is broken and won't lock.' Yokoyama-san: 'If that is the case, it is exceedingly dangerous.'

example_sentences.japanese: 松本さん：「あそこは開かずの踏切だ。」山端さん：「それなら陸橋を渡った方がいい。」
example_sentences.english: Matsumoto-san: 'That is a railway crossing that never opens.' Yamahata-san: 'If that is the case, it would be better to go over the overpass.'

example_sentences.japanese: 森口さん：「今鍋が使えない。」上田さん：「それなら代わりにフライパンを使えばいい。」
example_sentences.english: Moriguchi-san: 'Right now we can't use the pot.' Ueda-san: 'If that is the case, it would be good if we used a frying pan as a substitute.'

example_sentences.japanese: 岩田さん：「彼は漢字が苦手です。」井村さん：「それなら振り仮名を振りましょう。」
example_sentences.english: Iwata-san: 'He is bad at kanji.' Imura-san: 'If that is the case, we should show the furigana.'

example_sentences.japanese: 土屋：「今日、ちょっと体調が悪いんだよね。」水口：「それなら、早く寝た方がいいよ。」
example_sentences.english: Tsuchiya: 'Today I am feeling a little under the weather.'  Mizuguchi: 'If that is the case, you should go to bed early!

example_sentences.japanese: 平野さん：「タンスが大きすぎて入らない。」前野さん：「それなら分解するしかないな。」
example_sentences.english: Hirano-san: 'The dresser is too big and won't fit.' Maeno-san: 'If that is the case, we have no choice but to disassemble it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 井上さん：「あなたはゲームすると愚痴っぽくなって困る。」上条さん：「それなら、そうと言ってくれればいいのに。」
example_sentences.english: Inoue-san: 'When you game you become irritable and I don't know what to do.' Kamijo-san: 'If that is the case, you should do me the favor of telling me that.'

example_sentences.japanese: 村上さん：「土日祝日は休みです。」井口さん：「それなら平日にまた来ます。」
example_sentences.english: Murakami-san: 'Saturdays, Sundays and national holidays are days off.' Iguchi-san: 'If that is the case, I will come again on a weekday.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小林さん：「シフトがあまりにも不規則だ。」河村さん：「それなら以前の仕事の方がまだいいかもしれない。」
example_sentences.english: Kobayashi-san: 'The shifts are excessively irregular.' Kawamura-san: 'If that's the case, then your previous job would probably be better.'

example_sentences.japanese: 田中：「彼女はとても優秀な秘書です。」山田：「それなら、この仕事は彼女に任せましょう。」
example_sentences.english: Tanaka: 'She is an excellent secretary.' Yamada: 'If that is the case, let's entrust this job to her.'

general_translation: If, If one could, If something would be possible
formation: Verb［できる］+ ものなら + Phrase
casual_structure: Verb［できる］+ ものなら + Phrase
explanation: A strong hypothetical grammar point, stating that if the thing that is (A) were possible, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 私よりもっと上手くやれるものならやってみろ！
example_sentences.english: If you can do this better than me, I'd like to see you try.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺のことを捕まえることができると思うものなら、捕まえてみろ！
example_sentences.english: If you think that you can catch me, try and catch me!

example_sentences.japanese: すぐに直せるものなら直したいけど、今はちょっとお金がないから厳しいかな。
example_sentences.english: If it can be fixed soon, I'd like to fix it, but it might be tough right now because I don't have money.

example_sentences.japanese: もしあなたが私より上手に書けるものなら自分で書いてみたらどうですか？
example_sentences.english: If you can write it better than I can, why don't you write it yourself?

example_sentences.japanese: もし行けるものならケニヤに行ってみたいです。
example_sentences.english: If it's possible, I would like to go to Kenya.

example_sentences.japanese: もしできるものなら、二年前にビットコインを買ったんだが。
example_sentences.english: If I could, I would have bought bitcoins two years ago.

example_sentences.japanese: 行けるものなら僕だって大学院に行きたいです。
example_sentences.english: If I could go, even I want to go to graduate school.

example_sentences.japanese: なれるものなら体操選手になりたい。
example_sentences.english: If I could become one, I want to become a gymnast.

example_sentences.japanese: 直せるものなら短所を直したいが、簡単ではない。
example_sentences.english: If I could, I would like to fix my shortcomings, but it is not easy.

example_sentences.japanese: 許されるものなら、短期でアルバイトさせていただきたいです。
example_sentences.english: If you will permit it, please let me work part time for a short while.

example_sentences.japanese: 憧れのあの人に、近付けるものなら近づきたい。
example_sentences.english: If I could get closer to the person I adore, I would like to.

example_sentences.japanese: あの文章、縮められるものならもっと縮めてほしい。
example_sentences.english: If you could shorten that article, I would like you to shorten it further.

example_sentences.japanese: 帰国できるものなら 帰国したいが、お金が十分にない。
example_sentences.english: If I could return to my country, I would like to, but I do not have enough money.

example_sentences.japanese: 調整できるものなら、明日の予定明後日にしてもらえませんか？
example_sentences.english: If it could be adjusted, would you do me the favor of moving tomorrow's plan to the day after tomorrow?

example_sentences.japanese: 時の流れに逆らえるものなら過去に行ってみたいが、時間旅行は実現不可能だから。
example_sentences.english: If I could reverse the flow of time, I would like to travel to the past, but time travel is simply impossible.

example_sentences.japanese: この壁の塗り方が下手だって言うのか？だったらペンキを買いに行ってもっと上手く塗れるものなら塗ってみろ！
example_sentences.english: You're saying that the way I painted this wall is bad? If that's the case, go buy some paint and if you can paint it better, I'd like to see you try!

general_translation: Leave 〜 up to, Entrust 〜 to
formation: (Task) Nounを + (Target) Nounに + 任（まか）せる(Target) Nounに + (Task) Nounを + 任（まか）せる
casual_structure: (Task) Nounを + (Target) Nounに + 任（まか）せる(Target) Nounに + (Task) Nounを + 任（まか）せる
polite_structure: (Task) Nounを + (Target) Nounに + 任（まか）せます(Target) Nounに + (Task) Nounを + 任（まか）せます
explanation: A structure that shows that something is being entrusted to (A), or that (A) is being made responsible for it.

example_sentences.japanese: アンテナの修理を息子にまかせた。
example_sentences.english: I entrusted repairing the antenna to my son.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は忙しいから、あなたにペットの世話をまかせてもいい？
example_sentences.english: Is it alright if I trust you to take care of my pet since I'm busy?

example_sentences.japanese: 先月入社して来たばかりの新人くんにあの重要なプレゼンをまかせたの？
example_sentences.english: You entrusted that important presentation to a newcomer who just joined the company last month?

example_sentences.japanese: 研修生に掃除をまかせます。
example_sentences.english: I will leave the cleaning up to the trainee.

example_sentences.japanese: 奇跡が起こるかどうかを神様にまかせる。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not a miracle happens I will leave up to the gods.

example_sentences.japanese: 育児を親にまかせっきりというのはよくない。
example_sentences.english: Completely leaving child rearing to parents is not good.

example_sentences.japanese: 井戸の調査を専門家にまかせよう。
example_sentences.english: Let's leave the well inspection to a professional.

example_sentences.japanese: 大切な発表をいつも彼にまかせる。
example_sentences.english: I always leave the important presentations up to him.

example_sentences.japanese: 案内状の宛名書きを新入社員にまかせてみた。
example_sentences.english: I tried entrusting writing the address on the invitation to the new employee.

example_sentences.japanese: 大物政治家のインタビューをベテランアナウンサーにまかせた。
example_sentences.english: The big-shot politician's interview was entrusted to the veteran announcer.

example_sentences.japanese: 植木の手入れをお手伝いさんにまかせるのはどうでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: How does leaving the tree grooming up to the assistants sound?

example_sentences.japanese: 社運を占うような大きなプロジェクトを、誰にまかせたらいいか迷っています。
example_sentences.english: I am at a loss as to who would be good to entrust with the big project that will tell the future success of the company.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰もが羨むような仕事を私にまかせていただけて感謝しています。
example_sentences.english: I am thankful that (they) entrusted me with a job that everyone is envious of.

example_sentences.japanese: 絵の具の色選びを、幼稚園生の下の子にまかせてみた。
example_sentences.english: I left the choice of paint colors up to a child who was younger than kindergarten age.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女と付き合えるかどうかを神様にまかせる。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to leave it to God to decide if I can go out with her or not.

example_sentences.japanese: あの会社に入れるかどうかは運にまかせる。
example_sentences.english: I'll leave it to luck if I can join that company or not.

general_translation: To make use of (something), To take full advantage of, To capitalize on, To leverage (skills), Bring out (the quality of)
formation: Noun + を + 活（い）かす(1)Noun + を + 活（い）かした(2) + Noun(1) 生（い）かす(2) 生（い）かした
casual_structure: Noun + を + 活（い）かす(1)Noun + を + 活（い）かした(2) + Noun(1) 生（い）かす(2) 生（い）かした
polite_structure: Noun + を + 活（い）かします(1)Noun + を + 活（い）かした(2) + Noun(1) 生（い）かす(2) 生（い）かした
explanation: A construction meaning that (A) is being made good use of. Through putting life into (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「ぼくはこのチャンスをいかしたい。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'I want to take full advantage of this chance.'

example_sentences.japanese: このパソコンの機能を十分にいかすのにはたくさんの知識が必要だ。
example_sentences.english: You need to be very knowledgeable in order to make use of all the features of this computer.

example_sentences.japanese: この失敗を次にいかしてみてください。
example_sentences.english: Please try to make use of this failure next time.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のくせ毛をいかした髪型にカットしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please give me a haircut that makes good use of my curly hair.

example_sentences.japanese: この料理は鯖の旨味をいかした料理なので調味料はあまり使っていません。
example_sentences.english: This dish makes the most of the flavor of mackerel, so not much seasoning is used.

example_sentences.japanese: 新聞記事：「ルイスさんは技師としての経験をいかして修理業を始めました。」
example_sentences.english: Newspaper article: 'Louis made good use of his experience as a technician and started a repair business.'

example_sentences.japanese: ノートパソコンの生産者のサイト：「アルミニウムの美しさを最大限にいかしたノートパソコン」
example_sentences.english: Laptop producer's website: 'A laptop that takes full advantage of the beauty of aluminum'

example_sentences.japanese: 教師、生徒に：「マックス、すばらしい写真をとる才能があるのだから、それを最大限にいかすべきだよ。」
example_sentences.english: Teacher to pupil: 'Max, you are talented at taking excellent photos, so you have to take full advantage of it!'

example_sentences.japanese: ジョブ広告：「資格をいかした仕事です。一緒に頑張ってくれる仲間を募集中。」
example_sentences.english: Job advertisement: 'This is a job that takes full advantage of your qualifications. Recruiting colleagues who will work hard with us.'

example_sentences.japanese: 百科事典：「『利用』というのは物事や人の機能や利点をいかして使うということだ。」
example_sentences.english: Encyclopedia: ''Utilize' means to make use of a person's/thing's functions and advantages.'

example_sentences.japanese: ニスの生産者のサイトに：「木材の良さをいかすとともに保護するにはニスが必要だ。」
example_sentences.english: On the website of a varnish producer: 'Varnish is necessary to bring out the quality of the wood, as well as protect it.' (take full advantage of)

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「自分の能力を十分にいかす事は努力なしで不可能である。」
example_sentences.english: Essay: 'It is impossible to adequately capitalize on one's ability without effort.' (take full advantage of)

example_sentences.japanese: 通知：「この機械の全機能を最大限にいかすために、ソフトのアップグレードが必要です。」
example_sentences.english: Notification: 'In order to take full advantage of all of this device's functions, a software update is necessary.'

example_sentences.japanese: 料理・レシピサイト：「新鮮なじゃがいもの味を十分にいかした、簡単なポタージュです。」
example_sentences.english: On a cooking/recipe website: 'A simple potage that takes full advantage of fresh potato flavors.'

example_sentences.japanese: レストランのサイト：「ゲストの皆様の大切なお時間を有効にいかすために、予めテーブルの予約をされることをおすすめ致します。」
example_sentences.english: Website of a restaurant: 'In order to effectively make use of our guests' valuable time, we humbly advise reserving a table in advance.' (take full advantage of)

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「子供が才能をいかすか殺すか子供自身はもとより親や教師次第でもある。」
example_sentences.english: Essay/article: 'Whether children leverage their talent or waste it, depends not only on the children themselves, but on the parents and teachers as well. (take full advantage of)'

example_sentences.japanese: 私は仕事で日本語を十分に活かせるかが心配です。
example_sentences.english: I am concerned about my ability to fully make use of my Japanese at work.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強が出来る時間は限られている為、時間を有効に活かせるようにプランを立ててから勉強をするようにしています。
example_sentences.english: The time that I can study is limited, so in order to make good use of my time, I make sure to make a plan before I start studying.

general_translation: Won't, Intend not to, Probably not
formation: Verb + まいVerb［stem］+ まい
casual_structure: Verb + まいVerb［stem］+ まい
polite_structure: Verb (Polite) + まい
explanation: A strong formal way to determine that someone does not have the will to do (A), or intends not to.

example_sentences.japanese: あの店は行列がすごすぎる。もう行くまい。
example_sentences.english: The line at that shop is too crazy. I probably won't go again.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな接客が雑なレストランにはもう行くまい。
example_sentences.english: I probably won't go back to that restaurant with such poor customer service.

example_sentences.japanese: あのアパートの家賃は高いので、あそこには住むまい。
example_sentences.english: The rent for that apartment is expensive, so I probably won't live there.

example_sentences.japanese: 税金が高いから、この町には住むまい。
example_sentences.english: I don't intend to live in this town because the taxes are high.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のせいでものすごい苦情だ。もう失敗するまい。
example_sentences.english: I caused the terrible grievances. I intend not to fail again.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人の話は下品だ。二度と聞くまい。
example_sentences.english: That person's stories are vulgar. I probably won't listen to them a second time.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日飲みすぎてしまったので、二度と酒は飲むまい。
example_sentences.english: Because I drank too much last night, I don't intend to drink ever again.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は火曜日だから、あのダンスクラブにはお客さんがおるまい。
example_sentences.english: Because it is Tuesday, there probably won't be many people at that dance club.

example_sentences.japanese: この車の見た目からすると安くはあるまい。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the appearance of this car, it is probably not cheap.

example_sentences.japanese: 血圧が高くて調子が悪い。しばらく注文は取るまい。
example_sentences.english: My blood pressure is high and I don't feel well. I probably won't be taking orders for a while.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は人の話を聞かないらしい。それならもう何も言うまい。
example_sentences.english: Apparently he doesn't listen to what people have to say. If that is the case, I probably won't say anything more.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社公式の発言だから、嘘ということはあるまい。
example_sentences.english: Since it is an official company announcement, it probably won't be fake.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕がこっそり高級な香水をつけているなんて誰も知るまい。
example_sentences.english: Probably no one will know that I am secretly wearing expensive cologne.

example_sentences.japanese: １９５０年代、学者達は、コンピューターを使って天気を予報することはそう難しくはあるまいと考えていたが、１４日以上先の予報は不可能である事がすぐに明らかになった。
example_sentences.english: During the 1950s, it was thought by scholars that it probably would not be hard to predict the weather using computers, but it soon became clear that forecasting more than 14 days in advance was not possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中くんはとてもいい人なので、そんなひどい事はしまい。
example_sentences.english: Since Tanaka-kun is a nice person, he probably wouldn't do such a terrible thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 台風の警報が出ているので、今日中に届くはずだった荷物はこまい。
example_sentences.english: Since there was a warning announced for the typhoon, I probably won't get the package that I was expecting today.

general_translation: To not ~, Un~
formation: Verb［ない］+ ざる + Noun
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ ざる + Noun
explanation: An old-fashioned auxiliary verb that has the purpose of negation, and is primarily used with a very limited number of set phrases.

example_sentences.japanese: たゆまざる努力のおかげで成功者になった。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to my unrelenting efforts, I became a successful person.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はどんな辛い時でも弱音を言わざる人だ。
example_sentences.english: He is a person that will not complain, no matter how hard it gets.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事のタイトル：「演歌歌手鈴木太朗の知られざる過去。」
example_sentences.english: Title of an article: 'The unknown past of the enka singer Suzuki Taro.'

example_sentences.japanese: たゆまざる努力をすることが、成功への鍵だ。
example_sentences.english: Putting in unrelenting effort is the key to success.

example_sentences.japanese: あの作家の知られざる名画を僕は知っています。
example_sentences.english: I know that artist's unknown masterpiece.

example_sentences.japanese: 消えざる傷を負ってしまい、落ち込んでいる。
example_sentences.english: I suffered a wound that will not disappear, so I am depressed.

example_sentences.japanese: 嘘をつかざる人しか信頼することができない。
example_sentences.english: You cannot trust anyone apart from a person who does not lie.

example_sentences.japanese: 取り返しのつかざる大変なミスを犯しました。
example_sentences.english: I committed a serious error that cannot be undone.

example_sentences.japanese: 絶えざる失敗に、完全に心を折られてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I am completely shattered by these unending failures.

example_sentences.japanese: 耐えざる不安がのしかかって鬱になりました。
example_sentences.english: I became depressed due to anxiety that I cannot withstand hanging over me.

example_sentences.japanese: 絶えざる失敗にも、僕は決して負けません。
example_sentences.english: I will absolutely not lose, not even to unending failures.

example_sentences.japanese: あの有名な作家には、知られざる傑作があるのだ。
example_sentences.english: That famous artist has an unknown masterpiece.

example_sentences.japanese: たゆまざる努力があったからこそ、部長になることができたのです。
example_sentences.english: I was able to become a section manager precisely because of my unwavering efforts.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はその曲で有名ですが、実は知られざる名曲が他にもあります。
example_sentences.english: She is famous for that song, but she actually also has other great songs that are unknown.

example_sentences.japanese: 病気や事故などの理由で、宿泊をキャンセルせざるをえない場合はキャンセル料は発生致しません。
example_sentences.english: No cancellation fee will be charged if you need to cancel your stay due to illness or accident.

general_translation: Approximately, Roughly, About, Outline, Gist
formation: おおよそ(1) + Noun(1)およそ
casual_structure: おおよそ(1) + Noun(1)およそ
explanation: A slightly formal adverb that is often used in announcements to indicate something that is not exactly (A), but expected to be close to it.

example_sentences.japanese: まずは計画のおおよそを説明しよう。
example_sentences.english: To start with, let's roughly explain the plan.

example_sentences.japanese: この物件から最寄りの駅までは徒歩でおよそ１０分かかります。
example_sentences.english: It takes approximately 10 minutes to walk to the nearest train station from this property.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はおおよそ理解したけど、周りの子達はポカーンとした表情で先生を見ていた。
example_sentences.english: I understood most of it, but the people around me were looking at the teacher with a blank stare.

example_sentences.japanese: 地震による犠牲者はおおよそ１２０人です。
example_sentences.english: There are approximately 120 victims as a result of the earthquake.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家から実家までおよそ１０キロ離れている。
example_sentences.english: My house is separated from my family home by approximately 10 kilometers.

example_sentences.japanese: およその見積もりを立ててから詳細をつめる。
example_sentences.english: Let's hammer out the details after setting up a rough approximation.

example_sentences.japanese: パーティーにくるおおよその人数を把握する。
example_sentences.english: To figure out roughly how many people will come to the party.

example_sentences.japanese: カーナビ：「目的地までおおよそ３０分です。」
example_sentences.english: Car navigation: 'The destination is approximately 30 minutes.'

example_sentences.japanese: 機長：「およそ１時間半のフライトになります。」
example_sentences.english: Pilot: 'It will be a roughly one and a half hour flight.'

example_sentences.japanese: この図書館にはおよそ一万冊の本があるらしい。
example_sentences.english: It would seem that there are approximately 10,000 books in this library.

example_sentences.japanese: 注文した品はおよそ２週間で到着する予定です。
example_sentences.english: The goods I ordered are scheduled to arrive in roughly 2 weeks.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕と妻が結婚したのはおおよそ１０年くらい前だ。
example_sentences.english: My wife and I got married approximately 10 years ago.

example_sentences.japanese: 事情はおおよそ見当がつくが、一応説明してくれるかい？
example_sentences.english: I can roughly assume the situation, but will you explain it to me nonetheless?

example_sentences.japanese: 発見された化石の生物はおよそ二千万年前に生きていたそうです。
example_sentences.english: It is said that the creature's fossil that was discovered was living approximately 20 million years ago.

example_sentences.japanese: 美術館では、およそ高価な作品を展示している。
example_sentences.english: As a rule, museums display expensive pieces.

general_translation: From the standpoint of
formation: Noun + 上（じょう）
casual_structure: Noun + 上（じょう）
explanation: A word that expresses a standpoint of something from the elevated perspective of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 予算じょう、その依頼は断るしかない。
example_sentences.english: From a budget standpoint, I have no choice but to deny that request.

example_sentences.japanese: 法律じょう、伊勢海老を許可なく釣り上げて持って帰ることが禁止されている。
example_sentences.english: From a legal standpoint, it is prohibited to fish for lobsters and bring them home without a permit.

example_sentences.japanese: 規則じょう、生徒は髪を染めてはいけないのに、髪を染めている生徒が複数います。
example_sentences.english: From the standpoint of the rules, it is prohibited for the students to dye their hair, but there are a few students that have dyed hair.

example_sentences.japanese: あのビルは構造じょう地震に弱い。
example_sentences.english: That building, from a construction standpoint, is weak to earthquakes.

example_sentences.japanese: 規則じょう、このアパートでペットを飼うのは禁止です。
example_sentences.english: From the standpoint of the rules, this apartment prohibits pets.

example_sentences.japanese: それは飽くまで計算じょうの話で、実際にはそう簡単にはいきません。
example_sentences.english: That is a discussion that will only ever be viewed from the standpoint of forecasting. In practice, it wouldn't go that easily.

example_sentences.japanese: 立場じょうああいう発言をしたが、個人的には争う気持ちは全くない。
example_sentences.english: From that (situation's) standpoint, I made that sort of remark, but personally I'm not in the mood to quarrel at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 一応お伝えしておきますが、龍は想像じょうの生き物です。
example_sentences.english: I'll go ahead and say this: dragons are only creatures from the standpoint of your imagination.

example_sentences.japanese: 面倒臭いとは思いますが、形式じょうこの書類に全部記入してください。
example_sentences.english: I think it is bothersome, but for formalities' sake, please fill out all these documents. (From a formality standpoint)

example_sentences.japanese: 正式な野球のルールとは違うが、便宜じょう盗塁なしでお願いします。
example_sentences.english: It is different from the official rules of baseball, but from the standpoint of convenience, no stealing bases please.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社の規律じょう、５時半までは仕事をしなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: From the standpoint of the workplace's rules, you must work until 5:30.

example_sentences.japanese: 空飛ぶ車はもはや空想じょうの乗り物ではない。
example_sentences.english: Flying cars are no longer vehicles of fantasy. (From a fantasy standpoint)

example_sentences.japanese: 法律じょう、学校は個人情報を漏らしてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: From a legal standpoint, schools must not leak personal information.

example_sentences.japanese: 採点じょうあの順位だったが、観客の記憶に残る演技だった。
example_sentences.english: That rank was from a scoring standpoint, but it was a performance that stayed in the audience's memory.

example_sentences.japanese: 鈴木上、会社Ａが会社Ｂに買収される事はいい事だと思っている。
