example_sentences.japanese: 私は第２土曜日をのぞいて、毎日働いています。
example_sentences.english: With the exception of the second Saturday of the month, I work every day.

example_sentences.japanese: そこの壁にかけてあるギターをのぞく全てのギターは母親のものです。
example_sentences.english: With the exception of that guitar hanging on the wall, all of it is my mother's.

example_sentences.japanese: 中田先生をのぞく全ての先生は同じ大学を卒業したらしい。
example_sentences.english: Apparently, all of the teachers, except Mr. Nakata, graduated from the same college.

example_sentences.japanese: エウロパをのぞいて、これらすべての世界が人間に属しています。
example_sentences.english: All these worlds belong to humans, except Europa.

example_sentences.japanese: 一部の作業をのぞいて、ほとんどがオートメーション化されている。
example_sentences.english: With the exception of one part of the work, it was mostly converted to automation.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたをのぞいて、他の社員は皆お帰りください。
example_sentences.english: Would all staff please go home, except you.

example_sentences.japanese: あの楽器をのぞくすべての楽器はわたしの私物です。
example_sentences.english: Excluding that instrument over there, all of the instruments are mine.

example_sentences.japanese: 動物園をのぞくすべての都立公園は無料である。
example_sentences.english: All metropolitan parks, excluding zoos, are free.

example_sentences.japanese: 動物園にいるものをのぞくすべてのライオンはアフリカに生息している。
example_sentences.english: All lions, excluding those in zoos, live in Africa.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近の落し物をのぞいて、他のものはすべて処分しましょう。
example_sentences.english: With the exception of recent lost and found items, let's dispose of everything else.

example_sentences.japanese: 学級委員長をのぞいて、皆教室で待っていてください。
example_sentences.english: Everyone, with the exception of the class representative, please wait in the classroom.

example_sentences.japanese: スイス連邦の国のものをのぞくすべてのヨーロッパの国旗は長方形である。
example_sentences.english: All European national flags, excluding the Swiss, are rectangles.

example_sentences.japanese: 往復の移動時間をのぞくすべての時間が給与の対象となります。
example_sentences.english: Excluding round trip travel, you are subject to payment for the time spent (on the project).

example_sentences.japanese: 警察は捜索状を持っている場合をのぞいては、家を捜索することができません。
example_sentences.english: Police cannot search a building unless they have a search warrant.

general_translation: Might, Could be, Capable of, Possible
formation: Verb［stem］+ かねないNoun + に + ​​かねない
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ かねないNoun + に + ​​かねない
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ かねませんNoun + に + ​​かねません
explanation: A grammar point highlighting that some negative situation might or could be possible due to the logic behind it not being spread too thin.

example_sentences.japanese: この事をそのままにしていたら、摩擦をうみかねない。
example_sentences.english: If you leave it at that, it might cause conflict.

example_sentences.japanese: それは命を落としかねない感染症らしい。
example_sentences.english: Apparently that is an infectious disease that could lead to death.

example_sentences.japanese: 地震の後には津波が起こりかねないので、出来るだけ早く避難しましょう。
example_sentences.english: A tsunami might follow an earthquake so try to evacuate as soon as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: ベッドでの喫煙は火災になりかねないのでご遠慮ください。
example_sentences.english: Please refrain from smoking on the bed as it might cause a fire.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事のやりすぎは、鬱の原因になりかねない。
example_sentences.english: Working too much could be a cause of depression.

example_sentences.japanese: 操作を間違えれば怪我人が出かねない。
example_sentences.english: If you operate it wrong, it could cause injuries.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに注意をしていても、事故は起こりかねない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how careful you are, accidents might happen.

example_sentences.japanese: 危険な運転をすれば、事故がおこりかねない。
example_sentences.english: If you drive dangerously, an accident might occur.

example_sentences.japanese: この犬に噛まれたら、大怪我をしかねない。
example_sentences.english: If this dog bites you, it is capable of causing serious injury.

example_sentences.japanese: この程度の怪我でも、ウイルスに感染しかねない。
example_sentences.english: Even with this degree of injury, you might get a viral infection.

example_sentences.japanese: 灯油の保管をちゃんとしないと、火事になりかねない。
example_sentences.english: If you don't properly store kerosene, a fire is possible.

example_sentences.japanese: この書類を開示されてはスキャンダルがおきかねないから、処分する必要があります。
example_sentences.english: If those documents are disclosed, it might cause a scandal, so it is necessary to get rid of them.

example_sentences.japanese: このままでは以前と同じパターンになりかねないから、もっと工夫してください。
example_sentences.english: Continuing like this, we could end up with the same pattern as before, so please think of a better idea.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は問題をふやしかねないから、誰かちゃんとアドバイスしてください。
example_sentences.english: Since it is possible he may end up increasing the problems, someone please give him some proper advice.

example_sentences.japanese: この暑さでマラソン大会を行なったら、死者もでかねない。
example_sentences.english: If we hold a marathon in this heat, it is possible someone might die.

example_sentences.japanese: 賞味期限切れの食品は、下痢の原因になりかねない。
example_sentences.english: Expired food could be a cause of diarrhea.

example_sentences.japanese: あの財閥は、目的を達するためなら他人などかまわず何でもやりかねない。
example_sentences.english: That firm is quite capable of doing anything to reach their goals without any regard to other people.

example_sentences.japanese: あの様子だとまた家出しかねない。そうならないように、話を聞いてあげてください。
example_sentences.english: It looks like they might run away from home again. Please listen to them so that doesn't happen.

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんと毎日勉強すれば、来週のテストは合格できかねない。
example_sentences.english: If I study everyday, I might do well on the test next week.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はどんな病気でも治しかねない。
example_sentences.english: It wouldn't be a stretch to say that she can cure any disease.

general_translation: Regardless of, Whether or, No matter, With or without
formation: Noun (A) + 、(1) + Noun (B) +  にかかわらず(2)A(3) + か + B(3) + か + にかかわらず(2)A(4) + (Antonym) A(4) + にかかわらず(2)A(3) + かどうか(5) + にかかわらず(2)A(3) + A［ない］(3) + にかかわらず(2)(1) ・、と、や(2) にかかわりなく(3)  Noun、 ［な］Adjective、 ［い］Adjective、 Verb(4) ［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective(5) か否（いな）か
casual_structure: Noun (A) + 、(1) + Noun (B) +  にかかわらず(2)A(3) + か + B(3) + か + にかかわらず(2)A(4) + (Antonym) A(4) + にかかわらず(2)A(3) + かどうか(5) + にかかわらず(2)A(3) + A［ない］(3) + にかかわらず(2)(1) ・、と、や(2) にかかわりなく(3)  Noun、 ［な］Adjective、 ［い］Adjective、 Verb(4) ［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective(5) か否（いな）か
explanation: A phrase expressing that there is no link to (A), and therefore regardless of (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 点数にかかわらず、参加しただけで合格できる試験もある。
example_sentences.english: There are tests that you can pass just by attending, regardless of your score.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が降るか降らないかにかかわらず、運動会は開催されます。
example_sentences.english: The sports day will be held, regardless of whether it rains or not.

example_sentences.japanese: このビーチは天気がいいかどうかにかかわらず、毎日サーファーたちで賑わっています。
example_sentences.english: This beach is crowded with surfers regardless of the weather.

example_sentences.japanese: 上手い下手にかかわらず、何事も一生懸命やるのが大切だ。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of if you are good or bad, it is important to do your best at everything you do.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は性別や国籍にかかわらず、誰とでも友達になれる。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of gender or nationality, he is able to become friends with anyone.

example_sentences.japanese: このゲームは年齢にかかわらず、誰でも楽しめます！
example_sentences.english: Regardless of age, anyone can enjoy this game!

example_sentences.japanese: 好き嫌いにかかわらず、この課題はやってもらわないと困ります。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether you like it or not, I need you to do this assignment.

example_sentences.japanese: 流行にかかわらず、彼は昔からああいう格好をしています。
example_sentences.english: No matter if it is in vogue or not, he has been wearing that kind of clothing for a long time.

example_sentences.japanese: 実力にかかわらず仕事を与えるから、かなり効率が悪い。
example_sentences.english: They are given a job regardless of their ability, so performance is quite bad.

example_sentences.japanese: この棚の商品に限り、大きい小さいにかかわらず、全品100円。
example_sentences.english: Limited to only this shelf: regardless of whether it is big or small, all products are 100 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 中身の良し悪しにかかわらず、とにかく安いから福袋をたくさん買ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: No matter if the contents are good or bad, I just bought a bunch of grab bags because they were cheap.

example_sentences.japanese: お天気にかかわらず雨天でも、例年通り、マンション周辺の草取りを行います。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of the weather, even if it's rainy, the annual apartment building weeding event will take place.

example_sentences.japanese: 性別や年齢にかかわらず、人は毎日健康の為に散歩をします。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of gender or age, people walk for their health every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 走っている車は、速いか遅いかにかかわらず、歩行者からすると常に危険だ。
example_sentences.english: Moving cars, regardless of whether they are fast or slow, are always dangerous from the perspective of pedestrians.

example_sentences.japanese: 正義感が強いかどうかにかかわらず、責任をもって活動できる限り、ボランティアになることができる！
example_sentences.english: Regardless of having a strong sense of justice or not, as long as one can perform the activities responsibly, then they can become a volunteer.

example_sentences.japanese: 商品の使用前使用後にかかわらず、会社方針により返品は受け入れられません。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether you have used the product or not, according to the company policy, we do not accept refunds.

example_sentences.japanese: 広告：「このジムの開店記念日のため、今週のみ、会員の有無にかかわらず入場無料の行事を実施します！」
example_sentences.english: Advertisement: 'Due to it being the anniversary of this gym, for this week only, regardless of if you are a member or not, we are holding a free admission event!'

general_translation: Despite, In spite of, Regardless, Nevertheless
formation: Verb + にもかかわらず［い］Adjective +  にもかかわらず［な］Adjective + である + にもかかわらずNoun + （である）+ にもかかわらず
casual_structure: Verb + にもかかわらず［い］Adjective +  にもかかわらず［な］Adjective + である + にもかかわらずNoun + （である）+ にもかかわらず
explanation: A somewhat formal phrase highlighting that regardless of (A), (B). Without fixating on (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 勘違いしたにもかかわらず、彼は一切謝らない。
example_sentences.english: Even though he made a mistake, he will never apologize.

example_sentences.japanese: 浜崎さんは毎日一生懸命働いていたのにもかかわらず、会社をクビになった。
example_sentences.english: Despite working hard every day, Hamasaki-san was fired by the company.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が悪いのにもかかわらず、私に謝らせようとしてきた。
example_sentences.english: Despite him being in the wrong, he tried to make me apologize.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんは優しくて親切であるにもかかわらず、見た目が怖いから田中さんのことをよく知らない人からは怖がられて避けられている。
example_sentences.english: Despite Tanaka-san being kind and helpful, he's feared and avoided by those who don't know him well because of his scary appearance.

example_sentences.japanese: 深夜にもかかわらず上司が鬼電をしてきたので、労基に報告しようと思う。
example_sentences.english: Despite being late at night, my boss blew up my phone, so I'm thinking of reporting it to the labor standards inspection office.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなにかわいがったにもかかわらず、裏切られるなんて…
example_sentences.english: Despite showing them that much adoration, (who would have thought) that they would betray us...

example_sentences.japanese: 間隔があいたにもかかわらず、相変わらずいいプレーをしますね。
example_sentences.english: Even though a space opened, they made a nice play, like usual.

example_sentences.japanese: 乾燥しているにもかかわらず加湿しないから、喉をやられた。
example_sentences.english: Since I didn't run the humidifier regardless of it being dry, my voice got hoarse.

example_sentences.japanese: 喉が渇いているにもかかわらず、飲み物を与えないのは虐待だ。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of them being thirsty, not giving them anything to drink is cruel.

example_sentences.japanese: 物理の授業：「この物体は小さいにもかかわらず、真空では大きい物体と同じ速度で落下します。」
example_sentences.english: Physics class: 'Despite being small, in a vacuum this object falls at the same speed as a large object.'

example_sentences.japanese: カロリーが高いにもかかわらず、甘いものを毎日たくさん食べてしまう...
example_sentences.english: Even though they are high in calories, I unfortunately eat a lot of sweets every day...

example_sentences.japanese: オデュッセウスは多数の危険にもかかわらず、大変な努力の結果、ついに彼の国に帰ることができた。
example_sentences.english: Despite numerous dangers, Odysseus was able to finally return to his country as a result of his great efforts.

example_sentences.japanese: 農民が一生懸命に働いていたにもかかわらず、悪天候のせいで、作物の収穫が少なかった。
example_sentences.english: Despite the farmers giving it their all, due to the bad weather, there was a low harvest of crops.

example_sentences.japanese: 古代ローマ時代、ガリアはローマによって征服されたにもかかわらず、ある小さな村はなおも戦い続けた。
example_sentences.english: In Ancient Roman times, despite Gaul being conquered by Rome, a certain small village was still fighting.

example_sentences.japanese: 熊は重いにもかかわらず、速く走れたり、木に登れたりするので、危険な動物だ。本物を見かけたら、じっとして驚かさないでください。
example_sentences.english: Despite being heavy, since bears run fast, climb trees, and more, they are dangerous animals. If you happen to see one, stand still and do not surprise them.

example_sentences.japanese: 単独の無名の英雄は満身創痍（傷だらけ）だった。それにもかかわらず、気力のみで、像のように立った。素晴らしい景色だったと思う。
example_sentences.english: A sole, nameless hero was wounded all over. Nevertheless, by sheer force of will, he remained standing like a statue. It was quite a beautiful sight.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんが来ることを知っていたにもかかわらず、部屋の掃除をしていなかったので息子を叱った。
example_sentences.english: Despite knowing that we were going to have guests over, my son did not clean his room so I scolded him.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんが来るかどうかに関わらず、部屋は綺麗にしておいてください。
example_sentences.english: Please keep your room clean no matter if guests are coming or not.

general_translation: Particularly when, Those who, Only when
formation: Noun + に限（かぎ）って
casual_structure: Noun + に限（かぎ）って
explanation: A structure that expresses that something is limited to things in (A), or within the situation of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 昼寝をしている時にかぎって電話が鳴る。
example_sentences.english: Particularly when I am napping does the phone ring.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの子にかぎって、他の子に手を出すなんて考えられない。
example_sentences.english: I can't imagine that my child, in particular, would hit another kid.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼にかぎって、こんな簡単なことでミスをする訳が無い。
example_sentences.english: There is no way that he, in particular, would make a mistake on something this simple.

example_sentences.japanese: 武くんと釣りに行く日にかぎって、いつも雨が降るんだよな。
example_sentences.english: Only on days when I go fishing with Takeshi-kun does it always rain.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩は忙しい日にかぎって、飲みに誘ってくる。
example_sentences.english: My senpai invites me to go drinking with him only on days that I am busy.

example_sentences.japanese: 「クレームを入れるぞ」って言う人にかぎってクレームを入れないからあまり気にしていない。
example_sentences.english: I'm not too worried because particularly those who say, 'I'm going to file a claim', never do (file a claim).

example_sentences.japanese: 「絶対後でやる」って言う人にかぎって、いつまでもやらない人が多い。
example_sentences.english: Many of those who say, 'I'll definitely do it later', never do.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕がカメラを忘れた日にかぎって虹が出る。
example_sentences.english: Only on days when I forget my camera do rainbows appear.

example_sentences.japanese: 新曲発売日にかぎって大雨だ。
example_sentences.english: Only on days when a new song is released is it pouring rain.

example_sentences.japanese: 早口の人にかぎってたくさんしゃべるから、聞き取れない。
example_sentences.english: It’s always the fast talkers who talk a lot, so I can’t catch what they’re saying.

example_sentences.japanese: 外に調査へ出かける時にかぎって、雨が降る。
example_sentences.english: It is only when I go out to investigate that it rains.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は大事な時にかぎって力を発揮できない。
example_sentences.english: Only when it is important, am I unable to demonstrate my strength.

example_sentences.japanese: 飛行機に乗る時にかぎって、天候が悪かったりする。
example_sentences.english: The weather becomes bad and such particularly when I board an airplane.

example_sentences.japanese: 花火の日にかぎって仕事が入り見に行けない。
example_sentences.english: Particularly on days when there are fireworks I have to go to work, preventing me from being able to go watch.

example_sentences.japanese: 歯磨きをした後にかぎって夫がお土産を買ってくる。
example_sentences.english: Only when I brush my teeth will my husband buy me a present.

example_sentences.japanese: 人通りが多い日にかぎってあの場所に行かなければいけないから嫌だ。
example_sentences.english: I dislike it because, only on days when there is a lot of pedestrian traffic do I have to go to that place.

example_sentences.japanese: 定休日ではないのに、僕があの店に行く日にかぎって臨時休業している。
example_sentences.english: Despite it not being a set holiday, only on days when I go to that store is it temporarily closed.

example_sentences.japanese: よく節約を口にしている人にかぎって、給料を受け取っては、後で身につけもしない服など無駄遣いしがちだ。
example_sentences.english: Those who often speak about 'economizing' tend to waste their money on things like clothes they don't even wear whenever they receive salary.

general_translation: Not just, Not only… but also
formation: Noun + に限（かぎ）らず
casual_structure: Noun + に限（かぎ）らず
explanation: A slightly formal phrase used to highlight that something is not limited to being within (A), or in (A).

example_sentences.japanese: ラッシュアワーにかぎらず、電車にはあまり乗りたくない。
example_sentences.english: Not only during rush hour, but I don't really want to ride the train.

example_sentences.japanese: ＵＳＪは週末にかぎらず、平日でも多くの人で賑わっています。
example_sentences.english: USJ is crowded not only on weekends, but also on weekdays.

example_sentences.japanese: この遊園地は子供にかぎらず、大人でも楽しめます。
example_sentences.english: This amusement park is enjoyable not only for children, but also for adults.

example_sentences.japanese: このカフェは女性にかぎらず、男性の方にも人気があります。
example_sentences.english: This café is popular not only with women, but also with men.

example_sentences.japanese: このブランドは日本だけにかぎらず、韓国でも中国でも愛されています。
example_sentences.english: This brand is loved not only in Japan, but also in Korea and China.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい言語を習う場合、文法にかぎらず、その国の文化もニュアンスも同じぐらい勉強したほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: When learning a new language, you should study not only the grammar, but also the culture and nuances of the country, if possible.

example_sentences.japanese: マンションにかぎらず、綺麗な部屋なら住んでみたい。
example_sentences.english: Not just apartments, but if there are beautiful rooms I want to try living there.

example_sentences.japanese: オルガンにかぎらず、鍵盤楽器はだいたい弾けます。
example_sentences.english: Not just the organ, but I can somewhat play any instrument with a keyboard.

example_sentences.japanese: 生け花にかぎらず、正座をするのが苦手です。
example_sentences.english: Not just in ikebana, but I don't like (sitting in) seiza (in general).

example_sentences.japanese: 英文にかぎらず、アルファベットを使った文章が好きです。
example_sentences.english: Not only English sentences, but I like sentences that use the alphabet.

example_sentences.japanese: 宴会にかぎらず、誰かと騒ぎたいと思うことがある。
example_sentences.english: Not just a party, but I think I want to get wild with someone.

example_sentences.japanese: ペラペラになるためには勉強にかぎらず練習を積むことが大切だ。
example_sentences.english: In order to become fluent, it is important to not only study, but also to practice.

example_sentences.japanese: リボンにかぎらず、女の子らしい飾りは私には似合わない。
example_sentences.english: Not just ribbons, but any girly decorations don't suit me.

example_sentences.japanese: 女の人にかぎらず、知らない人と話すと緊張する。
example_sentences.english: Not just women, but I get nervous when I talk to anybody I do not know.

example_sentences.japanese: 酔っ払いにかぎらず、お酒を飲んでいる人と話すのが苦手です。
example_sentences.english: Not only drunks, but I dislike talking to people who are drinking alcohol.

example_sentences.japanese: 均整で良い姿になるために、夏にかぎらず、年中運動すべきです。
example_sentences.english: In order to have a well-balanced appearance, we should exercise not only in summer, but throughout the year.

example_sentences.japanese: イエローストーン火山の爆発の可能性は、アメリカにかぎらず世界レベルの問題だ。
example_sentences.english: The possibility of the Yellowstone super volcano erupting is not only a problem in the U.S., but also on an international level.

general_translation: Still, Even, Yet
formation: なお + Verb［ている］なお + Nounもいるなお + Nounもあるなお + Noun + だ(1)(1) である
casual_structure: なお + Verb［ている］なお + Nounもいるなお + Nounもあるなお + Noun + だ(1)(1) である
explanation: A formal phrase which highlights that something is still now or even now continuing. Esteeming or supplementing the base information of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: アメリア・イアハートの消失は今もなお謎である。
example_sentences.english: The disappearance of Amelia Earhart is still a mystery.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司のパワハラを人事に報告してもなお、上司のパワハラが続いている。
example_sentences.english: Even after reporting my boss to human resources for power harassment, his harassment is still continuing.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は先生に注意されてもなお、指摘された事を直そうとしない。
example_sentences.english: He still refuses to fix what was pointed out to him, even after being warned by his teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 豊橋市では今もなおチンチン電車が走っている。
example_sentences.english: Trams are still running in Toyohashi-city.

example_sentences.japanese: 浜崎先生は卒業後もなお、私たちの事をしっかりと覚えている。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Hamasaki still remembers us even after graduation.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学院生になってもなお、夜遊びをやめない人もいる。
example_sentences.english: There are people who become graduate school students, but still don't quit their nightlife.

example_sentences.japanese: 大工になってもなお、高いところが苦手な人もいるらしい。
example_sentences.english: Apparently there are people who become carpenters but are still scared of heights.

example_sentences.japanese: 短所に気づいてもなお認めようとしない人に未来はありませんよ。
example_sentences.english: People who notice their shortcomings and still don't acknowledge them, have no future.

example_sentences.japanese: 蒸気機関車は今もなお、電気がない地域において使用されている。
example_sentences.english: Steam locomotives are still used in areas where there is no electricity.

example_sentences.japanese: 討議を続けてもなお問題の解決が見られなかった。
example_sentences.english: Even after continuously discussing the problem, a solution has yet to present itself.

example_sentences.japanese: 時間を超過してもなお話し続ける校長先生をなんとかしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please do something about the principal who (still) continues to talk even after talking too much.

example_sentences.japanese: 追加してもなお足りないということなので、工場で商品を生産します。
example_sentences.english: Even if it received supplementation, it is still insufficient, so they will make merchandise at the factory.

example_sentences.japanese: 店を潰してもなお強気な元店長のあの態度は謎だ。
example_sentences.english: Even though (he) shut the store down, it is a mystery why the former store manager still has such an attitude.

example_sentences.japanese: 定員に達してもなお申し込みの電話が鳴り止まないほど人気だ。
example_sentences.english: It is so popular that even if we reach our staff quota, the phone calls will still not stop coming in with requests.

example_sentences.japanese: ある旅館は７１８年以来今もなお一家族によって経営されている。これからもそのまま続いていくだろう。
example_sentences.english: A certain ryokan is still managed by one family since 718. It seems it will continue like that in the future.

example_sentences.japanese: 退院してもなお病院に遊びに来る人が絶えないほど人気の病院があるらしい。
example_sentences.english: Apparently there are hospitals that are so popular that even after being released, people still come to visit.

general_translation: In addition, Incidentally, Furthermore, Moreover
formation: Phrase. なお、+ Phrase
casual_structure: Phrase. なお、+ Phrase
explanation: A formal expression which aims to esteem or supplement the base information of (A). (A) and furthermore (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は臨時休業です。なお、定休日は水曜日です。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow is a temporary holiday. In addition, Wednesday is our set store holiday.

example_sentences.japanese: それでは只今から説明会を開始したいと思います。なお、ご不明な点がある場合はお気軽にお申し付けください。
example_sentences.english: Well then, I'd like to begin the information session. In addition, if you have any questions, please feel free to ask.

example_sentences.japanese: ５日の土曜日には１１時までに待ち合わせ場所に集合してください。なお、遅れる場合は私のＬＩＮＥまで連絡をください。
example_sentences.english: Please be at the meeting place by 11:00 am on Saturday the 5th. Moreover, if you are going to be late, please message me on LINE.

example_sentences.japanese: 内容の確認が出来ましたら、「次へ」をクリックしてください。なお、「次へ」をクリックした後には内容の変更ができないのでご注意ください。
example_sentences.english: After confirming the details, please click 'Next'. Furthermore please note that you cannot make changes after clicking 'Next'.

example_sentences.japanese: 作品の提出は今月いっぱいまで。なお、テーマは各自で考えること。
example_sentences.english: The window for turning in your work is through the end of the month. In addition, you should think about your theme individually.

example_sentences.japanese: 只今パンを焼いております。なお、出来上がりは１１時を予定しております。
example_sentences.english: Bread is currently being baked. In addition, it is scheduled to be ready at 11.

example_sentences.japanese: 説明は以上です。なお、手続きは明後日までにお願いします。
example_sentences.english: This concludes the explanation. In addition, please do the formalities by the day after tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: では、これで試験を終わります。なお、点数は追って発表いたします。
example_sentences.english: Well, this concludes the test. In addition, I will announce the score afterwards.

example_sentences.japanese: 本日はありがとうございました。なお、お問い合わせは私ではなく会社にお願いします。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for today. In addition, please send all inquiries to the company, not me.

example_sentences.japanese: マングースにはすばやい反射神経や分厚い毛皮がある。なお、コブラの毒に対して強い。したがって、蛇を食べることが多い。
example_sentences.english: The mongoose has fast reflexes and thick fur. Moreover, the mongoose is also resistant to snake venom. Therefore, it often eats snakes.

example_sentences.japanese: 打ち合わせはこれくらいでいいですね。なお、意見を統一した文書を作成し、後ほどメールで送ります。
example_sentences.english: This is good for the business meeting, I believe. In addition, I will write up a document with our unified opinions and email it later on.

example_sentences.japanese: 就職面接は８月２日に開催されます。なお、希望者は何か質問があれば、ご連絡ください。
example_sentences.english: The job interview will be held on August 2nd. Furthermore, if you have any questions, feel free to contact us.

example_sentences.japanese: 大会の日程は以下の通りです。なお、当日の天候によっては延期になる場合がありますので、ご了承ください。
example_sentences.english: The schedule for the tournament is as follows. In addition, please understand that the weather on the day of could result in a postponement.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋はご自由にお使いください。なお、盗難などの責任は負いかねますので、ご自分で管理してください。
example_sentences.english: Please use this room freely. In addition, please manage it yourself as we are not responsible for lost or stolen items.

example_sentences.japanese: ２０２Ｘ年７月２４日にマンション周辺の草取りを行います。なお、同時に、住人の子供向きのイベントも行います。
example_sentences.english: On 07/24/202X, weeding will take place around the apartment buildings. In addition, an event for residents' children will also be held at the same time.

general_translation: As long as, While… is the case, Limited to
formation: Verb［る］(1) + 限（かぎ）り + PhraseVerb［ない］+ 限（かぎ）り + PhraseVerb［ている］+ 限（かぎ）り + PhraseNoun + である + 限（かぎ）り(1) Verb［た］
casual_structure: Verb［る］(1) + 限（かぎ）り + PhraseVerb［ない］+ 限（かぎ）り + PhraseVerb［ている］+ 限（かぎ）り + PhraseNoun + である + 限（かぎ）り(1) Verb［た］
explanation: A structure showing that limited to (A) continuing, (B) will not change. As long as (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 行列に並ばないかぎり、あのパンは買えない。
example_sentences.english: As long as you do not get in the large line, you cannot buy that bread.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が真剣に芸人になりたいと言っているかぎり、彼の夢は叶うだろう。
example_sentences.english: As long as he keeps saying he seriously wants to become a comedian, his dream will probably come true.

example_sentences.japanese: この商品の販売は今週かぎりとさせていただきます。
example_sentences.english: Sales of this item will be limited to this week.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼から聞いたかぎり、田中君は退学になるらしい。
example_sentences.english: As far as I heard from him, apparently, Tanaka-kun is getting expelled.

example_sentences.japanese: このアパートの住人であるかぎりは、アパートのルールを守っていただかないと困ります。
example_sentences.english: As long as you are a resident of this apartment, we need you to follow the apartment rules.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に住むかぎり、日本の法律を守らなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: Assuming that you live in Japan, you need to obey Japanese law.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族の大黒柱であるかぎり、家族を支えなければならない。
example_sentences.english: Since I am the pillar of the family, I must support my family.

example_sentences.japanese: 意識して気を付けないかぎり、あの癖は直らない。
example_sentences.english: As long as you are not mindful, you will not break that habit.

example_sentences.japanese: 離島に漂流者：「見るかぎり、水しかない...」
example_sentences.english: Castaway on an isolated Island: 'As far as I can see, there's nothing but water...'

example_sentences.japanese: 休息をとらないかぎり、体調は回復しませんよ。
example_sentences.english: You will not regain your strength, as long as you do not rest.

example_sentences.japanese: あの教えを心に刻んでいるかぎり、人の道を踏み外したりはしないはずだ。
example_sentences.english: As long as those teachings are etched in their mind, they should not lose their way.

example_sentences.japanese: 基礎からやり直さないかぎりどうにもならないと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that it is futile as long as we do not rethink our foundations.

example_sentences.japanese: 何か大きなきっかけがないかぎり、彼は変わらないだろう。
example_sentences.english: As long as there isn't some big chance, he will not change, right?

example_sentences.japanese: ウォーミングアップを忘れないかぎり、怪我する可能性は低い。
example_sentences.english: As long as you don't forget to warm-up, the possibility of getting injured will be low.

example_sentences.japanese: ホラー映画の主人公：「ぴたりと寄り添って歩いているかぎり、だれも迷子にならないだろう。」
example_sentences.english: Horror movie protagonist: 'As long as we are walking close to one another, no-one will get lost.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「田中さんって結婚してるの？」 Ｂ：「聞いたかぎりでは、まだ独身よ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Is Tanaka-san married?' B: 'As far as I have heard, he is still single.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「すみません、スーパーはこの辺りですか？」 Ｂ：「知っているかぎりでは、もうちょっと前にあります。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Excuse me, is there a supermarket around here?' B: 'As far as I know, it is a bit further down the road.'

example_sentences.japanese: 銀行強盗のお互いの会話：「動作中は誰も私たちの顔を見てない、調べたかぎりね。」
example_sentences.english: Conversation between bank robbers: 'As far as I know (after making sure), no-one has seen our faces during the operation.'

general_translation: Depending on, So
formation: Noun + 次第（しだい） + だNoun + 次第（しだい）で
casual_structure: Noun + 次第（しだい） + だNoun + 次第（しだい）で
polite_structure: Noun + 次第（しだい） + ですNoun + 次第（しだい）で
explanation: A phrase which indicates (A) as determining what will happen next, or any following result depending on it.

example_sentences.japanese: ワインの渋味は濃度しだいだ。
example_sentences.english: Wine's astringency depends on its concentration.

example_sentences.japanese: 夢をかなえられるかどうかは君の努力しだいだ。
example_sentences.english: Being able to make your dream come true or not depends on you.

example_sentences.japanese: 第一希望の大学へ入れるかは、試験の結果しだいだ。
example_sentences.english: Whether I can go to the college of my first choice or not, depends on my test results.

example_sentences.japanese: 内装工事の完成日しだいで、鍵の引き渡し日が変わる可能性があります。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the completion date of the interior construction, the date for handing over the key may change.

example_sentences.japanese: 値段しだいで、ナビを付けるか付けないかを決めます。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the price, I will decide on whether I want to install a navigation system or not.

example_sentences.japanese: 成功は大抵努力しだいだ。
example_sentences.english: Success depends mostly on effort.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気しだいで、日帰りか一泊二日かを決めます。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the weather, we will decide on a daytrip or staying overnight.

example_sentences.japanese: アイデアしだいで、売上にかなりの違いが出てきます。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the idea, a considerable difference in sales will show up.

example_sentences.japanese: 応援しだいで、試合の結果が変わることもあり得ます。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the support, it is likely that the result of the match could change.

example_sentences.japanese: うどんの旨さは、麺のコシしだいだと言っても過言ではない。
example_sentences.english: To say that the deliciousness of udon depends on the elasticity of the noodles is not an exaggeration.

example_sentences.japanese: ライバルを追い越せるかどうかは、今日のテストの結果しだいだ。
example_sentences.english: Whether you overtake the competition or not depends on the results of today's test.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はおとなしそうに見えるが、相手しだいではかなりしゃべります。
example_sentences.english: He looks like he is quiet, but depending on who he is with, he will talk quite a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 温泉の泉質しだいでは入れないことがある。アレルギーがあるから。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the quality of the onsen's spring I might not be able to get in. Because I have allergies.

example_sentences.japanese: 羨ましいと思うかどうかは、各自の価値観しだいだ。
example_sentences.english: Whether you think it is enviable or not depends on your personal values.

example_sentences.japanese: 育児がどれくらい大変になるかは、夫や家族がどれくらい協力してくれるかしだいだ。
example_sentences.english: How difficult child raising becomes depends on how much cooperation your husband and family give you.

example_sentences.japanese: 結果しだいでは、改めて別の検査が必要になります。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the results, you will need to be checked again using a different test.

general_translation: Gradually
formation: 次第（しだい）に + Phrase
casual_structure: 次第（しだい）に + Phrase
explanation: An adverb that expresses that the course of events changes gradually or little by little.

example_sentences.japanese: 膝の痛みはしだいに和らいでいった。
example_sentences.english: My knee pain has gradually eased up.

example_sentences.japanese: 薬を飲んだら、しだいに痛みが引いてきたよ。
example_sentences.english: Once I took some medicine, the pain gradually receded.

example_sentences.japanese: しだいに雲行きが怪しくなり、イベントの中止をせざるを得なくなった。
example_sentences.english: As the outlook gradually turned ominous, we had no choice but to cancel the event.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の表情がしだいに暗くなっていき、最終的には涙を流していた。
example_sentences.english: Her expression gradually went dark, and she ended up in floods of tears.

example_sentences.japanese: しだいに雨も止むであろうから、このまま練習を続けよう。
example_sentences.english: Since the rain will probably gradually let up, let’s keep practicing as we are.

example_sentences.japanese: 二人暮らしに慣れていなかったけど、しだいに居心地が良くなっていったよ。
example_sentences.english: I wasn’t used to living with someone else, but it’s gradually come to be comfortable.

example_sentences.japanese: 初対面は緊張したけど、しだいに打ち解けていった。
example_sentences.english: I was nervous when we first met, but I’ve gradually opened up.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝晩の冷え込みがしだいに激しくなり、冬の訪れを感じた。
example_sentences.english: As the morning and evening cold has gradually become harsher, I felt winter’s arrival.

example_sentences.japanese: トレーニングを始めてから、しだいに体脂肪率が減少していった。
example_sentences.english: Since I started training, my body fat percentage has gradually decreased.

example_sentences.japanese: 時が経つにつれ、しだいに彼への愛情は無くなっていった。
example_sentences.english: With the passing of time, I gradually lost my love for him.

example_sentences.japanese: 人々の関心は時とともにしだいに薄れていき、話題に上ることも少なくなった。
example_sentences.english: People’s interest gradually faded with time, and it became broached less often as a topic of discussion.

example_sentences.japanese: 沈黙の中、しだいに空気が重くなっていくのを誰もが感じていたが、それを破ろうとする者はいなかった。
example_sentences.english: Within the silence, everyone felt the atmosphere gradually turn oppressive and yet there was no one who tried to break it.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい制度を導入してから数ヶ月が経ち、しだいに社内に定着していった。
example_sentences.english: Several months passed since the new system was introduced, and it gradually established itself within the company.

example_sentences.japanese: 幼少期に苦手意識のあった納豆も、大人になるにつれて、しだいに食べられるようになった。
example_sentences.english: Even natto, which I was very aware of not liking as a young child, I gradually came to be able to eat as I became an adult.

example_sentences.japanese: エネルギー価格の高騰が家計を圧迫し、しだいに生活に深刻な影響を及ぼし始めている。
example_sentences.english: The extreme inflation of energy prices is putting pressure on household budgets, and gradually starting to have a serious influence on daily life.

example_sentences.japanese: わずか数ヶ月のうちに二人は次第に疎遠になった。
example_sentences.english: Within a few months, the two gradually drifted apart.

example_sentences.japanese: ガソリンの価格は次第に安くなると予測されている。
example_sentences.english: Gasoline prices are expected to gradually become cheaper.

example_sentences.japanese: 友人の祖父の健康状態が次第に悪化していることも知らずに、変なことを聞いてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I asked him such insensitive questions, unaware that his grandfather’s health was gradually deteriorating.

example_sentences.japanese: この対策により、次第に経済が回復すると予想されています。
example_sentences.english: This measure is expected to gradually restore the economy.

example_sentences.japanese: なんか最近物価がだんだん上がってきたね。
example_sentences.english: Don't you think prices of things have been gradually going up?

general_translation: Only if, Because, By, Unless, Until
formation: Verb［て］+ こそ
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ こそ
explanation: An expression that indicates doing (A) as being the precise reason for something, in a similar way to capitalization of a word in English.

example_sentences.japanese: たすけあってこその親友じゃないか。
example_sentences.english: One is being a friend only by helping one another, isn't that right? (only because)

example_sentences.japanese: 海外に留学してこそ、日本食の美味しさが分かる。
example_sentences.english: Only by studying abroad can one appreciate the deliciousness of Japanese food.

example_sentences.japanese: 親になってこそ、子育ての大変さがわかる。
example_sentences.english: It's only when you become a parent that you understand how hard it is to raise a child.

example_sentences.japanese: チーム全員の責任を背負ってこそ、キャプテンになれる。
example_sentences.english: You become a captain only if you take on the responsibility of the whole team.

example_sentences.japanese: 他のチームに勝ってこそ、世界一になれる。
example_sentences.english: Only by beating other teams can we become the best in the world.

example_sentences.japanese: 全部そろえてこそのコレクションだ。
example_sentences.english: A collection is a collection only when everything is complete. (because・until/unless)

example_sentences.japanese: 優勝してこそ、自信に繋がる。
example_sentences.english: It is only by winning that one becomes confident. (unless/until)

example_sentences.japanese: くだらないプライドをすててこそ、男らしくなれる。
example_sentences.english: Only if you throw aside your worthless pride will you be able to become more manly. (until/unless)

example_sentences.japanese: 全員参加してこその遠足だ。
example_sentences.english: It is only because everyone is participating that it is an outing. (until/unless)

example_sentences.japanese: 責任をとってこそ、真のリーダーだ。
example_sentences.english: Now that you have taken responsibility, you are a true leader. (only because)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本へいってこそ、京都の魅力が分かる。
example_sentences.english: Only by going to Japan, one can understand the charm of Kyoto.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗してこそ、本当の成功に辿り着ける。
example_sentences.english: Only by failing, one can truly walk the path to success.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分でやってみてこそ、撮影の難しさが分かるはずです。
example_sentences.english: You are expected to understand the difficulties of photography only by trying it yourself. (until/unless)

example_sentences.japanese: 体験してこそ、作者が苦悩した理由が分かる。
example_sentences.english: Only by personally experiencing it, you will understand the reason the author was distressed. (until/unless)

example_sentences.japanese: 手紙は手書きでかいてこそ、気持ちが伝わるものだ。
example_sentences.english: Only if you write the letter by hand will your feelings will be conveyed.

example_sentences.japanese: 親になってこそ、子供は奇跡だという考え方が分かる。
example_sentences.english: Only by becoming a parent, you can understand the mindset that children are miracles.

general_translation: Regardless of, Whether or not, No matter, With or without
formation: Noun + を問（と）わず(5)Noun (A) + 、(1) + Noun (B) +  を問（と）わず(5)A(2) + か + B(2) + か + を問（と）わず(5)A(3) + (Antonym) A(3) + を問（と）わず(5)A(2) + かどうか(4) + を問（と）わず(5)A(2) + A［ない］(2) + を問（と）わず(5) (1) ・、と、や(2)  Noun、 ［な］Adjective、 ［い］Adjective、 Verb(3) ［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective(4) か否（いな）か(5) を問（と）わない。
casual_structure: Noun + を問（と）わず(5)Noun (A) + 、(1) + Noun (B) +  を問（と）わず(5)A(2) + か + B(2) + か + を問（と）わず(5)A(3) + (Antonym) A(3) + を問（と）わず(5)A(2) + かどうか(4) + を問（と）わず(5)A(2) + A［ない］(2) + を問（と）わず(5) (1) ・、と、や(2)  Noun、 ［な］Adjective、 ［い］Adjective、 Verb(3) ［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective(4) か否（いな）か(5) を問（と）わない。
polite_structure: Noun + を問（と）わず(5)Noun (A) + 、(1) + Noun (B) +  を問（と）わず(5)A(2) + か + B(2) + か + を問（と）わず(5)A(3) + (Antonym) A(3) + を問（と）わず(5)A(2) + かどうか(4) + を問（と）わず(5)A(2) + A［ない］(2) + を問（と）わず(5) (1) ・、と、や(2)  Noun、 ［な］Adjective、 ［い］Adjective、 Verb(3) ［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective(4) か否（いな）か(5) を問（と）いません。
explanation: A construction stating that (A) need not be questioned. Often meaning regardless of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: どんな役かはとわず、主役であればね。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of the role, if it is a leading role (it doesn't matter). (no matter)

example_sentences.japanese: 宗教や国籍をとわず、このイベントには誰でも参加できます。
example_sentences.english: Everyone is welcome to attend this event, regardless of religion or nationality.

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンの上級者か初心者かをとわず、初めてこのサービスをお使いになられる方には初心者コースから始めてもらいます。
example_sentences.english: Whether you are an advanced computer user or a beginner, we ask first-time users of this service to start with the beginner course.

example_sentences.japanese: このマンションを買うかどうかをとわず、この物件を押さえたい場合は手付金を払ってください。
example_sentences.english: If you want to hold on to this property, whether you buy this apartment or not, you must pay a deposit.

example_sentences.japanese: どのブランドかはとわず、とにかく新しい靴が欲しいです。
example_sentences.english: I just want a new pair of shoes, regardless of which brand.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は彼女と結婚したい。手段をとわない。
example_sentences.english: I want to marry her! No matter what. (regardless・whether or not)

example_sentences.japanese: 買う買わないをとわず、商品を試しに来てください。
example_sentences.english: (Regardless of) whether you will buy it or not, please come and try the product.

example_sentences.japanese: 好き嫌いをとわず探せば、仕事は見つかります。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of your likes and dislikes, if you look, you will find a job.

example_sentences.japanese: 上手い下手をとわず、習字の練習は続けてください。
example_sentences.english: Whether you are good at it or bad at it, please continue to practice your penmanship (calligraphy). (regardless of)

example_sentences.japanese: 資格をとわず募集したら、変な人ばかり集まってしまう。
example_sentences.english: If you recruit regardless of qualifications, you'll end up with only odd people. (with or without)

example_sentences.japanese: 速い遅いをとわず、みなさんにマラソンに参加していただきたいです。
example_sentences.english: Whether you are fast or slow, we would like everyone to participate in the marathon. (regardless of)

example_sentences.japanese: 契約するしないはとわず、とりあえず説明は聞いてもらいたい。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not you sign a contract, for the time being, I would like you to listen to my explanation. (regardless)

example_sentences.japanese: 学歴や経験をとわず、やる気のある応募者を雇う！
example_sentences.english: We are hiring motivated applicants with or without experience or academic background! (regardless of)

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいか古いかをとわず、全ての車は保険が法律で義務付けられている。
example_sentences.english: (Regardless of) whether it is new or old, all cars are obligated by law to have insurance.

example_sentences.japanese: 裕福な家庭であるか否かをとわず、日本では初等・中等教育は無料だ！
example_sentences.english: (Regardless of) whether the family is wealthy or not, primary and secondary education is free in Japan!

example_sentences.japanese: このアプリケーションは、管理者権限の有無をとわず誰でも使うことができる。
example_sentences.english: This application can be used by anyone, (regardless of) whether they have administrator's rights or not.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は昼夜を問わず、ずっと働いている。
example_sentences.english: Whether it is day or night, he is always working.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は昼夜に関わらず、ずっと働いている。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of day or night, he is always working.

grammar_point: より仕方（しかた）がない
general_translation: There is no choice but, Can't be helped, Inevitable
formation: Verb + より + （ほか(1)）+ 仕方（しかた）がない(2)(1) ほかに(2) 仕方（しかた）ない
casual_structure: Verb + より + （ほか(1)）+ 仕方（しかた）がない(2)(1) ほかに(2) 仕方（しかた）ない
explanation: A somewhat casual phrase, highlighting that apart from (A), there is no way for anything to be done.

example_sentences.japanese: 税金は、高くとも納めるよりしかたがない。
example_sentences.english: We have no choice but to pay taxes, even if they are high.

example_sentences.japanese: この建物はボロボロでいつ倒れてもおかしくないから、倉庫として使いたいなら立て直すよりしかたがない。
example_sentences.english: This building is in bad condition and could fall down at any time, so if I want to use it as a warehouse, I have no choice but to rebuild it.

example_sentences.japanese: 高速道路が通行止めになっている為、下道を使うよりしかたがない。
example_sentences.english: Since the expressway is closed, there is no choice but to take the normal road.

example_sentences.japanese: 生活をするにはお金が必要だから働くよりしかたない。
example_sentences.english: I need money in order to live, so there is no choice but to work.

example_sentences.japanese: 自転車のチェーンとブレーキがぶっ壊れたから、捨てるより他にない。
example_sentences.english: My bicycle chain and brakes are busted, so I have no choice but to throw them away.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司のパワハラのせいで病んできたので、精神科に行くより他にない。
example_sentences.english: My mental health is not doing well because of my boss' power harassment, so I have no choice but to go to a therapist.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなひどい事を言ってしまったので、謝るより他ない。
example_sentences.english: Because I said such a terrible thing, I have no choice but to apologize.

example_sentences.japanese: 税金は、納めるよりしかたのないものだ。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that there is no choice but to pay taxes.

example_sentences.japanese: ミシンが故障しているから、手で縫うよりしかたがない。
example_sentences.english: Since the sewing machine is broken, there is no choice but to sew (it) by hand.

example_sentences.japanese: 見本がないから、頭の中でイメージして作るよりしかたがない。
example_sentences.english: Since there is no example, there is no choice but to make an image in my head.

example_sentences.japanese: マラソン大会に出たいなら、地道にトレーニングを積むよりしかたがない。
example_sentences.english: If you want to enter a marathon, there is no choice but to steadily pile on the training.

example_sentences.japanese: この先で工事をしているようだから、回り道するよりしかたがない。
example_sentences.english: Since it seems that they are doing construction up ahead, there is no choice but to take a detour.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回のこの結果では、承認は見送るよりしかたがない。
example_sentences.english: Given the results from this time, we have no choice but to postpone this approval.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の名字を思い出せないから、名前で呼ぶよりしかたがない。
example_sentences.english: Since I can't remember his last name, there is no choice but to call him by his first name.

example_sentences.japanese: 親になると夜中赤ちゃんに起こされることに慣れるよりしかたがない。
example_sentences.english: If you become a parent, you have no choice but to get accustomed to being woken up in the middle of the night.

example_sentences.japanese: 行政のサービスが悪いから、お金がかかっても民間のサービスに頼るよりしかたがない。
example_sentences.english: Since the administrative services are bad, there is no choice but to rely on a private service even if it costs money.

example_sentences.japanese: 人生には好調な日もあれば、不調な日もある。したがって、不調の日は受け入れるよりしかたがないと思う。
example_sentences.english: In life, there are both good days and bad days. Therefore we have no choice but to accept the bad ones.

example_sentences.japanese: この遊園地は大人気だから、アトラクションに乗るには行列に並ぶよりしかたがない。
example_sentences.english: Since this amusement park is very popular, there is no choice but to line up in long lines to ride the attractions.

grammar_point: に越（こ）したことはない
general_translation: There is nothing better than, It is the best, Would be the best
formation: Verb + に越（こ）したことはない［い］Adjective + に越（こ）したことはない［な］Adjective + （である） + に越（こ）したことはないNoun + （である） + に越（こ）したことはない
casual_structure: Verb + に越（こ）したことはない［い］Adjective + に越（こ）したことはない［な］Adjective + （である） + に越（こ）したことはないNoun + （である） + に越（こ）したことはない
polite_structure: Verb + に越（こ）したことはありません［い］Adjective + に越（こ）したことはありません［な］Adjective +（である）+ に越（こ）したことはありませんNoun +（である）+ に越（こ）したことはありません
explanation: A phrase stating that (A) is the best, by indicating that, in general, there is nothing which surpasses it.

example_sentences.japanese: 休息できるにこしたことはないが、あまりにもひまだ。
example_sentences.english: Being able to take a break is the best, but I'm too bored.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩と待ち合わせているなら、待ち合わせ時間の１０分前に着くにこしたことはない。
example_sentences.english: If you are meeting a senpai, it is best to arrive 10 minutes before the meeting time.

example_sentences.japanese: 家は広いにこしたことはないが、値段と場所も大切だ。
example_sentences.english: There's nothing better than a spacious house, but the price and location are also important.

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋は綺麗であるにこしたことはないので、毎日掃除をしています。
example_sentences.english: I clean my room every day because there's nothing better than a clean room.

example_sentences.japanese: 億万長者であるにこしたことはない。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than being a billionaire.

example_sentences.japanese: 応援してもらうことにこしたことはないが、ちょっとやり過ぎです。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than having someone cheer for you, but I think they are overdoing it.

example_sentences.japanese: 受験は受かる確率が高いにこしたことはない。
example_sentences.english: There would be nothing better than if my chances of passing the exam are high.

example_sentences.japanese: オーケストラの楽器は多いにこしたことはないが、限度がある。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than having many instruments in an orchestra, but there are limits.

example_sentences.japanese: 基礎がしっかりしているにこしたことはないが、基礎にばかり時間をかけられない。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than having a strong foundation, but you can't spend all of your time on foundation alone.

example_sentences.japanese: 売上が上がるにこしたことはないが、強引に売ってはいけません。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than rising sales, but I must not sell forcibly.

example_sentences.japanese: 学力が高いにこしたことはないが、性格が悪いのは困りものだ。
example_sentences.english: His scholarly ability being high is the best, but his personality isn't good, so I am troubled (about what to do).

example_sentences.japanese: 退院できるにこしたことはないが、万全ではないなら退院するべきではない。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than being able to leave the hospital, but if you're not perfect, then you ought not leave.

example_sentences.japanese: 客席が埋まるにこしたことはないが、迷惑な客が多いと大変です。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than having all seats filled, but if there are many bothersome customers then it can get hectic.

example_sentences.japanese: 語学の習得を目指すなら、子供の頃から始めるにこしたことはないが、年をとってから勉強をし始めて流暢になった人もいる。
example_sentences.english: If you are aiming at learning a language, there is nothing better than starting as a child, however, there are also people who became fluent after getting older.

example_sentences.japanese: 合格するために教科書を全部覚えるにこしたことはないが、それほど時間がある人はいない。
example_sentences.english: In order to pass an exam, it would be best to memorize the whole textbook, but no one has that kind of time.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんの回転が速いにこしたことはないが、あまりにも注文が少ないのも困る。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than having a quick turn around of customers, but they are not ordering much, so I am bothered.

example_sentences.japanese: 災害は起きないにこしたことはない。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than a disaster not happening.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画はつまらなくないにこしたことはない。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than a movie not being boring.

example_sentences.japanese: テストは複雑ではないにこしたことはない。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than a test that is not complicated.

example_sentences.japanese: こう言う時には一人っ子ではないにこしたことはない。
example_sentences.english: At times like this, there is nothing better than not being an only child.

general_translation: To sum up, In summary, In short
formation: 要（よう）するに + Phrase
casual_structure: 要（よう）するに + Phrase
explanation: A sentence starter used for summarization, which explains that (A), but to say only what's needed, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: ようするに何でもいいよね？
example_sentences.english: In short, it is all the same to you?

example_sentences.japanese: ようするに、あなたは履歴書に嘘を書いたと言う事ですね。
example_sentences.english: In short, this means that you lied on your resume, doesn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: ようするに、小麦が入っている食べ物は食べれないと言う事ですね？
example_sentences.english: So, in summary, I can't eat any food that has wheat in it?

example_sentences.japanese: ようするに、俺はあいつに使われていたと言うことだ。
example_sentences.english: In short, I was being used by him.

example_sentences.japanese: ようするに、あなたは反省していないということですよ。
example_sentences.english: In summary, you aren't contemplating your actions.

example_sentences.japanese: ようするに、発想が貧弱だということでしょう。
example_sentences.english: In summary, this way of thinking is insubstantial, right?

example_sentences.japanese: ようするに、期限を延ばすことは許されないということです。
example_sentences.english: In summary, you will not let me extend the deadline.

example_sentences.japanese: ようするに、乗換を間違えて遅刻したということですね？
example_sentences.english: In summary, you made a mistake on your train transfer and are late, right?

example_sentences.japanese: ようするに、我々は会社の歯車にすぎないということだ。
example_sentences.english: In summary, we are no more than cogs in the wheel (company).

example_sentences.japanese: ようするに、今年の花火大会は中止にしたいということでしょ。
example_sentences.english: In summary, you want to suspend this years firework festival, right?

example_sentences.japanese: ようするに、能率の悪い仕事は引き受ける気がないんですね。
example_sentences.english: In summary, you don't feel like undertaking jobs that are inefficient, right?

example_sentences.japanese: ようするに、花嫁が結婚直前に逃げてしまったんですね？
example_sentences.english: In summary, the bride ran away right before the wedding, right?

example_sentences.japanese: ようするに、農薬は一切使ってはいけないということですよね？
example_sentences.english: In summary, without exception, you must not use agricultural chemicals, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 行員：「ようするにお金が足りない場合デビットカードを使えないということです。」
example_sentences.english: Bank clerk: 'In summary, if there is not enough money on the debit card, you won't be able to use it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 車の職人：「ようするに部品を替えるよりも機械を買い替えればいいってことだ。」
example_sentences.english: Car mechanic: 'In short, it's better to replace the whole machine, rather than just parts.'

general_translation: (Not) unless ~ cannot, (Not) until ~ cannot
formation: Verb［て］ + からでないと + (Negative)Verb［て］ + からでなければ + (Negative)
casual_structure: Verb［て］ + からでないと + (Negative)Verb［て］ + からでなければ + (Negative)
explanation: A hypothetical structure highlighting that if not done from (A), (B) will not be possible. Unless from (A), (B) won't happen.

example_sentences.japanese: サンプルをみてからでないと、買うかどうかは決められません。
example_sentences.english: Until I see the sample, I cannot decide whether to buy it or not.

example_sentences.japanese: 全ての書類が揃ってからでないと、本申し込みができません。
example_sentences.english: You can't submit the actual application unless you have all the documents.

example_sentences.japanese: このアプリをインストールしてからでないと、携帯に入れた音楽は聴けません。
example_sentences.english: You cannot listen to the music you put in your phone until you install this app.

example_sentences.japanese: 資格をとってからでなければ、面接が受けられません。
example_sentences.english: Unless you get the qualification, you cannot be interviewed.

example_sentences.japanese: その件については上司と相談してからでなければ、ご回答できません。
example_sentences.english: I will not be able to respond to you until I have discussed this matter with my supervisor.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫舌なので、さめてからでないと飲めない。
example_sentences.english: Since I am sensitive to hot things, until it cools, I cannot drink it.

example_sentences.japanese: 電源をきってからでないと、コンセントを抜いてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: Unless you turn off the power, you cannot unplug it.

example_sentences.japanese: サークルにはいってからでないと、活動に参加できない。
example_sentences.english: Unless you join (enter) the club, you cannot participate in the activities.

example_sentences.japanese: 撮影してからでないと、ギャラは入りません。
example_sentences.english: Until you (take) some photographs, you will not be paid.

example_sentences.japanese: 再来月になってからでないと、あのサービスには申し込めない。
example_sentences.english: Until (it becomes) the month after next, you cannot apply for that service.

example_sentences.japanese: さすがにお金をはらってからでないと、サービスを利用してはダメでしょ。
example_sentences.english: As expected, until you pay, you must not use the service.

example_sentences.japanese: 災難にあってからでないと分からないことがたくさんあります。
example_sentences.english: Unless you experience (meet) tragedy, there is a lot of things you won't understand.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人前になってからでなければ、親が酒なんて飲むのを許さない。
example_sentences.english: Until I become an adult, my parents won't allow me to drink alcohol.

example_sentences.japanese: 刺身をたべてからでないと寿司を食べないというこだわりがある。
example_sentences.english: (He) is picky about how (he) eat(s) sushi. (He) will not eat sushi unless (he) eats sashimi.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供：「いま出かけていい？」親：「まだだめ、部屋をかたづけてからでないと...」
example_sentences.english: Child: 'Is it ok if I go out?' Parent: 'Not yet, not unless you tidy up your room...'

example_sentences.japanese: このITコーポレーションでは、修士号を取得してからでないとシニアプログラマーになれない。
example_sentences.english: In this IT corporation, you cannot become a senior developer until you (get) a master's degree.

general_translation: It's not that…, Kind of, might, Slightly, Somewhat, In some respects
formation: Verb［なくて］+ はない［い］Adjective［く］ + なくはない［な］Adjective + では(1) + なくはないNoun + が(2) + なくはない(1)じゃ (2)は、に
casual_structure: Verb［なくて］+ はない［い］Adjective［く］ + なくはない［な］Adjective + では(1) + なくはないNoun + が(2) + なくはない(1)じゃ (2)は、に
explanation: A phrase highlighting that (A) not being the case is not generally true, or that it may be true in some respects.

example_sentences.japanese: 貯金すればかえなくはない。
example_sentences.english: If I save, I may be able to buy it. (Literally - I won't not be able to buy it)

example_sentences.japanese: 納豆は食べれなくはないけど、どうせ食べるならもっと美味しいものを食べたいかな。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I don't like natto, it's just that if I am going to eat something, I want to eat something more delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: その距離だったら、頑張れば走れなくはない。
example_sentences.english: If it was that distance, it would be hard work, but I may be able to run that.

example_sentences.japanese: 別に出来なくはないけど、めんどくさいから業者に頼むわ。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I can't do it, but since it is too much of a hassle, I'm going to hire someone to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: それを買うお金がなくはないが、そんなくだらないことにお金を使いたくない。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I don't have money to buy that, but that I don't want to spend my money on something so stupid.

example_sentences.japanese: 時間はなくはないんですが、もっと時間を有効に使いたいだけです。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I don't have time, but that I just want to make better use of my time.

example_sentences.japanese: 家にテレビがなくはないけど、アンテナがつながっていないからモニターとして使ってる。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I don't have a TV at home, but since the antenna is not connected, I am using it as a monitor.

example_sentences.japanese: かなり固い木だが、このカンナでけずれなくはない。
example_sentences.english: The tree is quite hard, but it's not that it can't be planed with this wood planer.

example_sentences.japanese: 難しそうだが、自分でくみたてられなくはない。
example_sentences.english: It looks difficult, but it's not that you can't put it together yourself.

example_sentences.japanese: その意見を考えた上で、賛成できなくはない。
example_sentences.english: After considering that opinion, I can somewhat agree. (Literally - I can't not agree)

example_sentences.japanese: 原理はわからなくはないが、すべてを理解するのは難しい。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I don't understand the principle, but comprehending it entirely is difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: 心当たりはなくはないのですが、証拠がありません。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I don't know that it happened, but there isn't any proof.

example_sentences.japanese: 集中できなくはないが、今は空想しかできない。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I can't focus, it's just that I can't do anything but daydream right now.

example_sentences.japanese: コレクションの中になくはないが、君にあげる気にはなれない。
example_sentences.english: It's not that it is not in/part of a collection, but I just don't feel like giving it to you.

example_sentences.japanese: 捜せばなくはないと思うが、捜すのが大変すぎる。
example_sentences.english: It's not that it doesn't exist if we look for it, but searching is too difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: 見学できなくはないのですが、特定の人しか許可してもらえません。
example_sentences.english: It's not that you can't take a tour, but only specific people can get permission.

example_sentences.japanese: これまでもかなり試行錯誤してきましたが、もっと工夫できなくはないです。
example_sentences.english: There was a considerable amount of trial and error to get to here, but it's not that I can't plan more.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の顕微鏡でもみえなくはないが、もっといい顕微鏡がほしい。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I can't see with my microscope, but I want an even better microscope.

general_translation: Unless you do something
formation: Verb［ない］ + ことには + Verb［ない］［い］Adjective［ない］+ ことには + Verb［ない］［な］Adjective. + でない + ことには + Verb［ない］Noun + でない + ことには + Verb［ない］
casual_structure: Verb［ない］ + ことには + Verb［ない］［い］Adjective［ない］+ ことには + Verb［ない］［な］Adjective. + でない + ことには + Verb［ない］Noun + でない + ことには + Verb［ない］
explanation: A phrase that highlights that a thing which is not (A) will also result in (B) not being the case.

example_sentences.japanese: やってみないことには、出来るかどうか分からない。
example_sentences.english: You won't know if you can do it or not unless you try.

example_sentences.japanese: ヘルメットを被らないことには、この工事現場には入れない。
example_sentences.english: You cannot enter this construction site unless you wear a safety helmet.

example_sentences.japanese: ジェットコースターは、スリルがないことには楽しくない。
example_sentences.english: Roller coasters are no fun, unless they are thrilling.

example_sentences.japanese: 何事も一生懸命でないことには、何も上手くなれない。
example_sentences.english: You won't get good at anything, unless you try your best in everything you do.

example_sentences.japanese: 許可書がないことには、ここへは入れません。
example_sentences.english: Unless you have a permit, you cannot enter beyond this point.

example_sentences.japanese: 髭をそらないことには、仕事に行けない。
example_sentences.english: Unless you shave your facial hair, you cannot go to work.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫婦では仲良くしないことには、うまくいかない。
example_sentences.english: Unless married couples get along, things won't go well.

example_sentences.japanese: 田植えをしないことには、米を収穫できません。
example_sentences.english: Unless you plant it, you cannot harvest rice.

example_sentences.japanese: 退院しないことには、仕事復帰できない。
example_sentences.english: Unless you are released from the hospital, you cannot return to work.

example_sentences.japanese: この体制をかえないことには、このチームは良くならないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Unless we change this team's structure, it won't get better, will it?

example_sentences.japanese: 資料をそろえないことには先方に提出できません。
example_sentences.english: Unless we put the documents in order, we cannot present them to the other party.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学院にいかないことには、あの研究はできないと思います。
example_sentences.english: Unless I go to graduate school, I think I cannot do that research.

example_sentences.japanese: テスト対策をしないことには、いい点は取れない。
example_sentences.english: Unless you plan (do study) for the test, you won't get a good score.

example_sentences.japanese: モチベーションをたかめないことには、もうこれ以上この勉強は続けられない。
example_sentences.english: Unless you increase your motivation, you won't be able to continue studying any more than this.

example_sentences.japanese: 卒業論文をおわらせないことには、気持ちがなかなか落ち着かない。
example_sentences.english: Unless I finish my thesis, I won't really calm down.

example_sentences.japanese: 足袋をはかないことには、大工の仕事はできない。
example_sentences.english: Unless you wear 'tabi' (Japanese split toe socks), you cannot work as a carpenter.

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字がかけないことには、このテストは難しすぎるかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: Unfortunately, this test may be too hard if you are unable to write kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 高速を使わないことには、待ち合わせ時間に遅れてしまう。
example_sentences.english: Without using the highway, I am going to be late.

general_translation: Cannot help doing something, Cannot resist doing something
formation: Verb［ない］+ では(1) + いられない(1) じゃ
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ では(1) + いられない(1) じゃ
polite_structure: Verb［ない］+ では(1) + いられません(1) じゃ
explanation: A phrase expressing that (A) cannot be avoided, by dramatically stating that the speaker would be unable to exist without doing it.

example_sentences.japanese: 悔しすぎて、のまないではいられない。
example_sentences.english: I am so frustrated, I can't help but drink.

example_sentences.japanese: セール品を見ると、買わないではいられなくなる。
example_sentences.english: When I see something on sale, I can't help but buy it.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は辛い物を食べると、牛乳を飲まないではいられないの。
example_sentences.english: When I eat something spicy, I can't help but drink milk.

example_sentences.japanese: ペットのワンちゃんが自分の尻尾を追いかけているのを見るとおかしくて、笑わないではいられない。
example_sentences.english: When I see my pet dog chasing his tail around, it's so funny that I can't help but laugh.

example_sentences.japanese: 大親友が事故でなくなったときは、泣かないではいられなかった。
example_sentences.english: When my best friend died, I couldn't help but cry. (Emotion)

example_sentences.japanese: おばあさんが困っているのを見ると助けないではいられない。
example_sentences.english: When I see an old lady in need, I can't resist helping them. (Feeling)

example_sentences.japanese: 上司に理不尽に怒られた時には、キレないではいられなかった。
example_sentences.english: When my boss yelled at me unreasonably, I couldn't help but lose my temper. (Reaction)

example_sentences.japanese: いい金魚を見つけてしまった。かわないではいられない。
example_sentences.english: I found a good goldfish. I can't help but buy it.

example_sentences.japanese: 架空請求され、おこらないではいられない。
example_sentences.english: I was charged with a fictitious claim. I can't help but feel angry.

example_sentences.japanese: 困ったことがあって、神様にたよらないではいられない。
example_sentences.english: I got into some trouble and I can't help but rely on the gods.

example_sentences.japanese: 引退試合に負けて、なかないではいられません。
example_sentences.english: Having lost his last game before retirement, he can't help but cry.

example_sentences.japanese: 高級なお寿司が半額だ。たべないではいられない。
example_sentences.english: Premium sushi is half price. I can't help but eat it.

example_sentences.japanese: 競馬の馬の毛並みがあまりに美しい。さわらないではいられない。
example_sentences.english: Race horses have such beautiful fur. I can't help but want to touch them.

example_sentences.japanese: 大好きなお笑い番組を見て、わらわないではいられない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but laugh while watching the comedy show I love.

example_sentences.japanese: 焼き鳥屋さんの横を通るとき、匂いをかがないではいられません。
example_sentences.english: When passing by a Yakitori restaurant, I can't help but take a whiff.

example_sentences.japanese: 毛糸が絡まり困っている娘に、手をださないではいられない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but give a hand to my daughter who is tangled up in yarn.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の辛い状況を見てたすけないではいられない。
example_sentences.english: Seeing his suffering, I can't help but feel like helping. (Literally - Can't help but help)

example_sentences.japanese: あまりにもひどい勘違いだから、口をださないではいられない。
example_sentences.english: Since it was a rather horrible misunderstanding, I can't help but speak up.

general_translation: Must, Have to, Should
formation: Verb［ない］+ ねばならないExceptions:する ￫ せねばならない
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ ねばならないExceptions:する ￫ せねばならない
polite_structure: Verb［ない］+ ねばなりませんExceptions:する ￫ せねばなりません
explanation: A formal old-fashioned phrase meaning one must do (A). If (A) is not done, nothing will become of it.

example_sentences.japanese: 家賃を月末までにはらわねばならない。
example_sentences.english: I have to pay rent by the end of the month.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月の１３日までに電気代を払わねばならない。
example_sentences.english: I have to pay the electric bill by the 13th of this month.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は一応私の先輩なので何を言われても、従わねばならない。
example_sentences.english: That person is my senpai, more or less, so no matter what he says, I must obey him.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんが来る前に掃除をせねばならない。
example_sentences.english: I must clean before the guests arrive.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を今より話せる様になりたいのならば、もっと努力をせねばならない。
example_sentences.english: If you want to be able to speak Japanese better than you do now, you have to work harder.

example_sentences.japanese: 後輩の意見もちゃんときかねばならない。
example_sentences.english: You must also listen to your kouhai's opinion.

example_sentences.japanese: 根本的な構造からみなおさねばならない。
example_sentences.english: We must review the fundamental structure.

example_sentences.japanese: 見学した感想を書いて提出せねばならない。
example_sentences.english: I must write and submit my impressions on the field trip.

example_sentences.japanese: 公衆の面前ではちゃんと秩序をたもたねばならない。
example_sentences.english: I must maintain order in the presence of the general public.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の功績はたたえられねばならないほどのものだと思います。
example_sentences.english: His achievements are so great that I think that we should give praise.

example_sentences.japanese: 体重が激減したため、生活パターンをみなおさねばならない。
example_sentences.english: Due to my weight dropping drastically, I must rethink how I live my life.

example_sentences.japanese: 血圧が高すぎるので、病院にいかねばならない。
example_sentences.english: Since my blood pressure is too high, I should go to the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: 指示によると日本語能力試験にはＨＢの鉛筆をつかわねばならない。
example_sentences.english: According to the instructions, you should use an HB pencil on the JLPT exam.

example_sentences.japanese: 情報が錯綜している。本社の公式の発表をまたねばならない。
example_sentences.english: The information is complicated. I have to wait for a formal announcement from HQ.

example_sentences.japanese: 自然環境は悪化の危機にさらされているため、保護するために国際社会が一致して協力せねばならない。
example_sentences.english: Because the environmental crisis is growing worse, the international community must join forces to protect it.

example_sentences.japanese: 通りがかりに意識を失った人がいたら、すぐに緊急用の番号に連絡せねばならない。
example_sentences.english: If you happen to come across a person that has lost consciousness, you have to immediately call an emergency phone number.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長には僕に任せてくださいと言ったので、何があっても成功せねばならぬ。
example_sentences.english: I told my boss to leave it to me, so no matter what happens, I must succeed.

example_sentences.japanese: もうこんな時間ですか、そろそろ帰らねば。
example_sentences.english: It's already so late! I must go home soon.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたたちは兄弟でしょう？もっと仲良くせねば。
example_sentences.english: You guys are siblings, aren't you? You guys have to be nice to each other.

general_translation: (Please) do!, Ask to, Beg to, (Order somebody to do something)
formation: Verb［stem］+ たまえ
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ たまえ
explanation: A formal, strong phrase used to ask favors or give commands to those below you.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強をやりたまえ。
example_sentences.english: Study! (bossy command)

example_sentences.japanese: まあまあ、とりあえず座りたまえ。
example_sentences.english: Well, please, take a seat.

example_sentences.japanese: 何か言いたそうな顔をしている君！考えてる事を言いたまえ！
example_sentences.english: You look like you want to say something! Please say what you are thinking!

example_sentences.japanese: 遠慮せずどんどん食べたまえ。
example_sentences.english: Please eat as much as you want without holding back.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司：「これを、明日までに終えたまえ。」
example_sentences.english: Boss: 'Finish this by tomorrow.' (bossy command)

example_sentences.japanese: 「神様、豊穣の願いをかなえたまえ。」
example_sentences.english: 'God, please grant us an abundant harvest!'(outdated way of asking a favor/praying・can also be a command)

example_sentences.japanese: オフィスの中で：「次の人、入りたまえ。」
example_sentences.english: In the office: 'Next person, come in.' (bossy command)

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「何て、言ったの。」Ｂ：「お前にうんざりだ！うちの会社をとっとと辞めたまえ！って言ったんだよ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'What did he say?' B: 'He said: 'I am fed up with you. Leave my company at once!'' (bossy command)

example_sentences.japanese: 上司、部下に：「現状について語ってくれたまえ。」
example_sentences.english: Boss, to subordinate: 'Tell me about the current state of things.' (bossy command)

example_sentences.japanese: 「オレの目を見ながら、事実を全部語ってくれたまえ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Please, tell me the whole truth while looking straight into my eyes.' (command mostly found in literature)

example_sentences.japanese: 「あなたの部下には慌てて計画の実装を終えるように命じてくれたまえ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Please, tell your people to finish implementing the plans in haste.' (command mostly found in literature)

example_sentences.japanese: 怒った上司：「何かを実行する前にまず少し考えたまえ！」
example_sentences.english: Angry boss: 'Before you do something, think a little first!' (bossy command)

example_sentences.japanese: 「君たち、やめたまえ！」は、昔の真面目な学級委員なんかが悪い奴や不良に言っているようです。
example_sentences.english: 'You guys, STOP!' seems like something an honest class representative in old times would say to bad guys. (Bossy command)

example_sentences.japanese: 上司、部下に：「皆、期限が間近に迫っているので今週末、会社に来てくれたまえ。」
example_sentences.english: Boss, to subordinates: 'Everyone, the deadline is approaching, so please come to the office this weekend.' (bossy command)

example_sentences.japanese: 怒った上司：「会社からすぐ出て行きたまえ！ 君はクビだ！」従業員：「もっといい案がありますよ。オレを社外コンサルタントとして今の給与のまま雇って下さい。」
example_sentences.english: Angry boss: 'Get out of the company! You are fired!' Employee: 'I have a better idea. You keep me as is, with my current salary as an outside consultant.' (bossy command)

example_sentences.japanese: 我らに罪を犯す者を、我らが許すごとく、我らの罪をも許したまえ。
example_sentences.english: Forgive us our trespasses as we forgive those who trespass against us.

general_translation: Of the, Among(st)
formation: Noun + のうち（で）Noun + のうち + （の）+ NumberNumber + （Counter）+ のうち（で）その(1) + うち（で）(1) この
casual_structure: Noun + のうち（で）Noun + のうち + （の）+ NumberNumber + （Counter）+ のうち（で）その(1) + うち（で）(1) この
explanation: A structure showing that something is within, amongst, or inside of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: ひなさん：「すべての食べ物のうちでイクラが一番好きです。」
example_sentences.english: Hina: 'I like the salmon roe the most of all foods.' (of the・among)

example_sentences.japanese: この会社のうちでもっとも偉い人は田中さんです。
example_sentences.english: Among everyone in this company, Tanaka-san is the most important.

example_sentences.japanese: ここにいる５人のうちで一番給料が高いのは鈴木さんです。
example_sentences.english: Among the 5 people that are present here, Suzuki-san has the highest salary.

example_sentences.japanese: 村上監督が監督した映画のうちで、一番好きな映画はどれですか。
example_sentences.english: Among the movies that Murakami has directed, which is your favorite movie?

example_sentences.japanese: ここにある釣竿、１０本のうちの４本は海釣り用だ。
example_sentences.english: 4 of the 10 fishing rods that are here are for saltwater fishing.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校の科目全てのうちから、一番好きな科目を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Out of all of the school subjects, what is your favorite subject?

example_sentences.japanese: ここにある１００枚のうちから１枚引いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please draw one of the 100 cards here.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「１９５国のうちで一番狭いのはバチカンだ。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Of the 195 countries, Vatican City is the smallest.' (among)

example_sentences.japanese: 「一万人のうち一人ぐらいが成功できるそうだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'It is said that about one in ten thousand people are able to achieve success.' (of the・among)

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「金属のうちで最も一般的なものはアルミニウムだ。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Aluminum is the most common among metals.' (of the)

example_sentences.japanese: 「山のように積み重ねたＣＤのうち１枚ぐらいは聞く価値があるかもしれない。」
example_sentences.english: 'Among the mountain of CDs, maybe (only) about one is worth listening to.' (of the)

example_sentences.japanese: この学校には１０名の外国人留学生がいるが、うち６名はアジアからの学生だ。
example_sentences.english: There are ten foreign exchange students in this school and six of them are from Asia.

example_sentences.japanese: 野球をする子供についての記事：「調べた８５４人の子供のうち１７％の子供が、肘の具合がとても悪いことがわかりました。」
example_sentences.english: Article about children playing baseball: '17% of the 854 children studied showed elbows in very poor health.' (among)

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「新たな報告によると、アメリカ人のうち１０％未満の人は１０００ドル以上のスマホを買います。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'According to a new report, less than 10% of Americans are buying $1000 or more smartphones.' (among)

example_sentences.japanese: ラブコメの序幕、語り手：「このアパートに住んでいる７人の大学生のうち、女性は５人で、残りは男性だ。」
example_sentences.english: Love comedy prologue, narrator: 'Among the 7 university students that live in this apartment, 5 are women, and the rest are men.' (of the)

example_sentences.japanese: カナダについての記事：「中国とカナダとアメリカのうちで、領域が最も広大な国はカナダであるが、人口は他の両国よりはるかに少ない。」
example_sentences.english: Article about Canada: 'Among China, Canada, and the USA, the biggest country is Canada, however, it is much smaller than the other two countries in terms of population.' (of the)

example_sentences.japanese: テレビ番組：「そのことにより、アルベルト・アインシュタインは近代科学者のうちで一番有名な人物になりました。」
example_sentences.english: TV program: 'Due to that, Albert Einstein became the most famous among modern scientists.' (of the)

example_sentences.japanese: 石油価格についての記事：「いくつかの国では税金が石油価格の部分のうちでもっとも多くを占めます。」
example_sentences.english: Article about the price of oil: 'In some countries, tax makes up most of the price of oil.' (among)

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「科学者が３７市町の大気の質を調べると、大気汚染とされたのは１３市町でした。このうち６市町は子供やお年寄りがマスクをせずに外出すると危険なほどでした。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'After investigating the air quality in 37 cities and towns, scientists decided that 13 of them have polluted air. Among those, 6 were polluted to the point that going outside without a mask is dangerous for children and the elderly.' (of the)

general_translation: While, And
formation: Verb［stem］+ つつ
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ つつ
explanation: A formal expression showing that (A) and (B) are being done at the same time, with both (A) and (B) being ongoing actions.

example_sentences.japanese: ツバメは飛行しつつ、寝ることができる。
example_sentences.english: The swallow can sleep while flying.

example_sentences.japanese: 環境に悪いと知りつつ、レジ袋を使い続けている。
example_sentences.english: While I know that it is bad for the environment, I continue to use plastic bags.

example_sentences.japanese: インターネットでレシピを見つつ、料理をしたので今日の晩御飯は美味しいはずです。
example_sentences.english: Dinner tonight should be delicious since I cooked while looking at a recipe on the internet.

example_sentences.japanese: 布団をしきつつテレビに見入ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: While laying out my futon, I got transfixed by the TV.

example_sentences.japanese: 集金しつつ、空き家の調査もしています。
example_sentences.english: While working as a bill collector, I am also surveying empty houses.

example_sentences.japanese: 育児をしつつ、フルタイムで働くのは大変なことです。
example_sentences.english: Working full time while raising children is really hard.

example_sentences.japanese: 父の足跡をたどりつつ、自分の生き方を探している。
example_sentences.english: While following in my father's footsteps, I am searching for how to live my own life.

example_sentences.japanese: 暖炉にあたりつつ、いつも編み物を編んでいる母が好き。
example_sentences.english: I am fond of my mother who is always knitting, while near the fireplace.

example_sentences.japanese: 裁判ではあらそいつつ、私生活では結構仲良くしている。
example_sentences.english: We get along well in our private lives while fighting (each other) in court.

example_sentences.japanese: 老人は沈む太陽の景色をみつつ、懐かしい青春を思い出した。
example_sentences.english: While watching the scenery of the setting sun, the elderly man recalled his nostalgic youth.

example_sentences.japanese: 連載コラムを多数執筆しつつ、長編小説も書いてしまうんだからすごいね。
example_sentences.english: That's amazing that you are writing a number of serial columns for the newspaper while also writing a full-length novel.

example_sentences.japanese: 将棋をしつつ、同時に囲碁もやる強者がいるらしい。
example_sentences.english: Apparently there is an exceptional person who plays Shogi while also playing Go (at the same time).

example_sentences.japanese: アドバイスに感謝しつつ、次の創作にそれを活かす方向で考えています。
example_sentences.english: While being thankful for advice, I am thinking about how best to make use of it for the next project.

example_sentences.japanese: 参加者は南極点遠征のために食料配給を準備しつつ、毎日のスケジュールを覚えたりする。
example_sentences.english: While preparing food rations for the south pole expedition, participants were memorizing things like the daily schedule.

example_sentences.japanese: 走りながら携帯でゲームをしていたら、電柱にぶつかった。
example_sentences.english: I bumped into a telephone pole because I was gaming on my phone while I was walking. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 走りつつ携帯でゲームをしていたら、電柱にぶつかった。
example_sentences.english: I bumped into a telephone pole because I was gaming on my phone while I was walking. (Physical action, unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事に関係ないことを考えながら仕事をしていたら、大きなミスをしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I made a big mistake at work because I was working while thinking about something unrelated to work. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事に関係ないことを考えつつ仕事をしていたら、大きなミスをしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I made a big mistake at work because I was working while thinking about something unrelated to work. (Non-physical, natural Japanese)

general_translation: Even while ~ing, Even though ~ing, Despite ~ing, Although ~ing
formation: Verb［stem］+ つつ（も）
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ つつ（も）
