explanation: A formal phrase expressing that even while (A), (B). Despite (A) being the underlying principle, (B) is contradictory.

example_sentences.japanese: 斜めになりつつもなんとか持ちこたえたジェンガ。
example_sentences.english: Despite becoming slanted, the Jenga tower somehow held out.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で洞窟に入るのは危ないと知りつつも、入ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Despite knowing that going in a cave alone is dangerous, I went in.

example_sentences.japanese: 初めてのライブで緊張しつつもものすごく楽しめました。
example_sentences.english: Despite being very nervous at my first concert, I was able to enjoy it.

example_sentences.japanese: 上をねらいつつも、まるで狙っていないかのような素振りをしています。
example_sentences.english: Despite aiming up, he is swinging like he isn't even aiming.

example_sentences.japanese: 南極点遠征はよくそなえつつも、失敗した。
example_sentences.english: Despite (everyone) preparing well, the south pole expedition failed.

example_sentences.japanese: 車庫のシャッターをあけつつも、まだ行こうか行くまいか迷っていた。
example_sentences.english: Despite opening the garage door, I was still debating whether or not to go.

example_sentences.japanese: 船は、沈みそうになりつつも、なんとか港まで帰って来た。
example_sentences.english: Even though the ship was on the verge of sinking, it somehow made it to the harbor.

example_sentences.japanese: 主人公はこの地下牢に入るのは危ないとおもいつつも、また入った。
example_sentences.english: Despite thinking that entering the dungeon was dangerous, the protagonist still went inside.

example_sentences.japanese: 臭いが気になりつつも、汚れを放置したら大変なことになった。
example_sentences.english: Despite being bothered by the smell, I left the dirty thing as it was and it got worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 弱点をしりつつほったらかしにしたからこんな悲惨なことになったんだ。
example_sentences.english: It became this sort of disaster because we/they neglected it despite knowing its weaknesses.

example_sentences.japanese: 実力不足を実感しつつも、未だにプロを諦められません。
example_sentences.english: Despite feeling that I lack the ability, I will still not give up being a professional.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の言うことは怪しいとおもいつつもとりあえず従うことにした。
example_sentences.english: Even while I think what he says is suspicious, for the time being I have decided to do as he says. (I am thinking)

example_sentences.japanese: 現代人は朝ご飯を食べるのは重要だとしりつつも、そうしようとすることを拒否している。
example_sentences.english: Modern people, despite knowing that eating breakfast is important, refuse to do so.

example_sentences.japanese: 危ないことだとしりつつも、科学者は知識のために、命を掛けつつ実験する場合もある。
example_sentences.english: Despite knowing that it is dangerous, there are cases when scientists, for the sake of knowledge, carry out experiments while putting their lives on the line.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は足を骨折していながらも、大会に出場しようとしたところ、監督に止められた。
example_sentences.english: Despite having a broken leg, he tried to enter the tournament, but was stopped by the coach. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は足を骨折していつつも、大会に出場しようとしたところ、監督に止められた。
example_sentences.english: Even while having a broken leg, he tried to enter the tournament, but was stopped by the coach. (Physical action, unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: なんかこの話は怪しいなと思いながらも、彼のことを信じてみた。
example_sentences.english: Despite thinking, 'this sounds fishy,' I believed him. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: なんかこの話は怪しいなと思いつつも、彼のことを信じてみた。
example_sentences.english: Even though I thought that the story was fishy, I believed him. (Non-physical, natural Japanese)

general_translation: On the occasion of, At the time of
formation: Noun + に際（さい）し（て）Verb［る］+ に際（さい）し（て）Noun + に際（さい）しての + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + に際（さい）し（て）Verb［る］+ に際（さい）し（て）Noun + に際（さい）しての + Noun
explanation: A formal grammar point highlighting the unique, uncommon occasion of (A), often in relation to some form of preparation.

example_sentences.japanese: 応援にさいして守ってほしいルールがあります。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of supporting (someone), there are some rules that I would like you to follow.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいプロジェクトを始めるにさいして、新しいグループリーダーを決めた。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of starting a new project, we chose a new leader.

example_sentences.japanese: クレジットカードを申し込むにさいして、運転免許証が必要です。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of signing up for a credit card, you will need your driver's license.

example_sentences.japanese: 引越しにさいして、いらなくなった家具を全部捨てた。
example_sentences.english: At the time of my move, I threw out all the furniture I don't use anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: 移転にさいして必要なものがあれば言ってね。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of being transferred, let me know if there is anything that (you) need.

example_sentences.japanese: 「受験にさいしての注意事項」をよくお読みください。
example_sentences.english: Please, read the 'points to keep in mind at the time of the exam' carefully.

example_sentences.japanese: 車を追い越すにさいして気をつけるべきことがある。
example_sentences.english: At the time of passing another vehicle, you should take necessary precautions.

example_sentences.japanese: 独立するにさいして、先輩のご意見をいただけませんか？
example_sentences.english: May I get your (senpai's) opinion at the time of becoming independent?

example_sentences.japanese: アンテナの取り付けにさいしての注意事項をお伝えいたします。
example_sentences.english: I will disclose the important points at the time of the installation of the antennae.

example_sentences.japanese: 温泉を掘るにさいして必要なことを全て教えてください。
example_sentences.english: At the time of digging out an onsen, please tell me everything that I need (to know).

example_sentences.japanese: 大会の開会式にさいして準備をしています。
example_sentences.english: I am preparing for the occasion of the opening ceremony for the convention.

example_sentences.japanese: 会館を借りるにさいして必要な手続きをしてもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: Could I please have you handle the necessary arrangements at the time of renting the assembly hall?

example_sentences.japanese: 契約延長にさいして、いくつか契約内容に変更がありますのでご確認ください。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of a contract extension, please check the contents for things that have changed.

example_sentences.japanese: このたび初めての本の出版にさいして、家族や友人に感謝申し上げたいと思います。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of publishing my first book, I would like to thank my family and my friends.

example_sentences.japanese: ローレンス様とのご契約にさいしまして、当方の契約書に誤りがございましたことをお詫び申し上げます。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Lawrence, at the time of setting up a contract with you, there were errors in the agreement on our side and I would like to sincerely apologize.

example_sentences.japanese: 面接でくるに際して印鑑と運転免許証をお持ちください。
example_sentences.english: Please bring your stamp and driver's license at the time of your interview.

example_sentences.japanese: 面接でくる際には印鑑と運転免許証をお持ちください。
example_sentences.english: When you come to your interview, please bring your stamp and driver's license.

example_sentences.japanese: ホームページから登録されたに際して、確認のためこちらからメールを送信することがあります。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion where you have registered using our website, we may send you an email for confirmation. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: ホームページから登録された際には、確認のためこちらからメールを送信することがあります。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion where you have registered using our website, we may send you an email for confirmation. (Natural Japanese)

general_translation: When, At the time of, In case of, On the occasion of
formation: Verb［た］+ 際（さい）(に)(1)Noun + の + 際（さい）(に)(1) Verb［る］
polite_structure: Verb［た］+ 際（さい）(に)(1)Noun + の + 際（さい）(に)(1) Verb［る］
explanation: A formal structure highlighting the occasion of (A), with the nuance of not being an ordinary event.

example_sentences.japanese: 炎天下で働くさいには帽子などを持ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: When working under the scorching sun, remember to bring things like a hat.

example_sentences.japanese: この建物に入るさいには、必ずヘルメットを被ってください。
example_sentences.english: When entering this building, please wear a helmet.

example_sentences.japanese: この薬品が誤って肌に飛び散ったさいには、直ぐにかかりつけの医者に相談してください。
example_sentences.english: If this chemical accidentally splashes onto your skin, consult your physician immediately.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の面接のさいには、印鑑を持ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: Please bring your stamp when you come to the interview tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 商品を並べるさいに、注意しないといけない事はなんですか。
example_sentences.english: Is there anything I should be careful about when arranging the products?

example_sentences.japanese: 車を動かすさいには、周りに子供がいないか確認してください。
example_sentences.english: When moving your car, please make sure there aren't any kids around.

example_sentences.japanese: 休講のさいには連絡しますから、ちゃんと授業に出てください。
example_sentences.english: We’ll notify you in the event of a class cancellation, so please attend class properly.

example_sentences.japanese: 稽古のさいに教わったことを本番でどこまで発揮できるかが問題だ。
example_sentences.english: The issue is to what extent you can demonstrate what you were taught when training at an actual performance.

example_sentences.japanese: 警備のさいに注意してほしいことを書き出しておきましたので、確認してください。
example_sentences.english: Since I wrote out the things I want you to be careful of when on guard, please verify it.

example_sentences.japanese: 血圧を測るさいには、できるだけ平常心でいたほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: It would be best to have as much presence of mind as possible on the occasion of having your blood pressure measured.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の見学のさいには、身分証明書を持ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: Please carry your identification with you when you go on your tour tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 研修のさいに知った情報は、一切口外してはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You cannot ever disclose the information you learned when training.

example_sentences.japanese: 看病のさいに自分も感染しないように万全の体制を整えている。
example_sentences.english: I am putting in place flawless systems to not get infected when I am caring for someone.

example_sentences.japanese: 鼻血、アレルギー反応などの症状のさいには、直ちに最寄りの病院にご連絡ください。
example_sentences.english: In case of symptoms like a bloody nose or an allergic reaction, please contact the nearest hospital right away.

example_sentences.japanese: 初めて沖縄に来たさいに、綺麗な景色に驚きました。今までそのような景色を見たことがなかったと思いました。
example_sentences.english: When I visited Okinawa for the first time, I was surprised by the beautiful landscape. I had never seen anything like that before.

example_sentences.japanese: トラブルと対策など質問：「海外旅行中にビザを無くした場合は、どうすればいいですか？」質問の答え：「そのさいは、最寄りの大使館に連絡をお願いします。」
example_sentences.english: FAQ: 'What should I do if I lose my visa while traveling abroad?' Answer: 'In that case, please contact the nearest embassy.'

example_sentences.japanese: 工事のさいにかかった費用はすべて会社が負担してくれるから助かる。
example_sentences.english: It is helpful that the company will take responsibility for all of the expenses when construction occurred.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では家を出る時に行ってきますと言う。
example_sentences.english: In Japan we say, 'I'm leaving,' when we leave the house. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では家を出る際に行ってきますと言う。
example_sentences.english: In Japan we say, 'I'm leaving,' when we leave the house. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: When, When doing something, On the occasion, At the time
formation: Verb［る］+ にあたり(1)Noun + にあたり(1)(1) にあたって
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ にあたり(1)Noun + にあたり(1)(1) にあたって
explanation: A formal expression meaning at the time of (A), (B). When hitting upon doing (A), (B). Often in regard to preparations.

example_sentences.japanese: レーザーの試験にあたり、必ず保護メガネを着用してください。
example_sentences.english: Be sure to wear safety glasses when testing the laser. (on the occasion of)

example_sentences.japanese: 就活を始めるにあたり、新しいスーツを買った。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of starting my job search, I bought a new suit.

example_sentences.japanese: 卒業にあたって、みんなで卒業旅行として韓国に行った。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of my graduation, we all went to Korea as a graduation trip.

example_sentences.japanese: 転職をするにあたり、インターネットで自分に合った会社を探すことにした。
example_sentences.english: At the time of changing jobs, I looked for a company that would suit me well on the internet.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいお店の開店にあたって、オープニングスタッフを募集しました。
example_sentences.english: We recruited opening staff at the time of opening a new restaurant.

example_sentences.japanese: 綱渡りをするにあたり、命綱をつけてもらった。
example_sentences.english: When I did a tightrope walk, I had a safety wire connected. (at the time of)

example_sentences.japanese: 彫刻を彫るにあたり、彫刻刀を買い換えた。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of carving a sculpture, I bought a new chisel.

example_sentences.japanese: 課長の退職にあたって、お別れの一言を述べさせていただきます。
example_sentences.english: Let me say a few words of farewell on the occasion of the section manager's retirement.

example_sentences.japanese: パスポートの申請にあたり、顔写真を必ず持ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: Be sure to bring headshots at the time of passport application.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼と付き合うにあたり、幾つかの条件を提示した。
example_sentences.english: At the time of dating him, I suggested several conditions.

example_sentences.japanese: 定価を下げるにあたり、社員とかなりの話し合いがなされた。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of lowering the set price, they would hold considerable discussions with the staff.

example_sentences.japanese: 予約を取り消すにあたり、幾つか手続きをしていただきたい。
example_sentences.english: When cancelling a reservation, there are several steps that you must go through. (on the occasion of)

example_sentences.japanese: 今回の特売にあたっての準備は大変でした。
example_sentences.english: When doing the preparation for the the special sale, it was a lot of work this time. (on the occasion of)

example_sentences.japanese: 手帳を買うにあたって、何軒も店を回って探しました。
example_sentences.english: At the time of buying a memo pad, I looked around at several shops.

example_sentences.japanese: 作品を作るにあたって、必要なものを買ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: When making a product, please buy and bring the necessary things. (on the occasion of)

example_sentences.japanese: 通訳をするにあたって、万全に準備を整えた。
example_sentences.english: When I would interpret, I would prepare to perfection. (on the occasion of)

example_sentences.japanese: 母の葬式に際して必要な書類を準備した。
example_sentences.english: I gathered all the necessary documents at the time of my mother's funeral. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 母の葬式にあたって必要な書類を準備した。
example_sentences.english: I gathered all the necessary documents at the time of my mother's funeral. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Lead to, As a good opportunity to, As a result of, As a trigger
formation: Noun + を契機（けいき） + に(1)Verb + の(2) + を契機（けいき） + に(1)(1) にして、として(2) こと
casual_structure: Noun + を契機（けいき） + に(1)Verb + の(2) + を契機（けいき） + に(1)(1) にして、として(2) こと
explanation: A formal phrase, indicating the important opportunity of (A). (A) contains all of the base mechanisms required to trigger (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の独立をけいきに家を改造することにした。
example_sentences.english: As a result of my children becoming independent, I decided to remodel the house.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が生まれたのをけいきに、パチンコをやめることに決めた。
example_sentences.english: I decided to quit pachinko as a result of my child being born.

example_sentences.japanese: 移動制限が緩和されたことをけいきに、観光客の数が増えた。
example_sentences.english: The travel restriction being eased led to an increase of tourists.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は出産をけいきに、会社を辞めた。
example_sentences.english: She quit her job as a result of giving birth.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんは入院をけいきにして、タバコを止めました。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-san being hospitalized led him to quit smoking.

example_sentences.japanese: 大統領の暗殺をけいきとして、戦争が始まった。
example_sentences.english: The assassination of the president led to a war.

example_sentences.japanese: テレビ取材をけいきに、人気が加速していった。
example_sentences.english: The television coverage triggered the acceleration of popularity (for the restaurant).

example_sentences.japanese: 転職をけいきに落ち着きを取り戻した。
example_sentences.english: As a result of my change in occupation, I was able to regain my composure.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに大人しかった彼が、引越しをけいきによく話すようになった。
example_sentences.english: He, who was so quiet, has, as a result of moving, become quite talkative.

example_sentences.japanese: 温泉を掘り当てたことをけいきに大金持ちになりました。
example_sentences.english: Digging up the hot spring led to me becoming very rich.

example_sentences.japanese: チームの優勝をけいきに、練習施設を拡張した。
example_sentences.english: The team used their championship win as a good opportunity to expand their practice facility.

example_sentences.japanese: 退職をけいきに、一つの部屋を図書室として開放しました。
example_sentences.english: As a result of (her) retirement, a room was made available as a library room.

example_sentences.japanese: あの法律の可決をけいきに会社の売り上げが安定した。
example_sentences.english: The adoption of that law led to the company's steady sales.

example_sentences.japanese: 初めてのトランジスタが考案されたのをけいきに新しい技術革新が持ち上がった。
example_sentences.english: A new innovation in technology suddenly happened with the transistor being developed for the first time as a trigger.

example_sentences.japanese: 学力の向上をけいきに、入学を希望する学生の数は増えていきました。
example_sentences.english: As a result of the rising literary ability, the number of students looking to apply has been increasing.

example_sentences.japanese: スプートニクは１９５７年に打ち上げられた。それをけいきに宇宙開発の時代が始まった。
example_sentences.english: Sputnik was launched in 1957. As a result of the launch, the space race began.

example_sentences.japanese: 鎖国とは、日本では海外との交流を遮断する政策であった。黒船の到着をけいきに鎖国が終わった。
example_sentences.english: 'Sakoku' was the Japanese policy of cutting off any cultural exchange with foreign countries. The arrival of the black ships led to the end of 'Sakoku'.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩が楽しそうに料理をしている姿を見たのをきっかけに、私も料理を始めることにした。
example_sentences.english: Seeing my senpai enjoy cooking led me to start cooking too. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩が楽しそうに料理をしている姿を見たのをけいきに、私も料理を始めることにした。
example_sentences.english: Seeing my senpai enjoy cooking led me to start cooking too. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: -ing, Be -ing
formation: Verb［stem］+ つつある
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ つつある
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ つつあります
explanation: A formal expression showing that (A) is an ongoing process. Emphasis on being underway, especially with verbs that have an obvious point of completion.

example_sentences.japanese: おかげさまで、病気はなおりつつあります。
example_sentences.english: Fortunately, my disease is healing.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎年、年金の受給額が減りつつあるので、生活に困っている高齢者が増えてきている。
example_sentences.english: Every year, more and more elderly people are having trouble making ends meet because their pension benefits are decreasing.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では物価が上がりつつある。
example_sentences.english: Prices in general are rising in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近はインターネットを使って買い物ができるので、わざわざお店に行って買い物をする人が減りつつある。
example_sentences.english: These days, people can shop using the Internet, so fewer people are going out of their way to go to stores to shop.

example_sentences.japanese: 契約しつつあったのに決裂した。惜しいことをした。
example_sentences.english: Despite having been in the process of signing a contract, the discussions broke down. I did something regrettable.

example_sentences.japanese: 大流行したインフルエンザの猛威も、今はおちつきつつある。
example_sentences.english: The fury of the widespread influenza is now calming down.

example_sentences.japanese: アフリカの野生動物の数がへりつつあるのは残念だ。
example_sentences.english: It is a pity that the number of wild animals in Africa is decreasing.

example_sentences.japanese: 在庫過剰になりつつあるから、値下げしてでも売ってください。
example_sentences.english: Since inventory continues to overflow, please sell them even if you have to lower the price.

example_sentences.japanese: 反対派の抗議活動が加熱しつつあるから、なんとか抑えないと…
example_sentences.english: Since the opposing faction's protest action is heating up, we have to do something to hold them back...

example_sentences.japanese: 後半ものすごい売り上げを伸ばしていて、前期の損失をカバーしつつある。
example_sentences.english: Sales in the second half are great, they are covering losses from the first half.

example_sentences.japanese: ７０年代中、石油の価格が急にあがりつつあったので、オランダでは自転車の使用が広まった。
example_sentences.english: In the 70's, the price of oil was rising rapidly so riding bicycles became a common practice in the Netherlands.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａの事業とＢの事業の仕事内容がかさなりつつあるから、統合しようと思う。
example_sentences.english: Since the subject matter of business A and business B continue to overlap, I am thinking about merging them.

example_sentences.japanese: 地球温暖化のために砂漠に変わりつつある国がある。また、海に沈みつつある島国もある。
example_sentences.english: There are countries that are changing into deserts due to global warming. In addition, there are also island countries that are sinking into the ocean.

example_sentences.japanese: 近年、経済的にはＡ国とＢ国の協力関係は強化されつつあるが、軍事的には国境付近において小規模紛争が絶えない。
example_sentences.english: In recent years, the economical relationship between country A and country B is strengthening. However, when it comes to the military, small-scale conflicts close to the border do not cease.

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんと水をあげなかったから、植木がかれつつある。
example_sentences.english: Since I didn't properly water it, the potted plant is withering.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はりんごを食べている。
example_sentences.english: He is eating an apple. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はりんごを食べつつある。
example_sentences.english: He is eating an apple. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: At the time, When, While, Timing
formation: Verb［ている］+ ところ（に (1)）Verb［ていた］+ ところ（に (1)）(1) へ
casual_structure: Verb［ている］+ ところ（に (1)）Verb［ていた］+ ところ（に (1)）(1) へ
explanation: A construction which puts emphasis on being in the state or situation in which (A) is happening, or has just happened.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬を散歩させているところにＴさんに出くわした。
example_sentences.english: When I was walking the dog, I came across T-san.

example_sentences.japanese: 車で左折しているところに、急に自転車が飛び出してきた。
example_sentences.english: I was making a left turn in my car when a bicycle suddenly came out of nowhere.

example_sentences.japanese: 休憩室で踊っていたところに後輩たちが休憩室に入ってきた。
example_sentences.english: I was dancing in the break room when my juniors came in.

example_sentences.japanese: 倉庫を取り壊しているところへ近所の人が来て手伝ってくれた。
example_sentences.english: My neighbor came to help me when I was tearing down the shed.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司に怒られて落ち込んでいたところへ、先輩がきて慰めてくれた。
example_sentences.english: My senpai came to comfort me when I was feeling down because I was yelled at by my boss.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょうどジャガイモの皮をむこうとしているところに電話が鳴った。
example_sentences.english: The telephone rang while I was trying to peel the potatoes.

example_sentences.japanese: セメントを入れているところへ猫がやって来て足跡を付けた。
example_sentences.english: A cat came by and left prints when the cement was being poured.

example_sentences.japanese: 店を閉めているところへお客さんが来ちゃった。
example_sentences.english: A customer came right when I was closing up the shop.

example_sentences.japanese: 車を洗っていたところにウチの犬がやってきて、車にオシッコをした。
example_sentences.english: While I was washing the car, my dog came over and peed on it.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で歌っているところに友達がやってきた。恥ずかしいわあ。
example_sentences.english: My friend came along when I was singing by myself. I am so embarrassed.

example_sentences.japanese: ドアに鍵をかけているところに急にドアが開いて、妹が入ってきた。
example_sentences.english: When I was locking the door, it suddenly opened and my sister came in.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、ゲームをしているところに、母に晩御飯に呼び出されたので、怒った。
example_sentences.english: I got mad because my mom called me to dinner while I was playing the game.

example_sentences.japanese: 片付けているところに急に男友達が来て、散らかった部屋を見られてしまったの。
example_sentences.english: A male friend suddenly came while I was tidying up, so my messy room was unfortunately seen.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官は、犯人が盗品を袋に入れているところに、たまたま通りかかった。
example_sentences.english: The policeman happened to pass by when the criminal was putting loot into the bag.

example_sentences.japanese: ジャムの瓶を開こうとしているところに、ちょうど夫が来て、手伝ってくれた。
example_sentences.english: Just when I was trying to open the jam jar, my husband came and helped me.

example_sentences.japanese: 清掃が終わったところに限っていつも汚れた靴のお客さんが入ってくる。
example_sentences.english: Always when I am finishing up cleaning, a customer with dirty shoes comes in...

example_sentences.japanese: お見苦しいところをお見せして申し訳ございません。
example_sentences.english: I am terribly sorry that you had to see such a thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 正直なところ、彼の言うことはあまり信じない方がいい。
example_sentences.english: To be honest, you shouldn't trust what he says.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩、お休みのところすみません。今お時間大丈夫でしょうか。
example_sentences.english: Senpai, I'm sorry to bother you on your break. Do you have some time right now?

general_translation: Right after, As soon as, Just when, Barely
formation: Verb［る］+ か + Verb ない(*) +  かのうちに(*) The same Verb has to be repeated
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ か + Verb ない(*) +  かのうちに(*) The same Verb has to be repeated
explanation: A formal grammar point that indicates when the state of (A) being finished or still going cannot be determined before (B) suddenly happens.

example_sentences.japanese: 焦がすか焦がさないかのうちに、肉を取るのが僕の流儀。
example_sentences.english: My style is to take off the meat just when it starts to burn.

example_sentences.japanese: 父はビールを飲み終わるか飲み終わらないかのうちに、新しい缶を開けた。
example_sentences.english: My father opened a new can of beer as soon as he finished his beer.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は椅子に座るか座らないかのうちに、テレビをつけた。
example_sentences.english: He turned his TV on just as he sat down.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は車が止まるか止まらないかのうちに、ドアを開けて駅へと走っていった。
example_sentences.english: Just as the car stopped, she opened the door and ran to the station.

example_sentences.japanese: 就活を初めて一週間経つか経たないかのうちに、仕事が見つかった。
example_sentences.english: In just a week of looking for a new job, I found a job.

example_sentences.japanese: 戦争が終わるか終わらないかのうちに、原爆が落とされた。
example_sentences.english: An atomic bomb was dropped, just when the war was about to end.

example_sentences.japanese: 御馳走をいただくかいただかないかのうちに、帰る時間になってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Just as I was about to eat, it was time to go home.

example_sentences.japanese: 削除されるかされないかのうちに、自ら手を引いた方がいい。
example_sentences.english: Just when you are about to be eliminated, it is better to withdraw oneself.

example_sentences.japanese: 清書するかしないかのうちに、下書きを紛失してしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Just as I was about to write a clean copy, I lost my rough draft.

example_sentences.japanese: 言葉が終わるか終わらないかのうちに、彼女は意識を失った。
example_sentences.english: As soon as she finished her remark, she had lost consciousness.

example_sentences.japanese: 乗車するかしないかのうちにドアを閉めるなんて危ないじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: Right after I boarded, they closed the doors. That is dangerous isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: 勝敗が決まるか決まらないかのうちに、お客さんが帰り始めた。
example_sentences.english: Just as they were about to determine the outcome, spectators started going home.

example_sentences.japanese: 宣伝するかしないかのうちに、有名人がツイートしてくれて人気が出た。
example_sentences.english: Just as I was about to advertise, a famous person tweeted about it and it became popular.

example_sentences.japanese: 車を洗いきるか洗いきらないかのうちに雨が降り出したんだ。とてもイライラしたよ。
example_sentences.english: Right after I washed my car, it started raining. I was so frustrated.

example_sentences.japanese: 現代人って目を覚ますか目を覚まさないかのうちに、スマホをとってネットサーフィンする。
example_sentences.english: These days, people take out their smartphones and surf the web as soon as they wake up.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が試験の答案を書き終えるか終えないかのうちに、火災警報が鳴った。
example_sentences.english: Just when I was about to finish filling out the test sheet, the fire alarm rang.

example_sentences.japanese: いつも、家の戸を開けるか開けないかのうちにうちの犬が家から飛び出して顔をなめる。
example_sentences.english: As soon as I open the door our dog always jumps out and licks my face.

general_translation: On the way to, As you go
formation: Verb［stem］+ がけに
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ がけに
explanation: A phrase showing that something is done along the way. While suspended in the action of (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 女の子の噂話：「さっきあいつ、きがけに妙なことを言ってたね。」
example_sentences.english: Girls gossiping: 'Just now, on the way here, that dude was saying weird things.'

example_sentences.japanese: 帰りがけに駅前のたこ焼き屋でたこ焼きを買った。
example_sentences.english: On my way home, I bought some takoyaki from the takoyaki store in front of the station.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は学校への行きがけにコンビニで弁当を買う。
example_sentences.english: Today, on my way to school, I will buy lunch at the convenience store.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さん、通りがけにサービスエリアにでも寄って行こ！
example_sentences.english: Dad, let's stop by the service area on the way!

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「かえりがけにタイコさんを誘って一緒に戻ろうか。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'Do you want to invite Taiko on the way home, and go back together?'

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は生徒と話している：「タカスさん、このプリントをかえりがけにアイサカさんに持って行ってください。」
example_sentences.english: A teacher is talking with a student: 'Takasu, please bring this handout to Aisaka on the way home.'

example_sentences.japanese: ライトノベル：「彼はスーパーへのいきがけに何かを思い出したように突然止まり速く家に帰った。」
example_sentences.english: Light novel: 'He suddenly stopped as if he remembered something on his way to the supermarket and quickly returned home.'

example_sentences.japanese: 病気の友達の見舞いに行く時、友達との話：「病院へのいきがけに花屋に寄って花束を買おう。」
example_sentences.english: Visiting a sick friend, chat between friends: 'Let's drop by the florist on the way to the hospital, and buy a bouquet.'

example_sentences.japanese: 親と子供の話：「子供の頃、学校へのいきがけにこの駄菓子屋によく立ち寄ったものだ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between parent and child: 'During my childhood, I often stopped by this small-time candy store on my way to school.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との電話：「とりあえずとおりがけにコンビニでコーヒーでも買おう。」
example_sentences.english: A phone call between friends: 'For the time being, I will buy something like coffee at the convenience store on the way.'

example_sentences.japanese: 両親が子供に拾ったものについて話している、父親：「これは？」母親：「かえりがけに道で拾ったんでしょう、その枝よ。」
example_sentences.english: Parents talking about an object picked up by their child, Father: '(What) is this?'Mother: 'She probably picked it up on the way home, that twig.'

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官の記者会見：「被害者の話によると、昨夜、会社からのかえりがけに突然四〜五人程のマスクを装着した集団に取り囲まれ、暴行を受けたとの事です。」
example_sentences.english: Police press conference: 'According to the victim, last night he was suddenly surrounded by a masked group of four or five people on his way home from work and then assaulted.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話、Ａ：「彼女が病気になった。」Ｂ：「そうならかえりがけに訪問したほうがいい。彼女も喜ぶだろう。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends, A: 'My girlfriend got sick.'B: 'If so, then you should visit her on your way home. She will be happy.'

example_sentences.japanese: 会社員との話：「コンビニからのかえりがけに外村さんに偶然出会った。彼女が笑っているところを、初めて見た。」
example_sentences.english: Conversation between company employees: 'On the way back from the convenience store I met Sotomura-san by chance. That was the first time I had ever seen her smile.

example_sentences.japanese: 怒った配偶者：「何にこんな時間がかかったの？」配偶者２：「かえりがけに図書館によったんだ。」
example_sentences.english: Angry spouse: 'What took you so long?'Spouse 2: 'I stopped by the library on the way back.'

general_translation: If one keeps doing something, When, If something is...
formation: Verb［て］ + いては
casual_structure: Verb［て］ + いては
explanation: A hypothetical phrase, indicating that in general, if one keeps doing (A), (B). Staying in the state of doing (A).

example_sentences.japanese: だまっていては、相手に気持ちが伝わらないんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: If you stay silent, how will the other person know how you feel?

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日お菓子ばかりを食べていては、いつまで経っても痩せませんよ。
example_sentences.english: If you keep only eating snacks, you'll never lose any weight.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎晩遊んでいてはお金はたまりませんよ。
example_sentences.english: If you keep going out every night, you won't save up money.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事の事ばかりを気にしていては、旅行は楽しめませんよ。
example_sentences.english: If you keep worrying about work, you won't be able to enjoy your trip.

example_sentences.japanese: 来るのが遅すぎます。先にはじめていてはいけませんか？
example_sentences.english: I will be very late. Would you mind if you start without me?

example_sentences.japanese: 力をぬいていては持てない。もっと力を入れて！
example_sentences.english: If you keep relaxing, you won't be able to hold it. Put more effort into it!

example_sentences.japanese: 暖房をつけていては暑すぎる。もう春なんだから。
example_sentences.english: If you keep turning on the heat, it is too hot. It's already spring, you know.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな歩き方をしていては、ペンギンかと思われますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you keep walking like that, people will think that you are a penguin.

example_sentences.japanese: ふとっていてはメンバーに入れない。ダイエットをしてください。
example_sentences.english: If you keep gaining weight, you cannot become a member. Please lose some weight.

example_sentences.japanese: みられていては具合が悪い。ブラインドを閉めてくれ。
example_sentences.english: If we keep being watched, I'll feel uncomfortable. Close the blinds for me, would you?

example_sentences.japanese: 味噌汁はひえていては飲めないなぁ。温めてもらえませんか？
example_sentences.english: If the miso soup is cold, I cannot eat it. Could you heat it up for me?

example_sentences.japanese: ひかっていては駄目だと言われた。もっと渋いのが好みらしい。
example_sentences.english: I was told that if it is brightly shining, it is no good. Apparently their tastes are more simple.

example_sentences.japanese: このまま毎日そんな風にお金をつかっていては、破産してしまいますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you keep spending money like this every day, you will go bankrupt.

example_sentences.japanese: 問題を最後までさけていては何も成し遂げられないでしょ。
example_sentences.english: If you keep avoiding problems till the end, you won't be able to accomplish anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 理想像の彼女をおいもとめていては、決して恋人と出会えないよ。
example_sentences.english: If you keep chasing the idealized image of a girlfriend, you will never be able to find a lover.

general_translation: Was just about to do something, Was in the middle of...
formation: Verb［る］ + ところだった
casual_structure: Verb［る］ + ところだった
polite_structure: Verb［る］ + ところでした
explanation: A structure expressing that something was in, or about to be in the position or situation of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 絵の具をつけてしまうところだった。
example_sentences.english: I was just about to apply the paint.

example_sentences.japanese: 危なかった。危うくあの人をひくところだった。
example_sentences.english: That was close. I was about to run over that person.

example_sentences.japanese: 起きるのが３分遅かったら、遅刻するところだった。
example_sentences.english: I was about to be late if I had woken up three minutes later.

example_sentences.japanese: 今から家を出るところだったのに、いきなり雨が降ってきたから雨が止むまで待つ。
example_sentences.english: I was just about to leave the house, but it suddenly started raining, so I'm going to wait until the rain stops.

example_sentences.japanese: もうすぐ犯人が自白するところだったのに、お前が余計なことを言うから...。
example_sentences.english: The killer was just about to confess, but you went off on a tangent...

example_sentences.japanese: 危うく期限が切れてしまうところだった。
example_sentences.english: I was just about to narrowly miss the deadline.

example_sentences.japanese: 今から関西弁を教わるところだったのに。
example_sentences.english: I was just about to be taught the Kansai dialect.

example_sentences.japanese: 出掛けるところだったが、雨が降ってきたのでやめました。
example_sentences.english: I was just about to go out, but because it started raining, I stopped.

example_sentences.japanese: 捕まえた犯人を危うく逃すところだった。
example_sentences.english: The captured criminal was just about to barely escape.

example_sentences.japanese: 悪友と付き合って、寿命を縮めるところでした。
example_sentences.english: I got involved with bad friends and nearly shortened my lifespan. (was just about to)

example_sentences.japanese: お風呂に入っているところだったから、電話に出られませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Since I was in the middle of taking a bath, I couldn't answer the phone.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな人だって知らなかったら、危うく付き合うところだった。
example_sentences.english: I was just about to go out with that person, if I didn't know who they were.

example_sentences.japanese: 今作るところだったけど、「夕飯はいらない」と連絡が入った。
example_sentences.english: I was just about to make it, but I got a message saying, 'I don't need dinner.'

example_sentences.japanese: 携帯の電池がなくなるところだったが、なんとか間に合った。
example_sentences.english: The battery on my phone was just about to die, but I somehow managed to make it in time.

example_sentences.japanese: やっと慣れてきたところだったのに、仕事を辞めなければいけなくなった。
example_sentences.english: Despite just about getting used to it, I had to quit my job.

example_sentences.japanese: お湯の温度を調整しているところだったのに、ブレーカーが落ちてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Just as I was in the middle of adjusting the hot water temperature, the breaker unfortunately tripped.

general_translation: This is not the time for…, Far from, Out of the question
formation: Phrase + どころ + ではないPhrase + どころ + じゃない
casual_structure: Phrase + どころ + ではないPhrase + どころ + じゃない
polite_structure: Phrase + どころ + ではありませんPhrase + どころ + じゃありません
explanation: An expression emphasizing that it is hardly the place or situation for (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 休みの日はたくさん寝たい。レジャーどころではない。
example_sentences.english: On my day off, I want to sleep a lot. Leisure activities are out of the question.

example_sentences.japanese: 出産は痛いどころではないらしい。
example_sentences.english: They say childbirth is far from just painful.

example_sentences.japanese: 締め切りが迫って来てるから、休憩を取るどころじゃない。
example_sentences.english: The deadline is approaching, so taking a break is out of the question.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんからお父さんが倒れたと連絡があったので、仕事どころではない。
example_sentences.english: It is not the time for working, since I got a message from my mother telling me that my father collapsed.

example_sentences.japanese: 今は仕事が忙しいし、お金も全然ないから、結婚どころじゃない。
example_sentences.english: Since I am busy with work and have no money, it is not the time to get married.

example_sentences.japanese: 腰を痛めてしまったから、マラソンどころではありません。
example_sentences.english: I unfortunately injured my lower back, a marathon is out of the question.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱があるというのに、遊園地どころではないよ。
example_sentences.english: When you have a fever, it is not the time to go to an amusement park.

example_sentences.japanese: なんとか通じればいい。アクセントどころではありません。
example_sentences.english: It would be good if you could somehow communicate. This is not the time to worry about accent.

example_sentences.japanese: 急用が入ったので、お出掛けどころではなくなった。
example_sentences.english: Urgent business came in, so going out became out of the question.

example_sentences.japanese: 落し物をしたので、買い物どころではなくなった。
example_sentences.english: I lost something, so going shopping became out of the question.

example_sentences.japanese: ゲリラ豪雨で、海水浴どころではない。
example_sentences.english: Going swimming in the ocean is out of the question when it is downpouring.

example_sentences.japanese: 火山が噴火して、学校どころではない。
example_sentences.english: The volcano is erupting, it is not the time for school.

example_sentences.japanese: 大病を患っているんだから、仕事どころではない。
example_sentences.english: Since I have become severely ill, this is not the time for work.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が忙しすぎて、年休を取るどころではない。
example_sentences.english: I am so busy at work, taking time off is out of the question.

example_sentences.japanese: 「早く美容室に行け」と言われても、今はそれどころではない。
example_sentences.english: Even if you were told, 'Go to a beauty parlor right away!', now is not the time for that.

example_sentences.japanese: 今まで恋人も出来たことがないのに、結婚どころではない。
example_sentences.english: Since I haven't even had a lover yet, getting married is out of the question.

general_translation: For the first time in, Haven't done for some time
formation: Noun + ぶり + だNoun + ぶりにNoun + ぶりの + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + ぶり + だNoun + ぶりにNoun + ぶりの + Noun
polite_structure: Noun + ぶり + ですNoun + ぶりにNoun + ぶりの + Noun
explanation: A common expression used to indicate that something happens for the first time in a while.

example_sentences.japanese: 歯医者に行くのは二年ぶりだ。
example_sentences.english: Going to the dentist is something I haven't done in 2 years.

example_sentences.japanese: 高橋選手が１０年ぶりの優勝！
example_sentences.english: Takahashi won for the first time in 10 years!

example_sentences.japanese: 一年ぶりに五キロも走ったから明日は絶対に筋肉痛だ。
example_sentences.english: I am definitely going to be sore tomorrow because I ran a 5K for the first time in a year.

example_sentences.japanese: ３年ぶりに風呂に入る。
example_sentences.english: I will bathe for the first time in 3 years.

example_sentences.japanese: ４年ぶりの寿司だ！やっぱり日本の寿司はうまいな！
example_sentences.english: This is my first time having sushi in 4 years! Man, Japanese sushi is the best!

example_sentences.japanese: 十年ぶりに、高校の友達に会った。
example_sentences.english: I met a high school friend who I hadn't seen for 10 years.

example_sentences.japanese: ２週間ぶりの寿司を食べた。
example_sentences.english: I ate sushi for the first time in two weeks.

example_sentences.japanese: 三年ぶりに日本食を味わえて幸せです。
example_sentences.english: For the first time in three years, I am happy that I could taste Japanese food.

example_sentences.japanese: 十日ぶりの快晴で、とてもさわやかだ。
example_sentences.english: For the first time in 10 days, the weather is nice and it is very refreshing.

example_sentences.japanese: １００年ぶりに火山が噴火しました。
example_sentences.english: The volcano erupted for the first time in 100 years.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父さんに会うのは半年ぶりですね。
example_sentences.english: It will be the first time in six months that you get to see your uncle, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 大谷が３打席ぶりにヒットを打った。
example_sentences.english: Ohtani got a hit for the first time after not getting one during the last three at bats.

example_sentences.japanese: 数日ぶりに原稿を書き始めた。
example_sentences.english: I began writing my manuscript after not having written for several days. (for the first time in...)

example_sentences.japanese: 演劇を見たのは何年ぶりだろう。
example_sentences.english: It has probably been several years since I saw a play. (for the first time in...)

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに綺麗な景色は３年前の秋ぶりだ。
example_sentences.english: This is the first time since fall three years ago that I've seen a view this beautiful.

example_sentences.japanese: 二大会ぶりに同じ組合せでの決勝戦だ。
example_sentences.english: For the first time in two tournaments, it is a finals game with the same match up (of teams/athletes).

example_sentences.japanese: しばらくぶりに見た運河は、とても美しかった。
example_sentences.english: Seeing the canal for the first time in quite a while, was exceedingly beautiful.

example_sentences.japanese: ５１分ぶりに家に帰る。
example_sentences.english: I will go home for the first time in 51 minutes. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: If, With, Since, Because
formation: Verb［て］+ は(1)［い］Adjective［て］+ は［な］Adjective + では(2)Noun + では(2)(1) Verb［て］ + ちゃ(2) じゃ
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ は(1)［い］Adjective［て］+ は［な］Adjective + では(2)Noun + では(2)(1) Verb［て］ + ちゃ(2) じゃ
explanation: A casual, hypothetical phrase showing that if the negatively evaluated (A) happens or exists, the negative (B) will also happen.

example_sentences.japanese: 無理に引っぱっては壊れてしまいますよ！
example_sentences.english: If you pull it forcibly, it will break!

example_sentences.japanese: そのように力を入れて回してはネジがだめになってしまいますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you turn it with such force, you're going to ruin the screw.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに長くては鞄に入らないので、半分に折ってください。
example_sentences.english: It won't fit in my bag if it's that long, so please fold it in half.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は掃除が苦手なので、そんな几帳面では私と住むことはできないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: I don't like cleaning, so if you are that well-organized, you probably won't be able to live with me. (You probably won't enjoy living with me)

example_sentences.japanese: そんな貧乏くさい格好ではあのレストランには入れないよ。
example_sentences.english: If you have such a poor-looking outfit, they won't let you into that restaurant.

example_sentences.japanese: リーダーがあの人じゃ嫌です。どうしてもあの人じゃないといけないなら私を別のチームに入れてください。
example_sentences.english: If that person is the leader, screw that. If there is really no other way than making that person the leader, then please put me on a different team.

example_sentences.japanese: ご飯を全部食べなくちゃ大きくなれないよ。
example_sentences.english: If you don't eat all your food, you won't grow.

example_sentences.japanese: 寝る前にそんなコーヒーをのんでは寝られない。
example_sentences.english: If you drink coffee before going to bed, you won't be able to sleep a wink.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに塩辛くては売り物にならないよ。
example_sentences.english: If it is this salty, it will not sell.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな服装ではあの店には入れてもらえないよ。
example_sentences.english: With those clothes, you won't be able to enter that shop.

example_sentences.japanese: そのような給与では、あの工場で働くには無理がある。
example_sentences.english: It is not worth working in that factory if that is what you will be paid.

example_sentences.japanese: ピザのパン生地がどろどろになるよ、水があまりに多くては。。。
example_sentences.english: The pizza dough will get all gooey if there is too much water…

example_sentences.japanese: 今シーズンの結果次第では、引退もあると思いますよ。
example_sentences.english: With this season's results, I think that (he) will retire.

example_sentences.japanese: このような間違いを何回もしていては、夏休みの課題はやりきれない。
example_sentences.english: If you continue to make mistakes like these, you won't be able to finish the summer assignment.

example_sentences.japanese: あの先生じゃ、無理。去年、生徒全員が試験に落ちたんだ。
example_sentences.english: If it is that teacher, it will be impossible. Last year all the students failed the exam.

example_sentences.japanese: ガソリンがこんなに高くては、車で通勤できないだろうね。自転車などを使うしかない。
example_sentences.english: If gasoline is expensive, I won't be able to come to work by car. I will have to use a bike or something.

example_sentences.japanese: ポーランドの悪天候のため、オウムを解放しては、必ず死んでしまうでしょう。
example_sentences.english: As a consequence of the poor Polish climate, if you set a parrot free, it would certainly die.

example_sentences.japanese: そのような振る舞いでは、周囲はあなたを「馬鹿な人」と評価し、誰もあなたに対して真面目に相手をしないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: With behavior like that, you will be labeled a fool by those around you and no one will treat you seriously.

general_translation: Repeating action, If, Since
formation: Verb［て］(A) + は + Verb［て］(B) + はVerb［て］(A) + は + Verb［て］(A) + は
casual_structure: Verb［て］(A) + は + Verb［て］(B) + はVerb［て］(A) + は + Verb［て］(A) + は
explanation: A hypothetical structure indicating that the general repetition of (A) and (B) will lead to (C). May highlight either positive or negative results.

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎者：「働いては寝て、働いては寝てばかりだ。このような人生はダメだ。」
example_sentences.english: Countryman: 'I only work and sleep, work and sleep (repeatedly)… This is not the good life.'

example_sentences.japanese: ここ最近は食べては寝て、食べては寝ての繰り返しだから太ってきた。
example_sentences.english: Recently I've been eating and sleeping, eating and sleeping, so I've gained some weight.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事ではミスしては怒られ、怒られてはミスをする。毎日この繰り返しだから仕事を辞めようと思う。
example_sentences.english: At work, I make a mistake and get yelled at, get yelled at and make a mistake. This repeats every day so I'm thinking of quitting my job.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動しないで食っちゃ寝食っちゃ寝ばかりしていると牛になるよ！
example_sentences.english: If you eat and sleep, eat and sleep without exercising, you are going to turn into a cow!

example_sentences.japanese: 薬を飲んじゃ吐いて、飲んじゃ吐いてを何回も繰り返したから喉が痛い。
example_sentences.english: My throat hurts because I've taken medicine and thrown up, then taken it and thrown up over and over.

example_sentences.japanese: あくびをしてはフリスクを食べ、あくびをしてはフリスクを食べ、何とか起きていられた。
example_sentences.english: By yawning and eating a mint, yawning and eating a mint, I was somehow able to wake up.

example_sentences.japanese: 曖昧なことを言ってははぐらかし、嘘をついては逃げようとし、あの人はどうしようもない。
example_sentences.english: That person is a lost cause, saying ambiguous things and lying and trying to run.

example_sentences.japanese: 酒を飲んでは暴れ、暴れては物を壊す。彼は酒癖が悪い。
example_sentences.english: Drinking alcohol and acting violently, raging and breaking things. He is a bad drunk.

example_sentences.japanese: 受け取っては誰かに渡し、渡されては受け取るというだけの仕事です。
example_sentences.english: The job is just taking stuff and handing it off to others, taking and handing off.

example_sentences.japanese: 威張っては人を見下し、怒鳴っては人を脅すという最低の上司だ。
example_sentences.english: Being proud and looking down on people, screaming at and threatening people. (He) is what you call a horrible boss.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、インターネット接続が悪い。接続しては切断して、接続しては、切断して。（を繰り返すことは）イライラさせられる。
example_sentences.english: Recently, my internet connection is terrible. It connects and disconnects, connects and disconnects (repeatedly)… It is driving me nuts.

example_sentences.japanese: ある研究によると、一番の勉強方法は２０〜４０分勉強しては休憩してを繰り返すことです。
example_sentences.english: According to some research, the best way to learn is to study for about 20-40 minutes, rest and repeat.

example_sentences.japanese: データを圧縮しては送信し、圧縮しては送信しを繰り返し、やっとすべて送れました。
example_sentences.english: After compressing and sending, compressing and sending, I was finally able to send it all.

example_sentences.japanese: 嫌がられてはやり方を変え、嫌がられてはやり方を変え、を繰り返して人との付き合い方を学ぶ。
example_sentences.english: Being disliked, changing your methods, being disliked and changing your methods over and over you learn how to get along with people.

example_sentences.japanese: 歩いては走り、走っては歩き、（を繰り返すことは）、ジョギングしてみたいけれど体力に不安な人にとって、いいトレーニング方法です。
example_sentences.english: Walking and running, running and walking (repeatedly) is a great method of training for people who want to try jogging, but are worried about endurance.

example_sentences.japanese: 納得のいく写真が撮れず、写しては消し、写しては消しを繰り返している。
example_sentences.english: Without taking a photo I am pleased with, I repeatedly take a photo, erase it, take another and erase it.

example_sentences.japanese: ５キロを休憩なしで走れるようになるには、疲れるまで１キロ走っては休憩しての繰り返しを１ヶ月間毎日続けることが必要です。
example_sentences.english: To be able to run 5 kilometers without taking a break, you need to run for a kilometer, then take a break, and repeat that process everyday for a month.

general_translation: Too, Also (with more emphasis than も alone), Again
formation: Noun + もまた［な］Adjective + なの + もまた［い］Adjective + の + もまたVerb + の + もまた
casual_structure: Noun + もまた［な］Adjective + なの + もまた［い］Adjective + の + もまたVerb + の + もまた
explanation: A construction emphasizing that something is in addition or again. Branching off from (A), also (B).

example_sentences.japanese: チームのキャプテン：「今日もまた頑張ろう！」
example_sentences.english: Team captain: 'Let's do our best today again!'

example_sentences.japanese: 高橋さんが提案したアイディアはいいのですが田中さんが提案したことを実行するのもまた、いい考えだと思います。
example_sentences.english: The idea suggested by Takahashi-san is good, but I also think it's a good idea to implement what Tanaka-san suggested.

example_sentences.japanese: カレーは甘くても美味しいけど、辛いのもまた美味しいんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Curry is good even if it's sweet, but spicy curry is also good.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生になるには知識がたくさん必要です。ですが、経験が必要なのもまた確かだ。
example_sentences.english: Being a teacher requires a lot of knowledge. However, experience is also necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日もまた同じ時間にここにきてね！
example_sentences.english: Please come here again at the same time tomorrow!

example_sentences.japanese: 社長：「今年もまた利益増大に取り組みます。」
example_sentences.english: Company president: 'This year, again, we will work on increasing profit.'

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「盆栽をいじるという趣味もまた中国がルーツである。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'The hobby of manipulating bonsais also has its roots in China.'

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「お金は、使うことだけでなく稼ぐこともまた楽しいです。」
example_sentences.english: Essay/article: 'Not only spending, but also earning money is fun.'

example_sentences.japanese: 子育てについての論文：「可愛い子に旅をさせてみること、それもまた大切なことです。」
example_sentences.english: Essay/article about parenting: 'Sending your beloved children out into the world, that is also important.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「海外旅行はカッコいいよ。けど田舎に行くのもまたいいね。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'Going abroad is cool. But going to the countryside is also nice, right?'

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「狐や犬だけではなく、イルカもまた哺乳類に分類される。」
example_sentences.english: Essay/article: 'Not just dogs and foxes, but dolphins are also classified as mammals.'

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「改革に対して民衆の支持が多かったのは嘘ではない。しかし、反対する者が少なくなかったのもまた、真実である。」
example_sentences.english: Essay/article: 'It is no lie that there was a lot of public support for the reform. However, it is also true that there were quite a few against it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「いい技師になるには良い指導が不可欠だと言われている。だが、豊富な現場経験が必要なのもまた確かだ。」
example_sentences.english: Essay/article: 'It is said that to become a good technician, guidance is essential. But, I am certain that experience is also important.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「うちの猫だけでなく、隣の猫もまた、肉が大好物だそう。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'I heard that meat is not only a favorite of my cat but also my neighbor's cat.'

example_sentences.japanese: 恋人たちとの話：「本当に君のためになるのなら君に全てを捧げよう。だが、その結果として君が一人になることを意味するのなら、そんなことはできないのもまた事実だ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between lovers: 'I will sacrifice everything if it is for you. However, it is also true that I won't be able to do that if you end up alone because of it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「部活動が面倒臭いことはよくわかるけどさ、楽しそうなのもまた事実だよ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'I know that club activities are a bother, but it is also true that they look fun.'

general_translation: As a result of
formation: Verb［た］+ 結果（けっか） + PhraseNoun + の + 結果（けっか） +  Phrase
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ 結果（けっか） + PhraseNoun + の + 結果（けっか） +  Phrase
explanation: An expression which specifically highlights things brought about as a result of (A).
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: 叫んで暴れたけっか、逮捕された。
example_sentences.english: As a result of shouting and acting violently, I got arrested.

example_sentences.japanese: お酒を飲んで運転したけっか、電柱にぶつかって免許を取り消された。
example_sentences.english: As a result of drinking and driving, I drove into a telephone pole and my license was revoked.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなが努力したけっか、大会で優勝することができた。
example_sentences.english: As a result of everyone doing their best, we were able to win the competition.

example_sentences.japanese: 話し合いのけっか、親が学費を払ってくれることになりました。
example_sentences.english: As a result of the discussion, it has been decided that my parents are going to pay my tuition.

example_sentences.japanese: 調査のけっか、この土地の土は汚染されていることが確認できました。
example_sentences.english: As a result of the examination, we were able to confirm that the soil on this property is contaminated.

example_sentences.japanese: 占いのけっかなど信じたりはしない。
example_sentences.english: I don't believe in such things as the results of fortunetelling.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動を怠ったけっか、太ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: As a result of neglecting exercise, I got fat.

example_sentences.japanese: 研究のけっか、新しい粒子が見つかった。
example_sentences.english: As a result of research, new particles were discovered.

example_sentences.japanese: 裁判で争ったけっか負けてしまうなんて…
example_sentences.english: I cannot believe that the result of the court battle will end up in me losing...

example_sentences.japanese: 調査のけっか、容疑者は無罪となった。
example_sentences.english: As a result of the investigation, the suspect has been found not guilty.

example_sentences.japanese: 打合せのけっか、僕のアイデアは却下されました。
example_sentences.english: As a result of the business meeting, my idea was rejected.

example_sentences.japanese: 脂を取りすぎたけっか、気持ち悪くなってきた。
example_sentences.english: As a result of consuming too much fried food, I came to feel unwell.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族とよく相談したけっか、一人暮らしを決めたんだ。
example_sentences.english: As a result of discussion with family, I decided to live alone.

example_sentences.japanese: 手厚い看病のけっか、元気になって本当に良かった。
example_sentences.english: As a result of some tender loving care, (you) became healthy. For that, I am very glad.

example_sentences.japanese: 国民が反対したけっか、増税の提案は破棄された。
example_sentences.english: As a result of public opposition, the tax increase proposal was abandoned.

example_sentences.japanese: 宿題を先延ばしにしたけっか、当日の明け方までかかってしまった。
example_sentences.english: As a result of putting off homework until late, it took me until dawn of the day it was due to finish.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事で頑張った結果、昇進する事が決まった。
example_sentences.english: As a result of my hard work, I'm getting promoted.

example_sentences.japanese: パートナーと話し合いをした挙句、離婚することになった。
example_sentences.english: After having a discussion with my partner, we have decided to get divorced.

general_translation: Since, Henceforth
formation: Verb［て］+ 以来（いらい）Noun + 以来（いらい）それ(1) + 以来（いらい）(1) これ、あれ
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ 以来（いらい）Noun + 以来（いらい）それ(1) + 以来（いらい）(1) これ、あれ
explanation: A construction showing when (B) has not changed since (A). Or that nothing is expected to change henceforth.
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: あの原稿をよんでいらい、すっかり彼のファンになった。
example_sentences.english: Since reading that manuscript, I have become a total fan of his.

example_sentences.japanese: 入社いらい、あの先輩には色々とお世話になっている。
example_sentences.english: That senpai has helped me in many ways since I've joined the company.

example_sentences.japanese: 久しぶり！卒業いらいじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Long time no see! (We haven't met) since graduation, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 二年前にタバコをやめていらい、一本も吸ってない。
example_sentences.english: I haven't smoked a single cigarette ever since I quit 2 years ago.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に来ていらい、全然母国の友達と連絡をとっていない。
example_sentences.english: I haven't kept in touch with my friends back home ever since I moved to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 紅葉がはじまっていらい、店は超満員だ。
example_sentences.english: Since fall colors started, it has been teeming with people at the restaurant.

example_sentences.japanese: 卒業していらいだな。この校舎を見に来たのは。
example_sentences.english: I haven't come to see this school building since  graduation.

example_sentences.japanese: シフトを交替していらい、彼とは全然会わなくなった。
example_sentences.english: Since changing shifts, I haven't seen him at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 休業していらい、再開の目処が立っていない。
example_sentences.english: Since closing my business, the prospect of reopening hasn't come up.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄が移住していらい、全然連絡が取れない。
example_sentences.english: Since my brother emigrated, I haven't been able to contact him.

example_sentences.japanese: 事実を公表していらい、いろんな方が支援してくれるようになった。
example_sentences.english: Since publishing the facts, various people have come to give me support.

example_sentences.japanese: カマチョさんが首相に就任していらい、税金が上がる一方だ。
example_sentences.english: Taxes keep on rising since Mr. Camacho assumed the office of prime minister.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんは３年前に引退した。それいらい、自由な時間がたくさん。
example_sentences.english: My father retired three years ago. Since then he has a lot of free time.

example_sentences.japanese: チームを強化していらいの連勝記録は今も続いている。
example_sentences.english: The series of victories since the strengthening of the team is still continuing now.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頃に見学していらい、父の会社には行っていません。
example_sentences.english: Since I went and visited when I was kid, I haven't gone to my father's company.

example_sentences.japanese: ８年前に日本語を勉強しはじめていらい、毎日、しっかり勉強してる。
example_sentences.english: Since I began studying Japanese 8 years ago, I study hard every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 海外転職していらい、５年も日本に帰っていない。
example_sentences.english: I have not been back to Japan for five years since I changed jobs overseas.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年この大学に入学していらい、１回しか実家に帰っていない。
example_sentences.english: I have only been back to my parents' house once since I entered university last year.

general_translation: Before, Prior to, In preference over
formation: Verb +  に先立（さきだ）って(1)Noun + に先立（さきだ）って(1)Noun (A)  + に先立（さきだ）つ + Noun (B)(1) に先立ち
casual_structure: Verb +  に先立（さきだ）って(1)Noun + に先立（さきだ）って(1)Noun (A)  + に先立（さきだ）つ + Noun (B)(1) に先立ち
explanation: A formal grammar point showing that prior to, or in preference to (A), (B). As (B) is standing before (A), it should come first.
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: このアプリの使用にさきだち、ライセンス契約を読んでおいてください。
example_sentences.english: Please read the license agreement prior to running this application.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい機械を導入するにさきだって、色々な会社のサイトを見てスペックを比較します。
example_sentences.english: Prior to installing a new machine, I will visit websites of various companies to compare the specs.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画の公開にさきだち、予告編が公開された。
example_sentences.english: Prior to the release of the movie, the trailer was released.

example_sentences.japanese: 引越しにさきだつ１日前に洗濯機や冷蔵庫の水抜きをしておかなければならない。
example_sentences.english: Washing machines and refrigerators must be drained one day prior to moving.

example_sentences.japanese: クリストファー・コロンブスにさきだってヴァイキングはアメリカを発見したと考えられている。
example_sentences.english: The vikings are considered to have discovered America before Christopher Columbus.

example_sentences.japanese: レーザーの電源を入れるにさきだって、保護メガネをかけておいてください。
example_sentences.english: Prior to turning on the laser, please put on safety glasses in advance.

example_sentences.japanese: あるゲームの通知：「冒険に挑むにさきだって仲間を集めよ。」
example_sentences.english: Certain game: 'You must gather your party before venturing forth.'

example_sentences.japanese: ＰＣケースを開けるにさきだち、万が一のためにまず電源を切っておかなければならない。
example_sentences.english: Before opening the computer case, as an extra precaution, you have to turn off the power.

example_sentences.japanese: 発光ダイオードの登場にさきだち、蛍光灯は最も一般的な省エネライトの一種だった。
example_sentences.english: Prior to the emergence of light emitting diodes (LED), fluorescent lights were the most common energy-efficient light type.

example_sentences.japanese: 産業革命という時代にさきだち、今とは違って大多数の人は農場で働いていた。
example_sentences.english: Prior to the industrial revolution, unlike now, the majority of people worked on farms.

example_sentences.japanese: フレディ・マーキュリーの逝去にさきだつ１９９０年、クイーンは「ショウ・マスト・ゴー・オン」という最後のヒットソングを録音した。
example_sentences.english: In 1990 before the death of Freddie Mercury, Queen recorded the last hit song called 'The show must go on'.

example_sentences.japanese: 携帯電話の普及にさきだち、ページャという機械がメッセージを受信するために使用された。
example_sentences.english: Prior to the popularization of mobile phones, the device known as a pager was used to receive messages.

example_sentences.japanese: 手術にさきだつ３日前からは、アルコール、ニコチンといった物質をいかなる場合でも摂取してはいけません。
example_sentences.english: From three days prior to the operation, you must not consume substances such as alcohol or nicotine under any circumstances.

example_sentences.japanese: 何に肯定をする時も、さきだって、忘れずに契約を読みぬいてゆっくりと考えろ。
example_sentences.english: Whenever you're going to consent to something, prior to that, don't forget to carefully read completely through the contract!

example_sentences.japanese: 運転免許証の再交付の申請にさきだち、必ず願書に最近の写真を貼っておいてください。
example_sentences.english: Prior to applying for the reissue of your driver's license, please make sure to attach your most recent photograph to the application form.

example_sentences.japanese: 海外へ移住したいけど、先立つものがない。
example_sentences.english: I want to move abroad, but I don't have the means to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい車を買いたいけど先立つものがない。
example_sentences.english: I want a new car, but I don't have the means to buy one.

general_translation: Wonder if ~ (really)?, Wonder how ~ (actually)?, Sure enough, As expected
formation: はたして + (Question) Phraseはたして + Phrase
casual_structure: はたして + (Question) Phraseはたして + Phrase
explanation: An expression used to highlight the end product of (A). Comes across as how actually when asking (A), or sure enough when stating (A).
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: 迷子：「はたしてどうやって帰るの？」
example_sentences.english: Lost child: 'I wonder how will I actually get back home?'

example_sentences.japanese: はたして彼が言っていることは本当なのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if what he is saying is the truth.

example_sentences.japanese: はたして、あのやり方で本当に成功するのでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if that approach will really work.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は取引先の信頼を失う事をしてしまった。はたして、彼はクビになった。
example_sentences.english: He did something to lose the trust of his clients. As expected he was fired.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は自分の意見を彼に押し付けようとしたが、はたして彼は自分の意見を変えなかった。
example_sentences.english: She tried to push her opinions onto him, but as expected he did not change his.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「バンジージャンプしてみたいなぁ〜。」 Ｂ：「はたしてできるかしら？」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I want to try bungee jumping.' B: 'I wonder if you can actually do it?'

example_sentences.japanese: あんな厚かましいお願いをして、はたしてうまくいくのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder, with such an impudent request, if it will actually turn out well.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学を中退するのははたして賢明な行動でしょうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if dropping out of university is really a wise thing to do?

example_sentences.japanese: 首相は減税を約束した。はたして首相は公約を守らなかった。
example_sentences.english: The prime minister promised to cut taxes. Sure enough, he broke his promise.

example_sentences.japanese: シンポジウムの中で科学者ははたして時間旅行が可能なのだろうかと疑問に思った。
example_sentences.english: At the symposium, scientists wondered if time travel is really possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が今の二倍の給料を得るとしたら、東京で３ＬＤＫの家をはたして買えるだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if I would actually be able to buy a 3LDK in Tokyo, assuming that I earn twice as much as I do now.

example_sentences.japanese: ゆきさんとともこさんは長い間、付き合っていた。はたして、彼らは結婚した。
example_sentences.english: Yuki-san and Tomoko-san had been going out for a long time. Sure enough, they got married.

example_sentences.japanese: かなり癖のある字で宛名を書いたが、はたして届くだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wrote the address in really quirky handwriting. I wonder if the letter will really make it.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな怪しい格好で、はたしてあのレストランに入れるのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if (he) will be really able to get into that restaurant with that dodgy clothing.

example_sentences.japanese: ある人は地球が平らであると証明しようとしたが、はたして失敗した。
example_sentences.english: A certain person tried to prove that the Earth was flat, however, just as expected that person failed to do so.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、「スポーツは健康に等しい」とスローガンをよく耳にする。はたしてそれは本当なのでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: Lately, I often hear the slogan 'Sport is equal to health'. I wonder if that is really the case?

example_sentences.japanese: 大学院に進学するのは果たして私にメリットがあるのでしょうか？
example_sentences.english: I wonder if going on to graduate school will actually benefit me in the end.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼以外誰も仕事に来なかったため、果たして彼が全員の仕事をすることになった。
example_sentences.english: Since no one came to work except him, he ended up having to do everyone's job in the end as expected.

general_translation: To be (not) worth, To (not) pay off
formation: Verb［た］(1) + 甲斐（かい） + がある(2)Verb［stem］+ がい + がある(2)Noun + の + 甲斐（かい） + がある(2)(1) Verb［る］, Less common(2) ない
casual_structure: Verb［た］(1) + 甲斐（かい） + がある(2)Verb［stem］+ がい + がある(2)Noun + の + 甲斐（かい） + がある(2)(1) Verb［る］, Less common(2) ない
polite_structure: Verb［た］(1) + 甲斐（かい） + があります(2)Verb［stem］+ がい + があります(2)Noun + の + 甲斐（かい） + があります(2)(1) Verb［る］, Less common(2) ありません
explanation: A grammar point expressing when the worth of (A) either exists or does not. (A) has paid off, or did not pay off.
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼は勉強しないのでおしえがいがない。」
example_sentences.english: 'It is not worth to teach him, because he is not studying.'

example_sentences.japanese: この食パンを買えて、朝の４時から並んだかいがあった。
example_sentences.english: It was worth standing in line since 4 a.m. as I was able to buy this bread.

example_sentences.japanese: こういう景色を見ると生きているかいがあると思う。
example_sentences.english: This kind of scenery makes me feel that life is worth living.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は何回注意しても上達しないから教えがいがない。
example_sentences.english: She is not worth teaching because she does not improve no matter how many times I give her advice.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなの努力のかいがあり、この大会で優勝する事ができました。
example_sentences.english: Everyone's hard work paid off, and we were able to win the tournament.

example_sentences.japanese: 看病のかいがあり、父がどんどんと元気になってきた。
example_sentences.english: Nursing my father paid off and he is rapidly getting better and better.

example_sentences.japanese: しょっぼ、なにこれ。こんなもんのために東京からきたかいがない。
example_sentences.english: What the heck is this, this is it? It was not worth coming all the way from Tokyo for something like this.

example_sentences.japanese: 移転したかいがあり、今やうちは人気店だ。
example_sentences.english: Now my shop is popular. Moving was worth it.

example_sentences.japanese: あの選手の本音を聞けて、インタビューしたかいがありました。
example_sentences.english: The interview was worth it as I was able to hear what that athlete truly thinks.

example_sentences.japanese: あんだけ喜んでもらえれば、頑張って手で編んだかいがある。
example_sentences.english: If they are going to be that happy about it, it is worth it to knit it by hand.

example_sentences.japanese: やっぱり、消火器を取り付けておいたかいがあって、今回役に立った。
example_sentences.english: As expected, it paid off to install a fire extinguisher, which proved to come in handy this time.

example_sentences.japanese: やっぱり電気や水を節約したかいがあって、請求額が減ったんだ。
example_sentences.english: As expected it was worth it to cut back on electricity and water use since my amount billed decreased.

example_sentences.japanese: 一斉に調査したかいがあり、良いアンケート結果が得られた。
example_sentences.english: Doing the surveys all at once was worth it, as I got good results on the questionnaire.

example_sentences.japanese: 裁判で争ったかいがあって、かなりの賠償金を手に入れることができました。
example_sentences.english: It was worth it to fight in court, as I am able to receive quite the large sum of reparations.

example_sentences.japanese: 嫌がらずにどんな仕事でも一生懸命やったかいがあり、昇進できました。
example_sentences.english: Working my hardest, without batting an eye, at any job that was thrown at me paid off. I got promoted.

example_sentences.japanese: 何度も打合せをしたかいがあって、本番は大成功でした。
example_sentences.english: The main event was a huge success. Looks like coming together to meet multiple times paid off.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日、日本語を勉強してたんだ。そのかいがあって、とうとう日本語能力試験に合格した。気持ちがいい。
example_sentences.english: I studied Japanese every day. My efforts paid off, and I finally passed the JLPT. I feel great!

example_sentences.japanese: 家族や友達と関係を断ち切ったかいがあった？いま、あんたがどんな金持ちだとしても孤独な暮らしをしてることに変わりはない。
example_sentences.english: Was it worth it to cut all ties with your family and friends? Now, no matter how rich you are, it doesn't change the fact that you will lead a lonely life.

general_translation: Before long, All too soon, In the end, Eventually
formation: やがて + Phrase
casual_structure: やがて + Phrase
explanation: A formal expression showing that all too soon, (A). Not necessarily coming quickly, but before long, (A).
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: やがてきみは失恋したことも忘れるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Perhaps, eventually you will forget you were once heartbroken.

example_sentences.japanese: そのアニメもあのアニメのようにやがて人気がなくなるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: That anime will probably lose popularity like that anime eventually.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日漢字を読む練習をしていれば、やがて小説を読めるようになるだろう。
example_sentences.english: If you practice reading kanji every day, eventually, you will be able to read a novel.

example_sentences.japanese: もう５時なので、やがて日が沈み始めるだろう。
example_sentences.english: It is already 5 p.m. so the sun will probably set soon.

example_sentences.japanese: やがて３０歳になるけど、お金も名声も持ってない。
example_sentences.english: Although I will be 30 all too soon, I have neither money nor fame.

example_sentences.japanese: それがきっかけで、やがて新たな戦争が起こる可能性がある。
example_sentences.english: As a result of that, a new war might break out soon.

example_sentences.japanese: オデュッセウス：「時間と手間をかけても、やがて家に帰れる！」
example_sentences.english: Odysseus: 'Even if it takes time and effort, I will eventually return home!'

example_sentences.japanese: どんな本もやがて読み終わります。けれど、果たしてそれは本当でしょうか？
example_sentences.english: No matter the book, it will come to an end before long. However, I wonder is that really true?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を教えようと決めて毎日勉強したら、やがて教師になれた。
example_sentences.english: I decided to teach Japanese and studied everyday. Before long I became a teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が眼鏡を探し始めてから、やがて３時間になる。
example_sentences.english: Before long, it will have been three hours since I started searching for my glasses  .

example_sentences.japanese: やがて３０年を迎える研究期間を経て、急所術という武道を修得する。
example_sentences.english: After a period of study spanning nearly 30 years, I will acquire a martial arts technique called the touch of death.

example_sentences.japanese: 親と話した末、やがて故郷に帰るという結論に達した。
example_sentences.english: After a chat with my parents, I have concluded that I will come back to my hometown soon.

example_sentences.japanese: 「今、子供のために家を買えなくても、やがて買えるだろう。」
example_sentences.english: 'Even if I won't be able to buy a house for my children now, I guess I will buy one eventually.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「歩いては探してを繰り返せば、やがて忘れ物が見つかるだろう。」
example_sentences.english: 'If you keep walking around and looking, you will find what you've lost eventually.'

example_sentences.japanese: 数年、日本に住んで、やがて日本語をぺらぺらと話せるようになった。
example_sentences.english: After a few years of living in Japan I eventually came to speak Japanese fluently.

example_sentences.japanese: やがて６０歳になるけど、経済的に余裕がないので死ぬまで働き続けざるを得ない。
example_sentences.english: I am nearly 60 years old, however, I have no choice but to keep working till I die because I have no excess money.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を勉強し始めてから、やがて２年が経つ。
example_sentences.english: It has been nearly 2 years since I have started studying Japanese.

general_translation: Therefore, Thus, As a result
formation: (Cause) + したがって + (Result)
casual_structure: (Cause) + したがって + (Result)
explanation: A formal phrase used to say (A), therefore also (B). Literally in compliance with (A), (B).
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: あの会社は業界大手だ。したがって、強気に出てくるはずです。
example_sentences.english: That company is a major enterprise. Therefore, they should show strength.

example_sentences.japanese: 現在東名高速の名古屋インターと岡崎インターの間でリニューアル工事が行われている。したがって、その区間は現在通行止めとなっている。
example_sentences.english: Renewal work is currently underway on the Tomei Expressway between the Nagoya Interchange and the Okazaki Interchange. Therefore, that section is currently closed.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年は去年より台風が多かったです。したがって、今年の米の値段は去年より高くなるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: There were more typhoons this year than last year. Therefore, the price of rice this year will be higher than last year.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社ではインフルエンザが流行っている。したがって、会議は全てオンラインで行われることになった。
example_sentences.english: The flu is going around in my company. Therefore, it has been decided that all meetings are going to take place online.

example_sentences.japanese: 値下げしないよう連絡がありました。したがって、定価で売るしかありません。
example_sentences.english: I received a message not to cut prices. Therefore I have no choice but to sell them at the fixed price.

example_sentences.japanese: 意見の相違がありすぎる。したがって、契約は破棄させていただきます。
example_sentences.english: There is too much difference in our opinions. Therefore, let's break the agreement.

example_sentences.japanese: 公害が増大している。したがって、工場は閉鎖する方向になります。
example_sentences.english: Pollution is increasing. Therefore, it has been decided that we will close the factory.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車が脱線してしまった。したがって、今日中の到着は無理だと思われます。
example_sentences.english: The train derailed. Therefore, I think it is impossible for me to arrive before the day is over.

example_sentences.japanese: 短期大学に進学します。したがって、２年後には就職するでしょう。
example_sentences.english: You are going to enter a junior college. Therefore, you will find employment two years from now, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は長男です。したがって、次期社長はおそらく彼でしょう。
example_sentences.english: He is the oldest son. Therefore, he will soon be the CEO, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 本番直前です。したがって、彼は極度に緊張しています。
example_sentences.english: It is right before the big game. Therefore, he is at maximum nervousness.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長が問題を起こしました。したがって、問い合わせが殺到するでしょう。
example_sentences.english: The CEO caused a problem. Therefore, the inquires will come flooding in, won't they?

example_sentences.japanese: この辺は二週間にわたって雨が降っていた。したがって氾濫の可能性がある。
example_sentences.english: In this area, rain has been falling over a span of two weeks. Thus, there is a possibility of flooding.

example_sentences.japanese: 銅には多くの用途があるにもかかわらず生産量がかなり少ない金属である。したがってトン当たりの価格が非常に高い。
example_sentences.english: Copper, in spite of having many uses, is a metal with a relatively low output. Therefore, price per ton is extremely high.

example_sentences.japanese: 「したがって」と「だから」は英単語「therefore」を意味する。したがって、この役割でどちらも使用できるが、例外がある。すべての場合に「したがって」を「だから」へ言い換えできるが、逆はできるとは限らない。
example_sentences.english: '______' and 'だから' both mean 'therefore' in English. As a result, both can take on the same role, however, there are exceptions. '______' can be rephrased into 'だから' in every case, but the reverse is not always true.

general_translation: After, In the end, After all, Eventually
formation: Verb［た］+ あげく + (に)  + (Past Tense) (Result)Verb［た］+ あげく + の + NounNoun + の possession + あげく + (に)  + (Past Tense) (Result)
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ あげく + (に)  + (Past Tense) (Result)Verb［た］+ あげく + の + NounNoun + の possession + あげく + (に)  + (Past Tense) (Result)
explanation: A construction often implying the negative result of (A), despite all efforts. To have all amounted to nothing when (A) happened.
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: 走って転んだあげくに、壁に衝突した。
example_sentences.english: After running and falling, I crashed into a wall.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は夫と話し合いをしたあげく、離婚することに決めた。
example_sentences.english: After having a discussion with my husband, we have decided that we are getting a divorce.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日落とした財布を長い時間探したあげく、見つける事ができなかったので交番に行った。
example_sentences.english: After looking for my wallet that I dropped yesterday, I couldn't find it, so I went to the police station.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんと中田さんは口論のあげく、喧嘩になってしまい、警察のお世話になった。
example_sentences.english: After an argument, Mr. Tanaka and Ms. Nakata got into a fight and were taken care of by the police.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生と色々と相談したあげく、レポートを書き直すことにした。
example_sentences.english: After much discussion with the teacher, I decided to rewrite the report.

example_sentences.japanese: 父親との議論のあげく、俺は大学を中退して会社を継ぐことになった。
example_sentences.english: After some discussion with my father, I decided to drop out of college and take over his company.

example_sentences.japanese: さんざん泣いたあげく、彼女は眠ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: After crying a lot she fell asleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 数回追い越したあげくに、ドライバーはガードレールにぶつかってしまった。
example_sentences.english: After overtaking a few times, the driver hit the guardrail.

example_sentences.japanese: お酒を飲んで泥酔したあげくに、財布を盗られた。
example_sentences.english: After drinking alcohol and getting drunk, I had my wallet stolen.

example_sentences.japanese: さんざん考えたあげくに親の意に反して大学を辞めた。
example_sentences.english: After considering it thoughtfully I have quit university against wishes of my parents.

example_sentences.japanese: 寝食を忘れて沢山の時間を費やしたあげくに、このプロジェクトは上司の一存で頓挫した。
example_sentences.english: After spending a lot of time on it, doing my best, the project was killed by higher-ups. (Literally - Denying myself food and sleep)

example_sentences.japanese: 数時間スーパーで歩き回ったあげくに何も買わず家に帰った。
example_sentences.english: After walking around at the supermarket for a few hours, I went home without buying anything.

example_sentences.japanese: お金や時間をさんざん費やしたあげくに、私の会社は倒産した。
example_sentences.english: After all the time and money I invested, my company went bankrupt.

example_sentences.japanese: 試験の合格のために徹夜したからバスに乗り遅れたあげくに、試験も受けられなかった。
example_sentences.english: Because I sat up all night in order to pass the test I missed the bus and I didn't take the test in the end.

example_sentences.japanese: 数年働けるだけは働いたあげく、昇進提示には目もくれず彼は会社を去った。
example_sentences.english: After working for years, he left the company, indifferent to any aspects of promotion.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はしばらく逃げ回ったあげく、とうとう警察に捕まえられた。
example_sentences.english: After running for a while, she has been finally caught by the police.

example_sentences.japanese: ３時間林で迷ったあげくに、道を探すのを諦めた。１時間後に、森林管理官が見つけてくれた。
example_sentences.english: After I got lost in the woods for three hours, I gave up searching for a way out. After an hour I was found by a forester.

general_translation: Lead to, Because of, As a start or trigger of, An opportunity
formation: Verb + の(1) + をきっかけ + に(2)Noun + をきっかけ + に(2)Verb + の(1) + がきっかけ + で(3)Noun + がきっかけ + で(3)Verb + きっかけ + をPhrase(4)(1) こと(2) にして、として(3) になって、となって(4) はなんだ、になる、となる、だ、である
casual_structure: Verb + の(1) + をきっかけ + に(2)Noun + をきっかけ + に(2)Verb + の(1) + がきっかけ + で(3)Noun + がきっかけ + で(3)Verb + きっかけ + をPhrase(4)(1) こと(2) にして、として(3) になって、となって(4) はなんだ、になる、となる、だ、である
