explanation: A phrase indicating the trigger for doing (B). Often describing an opportunity or process which led to (B).
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: 相手チームのエラーをきっかけに、逆転して勝った。
example_sentences.english: The opposing team's mistake triggered the turnaround and we won.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女とは、パーティーで会ったのをきっかけに付き合い始めた。
example_sentences.english: Meeting her at the party led us to start dating.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は入院をきっかけにタバコを止めることにしました。
example_sentences.english: Getting hospitalized led me to stop smoking.

example_sentences.japanese: この音楽は有名な歌手がカバーしたのがきっかけで再び有名になった。
example_sentences.english: This song became famous again because that famous singer made a cover of it.

example_sentences.japanese: このゲームがきっかけで、プログラマーになる事ができた。
example_sentences.english: This game led me to become a programmer.

example_sentences.japanese: クモに刺されたのをきっかけとして、彼はスーパーヒーローになった。
example_sentences.english: Being bitten by a spider has led him to become a superhero.

example_sentences.japanese: オランダで自転車が普及するようになったのは、オイルショックがきっかけである。
example_sentences.english: The popularization of bicycles in the Netherlands was triggered by the oil crisis.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の母はスモーカーだったけど、電子たばこを贈ってあげたのをきっかけに、止めてくれた。
example_sentences.english: My mother used to be a smoker, but gifting her an e-cigarette led to her stopping.

example_sentences.japanese: サラエボ事件をきっかけにして、１９１４年から１９１８年にかけて、後に世界大戦と呼ばれるようになった戦争が起きた。
example_sentences.english: With the incident in Sarajevo as a trigger, a war that lasted from 1914 to 1918 broke out and was later called a world war.

example_sentences.japanese: 小学校の頃、フリーオペレーティングシステムがあると聞いた。それをきっかけにしてＬＩＮＵＸとＩＴに興味を持つようになった。
example_sentences.english: When I was in elementary school, I heard that there was a free (from freedom) operating system. Because of that, I have developed an interest in Linux and IT.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「我が社で働くことを希望されたきっかけは何ですか？」Ｂ：「新聞広告を見て希望しました。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'What led you to apply to work for our company?' B: 'I decided when I saw an advertisement in the newspaper.'

example_sentences.japanese: ３月のライオンという漫画を読んだのをきっかけに、多くの人々が将棋に関心を持つようになった。
example_sentences.english: Reading the manga called 'March comes in like a lion' triggered many people to take interest in Japanese chess.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝、手を握りあっている恋人を見たのをきっかけに、自分の初恋のことを思い出しました。
example_sentences.english: This morning I saw lovers holding hands, which led to me suddenly recalling my first love.

example_sentences.japanese: テキサスでの蝶々の羽ばたきがきっかけとなって数日あとにブラジルで竜巻が起きると言われている。
example_sentences.english: It is said the flapping of a butterfly's wings in Texas will trigger a tornado to occur in Brazil a few days later.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は思い出を語っている：「小学校の時の引っ越しがきっかけで、母さんに出会えた。」
example_sentences.english: Father reminiscing: 'Moving during primary school days led to me meeting your mother.'

example_sentences.japanese: サー・アイザック・ニュートンは、庭木から落ちたリンゴを見たことがきっかけで、万有引力を思いついたということだ。
example_sentences.english: Sir Isaac Newton came up with universal gravitation as a result of seeing an apple that has fallen from a garden tree.

example_sentences.japanese: 木から落ちたのをきっかけに、両腕を骨折した。
example_sentences.english: As a result of falling from a tree, I broke both of my arms. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: When it comes to, Regarding, Concerning
formation: Noun + にかけては
casual_structure: Noun + にかけては
explanation: A construction showing that when wagering on (A), you can't go past (B). When it comes to (A), (B).
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: ＲＰＧゲームをすることにかけては誰にも負けない。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to playing RPG games, I won't lose to anyone.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はゲームは下手だけど、スポーツにかけては誰にも負けない。
example_sentences.english: I am bad at video games, but when it comes to sports, I won't lose to anyone.

example_sentences.japanese: あのスマホは機能にかけては、他のスマホとは比べ物にはならないほどいい。
example_sentences.english: There are no other smartphones that can compare to this one when it comes to features.

example_sentences.japanese: 大工の技術にかけては彼が一番だ。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to carpentry skills, he is the best.

example_sentences.japanese: 格闘にかけてはリュ◯の右に出る者はいない。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to hand to hand fighting, there is no one superior to Ry*.

example_sentences.japanese: 算数にかけてはあの子がうちのクラスでトップだと思う。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to math, I think that child is the top in my class.

example_sentences.japanese: 香水にかけては彼女が一番詳しいと思う。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to perfume, I think she is the most well versed.

example_sentences.japanese: クーラーの掃除にかけてはあの会社が一番だと思います。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to cleaning air conditioners, that company is number one, I think.

example_sentences.japanese: あのアイドルはダンスでは大したことはないけど、歌うことにかけては一流だ。
example_sentences.english: That idol's dancing skills are nothing special, but when it comes to singing — she is first class.

example_sentences.japanese: 稽古の量にかけては負けていませんよ。実力はまだまだですが。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to the amount of practice, I am not falling behind. But I am still a long way from competency.

example_sentences.japanese: 春子は運転の腕前にかけては僕よりずっと上手だ。
example_sentences.english: Regarding Haruko's driving skills, they are far superior to mine.

example_sentences.japanese: 金魚にかけては僕の叔父さんより詳しい人に会ったことがない。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to goldfish, I have never met someone more well versed than my uncle.

example_sentences.japanese: 君は空想にかけては超一流だよ。もっと現実を見て欲しいものだ。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to daydreaming, you are first rate. I want you to take a look at reality more.

example_sentences.japanese: クリーニングの技術にかけては君が我が社で一番だと思っている。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to (dry) cleaning techniques, I am thinking that you are the best in our company.

example_sentences.japanese: 原稿を書く速さにかけては、あの作家さんにかなう者はいないと思う。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to speed of writing a manuscript, I don't think there is anyone who can surpass that author.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩の歌唱力にかけては、社内で一番下手だ。
example_sentences.english: My senpai is the worst in the company when it comes to singing. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 朝から夕方にかけて肉をゆっくりと煮込んだ。
example_sentences.english: I slow-cooked the meat from morning to night.

general_translation: Already, A long time ago, Long ago
formation: とっくに + Phrase
casual_structure: とっくに + Phrase
explanation: A strong expression highlighting that (A) already happened. Far and away (A)
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: 「バス？とっくに行っちゃったよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'The bus? It has already left.'

example_sentences.japanese: とっくに食べちゃったよ。
example_sentences.english: I already ate.

example_sentences.japanese: もうとっくに寝る時間じゃん、まだ宿題も始めてないのに...どうしよう。
example_sentences.english: It is already time to sleep. I haven't even started my homework… What should I do?

example_sentences.japanese: 提出期限はとっくに過ぎているのでやってもやらなくても関係がない。
example_sentences.english: The due date has long since passed, so it won't matter if I do it or not.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅いぞ！みんなはもうとっくに帰ってるぞ！
example_sentences.english: You are late! Everyone has already gone home ages ago!

example_sentences.japanese: そんな事は言われなくてもとっくに知ってるよ！
example_sentences.english: I was aware of this well in the past, so no need to tell me!

example_sentences.japanese: 「お前はとっくに死んでいる。」
example_sentences.english: 'You are already long dead.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「うちの子はとっくに歩けるようになった。」
example_sentences.english: 'Our child has already developed the ability to walk!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「魔王と勇者の栄光時代はとっくに過ぎた。」
example_sentences.english: 'The golden era of heroes and demon kings has already passed.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「よく寝るために、暗号通貨からとっくに撤退した。」
example_sentences.english: 'In order to sleep well, I have already pulled out of cryptocurrency.'

example_sentences.japanese: とっくに最終バスを逃したせいで、徒歩で帰るしかない。
example_sentences.english: I have already missed the last bus, so I have no choice but to go back home on foot.

example_sentences.japanese:
９０年代の子供：「一体どこにカルメンがいるの？」
誰か：「とっくに遠くへ逃げたぞ」
example_sentences.english:
90's child: 'Where in the world is Carmen?'
Someone: 'She is already long gone.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「トムおじさんはどうですか？」Ｂ：「彼はとっくに死んだ。１０年前にね。」Ａ：「( ಠ_ಠ)」
example_sentences.english: A: 'How is uncle Tom?' B: 'He died a long time ago. 10 years back, actually…' A: '( ಠ_ಠ)'

example_sentences.japanese: 歳をとるにつれて時の流れを速く感じる。そのため気づけずにオレはとっくに老人だ。
example_sentences.english: As you grow older, it feels like the flow of time gets faster. And so, without noticing, I had already aged.

example_sentences.japanese: 「もうとっくに、約束の時間は越えていて、４時間も君を待っている！」
example_sentences.english: 'The time we decided on has already passed, I have been waiting 4 hours for you!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼はとっくに死んだ人だけど、ずっと私達の思い出として生きている。」
example_sentences.english: 'He has already passed away, but he is still living in our memory.'

example_sentences.japanese: 親：「部屋を片付けなさい。」子供：「とっくに終わったよ！」怒った親：「終わってないでしょ！もっと片付けなさい！」
example_sentences.english: Parent: 'Clean your room!' Child: 'I have already finished!' Angry parent: 'You haven't! Clean more!'

general_translation: Still, Not yet, Even now
formation: 未（いま）だに + … + Verb［る］未（いま）だに + … + Verb［ない］
casual_structure: 未（いま）だに + … + Verb［る］未（いま）だに + … + Verb［ない］
explanation: A slightly formal phrase emphasizing that (A) is still continuing, or is yet to happen. The unexpected state of (A) remains.
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: 小説、語り手：「そのようなことが起こったとは、いまだに信じられない。」
example_sentences.english: Narrator: 'I still cannot believe that such a thing happened.' (not yet・even now)

example_sentences.japanese: 部長は人事に注意されて２ヶ月も経つのに、彼の態度はいまだに変わらない。
example_sentences.english: It's been two months since the director was warned by HR and his attitude still hasn't changed.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年行方不明になった少女はいまだに発見されていない。
example_sentences.english: The girl who went missing last year has still not been found.

example_sentences.japanese: 小学生の頃、高橋くんにいじめられたことをまだ根に持っている。
example_sentences.english: I am still holding a grudge over the fact that I was bullied by Takahashi-kun when I was in elementary school.

example_sentences.japanese: 小学生の頃、高橋くんにいじめられたことをいまだに根に持っている。
example_sentences.english: I am still holding a grudge over the fact that I was bullied by Takahashi-kun when I was in elementary school.

example_sentences.japanese: スマホが普及している中、いまだにガラケーを使っている人がいる。
example_sentences.english: While smartphones are becoming more and more popular, there are people who still use flip phones.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が子供の頃に巻き込まれた事故のことはいまだに覚えている。
example_sentences.english: I still remember the accident that I was involved in when I was a child.

example_sentences.japanese: 歴史書：「いまだにクロサキマサキ氏の死に関して不明な点が多い。」
example_sentences.english: History book: 'There are still many unknowns concerning the death of Masaki Kurosaki.' (not yet・even now)

example_sentences.japanese: 小説、語り手：「いまだに俺は、なぜ彼女があんなにも怒っていたのか、よくわからない。」
example_sentences.english: A novel, the narrator: 'I still don't really know why she got so mad.' (not yet・even now)

example_sentences.japanese: 苦情の内容：「購入してから三週間経ったもののいまだに商品が届いていません。」
example_sentences.english: Letter of complaint: 'Even though it has been three weeks since I made my purchase, the goods haven't arrived yet.' (not yet・even now・still)

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「専門家はいまだに伝説上の街の位置を巡り論争している。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Even now experts dispute the location of the legendary city.' (not yet・still)

example_sentences.japanese: 小説、語り手：「五年間も一緒に住んでいるにも拘わらず、ジェイクはフィンの性格をいまだに完全に把握できていなかった。」
example_sentences.english: Novel, narrator: 'Even though they had been living together for 5 years, even now Jake wasn't able to completely grasp Finn's character.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「政府は既に石油にかかる税金を減らしたにもかかわらず、価格はいまだに変わっていない。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Even though the government has already reduced taxes on oil, the price has not yet changed.' (still・even now)

example_sentences.japanese: 技術関係サイト上のコメント：「何年も経ったというのにＡｉＫｌａｕｄの無料ストレージ容量はいまだに５ＧＢのままです。」
example_sentences.english: Comment on a website about technology: 'Even though it has been years, AiKlaud's free storage capacity is still 5GB.' (not yet・even now)

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「この化学物質が生態系に悪影響があることはみなが知っているはずだが、いまだに使用し続けている会社もある。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Although everyone is sure to know the negative impact that this chemical compound has on the ecosystem, there are companies that even now continue to use it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 推理物に関するサイトの記事：「この身元不明の男性の遺体の謎、いわゆるタマム・シュッド事件はいまだに未解決である。」
example_sentences.english: Article from a site about mysteries: 'This mystery of the unidentified male body, the so-called Tamam Shud case, is still unsolved.' (not yet・even now)

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「ディーゼルエンジンに対しての、新しい法律が成立した。しかしながら大都市大気汚染の問題はいまだに残っている。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'A new law against diesel engines has been established. However, pollution in major cities is still a lingering problem.' (not yet・even now)

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「なぜいまだにあちらこちらに戦争や飢えの問題が絶えないのだろうか？」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Why are there still places where the problems of war and hunger do not die out?' (not yet・even now)

general_translation: Based on, From, According to
formation: Noun + をもとに（して）Noun + をもとにした + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + をもとに（して）Noun + をもとにした + Noun
explanation: An expression showing that (A) is the basis or foundation from which (B) is going off.
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: これはクックパッドをもとに作ったうどんです。
example_sentences.english: This is udon made according to Cookpad.

example_sentences.japanese: このドラマは実際に起こったことをもとに作られたそうだ。
example_sentences.english: Apparently, this TV show was created based on actual events.

example_sentences.japanese: 研究の結果をもとにレポートを書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write a report based on the results of the research.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はこのデータをもとにこのグラフを作成しました。
example_sentences.english: I created this graph based on this data.

example_sentences.japanese: このインタビューをもとに記事を書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write an article based on this interview.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子の足跡をもとに後を追った。
example_sentences.english: I pursued my son based on his footprints.

example_sentences.japanese: 電話帳をもとに宛名を書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write the name and address according to the telephone book.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな主観をもとに恨まれても困るよ。
example_sentences.english: If you feel bitter about it based on that personal opinion, I will not be thrilled.

example_sentences.japanese: 編物の本をもとに編んだらうまくできた。
example_sentences.english: When I knitted according to the knitting book, it turned out well.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな不正確な情報をもとに怪しむなんてどうかしている。
example_sentences.english: To suspect (something) based on such inaccurate information is crazy.

example_sentences.japanese: 親の経験をもとに育児のアドバイスをもらっている。
example_sentences.english: I am receiving child rearing advice based on my parent's experience.

example_sentences.japanese: 市町村のホームページをもとに移転先を決めました。
example_sentences.english: I decided to move based on the town's homepage.

example_sentences.japanese: 税金の総額は年度の収入をもとにして計算される。
example_sentences.english: The amount of tax is calculated based on revenue in a fiscal year.

example_sentences.japanese: この恋愛漫画は実際に起こったことをもとに作られているらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that this romance manga is based on actual events.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当の魚の姿をもとにしたロボットは普通の魚とともに暮らし、海洋生物についてのデータを収集しています。
example_sentences.english: Robots based on the shape of an actual fish are living with ordinary fish and are collecting data about marine life.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は法律に基づいて処分されるだろう。
example_sentences.english: He will be receiving punishment according to the law.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は法律をもとに処分されるだろう。
example_sentences.english: He will be punished based on the law.

general_translation: As long as, Since, Given
formation: Verb［る］+ からにはVerb［た］+ からには［い］Adjective + からには［な］Adjective + である + からにはNoun + である + からには
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ からにはVerb［た］+ からには［い］Adjective + からには［な］Adjective + である + からにはNoun + である + からには
explanation: A structure indicating that from within the general situation of (A), the chance occurrence of (B) will also happen.
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: 二十歳になるからには、ドライブしに行こう！
example_sentences.english: Since I will be turning 20, let's go for a drive!

example_sentences.japanese: 沖縄に来たからには、一番綺麗なビーチへ行きたい。
example_sentences.english: Since I am in Okinawa, I want to go to the prettiest beach.

example_sentences.japanese: 高いスマホを買ったからには、様々な機能を使いこなさなければならない。
example_sentences.english: Given that I bought an expensive smartphone, I need to make the most of its various features.

example_sentences.japanese: 有名になったからには、その影響力を良い方向に使いたい。
example_sentences.english: Given that I have become famous, I want to use that influence in a positive course.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄弟として生まれたからには、お互いに助け合うつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: Since we were born as siblings, we intend to help each other out.

example_sentences.japanese: インタビューをするからには、本音を聞き出したい。
example_sentences.english: Since we are doing an interview, I want to get their true opinion.

example_sentences.japanese: 休業するからには、事前の説明をきちんとしてください。
example_sentences.english: As long as you are going to shutdown your business, please give a precise explanation in advance.

example_sentences.japanese: 行事を任されたからには、絶対に成功させます。
example_sentences.english: Since I was entrusted with the event, I will definitely make it a success.

example_sentences.japanese: 演劇をやるからには、まずは発声練習が大切です。
example_sentences.english: Since you will be performing, to start, speaking practice is important.

example_sentences.japanese: 植木職人になるからには、辛い下積み生活も覚悟しなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: Since he will become a gardener, he must be prepared to live a hard working class life.

example_sentences.japanese: 時間を延長するからには、それなりの料金を支払う必要があります。
example_sentences.english: Since you are getting a time extension, it will be necessary to pay that fee.

example_sentences.japanese: 温泉に行くからには、美味しい料理を出してくれる宿に泊まりたい。
example_sentences.english: As long as we are going to an onsen, I want to stay at an inn that will provide delicious food.

example_sentences.japanese: 衆議院を解散するからには、ちゃんとした大義が必要だ。
example_sentences.english: Since the lower house is going to be dissolved, proper moral law is needed.

example_sentences.japanese: 車を自分で改造するからには、それなりの技術がないと後が大変だ。
example_sentences.english: Since you are going to remodel the car by yourself, if you don't have the skills, it will be no good down the road.

example_sentences.japanese: 楽器をやるからには、近所迷惑にならないように配慮してください。
example_sentences.english: As long as you are going to play an instrument, please give consideration as to not become a neighborhood nuisance.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に行くからには、できるだけ日本の文化や食べ物を体験したり、味わってみるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: As long as I am going to Japan, I should try to experience Japanese culture and food as much as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 教師であるからは、生徒の手本となるべし。
example_sentences.english: As long as you are a teacher, you must be an example to your students.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に住むからは、日本語を勉強するべきだ。
example_sentences.english: As long as I am living in Japan, I must study Japanese.

general_translation: Suddenly, Unnoticed, Without noticing, Too soon
formation: いつのまにか + Phrase
casual_structure: いつのまにか + Phrase
explanation: A phrase implying that (A) happened very suddenly. In an uncertain interval when the speaker didn't notice it.
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: オレはみんなからいつのまにかポチと呼ばれるようになった。
example_sentences.english: Without noticing they have come to call me 'Pochi.'

example_sentences.japanese: ３年間日本人の友達と毎日日本語で話していたら、いつのまにか日本語が上手になっていた。
example_sentences.english: After three years of speaking Japanese every day with my Japanese friend, I became  fluent in Japanese without noticing.

example_sentences.japanese: 久しぶりにクレジットカードの明細を確認してみたら、いつのまにか自動車保険の値段が上がっていた。
example_sentences.english: I checked my credit card statement for the first time in a while and found that the price of my car insurance had suddenly gone up.

example_sentences.japanese: 気づいたら、いつのまにか冬になっていた。
example_sentences.english: Before I knew it, it was winter.

example_sentences.japanese: いつのまにかもう１年が経ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Without me realizing it, another year has passed (all too soon).

example_sentences.japanese: 「いつのまにか彼女はネイティブみたいに話せるようになった。」
example_sentences.english: 'Without me realizing, her speaking has grown to that of a native.'

example_sentences.japanese: 帽子を被ってないといつのまにか風邪を引く。だからきちんと帽子を被って。
example_sentences.english: If you do not wear a hat, you will catch a cold before you know it. That's why you should put on a hat.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの子供から目を離せばいつのまにか迷子になるかもしれない。ご注意ください。
example_sentences.english: If you take your eyes off of your child, they might get lost without you even noticing. Please be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: 「このままでいたらいつのまにかつまらない人になる。時間を無駄にするな！」
example_sentences.english: 'If you stay like this, you will become a boring person before you know it. Do not waste time!'

example_sentences.japanese: しばらく入院して久しぶりに外に出ると、いつのまにか冬になっていた事に気づいた。
example_sentences.english: After being hospitalized for a while, I went outside for the first time in ages and noticed that it had become winter without realizing it.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頃は、いつのまにか日が沈みかけていることも気付かずに、外で夢中になって遊んだ。
example_sentences.english: When I was a child, without noticing that the sun was about to set, I played outside completely absorbed in what I was doing.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨晩夕食を作り終えて夫の帰りを待っていた。ソファに横になってテレビを観ていたところ、いつのまにか眠ってしまったらしく、帰宅した夫に起こされた。
example_sentences.english: I was cooking dinner last night and then waited for my husband's return. As I was lying on the sofa and watching TV, I dozed off without realizing it and was woken up when my husband returned.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝公園を散歩した際、遠くの山々が色づき始めたのを観て、あんなに暑かった過ぎた夏を思い出しながら、「季節はいつのまにか移り変わっていくものだなぁ」と改めて感じた。
example_sentences.english: When I went for a walk in the park this morning, I saw the changing colors of the mountains, recalled the extremely hot summer and felt a new feeling of 'The seasons change without us realizing it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人に様々な言い回しや表現を教えられるうちに、いつのまにか言語のみならず日本文化や日本人の考え方をも学んでいることに気付いた。
example_sentences.english: While I was being taught various phrases by Japanese speakers, I noticed that, without realizing, I was learning not only the language but the culture and the way the Japanese think as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 楽しいことをしているとあっという間に時間が過ぎるよね。
example_sentences.english: Time flies when you're having fun, doesn't it?

general_translation: Once …, If … for a short time, Temporarily (stop), For now or the time being
formation: 一旦（いったん） + Verb［ば］一旦（いったん） + Verb［たら］一旦（いったん） + Verb + と
casual_structure: 一旦（いったん） + Verb［ば］一旦（いったん） + Verb［たら］一旦（いったん） + Verb + と
explanation: A structure used when stopping (A) temporarily. The thing stopped will be hard to return to, like returning to night once dawn has come.
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: いったんこれをしたら残りをＡさんに任せてください。
example_sentences.english: Once you do this, please leave the rest to A-san.

example_sentences.japanese: いったん再起動をすれば、もとに戻るはずです。
example_sentences.english: Once the system is rebooted, it should return to normal.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘はいったん泣き出したら、しばらく泣き止まないので大変です。
example_sentences.english: Once my daughter starts crying, she wont stop for a while, so it can get hard.

example_sentences.japanese: いったん集中力が切れてしまうと、再び集中するのに時間がかかる。
example_sentences.english: Once I lose focus, it takes me a while to regain my focus.

example_sentences.japanese: いったん勉強し始めたら、すべて知りたいです。
example_sentences.english: Once I start learning, I want to know everything (about what I am learning).

example_sentences.japanese: いったん機械の電源がはいるとなかなかとまらない。
example_sentences.english: Once this machine is turned on, it won't be easily stopped.

example_sentences.japanese: いったん一戸建てに住めばアパートに戻れない。
example_sentences.english: Once you live in a stand-alone house, you won't be able to go back to an apartment.

example_sentences.japanese: いったん何かを学ぶのを止めると再開しにくくなる。
example_sentences.english: Once you stop learning something, starting again becomes hard.

example_sentences.japanese: いったんチョコレートを初めて食べたらほかのを買いたくなるでしょ。
example_sentences.english: Once you start eating chocolate, you will start wanting to buy other ones, won't you?

example_sentences.japanese: いったん言葉に出したならば、約束を守るしかない。
example_sentences.english: Once you speak, you will have no choice but to keep your promise.

example_sentences.japanese: いったんこれがわかれば、このような課題は解きやすくなる。
example_sentences.english: Once you understand this, similar problems will become easy to solve.

example_sentences.japanese: いったん健康を失えば、健康の価値を理解するでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Once you lose your health, you will understand its value.

example_sentences.japanese: 「いったん赤いカプセルを飲むとワンダーランドに帰れないだろう。そしてきみにウサギの穴の奥を見せよう。」
example_sentences.english: 'Once you take the red pill, you won't be able to return to Wonderland. And I will show you just how deep the rabbit hole goes.'

example_sentences.japanese: いったん老人になると若い頃が懐かしくなる。
example_sentences.english: Once you become an old person, you will come to miss your youth.

example_sentences.japanese: いったん、この魔法の薬を飲んだら、その結果として想像を絶する力が与えられる。
example_sentences.english: Once you drink this magical potion, as a result, an unimaginable power will be bestowed upon you.

general_translation: Not only... but also, Let alone, Of course
formation: Noun + はもとより + PhraseVerb + こと(1) + はもとより + Phrase(1) の
casual_structure: Noun + はもとより + PhraseVerb + こと(1) + はもとより + Phrase(1) の
explanation: An expression highlighting that from the obvious origin of (A), (B) too. Of course (A), which is a base fact, but (B) too.
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: 速く走るのはもとより経済的でもある車を買いたい。
example_sentences.english: Not only a fast one, but I want to buy a car that's also economical.

example_sentences.japanese: この商店街は地元の人はもとより、全国からの観光客で賑わっています。
example_sentences.english: This shopping street is crowded with not only locals, but also tourists from all over the country.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近の車は自動運転はもとより、自動駐車もできるそうだ。
example_sentences.english: They say that modern cars can not only drive automatically, but also park automatically.

example_sentences.japanese: この学校では日本語が上手になることはもとより、日本でのマナーや文化を理解できる授業が行われています。
example_sentences.english: The school offers classes that not only help students become proficient in Japanese, but also give them an understanding of Japanese manners and culture.

example_sentences.japanese: このテストはもとより、合格できるとは思っていなかった。
example_sentences.english: I did not think that I could pass this test from the start.

example_sentences.japanese: 親は自分の子供を守るのはもとより、何不自由ない生活をしてほしいと思っている。
example_sentences.english: Parents want not only to protect their children, but also want them to live a comfortable life.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗はもとより、もっと酷くなることを覚悟していたから、そんなに悔しくない。
example_sentences.english: Let alone failure, because I was prepared for it to get even worse, I'm not that disappointed.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近ではコンピューターやスマホはもとより、歯ブラシさえＷＩＦＩを備えている。
example_sentences.english: Recently, not only computers and smartphones, but even toothbrushes are equipped with wifi.

example_sentences.japanese: 英語はイギリスやアメリカの母国語としてはもとより台湾でも使われている。
example_sentences.english: English is not only the native language of England and the US, but it is even used in Taiwan.

example_sentences.japanese: 我が社が製造する棒茶は日本全国はもとより、海外でもよく売られている。
example_sentences.english: The twig tea manufactured in our company is not only sold all over Japan, but also abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: アニメや漫画は子供はもとより大人や老人の関心も集める。
example_sentences.english: Anime and manga attract not only children, but also adults and the elderly.

example_sentences.japanese: ＬＩＮＵＸというオペレーティングシステムはサーバによく使われているのはもとより、最近デスクトップのコンピュータの中で人気があるようだ。
example_sentences.english: The operating system known as Linux is not only often used on servers, but also seems to be popular on desktops.

example_sentences.japanese: レオナルド・ダ・ヴィンチは偉大な画家であることはもとより、一流の発明家の一人でもある。
example_sentences.english: Leonardo da Vinci is not only a great painter, but is also among one of the top inventors.

example_sentences.japanese: インターネットでは世界中の人々とチャットができることはもとよりたとえどこに住んでいようとも人間の知識にアクセスできる。
example_sentences.english: Not only can you chat with people all over the world with the internet, but no matter where you live, you can also access the knowledge of humans.

example_sentences.japanese: 弔辞：「彼は一流の外科医であることはもとより、何より偉大な友達でした。」
example_sentences.english: A eulogy: 'He was not only a world-class surgeon, but above all, a great friend.'

example_sentences.japanese: 今日のスマホは、話したりゲームをしたりできるのはもとより、音声コマンドに応じてレストランや整備工を勧めるということだ。
example_sentences.english: On smartphones these days you can not only do things like talking and playing games, but they can also recommend car mechanics and restaurants among others in response to voice command.

example_sentences.japanese: 砂漠を横切る際、暑さや脱水はもとより急な洪水が非常に危険です。ウィキペディアによれば、脱水より水難で死ぬ人の方が多いということです。
example_sentences.english: When crossing a desert, not only can extreme heat and dehydration be dangerous, but also sudden floods. According to Wikipedia, there are more people who die from drowning than dehydration.

example_sentences.japanese: 健全な食生活は人間はもとより動物にも有益に決まっている。
example_sentences.english: Healthy eating habits are definitely beneficial not only for humans, but also for animals.

general_translation: Unlikely to, Showing no signs of
formation: Verb［stem］+ そうにない(1)(1) そうにもない
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ そうにない(1)(1) そうにもない
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ そうにありません(1)(1) そうにもありません
explanation: A grammar point highlighting that (A) does not seem to be gone toward, so therefore it is very unlikely to happen. No indication of (A) happening.
lesson_topic: It All Starts or Ends With

example_sentences.japanese: 明日雪はふりそうにない。
example_sentences.english: It is unlikely that it will snow tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: ごめん、定時で上がれそうにないから先に食べてて。
example_sentences.english: Sorry, it seems unlikely that I can leave work on time, so go ahead and eat without me.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は行けそうにないのでキャンセルでお願いします。
example_sentences.english: It is unlikely that I am going to be able to make it today, so please cancel my appointment.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は雨が降りそうにもないから釣りに行こう！
example_sentences.english: It is unlikely that it will rain today, so let's go fishing!

example_sentences.japanese: 列が進みそうにもないのでまた今度来ましょう。
example_sentences.english: The queue is showing no signs of moving so let's come back another time.

example_sentences.japanese: このストーブでは、いつまでたってもあたたまりそうにない。
example_sentences.english: This stove is showing no signs of warming up, no matter how much time is allotted.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は荷物をうけとれそうにない。
example_sentences.english: It is unlikely that I will be able to get my luggage today.

example_sentences.japanese: ２回連続で宝くじにはあたりそうにない。
example_sentences.english: It is unlikely you will win the lottery two times in a row.

example_sentences.japanese: 偉大すぎて、父をおいこせそうにない。
example_sentences.english: Being so great, it is unlikely that I will be able to surpass my father.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の貯金では、損失をおぎなえそうにない。
example_sentences.english: With my savings, it is unlikely that I will be able to compensate for the loss.

example_sentences.japanese: この問題は、来週になってもおちつきそうにない。
example_sentences.english: This problem is showing no signs of settling down, even by next week.

example_sentences.japanese: いくら考えても、いいアイデアは思いうかびそうにない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much I ponder, it is unlikely that a good idea will come to mind.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者：「この事故の後、彼女はあるけそうにない。」
example_sentences.english: Doctor: 'After this accident, it is unlikely for her to be able to walk again.'

example_sentences.japanese: 日中関係は今の状況からいって、好転しそうにない。
example_sentences.english: Judging from current Japan-China relations, a turn for the better is unlikely.

example_sentences.japanese: おかずが余ったら持って帰ろうと思ったのに、あまりそうにない。
example_sentences.english: I was thinking of bringing home some side dishes, but it doesn't seem like there will be any left over.

example_sentences.japanese: 二 週間、日本語能力試験の準備をしているが、合格できそうにない。でも、私は諦めない。
example_sentences.english: I have been preparing for the JLPT for two weeks, but passing it is unlikely. However, I won't give up.

general_translation: Go against, Contrary to
formation: Noun + に反（はん）し（て）Noun + に反（はん）する + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + に反（はん）し（て）Noun + に反（はん）する + Noun
explanation: A formal expression used when highlighting something that opposes, goes against, or is contrary to (A).
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: 神様の教えにはんするようなことをしてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: I cannot do things that go against God's doctrine.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らは会社のルールにはんして交際をしているらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that they are dating, which goes against the company rules.

example_sentences.japanese: 予想にはんしてクライアントの反応がいまいちだったので、最初からやり直さなきゃいけない。
example_sentences.english: Contrary to our expectations, the client's response was not good, so we had to start over from the beginning.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は上司の指示にはんすることはできません。
example_sentences.english: I cannot do anything that goes against my supervisor's instructions.

example_sentences.japanese: 予想にはんして早く終える事ができた。
example_sentences.english: Contrary to our expectations, we were able to finish early. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 予想に対して早く終える事ができた。
example_sentences.english: Contrary to our expectations, we were able to finish early. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は法律にはんして、大学に裏口入学した。
example_sentences.english: Going against the law, he bought his way into university.

example_sentences.japanese: うちのチームは予想にはんして、 昨年優勝したチームに勝ったよ！
example_sentences.english: Contrary to expectations, our team beat the team that won the race last year!

example_sentences.japanese: モラルにはんしてまで成り上がった彼を、羨ましいとは思いません。
example_sentences.english: I am not envious of he, who even went against morality to move up in the world.

example_sentences.japanese: 予想にはんしてものすごい売行きで、社員一同驚いている。
example_sentences.english: Contrary to expectations there was a huge (sales) demand, surprising all of the staff.

example_sentences.japanese: ルールにはんして、遠足に１０００円以上のお菓子を持って来た子がいる。
example_sentences.english: Going against the rules, there were some kids that brought snacks on the excursion in excess of 1000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父さんの忠告にはんしてまで進めたプロジェクトだから、失敗するわけにはいきません。
example_sentences.english: Since it is a project that goes against my uncle's advice, I cannot afford to fail.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長の意向にはんしてでも、人として正しい決定をすべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Even if it goes against the manager's ideas, people should do what is right.

example_sentences.japanese: 父母の意志にはんして、故郷を離れて首都に引っ越したんだ。
example_sentences.english: Contrary to the will of my parents, I left my hometown and moved to the capital.

example_sentences.japanese: 他の古代帝国が崩壊したのにはんし、アトランティスは現代まで存在している。
example_sentences.english: Contrary to other ancient empires that have collapsed, Atlantis still exists.

example_sentences.japanese: ある子どもは毎日勉強していても悪い成績をとる。それにはんして他の子どもは全然勉強をしていなくても良い成績をとる。
example_sentences.english: Contrary to some children receiving bad grades even if they study every day, others get good grades even if they do not study at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 魔法の存在は常識にはんすることだが、作家の想像力のおかげで、私たちは本や映画で楽しむことができる。
example_sentences.english: The existence of magic goes against common sense, but thanks to the rich imagination of authors, we can dive into the world of magic through movies and books.

general_translation: On the contrary
formation: Phrase (A) + 逆（ぎゃく）に + Phrase (B)
casual_structure: Phrase (A) + 逆（ぎゃく）に + Phrase (B)
explanation: A phrase that expresses something as being contrary to (A), due to it being the reverse or inverse.
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: あの話は事実らしいが、ぎゃくに信じにくい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that that story is true but on the contrary, it is hard to believe.

example_sentences.japanese: ぎゃくに、何歳に見えますか？
example_sentences.english: On the contrary, how old do I look?

example_sentences.japanese: 手袋をはめた方が安全だと思うかもしれませんが、手袋が回転部に巻き込まれるとぎゃくに危険なので、手袋を外してから作業をしてください。
example_sentences.english: You may think it is safer to wear gloves, but on the contrary, it is dangerous because they could get caught in the rotating parts. So, please remove your gloves before working.

example_sentences.japanese: 近道だと思っていたのに、地図アプリで調べてみたらぎゃくに回り道だった事がわかった。
example_sentences.english: I thought that it was a shortcut, but on the contrary, I found out that it was actually a detour when I checked on a map app.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べやすいようにスパゲティを半分にして茹でたけど、ぎゃくに食べにくくなった。
example_sentences.english: I broke the spaghetti in half  and boiled it to make it easier to eat, but on the contrary, it made it harder to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: ぎゃくに、ラーメンは？
example_sentences.english: I don't care too much what we eat, how about ramen?

example_sentences.japanese: 親切で声をかけたのに、ぎゃくに苦情を言われた。
example_sentences.english: Even though I called out to him in a gentle voice, on the contrary he complained.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅刻になると思って、急いだがぎゃくに余裕でした。
example_sentences.english: I thought that I would be late and hurried, but on the contrary, I made it with plenty of time.

example_sentences.japanese: クレーム対応をしっかりしたら、ぎゃくに売上げが伸びました。
example_sentences.english: I dealt with the complaint firmly (assuming there would be a negative impact), on the contrary my sales increased.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒いと思って厚着をして行ったら、ぎゃくに暑かった。
example_sentences.english: I thought it was cold and went wearing thick clothing. On the contrary, it was hot.

example_sentences.japanese: 喉が渇いた状態でコーラを飲むと、ぎゃくに喉が渇く。
example_sentences.english: If you drink cola while you are thirsty, on the contrary, you will become more thirsty.

example_sentences.japanese: 病気が治りそうだったが、薬を飲まずにいるとぎゃくにひどくなった。
example_sentences.english: The disease was on the verge of being healed, but I didn't take my medicine and on the contrary it got worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 少し派手かなと思っていたのに、ぎゃくに「地味なネクタイだね」と言われた。
example_sentences.english: Even though I thought it was a little gawdy, on the contrary, someone said, 'Your necktie is quite reserved.'

example_sentences.japanese: こんな靴を履いて行って笑われるかと思ったら、ぎゃくに羨ましがられました。
example_sentences.english: I thought if I went wearing shoes like these I would be laughed at, on the contrary people were envious of me.

example_sentences.japanese: 力一杯投げるようにしたら、ぎゃくにストライクが入る確率が上がった。
example_sentences.english: I started throwing it with all of my might (expecting it to be less accurate). On the contrary the probability of getting a strike increased.

example_sentences.japanese: 重たいものを持つと肩凝りが酷くなるかと思っていたけれど、鍛えられてぎゃくに肩凝りが治った。
example_sentences.english: I thought carrying heavy things would make my stiff shoulders worse, but working out on the contrary cured my stiff shoulders.

example_sentences.japanese: 年上の人にタメ口で話しかけたら、その人がぎゃくに敬語を使ってきたから気まずかった。
example_sentences.english: I talked casually with a person older than me. On the contrary, they used keigo (polite speech) with me and it was awkward.

general_translation: While, On the other hand, Although, However, On the flip side
formation: Verb + 反面（はんめん）［い］Adjective + 反面（はんめん）［な］Adjective + な(1) + 反面（はんめん）Noun + である + 反面（はんめん）Phrase + が + （、）+ 反面（はんめん）(1) である
casual_structure: Verb + 反面（はんめん）［い］Adjective + 反面（はんめん）［な］Adjective + な(1) + 反面（はんめん）Noun + である + 反面（はんめん）Phrase + が + （、）+ 反面（はんめん）(1) である
explanation: An expression used to say on the other hand, or on the reverse face of (A), (B)
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: 商品が豪華であるはんめん、参加費が高額だ。
example_sentences.english: While the products may be luxurious, the participation fee is high.

example_sentences.japanese: 都内に引っ越して色々と便利になったはんめん、家賃が前住んでいた所の倍になった。
example_sentences.english: While moving to Tokyo has made many things more convenient, the rent has doubled from where I used to live.

example_sentences.japanese: カリフォルニアの夏は日本より暑いはんめん、湿度が低いので過ごしやすいそうです。
example_sentences.english: Although summer in California is hotter than Japan, I heard that it is more comfortable because of the low humidity.

example_sentences.japanese: あの日本語教室の先生達は日本語を教えるのがとても上手なはんめん、生徒達にはとても厳しいそうだ。
example_sentences.english: Although the teachers at that Japanese language school are very good at teaching Japanese, they are very strict with their students.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中くんはとても頭のいい子であるはんめん、怠け者なのでいつも先生に怒られています。
example_sentences.english: Although Tanaka-kun is very smart, he is always getting scolded by the teacher because he is lazy.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は慎重なはんめん、消極的なところがあります。
example_sentences.english: He is cautious, but on the other hand, he also has a passive side.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人暮らしは楽しいはんめん、自分で料理したり掃除したりする必要もある。
example_sentences.english: While living alone is fun, it is also necessary for you to do all the cooking, cleaning, and the like.

example_sentences.japanese: 厳しいトレーニングを積むと筋力はつくはんめん、風邪をひきやすくなるらしい。
example_sentences.english: Relentlessly training builds physical strength, on the other hand, I seem to become more susceptible to catching a cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 消防署が近くにあると安心できるはんめん、夜中にサイレンがなるから大変だ。
example_sentences.english: Being close to the fire station gives a sense of safety, on the other hand, since sirens go off in the middle of the night, it can be troublesome.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、スマホは必要不可欠なはんめん、人はテクノロジーに溺れて、人間関係が希薄になるばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: Recently, while smartphones are essential, people are drowning in technology and human relations are getting more and more sparse.

example_sentences.japanese: 深夜の仕事は時給が高いはんめん、体には結構負担がかかる。
example_sentences.english: I make good money working the late shift, on the other hand, it is quite burdensome on my body.

example_sentences.japanese: 白菜は健康的だと言われている。そのはんめん、場合によってむくみの原因になる事もある。
example_sentences.english: Chinese cabbage is said to be healthy. On the other hand, depending on the situation, it can also become a cause of bloating.

example_sentences.japanese: 職人のこだわりは、いい作品を生み出すことにつながるはんめん、実生活ではそのこだわりはただの頑固となる。
example_sentences.english: Linked with the employees fixation on developing excellent products is, on the other hand, that their fixations manifest as stubborness in their daily lives.

example_sentences.japanese: 消毒して除菌すれば清潔さを保てるはんめん、菌に対する抵抗力が弱くなる危険性がある。
example_sentences.english: If you disinfect to remove germs, you will preserve cleanliness, on the other hand, there is a risk of having weak resistance to germs.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱帯林は綺麗に見えるはんめん、野生動物、熱帯病などのため、非常に危険だ。
example_sentences.english: While tropical forests look pretty, they are extremely dangerous because they house things like wild animals and tropical diseases.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動をよくすることは健康のためにいいことであるはんめん、人は能力以上の成果を望むため、怪我をしてしまう傾向がある。
example_sentences.english: Although exercising often is good for your health, since people desire achievements beyond their abilities, they tend to injure themselves.

example_sentences.japanese: あのパティシエが作るお菓子はとても美味しそうに見える反面、食べてみると味はいまいちだそうだ。
example_sentences.english: While the pastries made by that pastry chef look very tasty, the taste is not so good when you try them. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: あのパティシエが作るお菓子はとても美味しそうに見える反面、とても美味しいそうだ。
example_sentences.english: While the pastries made by that pastry chef look very tasty, apparently, they taste very good. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: All~, Completely, See through, Overcome, To the bitter end
formation: Verb［stem］+ ぬく
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ ぬく
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ ぬきます
explanation: A strong construction used to indicate that (A) is seen through completely. The situation of (A) has completely been extracted out of.
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: ウォルターさんは化学のことならしりぬいている。
example_sentences.english: Walter-san is all-knowing when it comes to chemistry. (completely)

example_sentences.japanese: 私の計画は彼に見ぬかれていた。
example_sentences.english: He saw through my plans.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の子供達を守りぬくためならなんでもできる。
example_sentences.english: I could do anything to protect my kids till the end.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は何があっても最後までやりぬかないと気が済まないです。
example_sentences.english: I can't have peace of mind until I finish something completely, no matter what happens.

example_sentences.japanese: 考えぬいた結果、俺は大学を中退して親父の会社を継ぐことにした。
example_sentences.english: After thoroughly thinking about it, I decided to drop out of college and take over my father's company.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中師匠は俳句の事なら知りぬいている。
example_sentences.english: Master Tanaka is all-knowing when it comes to haiku.

example_sentences.japanese: 木材に刺さった釘をひきぬく。
example_sentences.english: To completely pull out the nails in the lumber.

example_sentences.japanese: 徹夜してでも、このプロジェクトをやりぬきたい。
example_sentences.english: Even if I have to sit up all night, I want to complete this project.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は漁師として人生をいきぬいた。
example_sentences.english: He lived life completely as a fisherman.

example_sentences.japanese: 真の友というのなら、しんじぬく心が必要だ。
example_sentences.english: If they are a true friend, they need to have a heart that you can completely believe in.

example_sentences.japanese: アスリートはケガを負いつつも、最後までフルマラソンをはしりぬいた。
example_sentences.english: Even though the athlete was injured, he ran the marathon till the (bitter) end. (Literally - Bearing an injury)

example_sentences.japanese: 社長の方針をまもりぬくためならなんでもする覚悟だ。
example_sentences.english: I am resolved to do anything to completely protect the CEO's policies.

example_sentences.japanese: 兵士はひざに矢を受けたが、最後までたたかいぬいた。
example_sentences.english: Despite taking an arrow to the knee, the soldier fought till the bitter end.

example_sentences.japanese: 勇者は、魔王の計画をみぬき、それをはばむことにした。
example_sentences.english: The hero saw through the plan of the devil king, and decided to put a stop to it.

example_sentences.japanese: 研究には長い年月がかかったが、彼はたえぬき、自身の仮説を実証した。
example_sentences.english: The research took years, but he overcame (completely) adversities and proved his hypothesis. (to the bitter end)

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父の古い車を修復するのは無駄な努力だと知りつつも、やりぬいた。
example_sentences.english: Even though I knew that repairing my grandfather's old car would be a wasteful effort, I still went through with it. (completely)

example_sentences.japanese: チームは、たとえ試合に勝っても準決勝進出は不可能と知りつつも、最後までがんばりぬいた。
example_sentences.english: The team, despite knowing it was impossible to advance to the semifinals even if they won, fought to the bitter end.

example_sentences.japanese: この洗濯機ではこの量の洗濯物は洗いぬけない。
example_sentences.english: This washing machine cannot completely wash this amount of laundry. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: この洗濯機ではこの量の洗濯物は洗い切れない。
example_sentences.english: This washing machine cannot completely wash this amount of laundry. (Natural Japanese)

general_translation: Without, Unless
formation: Noun + 抜（ぬ）きで(は)Noun + 抜（ぬ）きに(は)Noun + を + 抜（ぬ）きにして(は)Noun + は + 抜（ぬ）きとして(は)Noun + 抜（ぬ）き + の + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + 抜（ぬ）きで(は)Noun + 抜（ぬ）きに(は)Noun + を + 抜（ぬ）きにして(は)Noun + は + 抜（ぬ）きとして(は)Noun + 抜（ぬ）き + の + Noun
explanation: A grammar point which expresses that something has had (A) extracted from it, which would usually be there. Without (A).
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: リスクぬきには決してフグを食べられない。
example_sentences.english: You can never eat fugu without risk.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は冗談ぬきで怖いから怒らせない方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: That guy is scary, no joke, so you shouldn't upset him.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつら全然来ないな、あいつらぬきで始めちゃおうぜ。
example_sentences.english: They aren't coming at all (it doesn't seem like they are coming anytime soon). Let's start without them.

example_sentences.japanese: ワサビぬきの寿司なんて寿司じゃないよ。
example_sentences.english: Sushi without wasabi is not sushi.

example_sentences.japanese: 若い労働者ぬきにしては、日本の建築業は成り立たない。
example_sentences.english: Without young workers, Japan's construction industry would not exist.

example_sentences.japanese: 公共交通機関ぬきにしては便利な生活ができない。
example_sentences.english: Without public transportation, you cannot live a convenient life.

example_sentences.japanese: 「クソ、渋滞だ。あいつら、パーティーをオレぬきで始めそうだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Damn, a traffic jam. It seems that they will start the party without me.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「食べれる」のような「ら」ぬきの言葉は人気になっている。
example_sentences.english: Words without 'ら', like '食べれる' are getting more popular.

example_sentences.japanese: Ｃ：「ＡとＢは付き合ってんのよ」Ｄ：「マジ！？冗談ぬきで？」
example_sentences.english: C: 'A and B are dating!' D: 'Whaa? No kidding? (without joking)'

example_sentences.japanese: 夫婦の会話：「子供ぬきでどこか面白いところに行こう！」
example_sentences.english: A conversation between a married couple: 'Let's go somewhere fun, without the children!'

example_sentences.japanese: 私にとってコーラぬきでハンバーガーを食べることは考えられない。
example_sentences.english: It is totally unacceptable for me to eat a hamburger without a coke.

example_sentences.japanese: くろさわあきらという監督ぬきにして日本の映画を語ることはできない。
example_sentences.english: It is impossible to talk about Japanese cinematography without mentioning the director Akira Kurosawa.

example_sentences.japanese: グルテンぬきの食べ物はセリアック病という病気の人のために必要である。
example_sentences.english: Gluten-removed food is necessary for those who are ill with celiac disease.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の場合、文脈ぬきのスタンドアロンの文は分かりにくい。
example_sentences.english: In the case of Japanese, standalone sentences without context are hard to understand.

example_sentences.japanese: 女の子：「あたしの料理、好きなの？」男の子：「お世辞ぬきで、今までの人生でこれよりうまいものは食べた事がない。」
example_sentences.english: Girl: 'Do you like my cooking?' Boy: 'Without flattery, I haven't eaten anything more delicious than this in my life.'

example_sentences.japanese: お寿司屋さん：「ご注文はお決まりですか？」お客さん：「はい、マグロのにぎりをワサビぬきでお願いします。」
example_sentences.english: Sushi restaurant employee: 'Are you ready to order?' Guest: 'Yes, I would like to have tuna nigiri without wasabi.'

general_translation: At last, Finally, More and more
formation: いよいよ + Phrase
casual_structure: いよいよ + Phrase
explanation: A very casual way of saying finally. Usually indicating great effort along the way, or having reached the most important stage.
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: いよいよ春がやって来た。
example_sentences.english: Spring has finally arrived.

example_sentences.japanese: いよいよ明日で卒業か...。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow is finally our graduation, isn't it…

example_sentences.japanese: いよいよ俺の番だ。緊張するけど頑張らなくちゃ！
example_sentences.english: It is finally my turn. I am nervous, but I must do my best!

example_sentences.japanese: 台風が接近するにつれて、いよいよ風が強くなってきた。
example_sentences.english: As the typhoon approached, the wind started to blow more and more.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の話を聞いていると彼がいよいよ怪しくなってきた。
example_sentences.english: Listening to his story makes him more and more suspicious.

example_sentences.japanese: じゃ、いよいよ俺の番だ！
example_sentences.english: Finally, it's my turn.

example_sentences.japanese: いよいよ夏休みが始まった！
example_sentences.english: Summer vacation has finally begun!

example_sentences.japanese: いよいよ大学を卒業する！
example_sentences.english: I have finally graduated college!

example_sentences.japanese: いよいよステージが始まる。わくわくしてきた。
example_sentences.english: The performance will finally start. I am getting excited.

example_sentences.japanese: いよいよ初出勤か。緊張するな。
example_sentences.english: It is finally your first day at work. Don't be nervous.

example_sentences.japanese: いよいよスタートだ。自分のペースで走ろう。
example_sentences.english: At last the time to start has come. I'll run at my own pace.

example_sentences.japanese: 君もいよいよ一人前の大工だね。
example_sentences.english: You have finally become a fully fledged carpenter too.

example_sentences.japanese: いよいよ娘が小学校に入学する。
example_sentences.english: Finally, my daughter will enter elementary school.

example_sentences.japanese: いよいよ寿命がない。身辺整理をしないと。
example_sentences.english: At last my life is coming to an end. I have to put my affairs in order.

example_sentences.japanese: いよいよ私の書籍が出版されます。買ってください！
example_sentences.english: My book will finally be published. Please buy it!

example_sentences.japanese: 契約がいよいよ成立する。本当に大変だった。
example_sentences.english: The contract will finally come together. It was quite a bit of work.

general_translation: Get by without doing something, To get away with
formation: Verb［ない］+ ずに済（す）むVerb［なくて］+ 済（す）むVerb［ないで］+ 済（す）む
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ ずに済（す）むVerb［なくて］+ 済（す）むVerb［ないで］+ 済（す）む
polite_structure: Verb［ない］+ ずに済（す）みますVerb［なくて］+ 済（す）みますVerb［ないで］+ 済（す）みます
explanation: A phrase that uses a somewhat old-fashioned expression to indicate that someone got away with not doing (A). It came to an end without (A).
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: 洗い物をせずにすむ。
example_sentences.english: To get away with not doing the dishes.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月契約すると初期費用を支払わないですむので、今月中に契約することをお勧めします。
example_sentences.english: We recommend that you sign the contract within this month so that you can get by without paying the initial cost.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の冬は去年より暖かかったので、ヒーターなしですみました。
example_sentences.english: Since winter this year was warmer than last year, I got by without using the heater.

example_sentences.japanese: 今宿題をやっておけば後でやらずにすむから、今のうちにやっておこう。
example_sentences.english: If I do my homework now, I can get by without doing it later, so I shall do it right now.

example_sentences.japanese: このＶＩＰパスを使えば待たずにすみます。
example_sentences.english: If you have this VIP pass, you can get by without waiting.

example_sentences.japanese: 事故が起こったけど、怪我をせずにすんだ。
example_sentences.english: An accident occurred, but I got away without getting injured.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人は警察から、つかまらずにすんだ。
example_sentences.english: The criminal got away without being arrested by the police.

example_sentences.japanese: 基礎からトレーニングを積んでいたから、つぶれずにすんだ。
example_sentences.english: Because I built my training up from the foundation, I got by without being crushed.

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんとペース配分したから、体力を消耗せずにすんだ。
example_sentences.english: Because I properly paced myself, I got by without exhausting my physical strength.

example_sentences.japanese: 運転士の巧みな技術のおかげで脱線せずにすんだ。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to the clever skill of the conductor, they got by without derailing.

example_sentences.japanese: 芸能人がツイートしてくれたから、宣伝費をつかわずにすんだ。
example_sentences.english: Because an entertainer tweeted for me, I got by without having to use advertising expenses.

example_sentences.japanese: 知人の紹介で入社できたので、テストはうけずにすんだ。
example_sentences.english: Since I was able to join the company through the introduction of a friend, I got by without taking a test.

example_sentences.japanese: 長女の的確な意見のおかげで、中途半端な決定をせずにすみました。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to the accurate opinion of the oldest daughter, we got by without settling a half-baked decision.

example_sentences.japanese: あの通訳さんのおかげで、海外での仕事で失敗せずにすみました。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to that interpreter, I got by without failing overseas.

example_sentences.japanese: 着々と計画通り進んだので、口をださずにすんだ。
example_sentences.english: Since everything progressed steadily according to the plan, we got by without having to say anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 君が予定を合わせてくれたら、みんなのスケジュールを変更せずにすむんだけど...
example_sentences.english: If you would match up your plans with everyone else's, then everyone can get by without having to change their schedule.

general_translation: Depending or based on, According to, In response to, Suitable for or to
formation: Noun + に応（おう）じ（て）Noun + に応（おう）じた + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + に応（おう）じ（て）Noun + に応（おう）じた + Noun
explanation: An expression implying that something is through (A), or through the application of what is suitable for (A).
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: ジムでは実力におうじて、練習を選べるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: At the gym, you should choose exercises suitable to your ability. (in response to)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を教える際には、生徒達のレベルにおうじてクラスを分ける必要があります。
example_sentences.english: When teaching Japanese, it is necessary to divide classes according to the level of the students.

example_sentences.japanese: この地域の土地は、面積におうじて値段が高くなります。
example_sentences.english: Land in this area is priced according to its surface area.

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちはクライアントの要望におうじたデザインを提供しています。
example_sentences.english: We provide designs that meet our clients' requests.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ん坊のために年齢におうじたダイエットが必要です。
example_sentences.english: For a toddler, it is necessary to have a diet that is suitable for their age.

example_sentences.japanese: 私共のホテルではＶＩＰレベルのニーズにおうじたサービスをご提供いたします。
example_sentences.english: In our hotel, we offer services suitable for VIP needs. (in response to)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人は相手への尊敬度におうじて、お辞儀の角度を変える。
example_sentences.english: The Japanese change the angle of their bow depending on the degree of respect for the other party. (in response to)

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官は状態や必要におうじて暴力を行使できる場合もあります。
example_sentences.english: In some cases, policemen can use force depending on circumstances or necessity. (in response to)

example_sentences.japanese: 住民からの依頼におうじて小学校の周辺での車の通行禁止が決定された。
example_sentences.english: In response to a request from the residents, a ban on passing through the area around the elementary school in vehicles has been decided.

example_sentences.japanese: 炎天下で働く際、必要におうじて水や帽子などをご用意下さい。
example_sentences.english: When working under the burning sun, please prepare things like water, a hat, etc. if necessary. (Depending on)

example_sentences.japanese: クライアントの求めにおうじて、以下に記述しているアドレスに、品物を出荷させていただきました。
example_sentences.english: In accordance with the request of the client, we had the item shipped to the following address. (In response to)

example_sentences.japanese: このフードプロセッサーは条件や目的におうじてペースト状にしたり細かくチョッピングしたりするなどのさまざまな機能へ取り替えることができる。
example_sentences.english: This food processor can swap between various functions like creating a paste, fine chopping, and others, depending on the requirements or purpose. (In response to)

example_sentences.japanese: 会社におけるいい会社員とは、場所やその時の状況におうじて柔軟に方針を決定出来る人だ。
example_sentences.english: A good employee at a company is a person who can flexibly decide on a course of action depending on the place and circumstances at the time. (in response to)

example_sentences.japanese: 新たなパソコンを選択する場合、パフォーマンスやコンポーネントの品質におうじて価格が決められていることを心がけることが大事です。安いコンピューターはより悪い部分が普通にある。しかし、例外もある。
example_sentences.english: If you choose a new computer, it is important to be aware that the price is set based on the performance and component quality. A cheap computer has inferior components in general. But there are exceptions. (in response to)

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒は試験の結果におうじた成績を受け取る。
example_sentences.english: Students receive grades suitable for the results of their exams. (In response to)

general_translation: Through, Via, Throughout
formation: Noun + を通（とお）してNoun + を通（つう）じて
casual_structure: Noun + を通（とお）してNoun + を通（つう）じて
explanation: An expression which explains the means through which (A) was done. Literally with (A) as the flow point, (B).
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: このプロジェクトをつうじて多くのことを学んだ。
example_sentences.english: I have learned a lot through participating in this project.

example_sentences.japanese: その事件はネットニュースをつうじて知りました。
example_sentences.english: I learned about that incident through online news.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はアニメをつうじて日本語を学んだそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that he learned Japanese through anime.

example_sentences.japanese: 語学留学をとおして日本の文化などを学びました。
example_sentences.english: I learned about Japanese culture and other aspects of Japan through language study.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事をとおして今の妻と出会いました。
example_sentences.english: I met my current wife through work.

example_sentences.japanese: 看病をとおして人の愛を知りました。
example_sentences.english: Through nursing a patient, I came to know human affection.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父さんをとおして仕事の依頼がきた。
example_sentences.english: Through my uncle, I got a job commission.

example_sentences.japanese: 打合せをとおして新たな発見をすることもよくある。
example_sentences.english: There are many new discoveries made through business meetings.

example_sentences.japanese: 植木をとおして自然の尊さを学びました。
example_sentences.english: I learned the nobility of nature through planting.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の奥さんには友達をつうじて出会った。
example_sentences.english: I met my current wife through a friend.

example_sentences.japanese: オルガンをとおして練習することの大切さを学んだ。
example_sentences.english: Through the organ, I learned the importance of practice.

example_sentences.japanese: 学会をとおして与えられた指針が役立ちました。
example_sentences.english: Throughout the academic conference, the guidelines that were given were helpful.

example_sentences.japanese: 演劇をつうじてコミュニケーション能力が向上した。
example_sentences.english: Through the theatrical play, my communication ability improved.

example_sentences.japanese: 観測をつうじて、研究の大変さがよく分かった。
example_sentences.english: Through observation, I fully understood the difficulty of research.

example_sentences.japanese: 家屋調査をつうじて、建物の現状がかなり理解できた。
example_sentences.english: Through the house inspection, I was able to understand a lot about the state of the building.

example_sentences.japanese: 親と弁護士だけをつうじて連絡できることになった。親が私のことを憎んでいる。
example_sentences.english: I ended up being able to communicate with my parents only via the lawyer. My parents hate me.

example_sentences.japanese: ロシアには年間をつうじて寒い村があるらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that there is a town in Russia that is cold throughout the year. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 事故にあった際には弁護士をつうじて相手に連絡をするようにしてください。
example_sentences.english: If you are involved in an accident, you should contact the other party through your attorney. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 事故にあった際には弁護士をとおして相手に連絡をするようにしてください。
example_sentences.english: If you are involved in an accident, you should contact the other party through your attorney. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: ロシアには年間をとおして寒い村があるらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that there is a town in Russia that is cold throughout the year. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: In response to, Meet
formation: Noun + にこたえ（て）Noun + にこたえる(1) + Noun(1) にこたえた
casual_structure: Noun + にこたえ（て）Noun + にこたえる(1) + Noun(1) にこたえた
explanation: A structure meaning that something is being applied to meet (A), in response to its expectation.
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: 応援の声にこたえて、勝利したチームが礼をした。
example_sentences.english: In response to the cheering, the victorious team bowed.

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒達の要望にこたえて、レッスン料金を１０００円安くした。
example_sentences.english: In response to our students' request, we have reduced the lesson fee by 1,000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: クライアントのリクエストにこたえて、デザインを少しだけ変えました。
example_sentences.english: We changed the design slightly in response to the client's request.

example_sentences.japanese: 弊社ではお客様のニーズにこたえるサービスを提供するよう、日々努力しています。
example_sentences.english: We are committed to providing services that meet the needs of our clients.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの要望にこたえる自信はありますが、このデザインを完成させるには時間がかかると思います。
example_sentences.english: We are confident we can meet your request, but it will take time to complete this design.

example_sentences.japanese: 選手の活躍にこたえて、トレー二ングルームを新しくした。
example_sentences.english: In response to the athletes' great efforts, we remodeled the training room.

example_sentences.japanese: アイドル歌手の喝采にこたえた笑顔が素晴らしかった。
example_sentences.english: The idol singer's smile in response to the applause was wonderful.

example_sentences.japanese: 我が社はクライアントのニーズにこたえた商品を開発するべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Our company should develop products that respond to our clients' needs.

example_sentences.japanese: 演劇人気にこたえて建てた劇場の維持費が大変だ。
example_sentences.english: The maintenance cost for the theater built in response to the popularity of plays is enormous.

example_sentences.japanese: 加速する需要にこたえて、商品の増産を決断しました。
example_sentences.english: We decided to increase merchandise production in response to the increase in demand.

example_sentences.japanese: この水泳選手はこのオリンピックで期待にこたえる成績をあげた。
example_sentences.english: This swimmer got results that will meet expectations at this Olympics.

example_sentences.japanese: 神の依頼にこたえて、勇者はゼ〇ダ姫を助けに出かけた。
example_sentences.english: In response to God's request, the hero departed to save princess Ze*da.

example_sentences.japanese: 楽器を新しくして欲しいとの要望にこたえて、購入しました。
example_sentences.english: In response to the demand for new musical instruments, I bought some.

example_sentences.japanese: 学級会で出たアイデアにこたえて、授業を工夫してみた。
example_sentences.english: I tried to plan a class in response to the idea that came out in the class meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: 住民の皆様の希望にこたえ、犬や猫の糞のために、ごみ箱を設置することになりました。
example_sentences.english: In response to residents' wishes, it has been decided that trash bins for cat and dog litter will be installed.

example_sentences.japanese: 情報公開請求にこたえて、事故原因に関する書類が開示された。
example_sentences.english: In response to the freedom of information claim, the documents regarding the cause of the accident were released.

general_translation: Or, Or else, Rather
formation: Option (A) + それとも + Option (B)
casual_structure: Option (A) + それとも + Option (B)
explanation: A phrase which specifically expresses a choice between only (A) and (B). Literally, together with that (A), (B).
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: クレジットカードで払う？それとも現金で？
example_sentences.english: Are you paying with a credit card? Or rather, in cash?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は文法の勉強をしますか。それとも漢字の勉強をしますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you want to study grammar today? Or rather, do you want to study Kanji?

example_sentences.japanese: 来週はどこに行きたい？動物園に行く？それとも家でゆっくりする？
example_sentences.english: Where do you want to go next week? Do you want to go to the zoo? Or rather do you want to relax at home?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は海に行こうか、それとも川に行こうか、迷うな。
example_sentences.english: I don't know whether to go to the ocean or the river today.

example_sentences.japanese: 苦情を言うべきか、それとも我慢すべきか。
example_sentences.english: Should we complain? Or rather, should we persevere?

example_sentences.japanese: 今夜はカラオケに行く？それとも映画館？
example_sentences.english: Are you going to karaoke tonight? Or rather, to the cinema?

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの大学は国立？それとも私立？
example_sentences.english: Is your university a national one, or rather a private one?

example_sentences.japanese: 生きるべきか、それとも死ぬべきか。それが問題だ。
example_sentences.english: To live, or to die. That is the question.

example_sentences.japanese: 紺？それとも黒？どちらのスーツがいいと思いますか？
example_sentences.english: Dark blue, or rather black? Which suit do you think is good?

example_sentences.japanese: 競馬それとも競輪？今日はどちらに行くんですか？
example_sentences.english: Horse racing, or rather bicycle racing? Which are you going to today?

example_sentences.japanese: 白胡椒？それとも黒胡椒？どちらがいいですか？
example_sentences.english: White pepper? Or rather, black pepper? Which is good?

example_sentences.japanese: 継続すべきか、それとも心を鬼にして打ち切るべきか…
example_sentences.english: Should I continue? Or rather, should I harden my heart and abort.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分で洗おうか、それともクリーニングに出そうか迷うところです。
example_sentences.english: I am hesitant. Shall I wash it myself? Or rather, shall I send it off to the dry cleaners?

example_sentences.japanese: 敬語を使うべきか、それともタメ口で親しさをアピールすべきか。
example_sentences.english: Should I use keigo? Or rather, should I appeal to their intimate side and speak frankly?

example_sentences.japanese: 少し風邪気味だ。稽古をすべきか、それとも休むべきか、微妙だ。
example_sentences.english: I am feeling a little sick. It is questionable whether I should practice, or (rather) should I take it easy.

general_translation: From the point of view of
formation: Noun + にしたら(1)(1) にすれば
casual_structure: Noun + にしたら(1)(1) にすれば
explanation: A hypothetical phrase that indicates that if you go off the point of view of (A), then (B).
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: 妻にしたら、私はもっと家事をしなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: From the perspective of my wife, I have to help more with the house work.

example_sentences.japanese: お客様にしたら、値段が安い方がいいだろう。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of the customer, a lower price is probably better.

example_sentences.japanese: 納豆が嫌いな人にしたら、納豆はただ臭いだけに違いない。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of a person that does not like natto, natto must just stink (natto is something that stinks and nothing more).

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が何歳になろうとも、親にすればいつまでも子供に見える。
example_sentences.english: From the parent's point of view, their children look like kids no matter how old they are.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人にすれば普通なことでも、海外の方が見たら驚く事がたくさんあるらしい。
example_sentences.english: It seems that there are many things that are ordinary from the point of view of Japanese people that are surprising to people from other countries.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんは可愛いが、親にしたら苦労もあるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Babies are cute, but from a parent's point of view there are hardships as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 大人にしたら、童話は少し物足りない。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of an adult, fairy-tales are somewhat unsatisfactory.

example_sentences.japanese: 床屋さんにしたら、散髪はアートのようなものなのかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: From the perspective of a barber, cutting hair is probably something like art.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人にしたら、僕の成功が憎らしくてたまらないのだろう。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of that person, I imagine that he hates my success...

example_sentences.japanese: 女房にしたら、今の生活に不満があるらしい。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of my wife, it seems like she is dissatisfied with our current lifestyle.

example_sentences.japanese: 学生にしたら、テストは簡単ならば、簡単なほどいい。
example_sentences.english: From the student's point of view, the easier the test is, the better.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩にしたら、僕の意見は「生意気だ」と感じるのかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: From the perspective of my senpai, he probably feels like my opinions are brazen.

example_sentences.japanese: 翻訳者にしたら、あの東北訛りはかなり厄介だと思います。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of a translator, I think that the Tohoku accent is rather troublesome.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長にしたら、的確なアドバイスをしてくれる秘書がいると助かる。
example_sentences.english: From the perspective of the CEO, it is helpful to have a secretary that gives accurate advice.

example_sentences.japanese: 地域住民にしたら、連続放火事件が心配で夜も眠れない。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of the local residents, the series of arson incidents have them worried and they cannot sleep at night.

example_sentences.japanese: 主婦にしたら、あの店は手頃な値段でいい品物が置いてあるから救世主のようなものだ。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of a housewife, since that store has nice goods at a reasonable price, it is like a lifesaver.

example_sentences.japanese: 私にしたら、それは高すぎます。
example_sentences.english: Going off of me, that is too expensive. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼にしたら、それは高すぎるそうです。
example_sentences.english: Going off of him, apparently that is too expensive. (Natural Japanese)

general_translation: Regardless of whether
formation: Verb (A) + にしても + Verb (B) + にしてもNoun (A) + にしても + Noun (B) + にしても［い］Adjective (A) + にしても + ［い］Adjective (B) + にしても［な］Adjective (A) + にしても + ［な］Adjective (B) + にしても
casual_structure: Verb (A) + にしても + Verb (B) + にしてもNoun (A) + にしても + Noun (B) + にしても［い］Adjective (A) + にしても + ［い］Adjective (B) + にしても［な］Adjective (A) + にしても + ［な］Adjective (B) + にしても
explanation: A two-part expression that implies that going off either (A) or (B) will have the same result.
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: 貸すにしても売るにしても、とにかく元を取れればそれでいい。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether you rent it out, or sell it, it is fine as long as I break even somehow.

example_sentences.japanese: 忘年会に出席するにしても、しないにしても、参加費を払わないといけないのはおかしいと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think it is unfair that we need to pay the attendance fee for the year-end party regardless of whether we attend or not.

example_sentences.japanese: 家を立て直すにしても、リフォームするにしても、費用は同じぐらいになりそうだ。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether the house is rebuilt or remodeled, the cost is likely to be about the same.

example_sentences.japanese: 水深が深いにしても、浅いにしても、ライフジャケットは着ておいた方がいい。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether the water is deep or shallow, you should wear a life jacket.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語が上手にしても、下手にしても、勉強は毎日しておいた方がいい。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether you are good or bad at Japanese, you should study every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 平日にしても祝日にしても、ディズニーランドは多くの人で賑わっています。
example_sentences.english: Disneyland is crowded with people, regardless of whether it is a weekday or a holiday.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べるにしても、食べないにしても、料理代を払わないといけない。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether you eat or not, you still have to pay for the food.

example_sentences.japanese: 貸家にしても、自宅にしても、家族がいるだけで十分。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether you own a house or rent one, as long as you have family, that is enough.

example_sentences.japanese: 簡単にしても、難しいにしても、宿題を終わらせるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether the homework is easy or hard, you must finish it.

example_sentences.japanese: 煮るにしても焼くにしても、素材の良さを活かした料理にしてください。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether you boil it or fry it, please make use of the quality of the raw materials.

example_sentences.japanese: 入社するにしてもしないにしても、明後日までには返事をください。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether you join the company or not, please reply by the day after tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 進むにしても引き返すにしても、勇気がないと決断できない。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether you continue forward or turn back, you can't make a decision without courage.

example_sentences.japanese: 増やすにしても減らすにしても、先見の明が必要だ。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether it increases or decreases, it is necessary to anticipate it.

example_sentences.japanese: 平日にしても祝日にしても、都会はとにかく人が多い。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether it is a weekday or a holiday/weekend, there are generally a lot of people in the city.

example_sentences.japanese: 飛行機にしてもヘリコプターにしても、騒音問題をなんとかしてほしい。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether it is a plane or a helicopter, I want them to do something about the noise problem.

example_sentences.japanese: 方針を変えるにしても変えないにしても、決定を急ぐ必要があります。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether we change the plan or not, it is necessary to make the decision soon.

example_sentences.japanese: 車にしてもバイクにしても、比較的上手に運転できる方だと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think he is someone who can drive relatively well regardless of whether it is a car or a motorcycle.

general_translation: As a, For a, As for
formation: Noun + としては
casual_structure: Noun + としては
explanation: A hypothetical grammar point that expresses that going with the general conclusion of (A), (B) is the case.
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: 概論としては、まだ不十分です。
example_sentences.english: For an outline, it still needs work.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は先輩としてはいいけど、友達になろうとは思えない。
example_sentences.english: As a senpai, he is a good person, but I don't think I would want to be friends with him.

example_sentences.japanese: あの会社は建築会社としてはホワイトな方だと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that company is white as far as construction companies go.

example_sentences.japanese: アイデアとしてはいいんですが、実際にやるとなるとものすごい費用がかかると思います。
example_sentences.english: That is good as an idea, but I think it would cost a tremendous amount of money to actually do it.

example_sentences.japanese: ピアノは趣味としては好きだけど、ピアノで食べていこうとは思わない。
example_sentences.english: I like playing the piano as a hobby, but I don't want to make a living out of it.

example_sentences.japanese: 晴れ着としては、ぼろすぎないか？
example_sentences.english: For your Sunday best (clothes), aren't they a little raggedy?

example_sentences.japanese: アイデアとしてはいいが、実現するのは難しい。
example_sentences.english: As an idea, that is good. However, it will be difficult in practice.

example_sentences.japanese: イメージとしては分かりますが、説明が曖昧すぎます。
example_sentences.english: As a mental image I understand, but the explanation is too vague.

example_sentences.japanese: 趣味としてはいいが、編物だけで食べていくのは難しい。
example_sentences.english: As a hobby it is fine, but it is difficult to make a living off of just knitting.

example_sentences.japanese: 素質としては十分だが、まだまだ荒削りだ。
example_sentences.english: As for its qualities it is adequate, but it is still very much a work in progress.

example_sentences.japanese: いい作品だけど、生け花の先生としてはまだまだだ。
example_sentences.english: It is a good work, but for a flower arrangement teacher, you still have a ways to go.

example_sentences.japanese: 灯りとしては十分ですが、これで部屋を暖めるのは無理ですね。
example_sentences.english: As a light (source) it is sufficient, but it is impossible to heat this room with it.

example_sentences.japanese: 君が昨日言っていたこと、案外提案としてはいいのかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: What you said yesterday is probably good for an unexpected proposal.

example_sentences.japanese: 人気は出てきましたが、売上としてはまだ足りません。
example_sentences.english: It has become popular, but as for sales, it is still insufficient.

example_sentences.japanese: とてもいい友達だと思うけど、恋人としては考えられない。
example_sentences.english: I think of him as a very good friend, but I can't think of him as a lover.

example_sentences.japanese: 私にとって彼女の体型は完璧だが、彼女としては、それでは満足できないらしい。
example_sentences.english: According to me, I think that her body shape is perfect, but for her, it seems that she's not satisfied with it.

example_sentences.japanese: マラソンを完走してみんな「すごい」と言っているけど、叔父さんとしてはタイムに満足していないらしい。
example_sentences.english: Everyone is saying 'Amazing!' for finishing the marathon, but as for my uncle, it seems that he's not satisfied with the time.

general_translation: Even if (we assume), Assuming,  Also as
formation: Verb + としても［い］Adjective + としても［な］Adjective + （だ）+ としてもNoun + （だ）+ としても
casual_structure: Verb + としても［い］Adjective + としても［な］Adjective + （だ）+ としてもNoun + （だ）+ としても
explanation: A hypothetical phrase that expresses that even assuming or going with (A), (B) is still the case.
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: たとえできるとしても、やらないだろう。
example_sentences.english: I wouldn't do it even if I could.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ早くついたとしても、一番乗りになることはないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if we get there early, that probably doesn't mean that we will be the first to get on.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが言っている事が正しいとしても、私は賛成できません。
example_sentences.english: Even if we assume that what you are saying is correct, I do not agree with it.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ仕事が簡単だとしても、仕事は丁寧にやるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Even if work is easy, work should be done with care.

example_sentences.japanese: 冗談だとしても、そういうことは言わない方がいいと思う。
example_sentences.english: Even if that was a joke, I don't think that you should say something like that.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな急に内容を変えられたら、私としても困ります。
example_sentences.english: It will even inconvenience me if you change the details so suddenly.

example_sentences.japanese: 環境問題に取り組んでいる会社としてもこういうことをしたくないのですが、仕方がないんです。
example_sentences.english: As a company that works on environmental issues, we don't want to do this, but we really don't have a choice.

example_sentences.japanese: 例え話だとしても許されない。
