example_sentences.english: Even if it is a parable, I can't permit it.

example_sentences.japanese: 大人向きの本だとしても売れます。
example_sentences.english: Even if it's a book meant for adults, it will sell.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はピアノ奏者だが、オルガン奏者としても有名です。
example_sentences.english: He is a pianist, but he is also famous as an organ player.

example_sentences.japanese: それが正式な回答だとしても、僕はまだ諦めきれません。
example_sentences.english: Even if we assume that is the official answer, I still cannot accept it.

example_sentences.japanese: 落し物が見つかったとしても、ネコババされている可能性もある。
example_sentences.english: Even if we assume that the lost item was found, there is still the possibility that someone pocketed it.

example_sentences.japanese: 各自で決めるべき問題だとしても、アドバイスくらいしてほしい。
example_sentences.english: Even if we assume that it is a problem that should be decided individually, I would like some advice.

example_sentences.japanese: 例え伯母さんだとしても、あの秘密を打ち明けるわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Even assuming it is my aunt, it is impossible for me to open up about that secret.

example_sentences.japanese: 快晴だとしても、少し風邪っぽいなら休んだ方がいいと思います。
example_sentences.english: Even if we assume it is nice weather, I think it is better if you rested if you are feeling a little like you have a cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 無事解放されたとしても、その後の精神的なケアが必要です。
example_sentences.english: Even if we assume that he was safely released, he still needs mental health care afterward.

example_sentences.japanese: 有名な先生から教わったとしても、こんなに早く上達した人は見たことがない。
example_sentences.english: Even if we assume that they were taught by a famous teacher, I have never seen someone progress so quickly.

example_sentences.japanese: 何らかの恩恵を受けられるとしても、カジノの受け入れには反対だ。
example_sentences.english: Even if we assume that we'd get some kind of benefit from it, I am opposed to the casino's acceptance.

general_translation: Nevertheless, Even so
formation: Phrase (A) + それにしても + Phrase (B)
casual_structure: Phrase (A) + それにしても + Phrase (B)
explanation: A structure used to show that even going off that which was previously stated, (B) is still true.
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: ラッピングをお願いしたが、それにしても、かなりの過剰包装だ。
example_sentences.english: I asked for wrapping, but even so, the wrapping was excessive.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は新人だから仕方がないが、それにしても仕事ができなさすぎる。
example_sentences.english: She's new so we can't blame her, but even so, she is not good at her job at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中くんは遅れてくると言っていたが、それにしてもくるのが遅すぎる。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-kun said he will be late, but even so, it's taking him too long to come.

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字を勉強し始めてから１年になる。それにしても、まだ全然漢字が読めない。
example_sentences.english: It has been a year since I started studying kanji. Nevertheless, I still can't read kanji at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 家に来たばかりのときなんかお手もできなかったのにね。それにしても、大きくなったね。
example_sentences.english: When he first came to our house, he couldn't even give me his paw. Nevertheless, he got so big, don't you think?

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩、昨日はご馳走様でした！それにしても、あそこの料理は最高でしたね！
example_sentences.english: Senpai, thank you for treating me yesterday! Nevertheless, that restaurant was awesome, wasn't it?!

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らが問題の解決に手を貸していますが、それにしてもそれは難問です。
example_sentences.english: They are lending a hand to solve that problem. Even so, that is a tough one.

example_sentences.japanese: 古い車だから仕方がないが、それにしても加速が悪すぎる。
example_sentences.english: It is an old car so it can't be helped, but nevertheless, the acceleration is terrible.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司から許可を得ました。それにしても、本部に連絡しないといけません。
example_sentences.english: We received permission from the boss. Even so, we have to contact the headquarters.

example_sentences.japanese: 災害を防止するには、避難訓練が必要だ。それにしても、完全な予防は無理だろう。
example_sentences.english: In order to prevent disasters, disaster drills are necessary. Nevertheless, complete prevention is probably impossible.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女と付き合って一年になる。それにしても、女の人の気持ちはよく分からない。
example_sentences.english: It will be one year since I started dating my girlfriend. Even so, I don't understand women's feelings very well.

example_sentences.japanese: 送別会の準備をしなければいけない。それにしても、この会館は安く借りられてありがたい。
example_sentences.english: We have to prepare for the farewell party (ourselves). Nevertheless, I am thankful that we could rent this event hall for cheap.

example_sentences.japanese: 泳ぐのが好きなのだろうが、それにしても、何回海水浴に行けば気がすむんだ…
example_sentences.english: You probably like swimming, but nevertheless, how many times do you have to go to the beach for you to grow tired of it.

example_sentences.japanese: 不祥事の責任は取らなければいけないが、それにしても、解散する必要はなかったと思います。
example_sentences.english: Responsibility for the scandal must be taken, but even so, I don't think it was necessary for them to break up.

example_sentences.japanese: 作った野菜が荒らされる被害が出ているが、それにしても、そこまで厳重な垣根を作らなくてもいいのに…
example_sentences.english: The vegetables we are growing are being damaged by pests, even so, you don't need to make such a secure fence...

example_sentences.japanese: チャレンジするのはいいことだが、それにしても、成功する確率が低すぎる。
example_sentences.english: It is good to take on challenges, but nevertheless, the rate at which you succeed is too low.

example_sentences.japanese: 火山の噴火は落ち着いたが、それにしても、今回の被害はひどすぎます。
example_sentences.english: The volcanic eruption has died down, nevertheless the damage done this time is too severe.

general_translation: Classical negative, Classical verb [ない]
formation: Verb［ない］+ ぬVerb［ない］+ ぬ + NounExceptions: する ￫ せぬくる ￫ こぬいる ￫ おらぬ
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ ぬVerb［ない］+ ぬ + NounExceptions: する ￫ せぬくる ￫ こぬいる ￫ おらぬ
explanation: A classical negative verb structure that tends to be used in set phrases.
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: 「愚か者、男にはころせぬのだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Fool, no man can kill me.'

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに狭い道は通れぬ。
example_sentences.english: I cannot pass a road this narrow.

example_sentences.japanese: なんだこの飯は！こんなまずそうなものは口に入れぬ！
example_sentences.english: What is this food? I will not put this disgusting thing in my mouth!

example_sentences.japanese: 貴様みたいなものには、わしなど殺せぬ。
example_sentences.english: Someone like you cannot kill the likes of me.

example_sentences.japanese: 鈴木殿はここにはおらぬ。
example_sentences.english: Suzuki-dono is not here.

example_sentences.japanese: あの方は人を傷つけるようなことはせぬ。
example_sentences.english: That person would never do anything to hurt anyone.

example_sentences.japanese: 婆さんが川から帰ってこぬ。
example_sentences.english: My wife won't come back from the river.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらでは性による差別は許可されておらぬ。
example_sentences.english: Sex discrimination is not permitted here.

example_sentences.japanese: ペーネロペー：「オデュッセウスはまだもどってこぬのか？」
example_sentences.english: Penelope: 'Odysseus has not returned yet?'

example_sentences.japanese: 「隅におけぬ人」というのは「侮れない人」ということなのだ。
example_sentences.english: 'A person who (can't be placed) in a corner' means 'a person who cannot be taken lightly'.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司は部下が向上できるように、いたらぬ点を教えてあげるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: A superior should tell his/her subordinates where they fall short so that they can improve.

example_sentences.japanese: 海のデッドゾーンは魚などの大量死の原因となりうるかもしれぬ。
example_sentences.english: The ocean's dead zones might become the cause of large amounts of death among fish (and other sea life).

example_sentences.japanese: 予期せぬ事態が起きた場合は、この番号に電話をください。
example_sentences.english: If something unexpected happens, please call this number. (not)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は、自伝を書き上げて１年もたたぬうちに亡くなった。
example_sentences.english: He died without even one year passing after finishing his autobiography.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の「いわぬが花 」はおおよそ英語の「silence is golden」に当たるようである。
example_sentences.english: It seems that the Japanese 'a flower does not speak', is roughly equivalent to 'silence is golden' in English.

example_sentences.japanese: 魔王様：「 じゃからアンタを殺すと悪い気はせぬぞ。」
example_sentences.english: Demon King: 'That's why if I kill you I won't feel bad.'

example_sentences.japanese: 言うまでもないことだが、知人に対してそしらぬふりをするのは失礼である。
example_sentences.english: Needless to say, pretending not to know acquaintances is rude.

example_sentences.japanese: 何でジュリエットはロメオを愛せなくなったかというと変わらぬ愛などは存在せぬためだ。
example_sentences.english: If I were to say why Juliet stopped loving Romeo, well it is because there is no such thing as eternal love (unchanging).

general_translation: Without ~ing
formation: Verb + ことなく
casual_structure: Verb + ことなく
explanation: A formal expression indicating that the thing which is (A) will end without happening, or literally with not having happened.
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: 何ごとも理解されることなく終わる。
example_sentences.english: It will end without me understanding anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 怪我人を出すことなく、人質を全員救出する事ができたそうです。
example_sentences.english: They were able to rescue all the hostages without injuring anyone.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅刻することなく、職場に着いた。
example_sentences.english: I was able to arrive at work without being late.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人が捕まることなく１０年が経つ。
example_sentences.english: Ten years pass without the culprit being caught.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は社長に何も言うことなく会社を辞めた。
example_sentences.english: He quit his job without telling the boss.

example_sentences.japanese: 真実を知ることなく終わる。
example_sentences.english: It will end without me knowing the truth.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅れることなく到着した。
example_sentences.english: To arrive without being late.

example_sentences.japanese: 耕すことなく種を植えても、うまくいくはずがない。
example_sentences.english: Without tilling, even if you plant seeds, there is no way it will turn out well.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの子には、散らかすことなく遊ぶという特技があります。
example_sentences.english: Our child has a special skill where they can play without leaving things untidy.

example_sentences.japanese: 対立することなく話し合いを終えることができました。
example_sentences.english: The discussion was able to come to a close without confrontation. (without ~ing)

example_sentences.japanese: 挨拶をしたのに、友人は立ち止まることなく行ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Despite saying hello, my friend went without stopping.

example_sentences.japanese: この洗剤を使えば、セーターが縮むことなく洗えるからおすすめですよ。
example_sentences.english: If you use this detergent, you can wash a sweater without it shrinking, so I recommend it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の長所を知ることなく、別れの時がきてしまった。
example_sentences.english: It has come time for us to part ways without knowing his strong points.

example_sentences.japanese: ネットショップなら、直接話すことなく注文できて楽だ。
example_sentences.english: If you shop online, you can comfortably order without speaking to anyone directly.

example_sentences.japanese: あの選手は、準備体操をすることなく試合に出るらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that athlete plays without doing warming up exercises.

example_sentences.japanese: 貴乃花は一門に属することなく引退してしまった。
example_sentences.english: Takanohana retired without ever joining an ichimon (a  group of sumo stables).

general_translation: In, At, With, Using, By
formation: Noun + にて
casual_structure: Noun + にて
explanation: A somewhat formal, short pattern used to show that something happens in, at, or by using (A).
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: これにて一件落着。
example_sentences.english: With this, the case is closed.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は金時計にて集合しましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's meet tomorrow at the Golden Clock.

example_sentences.japanese: 当店は午前９時にて開店いたします。
example_sentences.english: This store will open at 9:00 a.m.

example_sentences.japanese: 予約をされる場合は電話にてご連絡ください。
example_sentences.english: If you want to make a reservation, please make one by phone.

example_sentences.japanese: 応接室にてお待ちしております。
example_sentences.english: I am waiting in the waiting room.

example_sentences.japanese: 面接は本社にて行います。
example_sentences.english: The interview will take place at the company headquarters.

example_sentences.japanese: メールにてご連絡いただけると助かります。
example_sentences.english: It would be helpful if you could contact me using email.

example_sentences.japanese: 午後五時にて閉店いたします。
example_sentences.english: We will close (the shop) at five in the afternoon.

example_sentences.japanese: 外部委員にて調査がなされます。
example_sentences.english: The investigation will be performed by an external committee.

example_sentences.japanese: 在学中にて、アルコールは控えている。
example_sentences.english: I am refraining from alcohol while in active school enrollment.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、東京駅にてお会いしましょう。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow, let's meet at Tokyo Station.

example_sentences.japanese: 学会にて新たな見解が発表された。
example_sentences.english: A new opinion was announced at the academic conference.

example_sentences.japanese: あれは、コンクールにて最優秀賞を受賞した絵画です。
example_sentences.english: That is the painting that was awarded the top award in the contest.

example_sentences.japanese: 実習にて学んだことを、本番で活かしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please make use of what you learned in training.

example_sentences.japanese: イベントは屋外にて行われますので、雨天時は中止となります。
example_sentences.english: Since the event will take place in the outdoors, when it is rainy weather, the event will be suspended.

general_translation: In order to, In regard to, For
formation: Verb + にはNoun + には
casual_structure: Verb + にはNoun + には
explanation: A short phrase indicating that for (A), or to arrive at end point of (A), (B) exists or is required.
lesson_topic: For and Against, Through and Without

example_sentences.japanese: 「移動にはスクーターを使ったらどう？」
example_sentences.english: 'What about using a scooter for transportation?'

example_sentences.japanese: このホームセンターは会員制なので、買い物をするには会員登録が必要です。
example_sentences.english: Since this home improvement store is only open to members, you will need to sign up in order to shop here.

example_sentences.japanese: 海外に行くにはパスポートが必要です。
example_sentences.english: You need a passport in order to travel abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: この本は子供には難しすぎるだろう。
example_sentences.english: This book is probably too difficult for children.

example_sentences.japanese: 通勤には車を使わないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please do not use your car for commuting.

example_sentences.japanese: 夢を実現するには時間がかかる。
example_sentences.english: It takes time in order to make one's dream happen.

example_sentences.japanese: 出産には、我慢強さが必要です。
example_sentences.english: In order to give birth, endurance is necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: 一戸建てを買うには多くの金がかかる。
example_sentences.english: It costs a lot of money to buy a detached house.

example_sentences.japanese: 間違いを認めてやり直すには勇気が要ります。
example_sentences.english: One needs courage in order to admit a mistake and start over.

example_sentences.japanese: ３ヶ月以上の滞在にはビザが必要です。
example_sentences.english: A visa is necessary for stays longer than three months.

example_sentences.japanese: 短所を改善するには、まずその短所を認めることが必要です。
example_sentences.english: In order to fix your weaknesses, it is necessary to first acknowledge those weaknesses.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国語を学ぶには一貫性が一番だと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that the best way to learn a foreign language is consistency.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動は、健康を維持するには不可欠です。
example_sentences.english: Exercise is essential in order to maintain good health.

example_sentences.japanese: 通勤には自転車を使う人が最近増えている。
example_sentences.english: The number of people who have been using a bicycle for commuting has increased.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で独り暮らしをするには、日本語を話せるようになるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: In order to live by yourself in Japan, you should be able to speak Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 「妹がブランコで遊ぶには、まだ小さすぎます。」と男の子は言いました。
example_sentences.english: 'As for playing on the swings, my sister is still too small', said the boy. (In order to)

general_translation: As one hopes, As desired, As one thought
formation: Phrase + 思（おも）うように + (Outcome)Phrase + 思（おも）うような + Noun
casual_structure: Phrase + 思（おも）うように + (Outcome)Phrase + 思（おも）うような + Noun
explanation: A phrase that indicates that the outcome of (A) either is or is not in the manner they had thought.

example_sentences.japanese: この車はおもうように加速しないからイライラする。
example_sentences.english: It is irritating that this car doesn't accelerate like I hoped it would.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近仕事がおもうように行かなくてストレスが溜まってきてるんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Recently, work has not been going as well as I hoped, so I am starting to get stressed out.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日漢字を練習しているがおもうように上達しない。
example_sentences.english: I am practicing kanji every day, but I am not making as much progress as I thought.

example_sentences.japanese: 事故に遭ってから指がおもうように動かなくなった。
example_sentences.english: Since the accident, my fingers have become unable to move as I had thought.

example_sentences.japanese: オーケストラのメンバー集めがおもうようにいきません。
example_sentences.english: Assembling orchestra members is not going as I had hoped it would.

example_sentences.japanese: プリンを作ったら、おもうように固まらなくて困った。
example_sentences.english: When I made pudding, I had trouble getting it to firm up like I hoped it would.

example_sentences.japanese: ケーキ屋みたいなお菓子がおもうように作れなかった。
example_sentences.english: Making sweets like they do at the pastry shop didn't go as I had hoped it would.

example_sentences.japanese: 育児というのは、親のおもうようにはいかないものです。
example_sentences.english: Childcare is known as something that is expected to not go how the parents hope it will.

example_sentences.japanese: おもうように売上げが伸びず苦労している。
example_sentences.english: I am having trouble with sales not increasing like I hoped they would.

example_sentences.japanese: おもうようにアイデアが浮かばないまま一週間が過ぎてしまった。
example_sentences.english: A week unfortunately passed without an idea coming to mind like I hoped it would.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強がおもうようにできず、日本語が上達しなかった。
example_sentences.english: Unable to study as I had hoped, my Japanese hasn't improved.

example_sentences.japanese: 一流のアスリートでも、いつもおもうようにプレーができるわけではありません。
example_sentences.english: Even top athletes can’t always play the way they hope to.

example_sentences.japanese: 生け花を綺麗にすることが難しくて、おもうようにできなかった。
example_sentences.english: Doing flower arrangement was difficult and I wasn't able to do it as I had hoped.

example_sentences.japanese: おもうように回転が掛けられるように、何度も卓球の練習をしました。
example_sentences.english: I practiced table tennis many times to be able to put a spin on the ball as I desired.

example_sentences.japanese: 安易に考えていたが、おもうような結果を出すにはもっと厳しい練習が必要らしい。
example_sentences.english: I was thinking it would be easy, but it looks like I need more strict training to get the result I hoped for.

general_translation: Then again, Just when I thought, No sooner than
formation: Verb［た］(1) + かと思（おも）ったら(2)［い］Adjective + かと思（おも）ったら(2)［な］Adjective + かと思（おも）ったら(2)Noun + かと思（おも）ったら(2)(1) Verb［る］(2) かと思（おも）うと、かと思（おも）えば
casual_structure: Verb［た］(1) + かと思（おも）ったら(2)［い］Adjective + かと思（おも）ったら(2)［な］Adjective + かと思（おも）ったら(2)Noun + かと思（おも）ったら(2)(1) Verb［る］(2) かと思（おも）うと、かと思（おも）えば
explanation: A hypothetical structure showing that when the uncertain thought of (A) arose, something conflicting with that thought occured.

example_sentences.japanese: ミスが続いたのであきれられたかとおもったら、そうでもなかった。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought they would grow disgusted of their continued mistakes, they didn't.

example_sentences.japanese: 何を言い出すかとおもったら、みんなの前で俺の悪口を言い出した。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought of something to say, he started bad-mouthing me in front of everyone.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんが泣き止んだかとおもったら、また大声で泣き始めた。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought the baby had stopped crying, he started to cry loudly again.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘が宿題を始めるのかとおもうと、パソコンを開いてユーチューブを見始めた。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought my daughter was going to start doing her homework, she opened the computer and started watching YouTube.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が転んだかとおもうと、立ち上がって走り出した。
example_sentences.english: No sooner than my kid fell down, she got up and started running. (just when (I) thought)

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんは冷たい人かとおもったら、ただ人見知りなだけだった。
example_sentences.english: No sooner than thinking that Tanaka-san is a cold person, I found out that he was just shy.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の試合が最後かとおもうと、悲しくなる。
example_sentences.english: Just when I remembered that today's game is the last one, I got sad.

example_sentences.japanese: 嫌がられるかとおもったら、あっさりＯＫしてくれた。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought they would hate it, they easily gave me the okay.

example_sentences.japanese: 暴れていたかとおもったら、やけに大人しくなることもある。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought that they were throwing a tantrum, they become extremely docile.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はあれだけ怒られて悲しんでいるかとおもったら、すぐに笑いだした。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought that he was sad because he got scolded, he started laughing.

example_sentences.japanese: 何を言い出すかとおもったら、コンビ解散の話だった。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought of something to say they were already talking about dissolving the duo.

example_sentences.japanese: 喧嘩をしていた彼女は、機嫌がよくなったかとおもったらすぐに悪くなった。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought that the fighting woman's mood had improved, it got worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事をし始めるかとおもうと携帯電話を触り始めた。
example_sentences.english: No sooner than work began, he started using his cell phone. (just when (I) thought)

example_sentences.japanese: 飽くまで譲らないタイプの人かとおもったら、かなり柔軟な人でした。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought he was the type of person who wouldn't surrender to the end, he turned out to be soft.

example_sentences.japanese: 意地悪な人かとおもったら、少し口が悪いだけでした。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought he was a malicious person, it turns out he just has a bit of a dirty mouth.

example_sentences.japanese: 感謝したかとおもったら、すぐに文句を言い出す人がいる。
example_sentences.english: There are people who, just when I thought they would say thank you, immediately start complaining.

example_sentences.japanese: 転んだかとおもったら、起き上がり、何事もなかったかのように歩き出した。
example_sentences.english: No sooner than he had fallen over, he got up and started walking as if nothing had happened. (just when (I) thought)

example_sentences.japanese: 厚かましい態度を取ったかとおもったら、急に優しい言葉をかけてきたりする。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought he had an impudent attitude, he suddenly used kind words with me.

example_sentences.japanese: 新人社員が入ってきたとおもったら、次の日には仕事を辞めていた。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought a new employee had joined us, he had quit by the next day.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子と息子の友達が喧嘩をしているとおもうと、友達とゲラゲラ笑いながらゲームをしていた。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought that my son and his friend were fighting, I heard him giggling while playing video games with his friend.

general_translation: I would appreciate it if, If you could, I would like to think that
formation: Verb［ば］+ と + 思（おも）う
casual_structure: Verb［ば］+ と + 思（おも）う
polite_structure: Verb［ば］+ と + 思（おも）います
explanation: An expression used when conveying one's wish or request, taking the other person into consideration.

example_sentences.japanese: 楽しい時間になればとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I would like to think that this will be a fun time.

example_sentences.japanese: タクシーでむかえればとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I would like to think that I can go by taxi.

example_sentences.japanese: 必要な書類をお持ちいただければありがたいと思います。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if you could bring the necessary documents.

example_sentences.japanese: 必要な書類をお持ちいただければと思います。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if you could bring the necessary documents.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の会議に契約書をお持ちいただければと思います。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if you could bring the contract to tomorrow's meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: ＦＡＸではなくメールでお送りできればと思います。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if you could send it over e-mail instead of faxing it.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は定時に帰れたらと思います。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if I could go home on time today.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の会議までに見積書をご準備いただければと存じます。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if you could prepare the quote before the meeting tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 司会：「では早速、紹介させていただければとおもいます。」
example_sentences.english: MC: 'And so moving on swiftly, I would appreciate it if you would allow me to introduce...'

example_sentences.japanese: １５時までに解散できればとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if we could finish up by 3 PM.

example_sentences.japanese: この中から選んでいただければとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if you could choose from among these.

example_sentences.japanese: 夕方には雨が降ってくれればとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I would like to think that it will rain in the evening.

example_sentences.japanese: 資料の右側をご覧いただければとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if you would look at the right side of the document.

example_sentences.japanese: 後からゆっくり来ていただければとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if you could come later at your convenience.

example_sentences.japanese: 当日は、ＺＯＯＭで面接ができればとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I would like to think that the interview could be conducted on Zoom on the day.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらをぜひお使いいただければとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if you would please use this.

example_sentences.japanese: 返答は、文書でいただければとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if I could receive the reply in writing.

example_sentences.japanese: 契約を延長させていただければとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if you would allow me to extend the contract.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日まとめて提出できればとおもいますので、よろしくお願いいたします。
example_sentences.english: I would appreciate it if I could submit them all tomorrow, so thank you for your understanding.

example_sentences.japanese: 客：「チェックインに間に合いません。」ホテル：「お気をつけてお越しいただければとおもいます。」
example_sentences.english: Guest: 'I won't make it in time for check-in.' Hotel: 'We would appreciate it if you could make your way here safely.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小池：「今日から仲間に入ります、小池と申します。ぜひ仲良くしていただければとおもいます。」
example_sentences.english: Koike: 'My name is Koike, and I'll be joining you from today. I would appreciate it if you would get along well with me.'

grammar_point: と言（い）うものでもない
general_translation: There is no guarantee that…, Not necessarily
formation: Verb + というものではない(1)［な］Adjective + というものではない(1)［い］Adjective + というものではない(1)Noun + というものではない(1)(1) でもない、じゃない
casual_structure: Verb + というものではない(1)［な］Adjective + というものではない(1)［い］Adjective + というものではない(1)Noun + というものではない(1)(1) でもない、じゃない
polite_structure: Verb + というものではありません(1)［な］Adjective + というものではありません(1)［い］Adjective + というものではありません(1)Noun + というものではありません(1)(1) でもありません、じゃありません
explanation: A strong phrase showing that even that which is called (A) may not be the case. Often meaning there is no guarantee that (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 愛があれば結婚できるというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: It is not necessarily true that you are able to get married if you love each other.

example_sentences.japanese: いい大学を出たからと言って、いい会社に入社できるというものではない。
example_sentences.english: There is no guarantee that you will get into a good company just because you graduated from a good university.

example_sentences.japanese: 洋服は高ければいいというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: It is not necessarily true that clothes are better if they are expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: アプリの機能は多ければ多いほど便利だというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: The more features the better is not necessarily true when it comes to apps.

example_sentences.japanese: あのブランドが人気だからと言って、あのブランドの商品がいいものだというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: There is no guarantee that that brand's products are good just because they are popular.

example_sentences.japanese: スマートに見える人が皆痩せているというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: There is no guarantee that everyone who looks slim is actually thin.

example_sentences.japanese: 車は高ければ高いほどいいというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: The more expensive the better is not necessarily true when it comes to cars.

example_sentences.japanese: 漫才は、素人だからといってできないというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: Just because you're a novice, it's not necessarily true that you can't do comic dialogue.

example_sentences.japanese: 図鑑にはすべての生き物が載っているというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: There is no guarantee that all living animals are listed in the field guide.

example_sentences.japanese: 動機が純粋であれば何をやってもいいというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: It is not necessarily okay to do anything as long as your motives are pure.

example_sentences.japanese: 末っ子はみんなおっとりしているというものでもない。例外もある。
example_sentences.english: There is no guarantee that the youngest child will be calm and gentle. There are exceptions.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい警報器を設置しても、泥棒を防げるというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: Even if you install the new alarm system, there is no guarantee it will protect you from a burglar.

example_sentences.japanese: 将棋は、強い人が絶対に勝つというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: In shogi, there is no guarantee strong players will win for sure.

example_sentences.japanese: 消極的な意見はまったく役に立たないというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: It is not necessarily true that negative opinions are completely unhelpful.

example_sentences.japanese: 小さい商店だからといって、売り上げが悪いというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: It is not necessarily true that just because it is a small shop, that it has bad sales.

example_sentences.japanese: 消毒したからといって、絶対にインフルエンザにかからないというものでもない。
example_sentences.english: Just because you sterilized everything, there is no guarantee that you won't catch the flu.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語が上手であれば日本語の勉強をし続けなくてもいいと言うものではない。
example_sentences.english: It is not necessarily true that you should stop studying Japanese, just because you are good at it.

example_sentences.japanese: プレゼントは高額であればいいと言うものではない。
example_sentences.english: It is not necessarily true that a gift is better the more expensive they are.

general_translation: Can be considered as, Is thought to be, One can think that, It is conceivable that
formation: Phrase + と考（かんが）えられる
casual_structure: Phrase + と考（かんが）えられる
polite_structure: Phrase + と考（かんが）えられます
explanation: A grammar point highlighting (A) as something that can be considered, or as widely accepted as being conceivable.

example_sentences.japanese: 衆議院、いよいよ解散するとかんがえられる。
example_sentences.english: It is thought that the lower house of representatives will finally dissolve.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語は文字種が多いことから、第二言語として習うのが難しいとかんがえられる。
example_sentences.english: It is thought that Japanese is difficult to learn as a second language due to having several different character types.

example_sentences.japanese: 私には彼がこの事件の犯人だとおもわれる。
example_sentences.english: It seems to me that he is the one responsible for this incident.

example_sentences.japanese: 私にはあなたが悪いとおもわれる。
example_sentences.english: It seems to me that you are in the wrong.

example_sentences.japanese: あの事故は煽り運転のせいだとかんがえられる。
example_sentences.english: Tailgating is thought to be the cause of this accident.

example_sentences.japanese: あの子の親は育児放棄しているとかんがえられる。
example_sentences.english: It is thought that that child's parents are neglecting the child.

example_sentences.japanese: あの政策なら、一定の支持が得られるとかんがえられる。
example_sentences.english: If it is that policy, it is conceivable that we would receive standardized support.

example_sentences.japanese: 安易に決定したとかんがえられるが、もしかしたら作戦かもしれません。
example_sentences.english: It is thought that the decision made was to be easy-going, but it might just be a tactic.

example_sentences.japanese: そのプロジェクト、一旦白紙に戻すということもかんがえられませんか？
example_sentences.english: Is it conceivable that you would think of wiping the slate clean on that project? (won't you?)

example_sentences.japanese: この形からすると、何かの入れ物だとかんがえられますが、謎ですね。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the shape, one can think that you put something in this, but it is a mystery.

example_sentences.japanese: あの部屋は薄暗いとかんがえられる。懐中電灯を持って行こう。
example_sentences.english: That room can be considered dim. I will (let's) bring a flashlight.

example_sentences.japanese: 光の性質は、実は粒子と波動の両方だとかんがえられる。
example_sentences.english: The nature of light is actually thought to be both a particle and a wave.

example_sentences.japanese: 中国は経済成長が続いていけば新たな超大国となるとかんがえられる。
example_sentences.english: China may well be considered the new superpower if it maintains its current economic growth.

example_sentences.japanese: すぐに新しい物を欲しがるのは、子供を甘やかして何でも買ってあげていたことが原因だとかんがえられる。
example_sentences.english: It is thought that children immediately desiring new things is caused by parents spoiling them and buying them whatever they want.

example_sentences.japanese: 動物性脂肪を摂ることは癌などの病気になる一因とかんがえられるが、果たしてそうでしょうか？
example_sentences.english: The consumption of animal fats is thought to be one of the causes of cancer and other conditions. But is it really so?

example_sentences.japanese: 糖分が豊富な食品をあまりに摂ることは２型糖尿病などの病気になる一因とかんがえられる。
example_sentences.english: The excessive intake of products rich in sugar is thought to be one of the causes of getting Type 2 diabetes and similar conditions.

grammar_point: と言（い）う点（てん）から考（かんが）えると
general_translation: From the standpoint of, From the perspective of, From the viewpoint of, Think in terms of, Viewed from the angle of
formation: Noun + の点（てん）から考（かんが）えるとNoun + という点（てん）から考（かんが）えるとVerb + という点（てん）から考（かんが）えるとその(1) + 点（てん）から考（かんが）えると(1) そうした、そういう
casual_structure: Noun + の点（てん）から考（かんが）えるとNoun + という点（てん）から考（かんが）えるとVerb + という点（てん）から考（かんが）えるとその(1) + 点（てん）から考（かんが）えると(1) そうした、そういう
explanation: A hypothetical phrase which shows that something is being considered from the point or aspect of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: もし、うまくいくとしても製造のコストのてんからかんがえるとまだ非効率である。
example_sentences.english: Even if we assume it will work, if one thinks in terms of production costs it is still inefficient.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本のデジタル化が遅れているというてんからかんがえると、デジタル人材の育成やデジタルインフラの整備に力を入れなければ日本のデジタル化はどんどん遅れていくだろう。
example_sentences.english: If we think in terms of Japan's digitalization lagging behind, if Japan doesn't focus on improving their digital workforce and infrastructure, it's digitalization will fall further and further behind.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の教育というてんからかんがえると、楽しく勉強をさせる事が重要です。
example_sentences.english: From the standpoint of educating children, it is important to make learning fun.

example_sentences.japanese: 健康のてんからかんがえると休む時はちゃんと休まなければ身体を壊す可能性が高まります。
example_sentences.english: From the standpoint of health, if you don't rest when you need to rest, the possibility of physical damage increases.

example_sentences.japanese: エンドユーザーの便利さというてんからかんがえるとそれはむしろ不便である。
example_sentences.english: If we think in terms of end user convenience, that might actually be inconvenient.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事の効率のてんからかんがえると１時間に５分の休憩を取る方がいい。
example_sentences.english: If we think in terms of work efficiency, it is better to take a 5 minute break every hour.

example_sentences.japanese: ビジネスというてんからかんがえると需要が高いということは高い利益の可能性があるということだ。
example_sentences.english: If we think in terms of business, high demand means a high probability of profit.

example_sentences.japanese: 健康のてんからかんがえると砂糖の多い食べ物を食すればするほど肥満の可能性が高くなる。
example_sentences.english: If we think in terms of health, the more sugary food you consume, the higher the chance of obesity.

example_sentences.japanese: さらに、子供向けの製品の開発というてんからかんがえると違ったアプローチが必要です。
example_sentences.english: Moreover, if one thinks in terms of the development of a product for children, a different approach is needed.

example_sentences.japanese: クライアントのてんからかんがえると値段が安い事は、ファストフードのレストランが人気になった主な理由の一つである。
example_sentences.english: If one thinks from the client's standpoint, then one of the main reasons why fast food restaurants have become popular is that they are cheap.

example_sentences.japanese: ハイテク企業というてんからかんがえると、利益創出のためのイノベーションが何よりも重要だ。
example_sentences.english: If we think in terms of a high-tech company, innovation in order to generate profit is more important than anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の教師は１週間に働く時間のてんからかんがえると部活動などにより世界で一番忙しい。
example_sentences.english: If we think in terms of hours worked per week, Japanese teachers are the busiest in the world due to club activities and the like.

example_sentences.japanese: お客様の個人情報を安全に扱うというてんからかんがえるとデータが暗号化されなければ、システムは完璧に安全ではない。
example_sentences.english: If we think in terms of safely managing guests' personal data, unless data is encrypted, the system won't be completely safe.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいスマートフォンを買うときに必要な要素を「 バッテリ寿命」「画面の種類」「値段」の３てんからかんがえると、やはりこのブランドのモデルは一番だろう。
example_sentences.english: If one thinks in terms of the three factors required at the time of buying a new smartphone, 'battery life', 'screen resolution', and 'price', then as expected the models of this brand are the best.

example_sentences.japanese: 今やワードプロセッサはドキュメントのすべてのエラーを自動的に直すことができると言われている。そうしたてんからかんがえると正しいスペルや文法を学ぶことが必要はないと見える。しかし…
example_sentences.english: It is said that nowadays, word processors can automatically fix all errors in documents. From such a perspective it seems that there is no need to learn proper spelling or grammar. However…

general_translation: That means, That is to say
formation: Phrase + ということは + Phrase
casual_structure: Phrase + ということは + Phrase
explanation: An expression which explains that which is (A), or that which is called (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 末っ子ということは、本当は甘えん坊なんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Is it not to say that the youngest child is really spoiled?

example_sentences.japanese: あの有名なＩＴ企業で働いているということは、結構いい大学を出たってこと？
example_sentences.english: You work at a very famous IT company. That means that you graduated from a pretty good university, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女から返事が来ないということは、今は忙しいということだろう。
example_sentences.english: The fact that she hasn't responded to me means that she is probably busy at the moment.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を上手に話せるということは、日本に長い間住んでいたということですか。
example_sentences.english: You can speak Japanese well. Does that mean that you have lived in Japan for a long time?

example_sentences.japanese: もう仕事終わったの？ということは、今日こそは一緒に晩御飯が食べれるということだね！
example_sentences.english: You are already done with work!? That means that we can finally eat dinner together today!

example_sentences.japanese: 妊娠したの！？ということは、私はおばあちゃんになるってこと？！
example_sentences.english: You are pregnant!? Does that mean that I am going to be a grandma?!

example_sentences.japanese: ステージに立つということは、誰にでもできることではないと思います。
example_sentences.english: I do not think that standing on a stage means that anybody can do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 素直であるということは、君の表情からも分かります。
example_sentences.english: You are docile. That is to say, I know this just from your facial expressions.

example_sentences.japanese: ここに隙間があるということは、欠陥住宅の疑いがある。
example_sentences.english: There is a crack here, that is to say I am suspicious of this residence being defective.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が一人で旅に行くということは、大人になったということだ。
example_sentences.english: He is going on a trip by himself. That is to say, he has become an adult.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は祝日です。ということは、あのスーパーは閉まっていますか？
example_sentences.english: Today is a national holiday. Does that mean that that supermarket is closed?

example_sentences.japanese: 自分で炊事するようになったということは、奥さん出て行ったの？
example_sentences.english: You are now able to do your own cooking. Is that to say that your wife left you?

example_sentences.japanese: その机はＩＫＥＡで買ったの？ということは、自分で組み立てたの？
example_sentences.english: Did you buy that desk at IKEA? Does that mean that you put it together yourself?

example_sentences.japanese: 血液がドロドロということは、水分が足りないということかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: My blood is syrupy. That probably means that I am not getting enough water.

example_sentences.japanese: 水曜は休みだ。ということは、大谷が出る試合がリアルタイムで観れる。
example_sentences.english: Wednesday is my day off. That is to say I can watch the game that Ohtani is playing in in real time!

example_sentences.japanese: スマートであるということは、普段から何かしら気をつけているということでしょう。
example_sentences.english: You are someone of style. That is to say, you are generally careful about something or another, aren't you.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べ物の好き嫌いが多いということは、人の好き嫌いとも関係があるという説もある。
example_sentences.english: If you have many likes and dislikes corresponding to food, that means it is related to your overall likes and dislikes. (that is to say)

general_translation: ~ way, In a way that suggests, Like ~
formation: こんな(1) + ふうに + Phrase Verb + ふうに + PhraseVerb + ふう +  ではない(1) そんな、あんな、どんな
casual_structure: こんな(1) + ふうに + Phrase Verb + ふうに + PhraseVerb + ふう +  ではない(1) そんな、あんな、どんな
explanation: A common phrase used to highlight that something is in the style or has the air of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: いつか自分もこんなふうになりたい。
example_sentences.english: At some point, I too want to become like this (way).

example_sentences.japanese: あんなふうには絶対なりたくない。
example_sentences.english: I never want to be like that.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は仕事をやっているふうに見えるけど、ただそう見えるだけで、何もしていない。
example_sentences.english: He looks like he is doing his job, but it just looks like it and he isn't actually doing anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩には頑張っているふうには見えないかもしれないけど、これでもめちゃくちゃ頑張っているんです。
example_sentences.english: Senpai, it may not look like I'm working hard, but this is me trying my hardest.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなふうに結んだらすぐ解けちゃうよ。
example_sentences.english: If you tie a knot like this, it will get undone easily.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなふうに私をみないでよ。私は本当に何もやってないから！
example_sentences.english: Don't look at me like that. I really didn't do anything!

example_sentences.japanese: どんなふうにやればいいのか分からない。
example_sentences.english: I don't know in what way doing it would be good. (I don't know how to do it)

example_sentences.japanese: どうすればあんなふうになれるのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder what it would take to (what if done would) be able to become that way.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄はすぐに嘘をつく。僕はそんなふうにはなりたくない。
example_sentences.english: My older brother will instantly lie. I don't want to become like that (way).

example_sentences.japanese: 聞いていないふうに振舞っているが、本当は聞いている。
example_sentences.english: He acts in a way that suggests he isn't listening, but he really is listening.

example_sentences.japanese: あの態度は、昇進を考えているふうには見えない。
example_sentences.english: With that attitude, (he) doesn't appear to be thinking about a promotion. (In that way)

example_sentences.japanese: 見ているふうではなかったが、彼はよく見ているタイプです。
example_sentences.english: He didn't act in a way that suggested that he was looking, but he's the type who watches closely.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はお金がないふうに見えるが、大富豪です。
example_sentences.english: He looks like he doesn't have money, but he is extremely rich. (In a way that suggests)

example_sentences.japanese: 知らないふうにしていたが、顔に出てバレてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I was acting in a way that suggested I didn't know, but it accidentally showed on my face.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は日本語が喋れないふうにしているが、実はペラペラだ。
example_sentences.english: He acts in a way that suggests he can't speak Japanese, but he is actually fluent.

example_sentences.japanese: 飛べないふうに見える鶏の中にも、かなり飛べるものもいる。
example_sentences.english: Even among the chickens that look like (in a way that suggests) they cannot fly, there are ones that can fly well.

example_sentences.japanese: 思ってもいないのに、好きだと思っているふうに装うのは不誠実だ。
example_sentences.english: Pretending in a way that suggests you think you like it, even though you really don't, is insincere.

general_translation: As if to say, As if to suggest that, In such a way that, Things like
formation: Verb + というふうに + Phrase(Topic)は(Method) + というふうに + Phrase
casual_structure: Verb + というふうに + Phrase(Topic)は(Method) + というふうに + Phrase
explanation: A structure meaning that something is being said in the way or wind of (A). As if to say (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 父：「母に、遅れるだろうというふうに言って。」
example_sentences.english: Father: 'Tell mom in such a way as to suggest that I will be late.'

example_sentences.japanese: 私は今まで自分が一番仕事ができる人だというふうに思っていた。
example_sentences.english: Until recently, I always thought in such a way as to suggest that I was the most capable person when it comes to work.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はデザイン、僕はプログラミング、というふうに役割を分けてアプリを開発することにした。
example_sentences.english: We decided to develop the application by dividing the roles in the following way: he would do the design and I would do the programming.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は昼休憩に帰るというふうに聞いています。
example_sentences.english: I heard something as if to suggest that she is going to go home during lunch break.

example_sentences.japanese: 鈴木さんはこの試験に命がかかっているというふうに勉強をした。
example_sentences.english: Suzuki-san studied as if to suggest that his life depended on this exam.

example_sentences.japanese: 秘書が仕事を辞めるというふうに聞いていた。
example_sentences.english: I heard something as if to suggest that the secretary decided to quit.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は命がかかってるというふうに走っていた。
example_sentences.english: She was running in a way that suggested her life depended on it.

example_sentences.japanese: 入団してすぐに活躍というふうになかなかいかない。
example_sentences.english: It is quite difficult to do things like activities immediately after enrolling.

example_sentences.japanese: 合格は堅いというふうに言われても、やっぱり不安です。
example_sentences.english: Even if I am told in such a way that suggests that passing is a given, I am still uneasy.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度の転勤、「関東」というふうにはいかないだろうな。
example_sentences.english: With this job transfer, I am wondering if it is to say that I won't be going to 'Kanto'.

example_sentences.japanese: 「これは仮定の話です」というふうに言われても、あまりにもリアルすぎる。
example_sentences.english: Even if I was told in such a way that suggested 'this is just a hypothetical conversation,' it is just too real.

example_sentences.japanese: わざとではないけど、「勘違い」というふうには思ってもらえないだろうな。
example_sentences.english: It wasn't on purpose, but I wonder if we can't get them to think that it was something like a 'misunderstanding'.

example_sentences.japanese: 過剰包装というふうに言われるが、これにはこだわりがある。
example_sentences.english: I was told in such a way that I overdo it when it comes to wrapping, but it is something that I am picky about.

example_sentences.japanese: 刑事：「武さんはその事故のことを知っていたというふうに私を見ていた。」
example_sentences.english: Detective: He looked at me as if to suggest that he knew some circumstances of that accident.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は掃除、母は晩御飯、父は暖炉に火を付ける、というふうにみんなが客の来訪のために、準備した。
example_sentences.english: We all prepared for a guest visit, in the following ways: I cleaned, mom made dinner, and dad fired up the fireplace.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は科学、武は人文科学、というふうにそれぞれが自分の好きな科目を専攻することにしました。
example_sentences.english: Each of us decided to major in our favorite school subjects in the following way: Me - science, Takeshi - humanities.

general_translation: Although, But, Even Though
formation: Verb + ものの +  Phrase［い］Adjective + ものの +  Phrase［な］Adjective + な(2) + ものの +  PhraseNoun + ではある(1) + ものの +  Phrase(1) である、であった(2) だった、ではある、であった
casual_structure: Verb + ものの +  Phrase［い］Adjective + ものの +  Phrase［な］Adjective + な(2) + ものの +  PhraseNoun + ではある(1) + ものの +  Phrase(1) である、であった(2) だった、ではある、であった
explanation: A formal conjunction particle used for highlighting that although (A), (B). (B) opposes or contradicts (A).

example_sentences.japanese: ＡとＢを組み合わせてみたものの、ほとんど味が変わらないな。
example_sentences.english: Although I tried combining A and B, it tastes almost the same.

example_sentences.japanese: マッチングアプリで出会った人とデートに行ったものの、共通点が何もなかったのでまた会うことはないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Although I went on a date with someone I met on a matching app, we had nothing in common, so I doubt we will meet again.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の仕事の給料は高いものの、家族と過ごせる時間が少ないから転職を考えている。
example_sentences.english: Although my current job pays well, I am considering changing jobs because I don't have much time to spend with my family.

example_sentences.japanese: あのお店が出す商品はユニークではあるものの、高すぎるので手が出せない。
example_sentences.english: Although the products offered by that store are unique, they are too expensive for me to afford.

example_sentences.japanese: 伊藤先生は英語の先生ではあるものの、日常的な英語は話せないそうだ。
example_sentences.english: Even though Ms. Ito is an English teacher, I have heard that she doesn't speak everyday English.

example_sentences.japanese: 工夫してみたものの、結果は大して変わらない。
example_sentences.english: Even though I tried solving (the problem), there won't be any significant change.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分で組み立ててみたものの、見栄えが悪すぎる。
example_sentences.english: Even though I built it myself, it has absolutely no charm.

example_sentences.japanese: クーラーを最大にしてみたものの、全然涼しくならない。
example_sentences.english: Even though I got the largest air conditioner, (the room) doesn't get cool at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 口紅をつけてみたものの、全然女性らしく見えないのはなぜ？
example_sentences.english: Although I put on lipstick, I don't look ladylike at all. Why!?

example_sentences.japanese: 高価な毛皮をいただいたものの、わたしには全然似合いません。
example_sentences.english: I received some expensive furs, but they do not suit me at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 競馬に行ってみたものの、ハマるのが恐くて馬券を買えなかった。
example_sentences.english: I went to a horse race, but the fear of getting addicted was so great that I could not buy a ticket.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年ようやく運転免許の試験を受けてみたものの、めったに運転しない。
example_sentences.english: Although I finally tried taking my driving test this year, I rarely drive.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のころはずっと医者になりたいと言っていたものの、本当になることは期待していなかった。
example_sentences.english: Although I constantly said 'I want to become a doctor' during my childhood, I never expected to actually become one.

example_sentences.japanese: 由美子先生は経済の専門家ではあるものの、学校以外の仕事をしたことがない。
example_sentences.english: Although professor Yumiko is an expert in economics, she has never worked outside of the university.

example_sentences.japanese: 金魚が好きだとは言ってみたものの、本当にプレゼントされたら少し困る。
example_sentences.english: Although I said I like goldfish, if I actually received one as a present I wouldn't be thrilled.

example_sentences.japanese: 「そんな意見はくだらない」と強がってみたものの、他のアイデアが思い浮かびません。
example_sentences.english: Even though I pretended to be tough and said 'Your opinions are preposterous,' I cannot think of any other ideas.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はいろんな楽器を演奏できるものの、楽譜は読めないらしい。
example_sentences.english: Although she can play a lot of instruments, I heard that she can't read music.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は日本語を勉強しているものの、韓国語も勉強している。
example_sentences.english: Although he is studying Japanese, he is also studying Korean.

general_translation: Speaker's impression, Criticism or conclusion
formation: Phrase  + というものだ
casual_structure: Phrase  + というものだ
polite_structure: Phrase  + というものです
explanation: A strong phrase that draws a conclusion about or criticizes the thing which can be called (A).

example_sentences.japanese: その言い分はわがままというものだ。
example_sentences.english: My impression is that your complaint is selfish.

example_sentences.japanese: 何があってもお互い助け合うのが友達というものだ。
example_sentences.english: Helping each other no matter what is just what friends do.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩が着く１０分前に着く。それがマナーというものだ。
example_sentences.english: Arriving 10 minutes before your senpai arrives. That is just manners.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに疲れていても諦めない。それがアスリートというものだ。
example_sentences.english: Not giving up no matter how tired you are. That is my impression of an athlete.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの好き嫌いは食わず嫌いというものだ。
example_sentences.english: My impression is that your likes and dislikes are prejudiced (dislike without trying).

example_sentences.japanese: 嘘はつかない。それがジャーナリストというものだ。
example_sentences.english: Not telling lies. That is my impression of what a journalist is.

example_sentences.japanese: 楽しくないと意味がない。それがサークルというものだ。
example_sentences.english: If it isn't fun, it is pointless. That is my impression of club sports.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも結果を出す。あれが実力というものだ。
example_sentences.english: He always gets results. That is my impression of competency.

example_sentences.japanese: すぐには忘れられないのが失恋というものだ。
example_sentences.english: Being unable to instantly forget about it is my impression of a broken heart.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰よりも汗をかく。それが主役というものだ。
example_sentences.english: To sweat more than everyone else. That is my impression of what being a leading role is.

example_sentences.japanese: 時には残酷な結果になることもある。それが勝負というものだ。
example_sentences.english: Sometimes encountering a terrible outcome. That is my impression of a contest (victory or defeat).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が知らない真実を話すことが、親切というものだ。
example_sentences.english: My impression is that it is kind to talk to him about truths he does not know.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日少しずつしか進まない。それが撮影というものだ。
example_sentences.english: I can only progress a little each day. That is my impression of what photography is.

example_sentences.japanese: どんな困難にも立ち向かおうとするのが職人というものだ。
example_sentences.english: My impression of a craftsman is someone who stands and faces any hardship.

example_sentences.japanese: 嫌な仕事もあるが、給料は安定しているのがサラリーマンというものだ。
example_sentences.english: My impression of being a salaryman is that you have a job that you hate, but your salary is steady.

example_sentences.japanese: 何があっても泣かない。それが男ってものだ！
example_sentences.english: Not crying no matter what. That is my impression of a man!

general_translation: From the point of view of, By the look of
formation: Noun + から見（み）るとNoun + から見（み）ればNoun + から見（み）て Noun + から見（み）たら
casual_structure: Noun + から見（み）るとNoun + から見（み）ればNoun + から見（み）て Noun + から見（み）たら
explanation: A hypothetical expression that points out how something looks from the perspective of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 外からみると、やりやすそうです。
example_sentences.english: From an outside point of view it looks easy.

example_sentences.japanese: アニメに興味がない人からみると、どのアニメも同じに見える。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of someone who is not interested in anime, all anime looks the same.

example_sentences.japanese: 外からみたら、私のコレクションはゴミに見えるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: From an outside point of view, my collection probably just looks like garbage.

example_sentences.japanese: 私からみれば、彼女はあまり美人じゃない。
example_sentences.english: From my point of view, she is not that much of a stunner.

example_sentences.japanese: このタイヤ跡の大きさからみて、犯人はトラックを使ったに違いない。
example_sentences.english: By the looks of the size of these tire tracks, the perpetrator must have used a truck.

example_sentences.japanese: 老人夫婦からみると、若者の恋愛は懐かしい。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of elderly couples, young love is nostalgic.

example_sentences.japanese: 例年からみて、今年は稀な気象が多かった。
example_sentences.english: From the view point of what is normal, there were a lot of rare weather phenomena this year.

example_sentences.japanese: 脇役からみると主役は羨ましいが、主役は主役で大変らしい。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of a supporting role, the lead part is enviable, however the lead role looks very tough.

example_sentences.japanese: 小学生からみると中高生は大人に見えるが、実際はそうでもない。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of an elementary schooler, junior and senior high schoolers look like adults, but that is not really the case.

example_sentences.japanese: 高級な食器だと思っていたのに、専門家からみると大したことないようです。
example_sentences.english: Even though I thought it was expensive tableware, from the point of view of a specialist, it seems like it isn't that big of a deal.

example_sentences.japanese: 素人からみるとかなりうまい人でも、プロの世界では全然通用しないらしい。
example_sentences.english: It seems that even people who are considerably skilled from a layperson's point of view would not get by in the pro world.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国人からみると日本語が上手な人でも、日本人からするとアクセントの違いが気になってしまう。
example_sentences.english: Even if a person seems proficient in Japanese from a foreigner's point of view, a Japanese person will notice a different accent.

example_sentences.japanese: 一般庶民からみると芸能人は憧れの職業だが、結構大変な仕事らしい。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of the general public, having a job as an entertainer is longed for, however it apparently is rather tough work.

example_sentences.japanese: 知らない人からみるとただ暴れているようにしか見えないが、あれは民族の正式な踊りです。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of a person who doesn't know, it looks like nothing more than someone flailing about, but that is a formal ethnic dance.

example_sentences.japanese: 相撲を知らない人からみると力士たちは太りすぎだと思うかもしれないが、彼らはアスリートです。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of people who don't know sumo, they probably think that the wrestlers are too fat, but they are athletes.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供はテレビゲームが大好きだが、大人からみると何が楽しいのかよく分からないゲームも多い。
example_sentences.english: Children love video games, but from the point of view of an adult, there are a lot of games that are hard to understand the appeal.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人の喋り方から見ると、あの人は日本人ではないだろう。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of how they speak, that person probably isn't Japanese. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Judging from, Seeing that
formation: Verb + ところを見（み）ると
casual_structure: Verb + ところを見（み）ると
explanation: A hypothetical construction that looks at the place or situation of (A), before making a judgement about it.

example_sentences.japanese: 香水をつけているところをみると、お出掛けですね？
example_sentences.english: Seeing that you are wearing perfume, are you going out?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼がニコニコしているところをみると、テストに合格したに違いない。
example_sentences.english: Seeing that he is smiling, I have no doubt that he passed the test.

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字を綺麗に書けるところをみると、彼は長い間漢字を勉強しているのかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the fact that he can write kanji very nicely, he probably has been studying kanji for a long time.

example_sentences.japanese: 怒られていてもずっと携帯を見ているところをみると、彼は全然反省していないんだろう。
example_sentences.english: Seeing that he is looking at his phone despite being scolded, he probably doesn't feel any remorse.

example_sentences.japanese: 心当たりがないところをみると、誤解かもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Seeing that you have no clue, it is probably a misunderstanding.

example_sentences.japanese: このタイミングで交替したところをみると、あのピッチャーは怪我をしたのかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the timing of the change, that pitcher was probably injured.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が落ち込んでいるところをみると、恋人に振られたのかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the fact that he is sullen, he was probably dumped by his lover.

example_sentences.japanese: 焦がしたところをみると、彼女は料理が苦手なのでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Seeing that she burned it, she is not that great at cooking, is she?

example_sentences.japanese: あの意見を肯定したところをみると、彼らは裏で繋がっているのかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Seeing that he backed that opinion, they are probably connected with each other behind the scenes.

example_sentences.japanese: ついにあの情報を公表したところをみると、切羽詰まっているのかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: Seeing that they finally published that information, they were probably under pressure.

example_sentences.japanese: 一軍に合流したところをみると、調子が上がってきたのでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Seeing that you joined the starting players, you have been getting better, haven't you?

example_sentences.japanese: 献立が急に代わったところをみると、何かトラブルがあったのだろう。
example_sentences.english: Seeing that they suddenly changed the menu, I wonder if there was some sort of trouble.

example_sentences.japanese: 英語を流暢に話すところをみると、彼女は帰国子女かもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the fact that she speaks English fluently, she probably lived abroad when she was young.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が反論しないところをみると、嘘をついていると私は確信した。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the fact that she did not deny it, I am convinced that she is lying.

example_sentences.japanese: 言葉遣いが悪かったところをみると、あまり良い仲間と付き合っていないのかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Judging from your poor use of language, you probably don't have any good friends.

general_translation: Judging from, Considering
formation: Noun + からするとNoun + からすれば
casual_structure: Noun + からするとNoun + からすれば
explanation: A hypothetical expression used to cast judgements that go off from the previous statement.

example_sentences.japanese: あの煙突からすると、たぶん薪ストーブですね。
example_sentences.english: Judging from that chimney, maybe it is a wood stove.

example_sentences.japanese: この成績からすると、あなたは全然勉強をしていないでしょう？
example_sentences.english: Judging from these grades, you didn't study at all, did you?

example_sentences.japanese: この甘さからすると、塩と間違えて砂糖を入れてしまったに違いない。
example_sentences.english: Judging from how sweet this is, they must've mistakenly added sugar instead of salt.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本育ちの私からすれば、これは寿司ではない。
example_sentences.english: Going off being a person raised in Japan, this is not sushi.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の反応からすると、本当に驚いているようだ。
example_sentences.english: Going off her reaction, it seems like she is genuinely surprised.

example_sentences.japanese: 歴史からすると、京都はかつて首都でした。
example_sentences.english: Judging from history, Kyoto was once the capital.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが言っていることからすると、彼はそこにいなかったようですね。
example_sentences.english: Judging from what you are saying, it seems that he wasn't there right?

example_sentences.japanese: 足の速さからすると、彼はプロの選手になれるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Considering how fast he is, he can probably become a professional athlete.

example_sentences.japanese: あのアクセントからすると彼は日本人ではないようです。
example_sentences.english: Judging from his accent, it appears that he is not Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: あの手さばきからすると、あの人は編物のプロに違いない。
example_sentences.english: Judging from that handiwork, there is no doubt that that person is a knitting pro.

example_sentences.japanese: お辞儀の仕方からすると、彼は日本にいたことがあるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: Judging from how he bowed, he is sure to have been to Japan before.

example_sentences.japanese: 植木のかんじからすれば、かなり腕のいい植木職人が手入れをしているな。
example_sentences.english: Judging from my impression of these trees, a rather skilled gardener is tending to them.

example_sentences.japanese: あの写し方からすると、これは有名な写真家が撮ったものだと思います。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the way that it was taken, I think this was taken by a famous photographer.

example_sentences.japanese: この仕上がりからすれば、作成者は大雑把な性格ですね。
example_sentences.english: Judging from this finish, the author is someone who doesn't worry about details.

example_sentences.japanese: あの落ち着きからすれば学生には見えないけど、まだ彼らは中学生なんだって。
example_sentences.english: Judging from their composure, they don't look like students, but I heard they are still junior high schoolers.

example_sentences.japanese: あのウエイトレスの対応からすれば、この店は社員教育がしっかりしているのだろう。
example_sentences.english: Judging from my interactions with that waitress, this restaurant has a solid employee training program.

general_translation: Even..., Judging from, Based on
formation: Noun + からして
casual_structure: Noun + からして
explanation: A phrase used when the speaker goes from (A), before giving their preformed opinion about it.

example_sentences.japanese: このスープは匂いからして美味しそうだ。
example_sentences.english: Judging from this soup's smell, it seems delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の性格からして、彼と一緒に住むことは無理だろう。
example_sentences.english: Based on his personality, it is probably impossible for me to live with him.

example_sentences.japanese: 値段からして、このお店は新鮮な食材を使っているに違いない。
example_sentences.english: Based on the price, this restaurant must be using fresh ingredients.

example_sentences.japanese: このゲームは名前からしてつまらなそうだ。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the name, this game seems boring.

example_sentences.japanese: あの演奏からして、彼は楽器のプロだ。
example_sentences.english: Judging from that performance, he is a professional with that instrument.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の感覚からして、このスイカは甘いと思う。
example_sentences.english: Judging from my intuition, I think this watermelon is sweet.

example_sentences.japanese: あの看板からして、店の中もきっとオシャレなのだろう。
example_sentences.english: Judging from that signboard, surely the inside of that store is also fashionable.

example_sentences.japanese: 稽古の内容からして、あの先生は厳しそうだ。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the contents of their training, that teacher seems strict.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は服装からして若そうだが、実は５０歳だ。
example_sentences.english: Judging from her attire, she looks young, but actually, she is 50 years old.

example_sentences.japanese: カロリーからして、このお菓子を全部食べたら必ず太りますよ。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the calories, if you eat all of these snacks, you will definitely get fat.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなの感想からして、この商品は良いものだと思います。
example_sentences.english: Judging from everyone's impressions, I think that this is a good product.

example_sentences.japanese: 行列からして、あのラーメン屋は美味しいに違いない。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the line, there is no doubt that that ramen shop is delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の給料からして一軒家を買うことは難しいだろう。
example_sentences.english: Based on my salary, buying a house would be difficult, wouldn't it. (judging from)

example_sentences.japanese: 血圧からして、精密検査を受けた方がいいと思います。
example_sentences.english: Judging from your blood pressure, I think it would be better if you underwent a thorough examination.

example_sentences.japanese: 原料からして、あまり栄養がなさそうだと分かる。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the ingredients, it seems like it doesn't really have any nutritional value.

general_translation: Just because
formation: Verb + からといって［い］Adjective + からといって［な］Adjective + だからといってNoun + だからといって
casual_structure: Verb + からといって［い］Adjective + からといって［な］Adjective + だからといってNoun + だからといって
explanation: A construction implying that from what is said about (A), (B). Often used to criticize.

example_sentences.japanese: ご機嫌斜めだからといって、八つ当たりしないで。
example_sentences.english: Please don't burst out in anger, just because you are in a bad mood.

example_sentences.japanese: たくさん勉強をしたからといって、テストに合格するとは限らない。
example_sentences.english: Just because you studied a lot doesn't mean that you will pass the test.

example_sentences.japanese: 公園が広いからといって、犬の放し飼いをしてもいいと言うわけではない。
example_sentences.english: Just because the park is spacious doesn't mean that dogs are allowed off leash.

example_sentences.japanese: 丈夫だからといって、雑に扱えば必ず壊れます。
example_sentences.english: Just because it is sturdy, it will definitely break if you handle it roughly.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人だからといって、漢字を書けるとは限らない。
example_sentences.english: Just because someone is Japanese doesn't mean that they can write kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 丼物だからといって、安いとは限りません。
example_sentences.english: Just because it is 'donburi', doesn't confine it to being cheap.

example_sentences.japanese: 慰められたからといって、すぐに気持ちは晴れない。
example_sentences.english: Just because I was comforted, doesn't mean that my mood will immediately improve.

example_sentences.japanese: 懐かしいからといって、なんでもすぐに買うのはやめてください。
example_sentences.english: Please, stop buying stuff on a whim just because you find it nostalgic.

example_sentences.japanese: 憎いからといって、人を殺していいわけないでしょ。
example_sentences.english: Just because you hate the person, that isn't a reason for it to be okay to kill them.

example_sentences.japanese: トレーニングをしたからといって、必ず試合に勝てるわけではない。
example_sentences.english: Just because you trained, it doesn't mean that you are certain to win the match.

example_sentences.japanese: 日課だからといって、機械的にやっていては成長しません。
example_sentences.english: Just because it is daily routine, doing it mechanically, you will not improve.

example_sentences.japanese: 生意気だからといって、無下に扱うわけにはいかない。お客さんだから。
example_sentences.english: You can't afford to treat him coldly just because he is impertinent. He is a customer after all...

example_sentences.japanese: 貧しいからといって人を差別することはこの学校で禁止されている。
example_sentences.english: Discriminating against someone just because they are poor is against our school policy.

example_sentences.japanese: 入社できたからといって安心はできません。本番はこれからです。
example_sentences.english: Just because you were able to get into the company doesn't mean you can relax. The real work is from here on.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんはよく買い物に行き、安いからといって買いすぎてしまい、買った食べ物を腐らせている。
example_sentences.english: Dad often goes shopping, buys too much just because it is cheap, and the food ends up going spoiled.

example_sentences.japanese: 近頃の人は便利だからといって不健康なファストフードを食べてばかり、いいことはないと思います。
example_sentences.english: Recently people are only eating unhealthy fast-food just because it is convenient. I think that is not a good thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に２年間住んでいたからとて、日本語が話せるとは限らない。
example_sentences.english: Just because someone has lived in Japan for 2 years doesn't mean that they can speak Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑いからって、そんなに休憩ばかりしていたら仕事が進まないだろ。
example_sentences.english: If you keep taking so many breaks just because it's hot, you will never get your job done.

general_translation: Speaking of which, By the way, Come to think of it
formation: そういえば + Phrase
casual_structure: そういえば + Phrase
explanation: A hypothetical expression that indicates that being on the topic of (A) has instigated the topic or question of (B). If saying (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、今日は母の日だ。
example_sentences.english: Come to think of it, it is Mother's Day today.

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、この前借りた本読み終わったよ！めちゃくちゃ面白かった！
example_sentences.english: By the way, I finished reading the book I borrowed from you the other day! It was super interesting!

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、大家さんに家賃振り込んでくれた？
example_sentences.english: Speaking of which, did you transfer the rent to the landlord for me?

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、さっき駅でお母さんの友達に会ったよ。よろしくだって。
example_sentences.english: Speaking of which, I met your friend at the station. She told me to tell you she said hi.

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、昨夜は何時に家に帰ったの？
example_sentences.english: Speaking of which, what time did you get home last night?

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、着替え持ってきてくれた？
example_sentences.english: Speaking of which, did you bring the change of clothes for me?

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、昨日の卒業式はどうだった？
example_sentences.english: Speaking of which, how was the graduation ceremony yesterday?

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、客席に君のお父さんとお母さんがいたよ。
example_sentences.english: Speaking of which, your father and mother were in the guest seating!

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、お芝居の稽古は順調？
example_sentences.english: Speaking of which, is the play rehearsal going well?

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、蛍光灯が切れたから買わないといけません。
example_sentences.english: Speaking of which, the fluorescent light went out, so I have to buy one.

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、最近全然親孝行してないな...
example_sentences.english: Speaking of which, recently I haven't been treating my parents with filial piety at all...

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、今度コーラスやるんだけど、一緒にやりませんか？
example_sentences.english: Speaking of which, I will be singing in a chorus, won't you join me?

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、今度のイベントで機関車に乗れるみたいですよ。
example_sentences.english: Speaking of which, it looks like you can ride a locomotive at the upcoming event!

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、クリーニングに出していたのを忘れてた。取りに行かないと。
example_sentences.english: Speaking of which, I forgot that I had sent stuff to the cleaners. I have to go get it.

example_sentences.japanese: そういえば、今度金魚屋さんに行くんだけど、買ってきてあげようか？
example_sentences.english: Speaking of which, I am going to the goldfish shop. Shall I buy you one?

example_sentences.japanese:
中田さん： 今度バッティングセンターに行こ！
高橋さん：そういえば、藤田さんと伊藤くんが付き合い始めたって聞いた？
example_sentences.english:
Nakata-san: Let's go to the batting cage next time!
Takahashi-san: Speaking of which, did you hear that Fujita-san and Ito-kun has started dating? (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Please, Could you please
formation: お + Verb［stem］+ 願（ねが）うご + (Chinese Origin) Noun + 願（ねが）う(Western Origin) Noun + 願（ねが）う
casual_structure: お + Verb［stem］+ 願（ねが）うご + (Chinese Origin) Noun + 願（ねが）う(Western Origin) Noun + 願（ねが）う
polite_structure: お + Verb［stem］+ 願（ねが）いますご + (Chinese Origin) Noun + 願（ねが）います(Western Origin) Noun + 願（ねが）います
explanation: A polite phrase which emphasizes that the speaker wishes or is petitioning that someone do (A) for them.

example_sentences.japanese: 書類のこの下にサインねがいます。
example_sentences.english: Please sign at the bottom of the document.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらからのメールが届いているか、お確かめ願います。
example_sentences.english: Could you please make sure that you have received our email.

example_sentences.japanese: 鈴木社長はもうすぐ到着するので、もう少々お待ち願います。
example_sentences.english: President Suzuki will be arriving shortly, so please wait a moment.

example_sentences.japanese: この契約書にご記入された情報に間違いがないか、ご確認願います。
example_sentences.english: Please make sure that the information you have entered in this contract is correct.

example_sentences.japanese: 歩道での禁煙にご協力願います。
example_sentences.english: We kindly ask for your cooperation in not smoking on the sidewalks.

example_sentences.japanese: この契約書の下の方と、この書類の下の方にサインねがいます。
example_sentences.english: Please sign at the bottom of this contract and at the bottom of this document.

example_sentences.japanese: 問題が起こった場合はごれんらくねがいます。
example_sentences.english: If you have any problems, please feel free to contact us.

example_sentences.japanese: ここは図書館です。おしずかにねがいます。
example_sentences.english: This is a library. Please be quiet.

example_sentences.japanese: 一週間以内におへんじねがいます。
example_sentences.english: Please reply within one week's time.

example_sentences.japanese: この文章で間違いないか、ごかくにんねがいます。
example_sentences.english: Please check if there are any mistakes in this sentence.

example_sentences.japanese: ＰＤＦでごていしゅつねがいます。
example_sentences.english: Please submit (the document) as a PDF.

example_sentences.japanese: できる限り早めにごたいおうねがいます。
example_sentences.english: Please handle it as quickly as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: これが我が社の企画書です。ごけんとうねがいます。
example_sentences.english: This is our company's business proposal. Please give it your consideration.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻は体調が悪いので、ごはいりょねがいます。
example_sentences.english: My wife is ill, so please keep her in your thoughts.

example_sentences.japanese: 公共の場での禁酒にごきょうりょくねがいます。
example_sentences.english: We ask for your cooperation in not drinking in public places.

example_sentences.japanese: 面会をご希望の方は担当者が会議中ですので、待合室でおまちねがえますか？
example_sentences.english: Those who are here for a meeting, could you please wait in the waiting room? The person in charge is having a conference.

example_sentences.japanese: はっきりとは申し上げられません。おさっしねがいます。
example_sentences.english: I cannot say for certain. I ask that you please understand.

general_translation: Please do
formation: Verb［て］ + 頂戴（ちょうだい）
polite_structure: Verb［て］ + 頂戴（ちょうだい）
explanation: An expression often used to make a request, used frequently by family members.

example_sentences.japanese: むしろ先に答えをおしえてちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: Rather, please tell me the answer first.

example_sentences.japanese: おばあちゃんに、白菜を届けにいってきてちょうだい！
example_sentences.english: Please go and deliver the cabbage to Grandma!

example_sentences.japanese: お母さん、そこのリモコンを、とってちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: Mom, please pass the remote.

example_sentences.japanese: これ以上待ちたくないわ。店員さんに、あとどれくらいかきいてきてちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: I don’t wanna wait any longer than this. Please go ask the shop assistant how much longer it will take.

example_sentences.japanese: ついでに車の荷物をはこんできてちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: While you’re at it, please carry the luggage from the car.

example_sentences.japanese: お兄ちゃん、腕が痛いから、代わりにカバンをもってちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: Big brother, since my arm hurts, please carry the bag instead of me.

example_sentences.japanese: 今忙しいんだから、私にかまわないでちょうだい！
example_sentences.english: Since I’m busy right now, would you please stop bothering me!

example_sentences.japanese: 先方から返事が来たら、すぐにおしえてちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: When we receive a response from the client, please tell me right away.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議室の予約をしてちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: Please book the meeting room.

example_sentences.japanese: いいからおちついてちょうだい！私からすると、その姿が一番痛々しいわ。
example_sentences.english: Would you just calm down please! From where I’m standing, seeing you like that is the most cringeworthy.

example_sentences.japanese: 「私のために…世界をすくってちょうだい♡」と姫が仰せです。
example_sentences.english: ‘Please save the world…for my sake ♡’, orders the princess.

example_sentences.japanese: お願い！今日こそ目覚まし止めずにおきてちょうだい！３日連続で遅刻はクビよ！
example_sentences.english: Please! Today of all days, please get up without snoozing your alarm! If you’re late three days in a row you’ll be fired!

example_sentences.japanese: こちらのお料理を、ありがたくちょうだいいたします。
example_sentences.english: I will gratefully receive this meal.

example_sentences.japanese: ご意見はしっかりとちょうだいしましたので、今後に活かして参ります。
example_sentences.english: We have duly received your feedback and will endeavor to make use of it from hereon.

example_sentences.japanese: 本日はお忙しい中、貴重なお時間をちょうだいしまして、誠にありがとうございました。
example_sentences.english: We are truly grateful to receive some of your time out of your busy schedule today.

example_sentences.japanese: お兄ちゃん、ちょっとこれあけてちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: Hey big brother, can you please open this?

example_sentences.japanese: お父さん、コンビニ行くなら砂糖買ってきてちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: Husband, if you are going to the convenience store, can you get sugar?

example_sentences.japanese: これお姉ちゃんに渡してきてちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: Go hand this to your big sister.

example_sentences.japanese: グミちょうだい！
example_sentences.english: Gimme gummies!

example_sentences.japanese: 少しお時間を頂戴しますが、よろしいでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: We would need to take a moment of your time, but would that be okay?

example_sentences.japanese: こちらのお土産はありがたく頂戴いたします。
example_sentences.english: I will receive this souvenir with great thanks.

general_translation: I heard that… something like, They said ... or something
formation: Verb + とか［い］Adjective + とか［な］Adjective + とかNoun + とか
casual_structure: Verb + とか［い］Adjective + とか［な］Adjective + とかNoun + とか
explanation: A phrase which expresses uncertainty about something heard, by questioning a quote.

example_sentences.japanese: 納豆は体にいいんだとか。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Natto is good for your body or something like that.

example_sentences.japanese: 遠藤さんと近藤さんが結婚するとか。意外じゃない？
example_sentences.english: I heard that Endo-san and Kondo-san are getting married or something. Isn't that surprising?

example_sentences.japanese: あの大手家電メーカーが開発した最新のスマホはたくさんのブロートウェアがインストールされているせいで動作がものすごく重いとか。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the latest smartphone developed by that major appliance manufacturer performs extremely slow because of all the bloatware that comes installed, or something like that.

example_sentences.japanese: 高橋くんの彼女が美人だとか。あんなやつに美人な彼女ができたとは信じられないけどな。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Takahashi's girlfriend is beautiful or something. I can't believe that a guy like that could have a beautiful girlfriend, though.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は実はお金持ちだとか。
example_sentences.english: I heard that person is actually rich or something.

example_sentences.japanese: このワンピースは体型をカバーするとか。
example_sentences.english: I heard that this dress conceals your physique or something like that.

example_sentences.japanese: ＡＫＢ４８という音楽グループは解散するとか。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the music group called AKB48 is going to break up or something like that.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近はカラーサングラスが流行っているとか。
example_sentences.english: I heard that color sunglasses are popular recently or something like that.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんが朝ごはんを食べるのは大事だとか言っていた。
example_sentences.english: Mom was saying that eating breakfast is important or something like that.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生がテストの問題は難しくないとか言ってたけど本当かな？
example_sentences.english: The teacher was saying that the test questions weren't hard or something like that, but I wonder if it's true.

example_sentences.japanese: 鉄分が不足すると無駄に落ち込みやすくなったりするんだとか…。
example_sentences.english: It's said that if you have an iron deficiency, it's easy for you to get pointlessly depressed or something like that.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長は年末年始に温泉旅行に行ってらっしゃるとか。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the company president is going on a hot springs trip over New Years or something like that.

example_sentences.japanese: この計画は絶対成功するとか言ってたけどさ、そんな甘くないよね。
example_sentences.english: You were saying that this plan will definitely succeed or something like that, right? You're not really that naive are you?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は雨が降るんだとか。だったら、傘を持って行かないわけにはいかない。
