example_sentences.english: It's going to rain today or something like that. If that's the case, then there's no way I can go without an umbrella.

example_sentences.japanese: 地球温暖化に関する問題は解決しうるとか…。でも、現状は悪くなる一方である。
example_sentences.english: It's said that we're able to solve the problems in relation to global warming or something like that... But the real situation is that it just keeps getting worse.

example_sentences.japanese: めがねちゃん：「彼が昨日、何て言ったか覚えてる？」 ヤンキー君：「明日、１１時ごろに学校の前で会おうとか言っていたようだけど、定かではない。」
example_sentences.english: Megane-chan: 'Do you remember what he said yesterday?' Yankee-kun: 'He said, 'lets meet in front of school around 11' or something like that, but I am not really sure.'

grammar_point: う・よう + ではないか
general_translation: Let's do something, Why don't we
formation: Verb［おう］ + ではないかVerb［おう］ + じゃないか
casual_structure: Verb［おう］ + ではないかVerb［おう］ + じゃないか
explanation: A formal expression asking whether someone does not have the will to do (A) with you, coming across as why don't we (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の成功をしんじようではないか。
example_sentences.english: Why don't we trust that he will be successful?

example_sentences.japanese: 正々堂々と戦おうではないか。
example_sentences.english: Why don't we fight fair and square?

example_sentences.japanese: この問題をどう解決するかみんなで考えようではないか。
example_sentences.english: Why don't we all think about how we can solve this problem?

example_sentences.japanese: こういう時こそお互い助け合おうじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: Why don't we help each other, especially in times like this.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく日本に来たのだから、食べれるだけの日本食を食べようじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: Since we have come all the way to Japan, why don't we eat as much Japanese food as we can.

example_sentences.japanese: 共に素晴らしい世界をつくっていこうではないか。
example_sentences.english: Why don't we (go and) build a wonderful world together.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を身につけるためにがんばろうではないか。
example_sentences.english: Why don't we try our best in order to learn Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: この瀬戸物をちゃんと鑑定してもらおうではないか。
example_sentences.english: Why don't we get this porcelain appraised?

example_sentences.japanese: 意見の相違があっても、はなしあおうではないか。
example_sentences.english: Even if our opinions differ, why don't we discuss it?

example_sentences.japanese: 南北を統一しようではないか。
example_sentences.english: Why don't we unify north and south?

example_sentences.japanese: 大変でも毎日トレーニングをおこなおうではないか。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is hard, why don't we perform training everyday?

example_sentences.japanese: 簡単なことではないが、憎しみをすてようではないか。
example_sentences.english: It isn't a simple thing, but why don't we throw away our hatred?

example_sentences.japanese: 遊んでばかりいないで勉強でもしようではないか。
example_sentences.english: Instead of doing nothing but play, why don't we do something like study.

example_sentences.japanese: 立場は変わっても、率直にかたりあおうではないか。
example_sentences.english: Even if you change your standpoint, why don't we talk about it together?

example_sentences.japanese: いつまで意地を張っているんだ。仲直りしようではないか。
example_sentences.english: How long are you going to keep acting like that. Why don't we make up?

example_sentences.japanese: 勝手に判断せず、診断が出るのをまとうではないか。
example_sentences.english: Why don't we wait for the diagnosis, without passing arbitrary judgment?

example_sentences.japanese: もっと綺麗に壁紙の張り替えができるのなら、張り替えてもらおうではないか。
example_sentences.english: If you think that you're able to reapply the wallpaper better, then why don't I just get you to do it?

example_sentences.japanese: 乗せていってくれるって言っているんだから乗せて行ってもらおうではないか。
example_sentences.english: They said that they will give us a ride, so why don't we have them give us a ride.

general_translation: As if, Just like
formation: Verb + かのようだ(1)［い］Adjective + かのようだ(1)［な］Adjective + である + かのようだ(1)Noun + である + かのようだ(1)(1) かのように + Phrase、かのような + Noun
casual_structure: Verb + かのようだ(1)［い］Adjective + かのようだ(1)［な］Adjective + である + かのようだ(1)Noun + である + かのようだ(1)(1) かのように + Phrase、かのような + Noun
polite_structure: Verb + かのようです(1)［い］Adjective + かのようです(1)［な］Adjective + である + かのようです(1)Noun + である + かのようです(1)(1) かのように + Phrase、かのような + Noun
explanation: An expression highlighting that the manner in which (B) is doing something is questionably like (A). As if it were (A).

example_sentences.japanese: その作品は、あの有名な作品を真似たかのようですね。
example_sentences.english: That piece looks as if it is imitating that other famous work.

example_sentences.japanese: このＶＲフライトゲームはものすごくリアルだ。まるで本物の飛行機を操縦しているかのようだ。
example_sentences.english: This VR flight game is so realistic. It is just as if I am flying an actual airplane.

example_sentences.japanese: なんだこの静けさは。この町には誰もいないかのようだ。
example_sentences.english: What is this quietness? It is as if there is no one in this town.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はまるで私と話すのが面倒であるかのようだ。
example_sentences.english: He talks to me as if it was a chore.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼と僕は兄弟であるかのようだが、実は彼は僕のパートナーです。
example_sentences.english: It is as if he and I are brothers, but actually he is my partner.

example_sentences.japanese: 長谷川くんのお母さんは私を自分の子供であるかのように小さい頃から可愛がってくれていた。
example_sentences.english: Hasegawa-kun's mother has taken care of me just as if I was her own child.

example_sentences.japanese: このスーパーに入ると、まるで母国に帰ってきたかのような感じがする。
example_sentences.english: When I enter this supermarket, I feel as if I am back in my home country.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はまるでお腹に風船を入れているかのようだ。
example_sentences.english: It is just as if he has a balloon in his belly.

example_sentences.japanese: あの会社は営業中も休業しているかのようだ。
example_sentences.english: That company looks as if they are closed even during operation hours.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は相当目がいい。望遠鏡を使っているかのようだ。
example_sentences.english: He has extremely good eyesight. It is as if he is using a telescope.

example_sentences.japanese: あのシャツの色と柄じゃあ、包帯をしているかのようですね。
example_sentences.english: That shirt's color and patterns makes it look as if you are wearing a bandage.

example_sentences.japanese: あのピッチャー、豆を撒いているかのような投げ方をする。
example_sentences.english: That pitcher's throw is as if he is spreading seeds.

example_sentences.japanese: ライバル会社のあの人、まるでうちの会社の方針を知っているかのようだ。
example_sentences.english: That person from a rival company acts as if he knows our company's plans.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かと待ち合わせているかのように見えたが、ただぼーっと立っていただけだった。
example_sentences.english: (He) appeared as if (he) was waiting for someone, but (he) was just standing there, spacing out.

example_sentences.japanese: 初めてなのに、分量が分かっているかのように料理を作っている。
example_sentences.english: Even though it's their first time, they are making food as if they understand how much of each item they need.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの犬は生きていたとき私をときどきじろじろ見たもので、あたかも何か言いたいかのようだった。
example_sentences.english: My dog used to stare at me from time to time when it was still around just like it was trying to tell me something.

example_sentences.japanese: その歌手の振る舞いは名高い歌手であるかのようだが、実はキャリアを始めたばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: That singer's behavior is as if she is famous, but in reality, she has just begun her career.

example_sentences.japanese: その日、隣の家の子供とすこし話した。１０才の子供でも喋り方はまるでもう大人であるかのようだった。
example_sentences.english: On that day I spoke to the neighbor's child a bit. Despite being a ten year old, they spoke as if they were an adult.

grammar_point: のではないでしょうか
general_translation: I think ... isn't it?, It might be that..., Don't you agree?
formation: Verb + の(1) + ではない(2)（だろう）か［い］Adjective + の(1) + ではない(2)（だろう）かNoun + （なの(3)）+ ではない(2)（だろう）か［な］Adjective + （なの(3)）+ ではない(2)（だろう）か(1) ん(2) じゃない(3) なん
casual_structure: Verb + の(1) + ではない(2)（だろう）か［い］Adjective + の(1) + ではない(2)（だろう）かNoun + （なの(3)）+ ではない(2)（だろう）か［な］Adjective + （なの(3)）+ ではない(2)（だろう）か(1) ん(2) じゃない(3) なん
polite_structure: Verb + の(1) + ではない(2)（でしょう）か［い］Adjective + の(1) + ではない(2)（でしょう）かNoun + （なの(3)）+ ではない(2)（でしょう）か［な］Adjective + （なの(3)）+ ではない(2)（でしょう）か(1) ん(2) じゃない(3) なん
explanation: A phrase used to ask a rhetorical question about whether (A) is not actually the case, or when seeking agreement. I wonder if it isn't (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はもしかして、あきれているのではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I think that he is probably amazed, isn't he? (don't you agree?)

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩は疲れているのじゃないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I think that our senpai is tired, don't you think?

example_sentences.japanese: 息子がおもちゃをじーっとみている。あのおもちゃが欲しいのじゃないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: Our son is staring at a toy. I think he wants that toy, don't you agree?

example_sentences.japanese: 長谷川さんは田中さんのことが好きなのではないでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: I think that Hasegawa-san likes Tanaka-san, don't you agree?

example_sentences.japanese: あの人の右腕に入ってるタトゥー、防犯カメラに映っていたのと全く同じです。あの人は犯人なのではないでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: The tattoo on that person's right arm is exactly the same as the one seen on the security camera. I think that he is the perpetrator, don't you agree?

example_sentences.japanese: あそこに見えるのは、虹ではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I think the thing you can see over there is a rainbow, isn't it? (don't you agree?)

example_sentences.japanese: この症状、伝染病ではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: With these symptoms, I think it's a contagious disease, isn't it? (don't you agree?)

example_sentences.japanese: この調子だと、停電が長引くのではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: At this rate, I think the blackout will drag on, won't it? (don't you agree?)

example_sentences.japanese: こんなお願いをしてしまって、厚かましかったのではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I think it was pretty bold/shameless to make a request like this, don't you agree? (isn't it?)

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩に意見を言ったら、生意気ではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I think it is impertinent to tell your opinion to your senior, isn't it? (don't you agree?)

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事に対する真剣な姿に、憧れるのではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I think a serious stance towards one's work is admired, isn't it? (don't you agree?)

example_sentences.japanese: あの店、水曜日は確か定休日ではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: If I am not mistaken, I think that store has its regular holiday on Wednesday, doesn't it? (don't you agree?)

example_sentences.japanese: 定価は一万円ではないでしょうか。随分安くなっていますね。
example_sentences.english: I think the regular price is 10,000 yen, isn't it? It has become considerably cheaper. (don't you agree?)

example_sentences.japanese: ドラマのあの展開は、誰にも予想できないのではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: No one could have predicted the development in that drama, don't you think? (couldn't have)

example_sentences.japanese: 今回のテストは難しかったけど、点数が悪すぎるのではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: This test was difficult, but I think my score is much too low, isn't it? (don't you agree?)

example_sentences.japanese: しまっていた宝石が見当たらない。盗難にあったのではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: It appears that the locked up jewels can't be found. I think they were stolen, don't you agree? (isn't it?)

general_translation: Natural, As a matter of course
formation: Verb［て］+ 当然（とうぜん） + だ［い］Adjective［て］+ 当然（とうぜん） + だ［な］Adjective + で + 当然（とうぜん） + だ
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ 当然（とうぜん） + だ［い］Adjective［て］+ 当然（とうぜん） + だ［な］Adjective + で + 当然（とうぜん） + だ
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ 当然（とうぜん） + です［い］Adjective［て］+ 当然（とうぜん） + です［な］Adjective + で + 当然（とうぜん） + です
explanation: A structure expressing that (A) is right on the mark, or as would naturally be expected.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに食べたら、ふとってとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: If you eat like that, of course you will get fat.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな生意気なやつは嫌われてとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: It is only natural that a cocky person like that is hated.

example_sentences.japanese: このスープは俺が作ったものだから、美味しくてとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: I am the one that made this soup so, of course it is delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: このビルは先月建てられたばかりだから、綺麗でとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: This building was only built last month, so of course it is beautiful.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は厚かましいから、さけられてとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: Because he is impudent, it is natural that you would avoid him.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は優しいから、すかれてとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: Because she is nice, of course she is liked.

example_sentences.japanese: アイデアがいいから、人気があってとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: Because the idea is good, it is natural that it would be popular.

example_sentences.japanese: 脂を取り過ぎたら、気持ちわるくなってとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: If you consume too much fat, it is natural that you would come to feel bad.

example_sentences.japanese: 育児をしているのだから、いそがしくてとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: Because you are raising a child, it is natural that you would be busy.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長なのだから「いばってとうぜんだ」と彼は思っている。
example_sentences.english: Since he is the CEO, he thinks that 'It is natural to be proud.'

example_sentences.japanese: あれだけのことをしたのだから、インタビューされてとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: Because you did it to that degree, it is natural that you would be interviewed.

example_sentences.japanese: アクセントが完璧だから、ネイティブとまちがえられてとうぜんです。
example_sentences.english: Because your accent is perfect, it is natural that you would be mistaken for a native.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はみんなに迷惑ばかりかけているから、きらわれてとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: Because she is always causing everyone trouble, of course she is hated.

example_sentences.japanese: 明け方までコーラを飲んだのだから、お腹がいたくなってとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: Because you drank cola until dawn, it is natural that you would have a stomachache.

example_sentences.japanese: 憧れの人にやっと会えたのだから、緊張してとうぜんです。
example_sentences.english: Because you were finally able to meet the person you look up to, it is natural that you would be nervous.

general_translation: It is only natural that, It is no wonder
formation: Verb + のは(1) + 当然（とうぜん）だ［い］Adjective + のは(1) + 当然（とうぜん）だ［な］Adjective + な(1) + のは + 当然（とうぜん）だ Noun + は(2) + 当然（とうぜん）だ (1) のも(2) も
casual_structure: Verb + のは(1) + 当然（とうぜん）だ［い］Adjective + のは(1) + 当然（とうぜん）だ［な］Adjective + な(1) + のは + 当然（とうぜん）だ Noun + は(2) + 当然（とうぜん）だ (1) のも(2) も
polite_structure: Verb + のは(1) + 当然（とうぜん） + です［い］Adjective + のは(1) + 当然（とうぜん）です［な］Adjective + な(1) + のは + 当然（とうぜん） + です Noun + は(2) + 当然（とうぜん）です (1) のも(2) も
explanation: A phrase highlighting (A) as only natural. Even that which is (A) is right on the mark.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: 税金を納めていないんだから、逮捕されるのもとうぜんです。
example_sentences.english: Since (he) didn't pay (his) taxes, it is only natural that (he) would be arrested.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社のお金を勝手に使ったなら、クビになるのはとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: If you did use company money without permission, it's only natural that you get fired.

example_sentences.japanese: このタワーマンションは六本木にあるので、家賃が高いのはとうぜんです。
example_sentences.english: This high-rise condo is located in Roppongi, it is only natural that the rent is expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: おばあちゃんは毎朝１０キロも散歩しているから元気なのもとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: My grandma walks 10 kilometers every morning, so it is no wonder she is so healthy.

example_sentences.japanese: この１年間全然勉強をしてこなかったから落第もとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: I have not studied at all for the past year, so it's no wonder I flunked out.

example_sentences.japanese: 練習を怠ったんだから、ああいう結果になるのもとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: Since you neglected practice, it is only natural that you would see those kinds of results.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなマッチョな体型では、エプロンが似合わないのもとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: It is only natural that an apron would not look good on such a muscular body.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼があんな風に振舞っていたなら、ほかの人からの受けが悪いのもとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: If he was behaving in that way, it is only natural that he is poorly received by other people now.

example_sentences.japanese: 久しぶりに彼に会ったのだから、彼女が嬉しそうなのはとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: Since she got to see him after being apart for a while, it is only natural that she seems happy.

example_sentences.japanese: あれだけ頑張って絵を描いていたら、すぐに絵の具がなくなるのもとうぜんです。
example_sentences.english: If you put that much effort into painting, it is only natural that you would run out of paint straight away.

example_sentences.japanese: 両親が園芸家なら、園芸のセンスがあるのもとうぜんですね。
example_sentences.english: If (your) parents are horticulturalists, it is only natural that they would have good taste when it comes to gardening.

example_sentences.japanese: 台風が来ているのだから、遠足が延期になるのもとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: Since a typhoon is approaching, it is only natural that the field trip would be postponed.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔車屋で働いていたから、自分でオイル交換できるのもとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: I used to work as a car salesman, so it is only natural that I can change my own oil.

example_sentences.japanese: オートメーション化が進めば進むほど、社員の数が減るのもとうぜんだ。
example_sentences.english: As automation technology advances, it is only natural that the number of employees will decrease.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当に惜しい結果でした。悔しくて涙が止まらないのもとうぜんですよ。
example_sentences.english: It was truly a regrettable outcome. It is only natural that (she) would be mortified to the point of being unable to stop crying.

example_sentences.japanese: その古くて枯れた木がとうとう倒れたのもとうぜんだよ。そんな長い間立っていたのはおどろくほどだよ。誰も怪我をしなくて嬉しい。
example_sentences.english: It is no wonder that old, withered tree has finally collapsed. It is surprising that it had been standing for such a long time as that. I am glad that no one was hurt.

general_translation: Only, Just, No more than
formation: たった + （の）+ Number
casual_structure: たった + （の）+ Number
explanation: A strong expression showing that something is merely or no more than (A). Emphasized form of merely.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼はたった一人の兄弟です。」
example_sentences.english: 'He is my only sibling.'

example_sentences.japanese: カップ麺はたった３分で出来上がる。
example_sentences.english: Cup noodles can be prepared in just 3 minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕、たった一人でここまで歩いてきたのかい？偉いね！
example_sentences.english: Kid, you walked here all alone? I'm proud of you!

example_sentences.japanese: クラスメイト全員を招待したのに、たったの３人しか僕の誕生日パーティーにこなかった。
example_sentences.english: I invited everyone in my class, but only 3 people showed up to my birthday party.

example_sentences.japanese: このホテルからビーチまでの距離はたったの１０メートルです！
example_sentences.english: It's merely 10 meters in distance from this hotel to the beach!

example_sentences.japanese: 友達１：「１０００円貸してくれる？」友達２：「たった５００円しかないよ。」
example_sentences.english: Friend 1: 'Can you lend me 1000 yen?'Friend 2: 'I only have 500 on me.'

example_sentences.japanese: そうまさん：「ケーキ、出来ました。」えりなさん：「え、たった５分で出来たの？！」
example_sentences.english: Souma: 'The cake is done.'Erina: 'Wha?! You finished it just in 5 minutes?!'

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の子供について、母親：「ケビンはずっと、たったひとりで家にいた！！」
example_sentences.english: Mother, about her son: 'Kevin was at home all alone the whole time!'

example_sentences.japanese: 市場の商人：「安いよ、安いよ、りっぱな高級時計がたった千円。」
example_sentences.english: Merchant on the market: 'Cheap! Cheap! Amazing, high-quality watches only 1000 yen.'

example_sentences.japanese: スマホ比較のウェブサイト：「『愛Ｐｈｏｎｅ』は薄さがたったの７．６ｍｍ程です。」
example_sentences.english: Smartphone comparison website: 'The 'Aiphone' is only about 7.6mm thin.'

example_sentences.japanese: 僻地医療で診療代について、患者：「たったこれだけでいいのですか？」医者：「もちろんですよ。」
example_sentences.english: Patient on the medical examination fee for medical care in a rural area: 'Is only this amount enough?'Doctor: 'Yes, of course.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「病気のせいで今週出かけたのはたった一度だけだそうだ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'I heard that he left the house only once this week because of illness.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達１：「このサラダ、美味しいよ。」友達２：「ありがとう。あたしの秘伝は小さじ３杯のチリパウダー。」友達１：「たったそれだけ？」
example_sentences.english: Friend1: 'This salad, it's delicious!'Friend2: 'Thanks. My secret is 3 teaspoons of chili powder.'Friend1: 'Only that?'

example_sentences.japanese: 道を聞く人：「あの、すみません。からくら町はここから遠いのですか？」通行人：「いいえ、バスでならたった８分です。」
example_sentences.english: A person asking for the way: 'Excuse me. Is Karakura Town far from here?'Passerby: 'No. It is just 8 minutes by bus.'

example_sentences.japanese: グチを言う：「彼女から先輩と呼べって言われちゃった。たった一日しか年上じゃないくせに。」
example_sentences.english: Complaining: 'I was told by her to call her senpai. Despite that she is just one day older...'

example_sentences.japanese: ライフスタイルに関するウェブニュースのタイトル名：「お母さんはたった６６５円で食べ放題！母の日プレゼント」
example_sentences.english: Title of a web-news article in relation to lifestyle: 'The moms' all-you-can-eat is just 665 yen! Mother's Day present.'

example_sentences.japanese: その電車はたった今出発したので次の電車が来るまで少々お待ちください。
example_sentences.english: That train has just departed, so please wait until the next train arrives.

general_translation: There is a risk or fear that, Be in danger of, Possibility of
formation: Verb［る］(1) + 恐（おそ）れがある［い］Adjective + 恐（おそ）れがある［な］Adjective + な(2) + 恐（おそ）れがあるNoun + の(2) + 恐（おそ）れがある(1) Verb［ない］(2) である
casual_structure: Verb［る］(1) + 恐（おそ）れがある［い］Adjective + 恐（おそ）れがある［な］Adjective + な(2) + 恐（おそ）れがあるNoun + の(2) + 恐（おそ）れがある(1) Verb［ない］(2) である
polite_structure: Verb［る］(1) + 恐（おそ）れがあります［い］Adjective + 恐（おそ）れがあります［な］Adjective + な(2) + 恐（おそ）れがありますNoun + の(2) + 恐（おそ）れがあります(1) Verb［ない］(2) である
explanation: A formal construction expressing that the fear of (A) exists. (A) is a possibility.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: お辞儀をしすぎると腰を痛めるおそれがある。
example_sentences.english: If you bow too much, there is a risk of hurting your back.

example_sentences.japanese: 津波のおそれがある場合には、速やかに避難所まで避難してください。
example_sentences.english: When there is a risk of a tsunami, please rapidly evacuate to the evacuation area.

example_sentences.japanese: 高温にすると爆発するおそれがあるので、直射日光が当たるところに置かないでください。
example_sentences.english: Since there is a possibility of explosion when this reaches high temperatures, please don't place this in direct sunlight.

example_sentences.japanese: 教わっても忘れるおそれがあるから、メモしておこう。
example_sentences.english: Even if I am taught (it), there is a risk of forgetting (it), so I will take notes.

example_sentences.japanese: このオイルだとエンジンに負担をかけるおそれがあるからやめたほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: Since there is fear that this oil may be taxing on the engine, it would be better to not use it.

example_sentences.japanese: あの勢いでお代わりされると、ご飯が足りなくなるおそれがある。
example_sentences.english: If I am asked that way for seconds, there is a risk that there won't be enough food.

example_sentences.japanese: この絵の具は中身が漏れるおそれがあるから袋に入れてください。
example_sentences.english: There is a risk that the contents of these paints will leak, so please place them in a bag.

example_sentences.japanese: 遠足に行ったのはいいが、急な天候の変化で帰れないおそれがある。
example_sentences.english: It is alright if you go on the trip, but there is the possibility of a sudden change in weather that would not let you return (home).

example_sentences.japanese: 医者：「倒れたせいで肩に怪我をしたおそれがあるので、レントゲンを撮ったほうがいいです。」
example_sentences.english: Doctor: 'You should have an X-ray since there is a risk that you injured your shoulder due to falling.'

example_sentences.japanese: この応援の仕方だと逆効果になるおそれがあるから変えましょう。
example_sentences.english: There is the possibility that this method of assistance could be counterproductive, so let's change it.

example_sentences.japanese: もし全住民がワクチンを接種しなければ、伝染病が拡がるおそれがある。
example_sentences.english: If the entire population is not vaccinated, there is a fear that the infectious disease will spread.

example_sentences.japanese: 商談の準備を怠ると失敗するおそれがあるからしっかり頼むよ。
example_sentences.english: I fear that I will be negligent and mess up the preparation for the negotiations, so I'm begging you to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 大雑把に詰め込むと全部入らないおそれがあるから、ちゃんと考えて鞄に入れてね。
example_sentences.english: If you just cram it all in, there is a risk of not everything fitting in the bag. So, think about it properly and pack.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気予報：「明日は、本州を中心に大雨の降る所がありそうです。関東から東北にかけては強風のおそれもあります。」
example_sentences.english: Weather forecast: 'It seems that the areas where rain will fall tomorrow are centered in Honshuu.There is also the possibility of strong winds from the Kanto to Tohoku areas.'

example_sentences.japanese: 若者が将来について恐れを抱くことは普通のことです。
example_sentences.english: It is normal for young people to have fears about the future.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏場の現場では熱中症の恐れが強まるので、作業員の方はこまめに水分補給と休憩を取るようにしてください。
example_sentences.english: Workers are encouraged to hydrate and take frequent breaks, as the risk of heat stroke increases at construction sites during summer.

general_translation: Probably, Perhaps, (Most) likely, (I) fear that
formation: おそらく + Phrase
casual_structure: おそらく + Phrase
explanation: A formal structure used to highlight the unfortunate likelihood of (A). I fear that (A)
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: おそらく彼はここにいないだろう。
example_sentences.english: He most likely isn't here.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻は今夜会社の人たちと飲み会に行くと言っていたので、おそらく１１時ごろぐらいまでは帰ってこないと思います。
example_sentences.english: My wife said she was going to a drinking party tonight with some people from work, so she probably won't be home until around 11:00 or so.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつの不自然な行動からして、おそらくあいつが犯人だろう！
example_sentences.english: Judging by that guy's unnatural behavior, he's probably the culprit!

example_sentences.japanese: おそらく明日は雨なので、明日予定していたピクニックは中止しましょう。
example_sentences.english: Perhaps it may rain tomorrow, so let's cancel the picnic we had planned for tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: おそらく明日雨が降る。
example_sentences.english: Perhaps it will rain tomorrow. (I fear that...)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼だったら、おそらくこんなことできっこないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: If it's him, he most likely won't be able to do it. (I fear that...)

example_sentences.japanese: 「くそ、おそらくあなたの結婚式には行けないじゃないか。」
example_sentences.english: 'Dang it, I think I probably won't be able to go to your wedding.' (I fear that...)

example_sentences.japanese: 道路に沿って行けばおそらくガソリンスタンドが見つかるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: If you go along the road, you will most likely see the gas station.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の兄はおそらく１１月頃アメリカから帰ってくるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: My older brother will probably return home from the US around November.

example_sentences.japanese: 凶器は怪我から察するにおそらくナイフのようなものでしょう。
example_sentences.english: The murder weapon was, judging from the injuries, most likely something resembling to a knife.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は何か言いたそうに私をみた。おそらく何か重要なことでしょう。
example_sentences.english: It seemed to me that he was about to say something. Most likely something important. (I fear that...)

example_sentences.japanese: 問題の原因を特定するために最もすべきことは、おそらくその機械の分解と分析だろう。
example_sentences.english: Probably, the most effective action to identify the cause of the problem would be the decomposition and analysis of the machine.

example_sentences.japanese: 妊婦：「赤ちゃんの性別はなんですか？」医者：「おそらく女の子です。でもまだわかりません。」
example_sentences.english: Pregnant woman: 'Is it a baby boy or girl?' Doctor: 'Probably a baby girl. However, I am not sure yet.'

example_sentences.japanese: 名探偵：「この人の背の高さを鑑みるとおそらく彼女が殺人犯だろう！」
example_sentences.english: Great detective: 'Taking this person's height into account, she is most likely our killer.'

example_sentences.japanese: 代表者が「大統領はおそらく再選をねらうまい」と言っていた。
example_sentences.english: The representative was saying that 'the president will most likely not aim for re-election'.

general_translation: Definitely not, Absolutely not, Impossible, Do you really think~?
formation: Verb［る］+ もの(1) + か［い］Adjective + もの(1) + か［な］Adjective + な + もの(1) + かNoun + な + もの(1) + か(1) もん
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ もの(1) + か［い］Adjective + もの(1) + か［な］Adjective + な + もの(1) + かNoun + な + もの(1) + か(1) もん
polite_structure: Verb［る］+ もの(1) + です + か［い］Adjective + もの(1) + です + か［な］Adjective + な + もの(1) + です + かNoun + な + もの(1) + です + か(1) もん
explanation: A phrase which strongly questions that which is (A), coming across as you must be joking, or absolutely not.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: あんなひどいこと言われたんだ。平気なものか。
example_sentences.english: Such a terrible thing was said. It is impossible to be calm.

example_sentences.japanese: バカ言うな。俺がそんな派手な服を着るものか！
example_sentences.english: Don't be stupid! Do you really think that I would wear something so flashy?!

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事？毎日怒られてばかりだから楽しいもんか。
example_sentences.english: Work? I get yelled at everyday, so I am definitely not having a good time.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日残業しているし、家に帰ったら家事を全部やっている。元気なものか。
example_sentences.english: I work overtime every day and when I get home I do all the chores. Do you really think I have any energy left?

example_sentences.japanese: お前みたいな奴は友達なものか！
example_sentences.english: A person like you is absolutely not my friend!

example_sentences.japanese: 一人でこの量の仕事を明日までにできたもんか。
example_sentences.english: As if it's possible to do this amount of work by tomorrow myself.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなまずい飯、食べられたもんか。
example_sentences.english: As if I could have eaten something so awful.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が皮肉なんて言うものか。そういう奴じゃない。
example_sentences.english: He absolutely will not use sarcasm. He is not that kind of a person.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな安っぽい言葉が心に響くものか。
example_sentences.english: Such insignificant wording absolutely will not make an impression.

example_sentences.japanese: それくらいの研究で理解など深まるものか。
example_sentences.english: Research to that degree absolutely will not deepen understanding.

example_sentences.japanese: あの山が噴火するものか。あれは火山じゃない。
example_sentences.english: That mountain absolutely will not erupt. It is not a volcano.

example_sentences.japanese: 君にボーナスなどあげるものか。まじめに働かないんだから。
example_sentences.english: You absolutely will not get a bonus. Because you don't work diligently.

example_sentences.japanese: 今から行ったって日の出になんか間に合うものか。
example_sentences.english: Even if we leave now we absolutely will not make it in time for sunrise.

example_sentences.japanese: 失恋なんて、経験のない君にわかるもんか！
example_sentences.english: You, who has never experienced something like a broken heart, absolutely won't understand it!

example_sentences.japanese: 君に文房具なんてやるものか。どうせ大切にしないんだから。
example_sentences.english: I absolutely will not give you any stationery, because I have no doubt that you won't use it with care.

example_sentences.japanese: 休日に牧場なんて行くものか。観光客が多すぎる。
example_sentences.english: It is impossible to go to a farm on a holiday. There are too many tourists.

example_sentences.japanese: 井上：「あなたの男友達が家の前で待っている。」 本田：「彼が何をしようが、かまうものか！」
example_sentences.english: Inoue: 'Your male friend is waiting in front of your house.' Honda: 'I absolutely do not care what he is doing!'

example_sentences.japanese: 永井：「長谷川さんって伊藤と付き合っているらしい。」 長谷川：「違うよ！伊藤さんと付き合うものか！」
example_sentences.english: Nagai: 'Hasegawa-san, I heard that you are going out with Itou-san.' Hasegawa: 'No! I am absolutely not going out with him!'

general_translation: In addition, On top of that, What is more, To make matters worse
formation: おまけに + Phrase
casual_structure: おまけに + Phrase
explanation: A casual construction highlighting that something is in addition to (A). What's even more defeating is (A). Often negative.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: 家を掃除した。おまけにランチを作っといた。
example_sentences.english: I cleaned the house. On top of that, I also made lunch in advance. (what is more)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は仕事に遅刻して部長に怒られたし、おまけに取引先の人も怒らせちゃったから、今日は最悪の日だったよ。
example_sentences.english: Today was one of the worst days because I got yelled at by my boss for being late to work, and to make it worse, I upset one of our clients.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は彼氏に美味しいご飯をご馳走してもらって、おまけにプレゼントまでもらった。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday, my boyfriend treated me to a delicious dinner and on top of that he even gave me a gift.

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンが全然立ち上がらない。おまけにスマホの充電がないから仕事が全然できない。
example_sentences.english: My computer won't turn on. To make matters worse, my smartphone is out of battery, so I can't work at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 宝石を買ったら、おまけに香水をサービスしてくれた。
example_sentences.english: They included perfume in addition to the jewel I bought. (on top of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 自転車が盗まれただけではなく、おまけに雨が降りそうだ。
example_sentences.english: Not only has my bike been stolen, but to make matters worse, it looks like it is going to rain. (what is more)

example_sentences.japanese: 競馬で負け、おまけに帰りに財布を落とし、最悪だ。
example_sentences.english: I lost at the horse races and, to make matters worse, I lost my wallet on the way home. Worst day ever.

example_sentences.japanese: 体重が激増し、おまけに髪まで薄くなった。ストレスですね。
example_sentences.english: On top of my hair thinning, my weight suddenly increased. This is definitely stress. (what is more)

example_sentences.japanese: 秘伝の味のレシピを教えてくれて、おまけに見学までさせてくれました。
example_sentences.english: (She) shared the recipe to the secret flavor in addition to allowing me to watch (her) make it (herself).(on top of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 紅葉を見に行ったら、おまけにリスを見ることができて良かった。
example_sentences.english: I was glad that we were able to see squirrels in addition to going to see the fall colors. (on top of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 胡椒を頼んだら、おまけに一味も付いてきたから両方かけてみた。
example_sentences.english: On top of the pepper I requested, they also brought some cayenne pepper powder. I gave them both a try. (what is more)

example_sentences.japanese: 頼まれた仕事を一生懸命やったら、おまけにお菓子もくれた。
example_sentences.english: What's more I also got some sweets for working hard on the job that I was requested. (on top of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 荷物を運ぶのを手伝ったら、おまけにコレクションを見せてくれた。
example_sentences.english: I helped carry the baggage, what is more they showed me their collection. (in addition)

example_sentences.japanese: あの店はサービスが悪いし、おまけに言葉遣いも悪いから、もう二度と行かない。
example_sentences.english: That shop's service is terrible and, to make matters worse, they are not very polite, so I will not be going a second time.

example_sentences.japanese: この中古のコンピューターは、ハードディスクの速度は速いし、おまけに安いし、すごくいいよ。
example_sentences.english: This second-hand computer has a hard disc that is fast, and what is more, it is cheap. It is really great. (on top of that)

general_translation: Surely, Bound to, Certainly, Be decided
formation: Verb + に決（き）まっている［い］Adjective + に決（き）まっている［な］Adjective + に決（き）まっているNoun + に決（き）まっている
casual_structure: Verb + に決（き）まっている［い］Adjective + に決（き）まっている［な］Adjective + に決（き）まっているNoun + に決（き）まっている
polite_structure: Verb + に決（き）まっています［い］Adjective + に決（き）まっています［な］Adjective + に決（き）まっていますNoun + に決（き）まっています
explanation: A strong phrase stating that (A) is certainly or surely true, due to it being decided.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: あの店のトロはどれも脂がのっているにきまっている。
example_sentences.english: That shop's tuna is bound to be rich in fat.

example_sentences.japanese: この家はあの有名な建設会社が建てた家だから、丈夫にきまってる。
example_sentences.english: This house was built by that famous construction company, so it is bound to be sturdy.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はみんなに好かれているからいい人にきまっている。
example_sentences.english: That person is liked by everyone, so he is bound to be a good person.

example_sentences.japanese: あの選手は足が速いから勝つにきまっている。
example_sentences.english: That athlete is fast at running, so they are bound to win.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらクリフダイビングのプロでも、あの高さからダイブするのは怖いにきまってる。
example_sentences.english: Diving off a cliff that high is surely scary, even for a professional cliff diver.

example_sentences.japanese: このセーター、ウール１００％でしょ？高いにきまっています。
example_sentences.english: That sweater is 100% wool, right? That is bound to be expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日お菓子を食べることはダメにきまっている！
example_sentences.english: Eating sweets every day is certainly no good!

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のことだから、あいかわらずいい人にきまっている。
example_sentences.english: Since it is him, he is bound to be a good person.

example_sentences.japanese: かなりひどいことを言ってしまったから、恨んでいるにきまっている。
example_sentences.english: Since I said a very terrible thing, (they) decidedly feel bitter towards me.

example_sentences.japanese: あんないいプレゼント、誰だって受け取るにきまっています。
example_sentences.english: Surely anyone would accept such a nice present.

example_sentences.japanese: Ｌｉｎｕｘオタク：「２０１８はデスクトップＬｉｎｕｘの年になるにきまっている！」
example_sentences.english: Linux Nerd: '2018 is bound to be the year of Linux on the desktop.'

example_sentences.japanese: あの社長、社員に対しては威張っているにきまっている。
example_sentences.english: That company chief is bound to put on airs in front of his employees.

example_sentences.japanese: 「あなたは裏口入学にきまっている」なんてひどいことを言われた。
example_sentences.english: I was told 'You are bound to bribe your way into school.' What nerve!

example_sentences.japanese: あの息子のお金の使い方からして、甘やかしているにきまっている。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the way that boy uses money, he is bound to be spoiled.

example_sentences.japanese: 優秀な職人はいつもいい仕事を見つけるにきまっている。
example_sentences.english: Excellent craftsmen are bound to always find good jobs.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻：「晩御飯、気に入ってくれたの？」 夫：「あなたが作った料理だから、おいしいにきまっているよ。」
example_sentences.english: Wife: 'Did you enjoy the dinner?' Husband: 'Any meal made by you is bound to be delicious.'

general_translation: To be expected to, To be scheduled to
formation: Verb［る］+ ことになっているVerb［ない］+ ことになっている
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ ことになっているVerb［ない］+ ことになっている
polite_structure: Verb［る］+ ことになっていますVerb［ない］+ ことになっています
explanation: A grammar point that indicates that the thing which is (A) is expected or scheduled to become that way.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: この寮では、起床時間は６時ということになっている。
example_sentences.english: In this dorm, it is expected that you are up by six o'clock.

example_sentences.japanese: 授業は１２時から始まることになっています。
example_sentences.english: The class is scheduled to start at 12.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長は来週の飲み会に参加しないことになっています。
example_sentences.english: The president is scheduled to not come to the party next week.

example_sentences.japanese: タクシーは左から乗ることになっている。
example_sentences.english: It is expected for customers to get into the cab from the left side.

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒たちは授業中に教室を出れないことになっている。
example_sentences.english: Students are expected to not leave the classroom during class.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年も契約を更新することになっています。
example_sentences.english: It is expected that the contract will be renewed next year as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 来週あの工場を見学することになっています。
example_sentences.english: We are expected to have a field trip at that factory next week.

example_sentences.japanese: 原稿は、郵送ではなく、メールで送ることになっている。
example_sentences.english: The manuscript is expected to be sent by email, not by post.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議は東京にある官庁で行うことになっている。
example_sentences.english: The meeting is scheduled to take place in a government office in Tokyo.

example_sentences.japanese: 締め切りは月末ということになっているが、早ければ早いほどいい。
example_sentences.english: The deadline is expected to be the end of the month, however it is best to do it as soon as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 寺の中に入る時は、礼儀として靴を脱ぐことになっている。
example_sentences.english: When you enter a temple, in terms of etiquette, you are expected to take off your shoes.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車は規則正しい時間に駅を通過することになっている。
example_sentences.english: The train is scheduled to pass through the station at regular times.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの会社では、仕事中は敬語で話すことになっています。
example_sentences.english: At my company, it is expected that you speak using keigo while working.

example_sentences.japanese: 月給３０万ということになっているが、いろいろと引かれるので、自由に使えるお金はそんなにない。
example_sentences.english: I expect to get a monthly salary of 300,000, but since various things are deducted, I don't really have much money to freely use.

example_sentences.japanese: あの学校の講師は一流ということになっているが、なんとなく怪しい。
example_sentences.english: That school's lecturers are expected to be first rate, but for some reason or another there is something off about them.

example_sentences.japanese: １００球投げたら交替ということになっていたが、今日はもう少し投げてもらおう。
example_sentences.english: They were scheduled to switch after throwing 100 balls, but today, I'll have them throw a little more.

general_translation: Feel like ~, Spirit
formation: Verb + 気（き）
casual_structure: Verb + 気（き）
explanation: A short word which indicates that someone has the spirit or attention necessary to do (A).
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かにみられているきがする。
example_sentences.english: I feel like I am being watched by someone.

example_sentences.japanese: お風呂でゆっくりしていたら、勉強をするきがなくなった。
example_sentences.english: I lost my motivation (spirit) to study, when I was relaxing in the bath.

example_sentences.japanese: よーし、やるきが出てきたぞ！
example_sentences.english: Alright! I am starting to get motivated!

example_sentences.japanese: やばい、明日までに終わるきがしない。
example_sentences.english: Shoot, I don't feel like I can finish this by tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 何もやるきが起きない。
example_sentences.english: I can't muster any motivation (spirit). (Feel like doing)

example_sentences.japanese: 応援されて、やるきが出た。
example_sentences.english: I was cheered on and found motivation (spirit). (Feel like doing)

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は好き嫌いがおおすぎるきがする。
example_sentences.english: I feel like my daughter is too picky.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の送別会にはいくきがしない。
example_sentences.english: I don't feel like going to his farewell party.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の実力では勝負にならないきがする。
example_sentences.english: I feel like it wouldn't be a contest with my real strength.

example_sentences.japanese: 結局賞金はもらえないきがします。
example_sentences.english: I feel like I won't receive the prize money after all.

example_sentences.japanese: 相手チームはせめるきがないらしい。
example_sentences.english: It seems like the opposing team doesn't feel like attacking. (lack the spirit to attack)

example_sentences.japanese: 確か彼は、醤油が苦手だったきがします。
example_sentences.english: If I remember correctly I feel like he disliked soy sauce.

example_sentences.japanese: あの助教授は本当におしえるきがあるのだろうか？
example_sentences.english: I wonder if that assistant professor really feels like teaching. (has the spirit)

example_sentences.japanese: しんじるきがない人には、何を言っても無駄です。
example_sentences.english: Anything you say to someone who doesn't feel like believing it, is a waste. (spirit)

example_sentences.japanese: 営業マンなのに、全然宣伝するきがない。
example_sentences.english: Despite being a salesman, he lacks the spirit to advertise at all.

general_translation: Seemingly, Giving appearance of, [Expresses emotions or feelings]
formation: Verb［stem］+ げ + に(1)［い］Adjective［い］+ げ + に(1)［な］Adjective + げ + に(1)(1) な + Noun
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ げ + に(1)［い］Adjective［い］+ げ + に(1)［な］Adjective + げ + に(1)(1) な + Noun
explanation: A short word used to indicate that something seems (A), or is giving off the vibe of (A).
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: 教養がありすぎてかわいげがないのもどうかと思う。
example_sentences.english: I wonder about things that are too refined and therefore don't give off the appearance of being cute.

example_sentences.japanese: 自信ありげに見えたかもしれないけど、実はめちゃくちゃ緊張してて吐きそうだった。
example_sentences.english: I may have given off the appearance of being confident, but actually, I was super nervous and felt like I was going to throw up.

example_sentences.japanese: 高校生たちがファストフード店で楽しげに話しているのを見て、自分が高校生の頃を思い出した。
example_sentences.english: When I saw highschool students seemingly having a good time talking to each other at a fast food restaurant, it reminded me of the time when I was a highschooler.

example_sentences.japanese: 高橋くんは不安げに手を上げました。
example_sentences.english: Seemingly nervous, Takahashi-kun raised his hand.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼がはずかしげに自分の弱点を教えてくれた。
example_sentences.english: Seemingly embarrassed, he told us about his weak points.

example_sentences.japanese: すずしげな顔でマラソンを走りきるんだから大したもんだよ。
example_sentences.english: It was considerable that he finished running the marathon while seemingly undeterred.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はとても素直だが、どことなくはかなげなのが気になります。
example_sentences.english: She is very honest, but I am concerned by her somehow fickle appearance.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供たちがうらやましげに見ているから、お菓子を分けてあげた。
example_sentences.english: Looking at the children they were giving the appearance of being envious, so I divided up the candy and gave it to them.

example_sentences.japanese: たのしげに遊ぶ子供を見るたびに、私は子供のころを思い出す。そして思わず笑顔になる。
example_sentences.english: Every time I see children seemingly enjoying themselves, I recall my childhood. And, without thinking, I smile.

example_sentences.japanese: 優勝した選手を見て彼はくやしげな表情をしていた。
example_sentences.english: Looking at the winning athlete, his facial expressions gave off the appearance of being frustrated.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が意味ありげな表情で僕を見つめている。何かあったのかな？
example_sentences.english: She is staring at me with the facial expression that gives off the appearance of knowing something about me. I wonder if something happened.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「どうしてそんなにまんぞくげなの？」 Ｂ：「日本語能力試験、合格したんだよ！」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Why are you giving off the appearance of being so satisfied?' B: 'I passed the Japanese Language Proficiency Test!'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は私の言葉を聞いてかなしげな顔で出かけた。どうしてそんな態度を取ったのか分からない。
example_sentences.english: She left with a seemingly sad look upon her face after hearing my words. I don't understand the change in her demeanor.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かに「私の言うとおりにすれば、いつの間にかお金持ちになれるんだ」と言われると、頭の中に赤ランプが点灯して、これはなにかあやしげな儲け話だと思うようになる。このような人には、いつも気を付けなければならない。
example_sentences.english: When someone says: 'Do as I say, and you will get rich in no time', a warning light in my head turns on and I begin to think that 'this gives off the appearance of a suspicious get-rich-quick scheme'. One must always be wary of people like this.

example_sentences.japanese: 父がなつかしげに自分の子供の頃の話をしてくれた。
example_sentences.english: My father talked about his childhood while giving off the appearance of nostalgia.

general_translation: It is exactly because
formation: Verb + ことだからNoun + の + ことだから［な］Adjective + な + ことだから
casual_structure: Verb + ことだからNoun + の + ことだから［な］Adjective + な + ことだから
polite_structure: Verb + ことですからNoun + の + ことですから［な］Adjective + な + ことですから
explanation: An expression that highlights that the thing which is (A) is the exact reasoning from which (B) can be determined.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: 神様のことだから、必ず助けてくれます。
example_sentences.english: It is exactly because it is God, that He will surely help me.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人がすることだから、どうせ人を騙して儲けているに違いない。
example_sentences.english: Precisely because it is something that person does, there is no doubt that he is making money scamming people.

example_sentences.japanese: いつも遅れてくる田中くんのことだから、今日も遅れてくるだろう。
example_sentences.english: It is exactly because Tanaka-kun always arrives late, that he will probably arrive late today.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんとお母さんが珍しくうちに来ていることだから、久しぶりにみんなで映画でも見よう。
example_sentences.english: Dad, mom, considering that you guys are here, which is a rare occasion, why don't we watch a movie together for the first time in a while.

example_sentences.japanese: 撮影が無事終わったことだから、打ち上げでもしましょう！
example_sentences.english: Considering that we have finished filming, it is a good opportunity for us to have a party!

example_sentences.japanese: お客様のプライバシーに関わることなので、これ以上詳しいことは言えません。
example_sentences.english: Because this is something that has to do with the privacy of our customer, we can't give you further details.

example_sentences.japanese: 部長のことだから、またミスをしたらクビにさせられると思う。
example_sentences.english: It is exactly because it is my boss, he will probably fire me if I mess up again.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのことだから間違いなくうまくいくと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: It is exactly because it's you that I definitely think it will go well.

example_sentences.japanese: あれは基礎問題ということだから、簡単だったでしょ？
example_sentences.english: It is exactly because that is a basic problem that it was easy, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の勘違いということだから、許してやってほしい。
example_sentences.english: It is exactly because he misunderstood that I want you to let it slide.

example_sentences.japanese: いつもウソをついている彼のことだから、今回も信じがたい。
example_sentences.english: It is exactly because he is always lying that it is hard to believe him this time too.

example_sentences.japanese: そういうことだから、一人でそういうところには行かない方がいい。
example_sentences.english: It is exactly because that is the case, it is better not to go alone to such a place.

example_sentences.japanese: それは学術的なことだから、僕はうまく説明できない。
example_sentences.english: It is exactly because it is scholarly that I can't explain it well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は鑑賞だけということだから、触ってはいけません。
example_sentences.english: It is exactly because today is all about aesthetic appreciation that you must not touch it.

example_sentences.japanese: 学級委員長のことだから、ちゃんと先生に伝えてくれるよ。
example_sentences.english: It is exactly because they are the class president, that they will properly tell the teacher for us.

example_sentences.japanese: お相手が「感激した」とのことだから、結果的にはあれで良かったと思います。
example_sentences.english: It is exactly because my partner said 'I was impressed' that I think that in terms of the results, it was good.

example_sentences.japanese: 出身が関西ということだから、所々で関西弁が出ていた。
example_sentences.english: It is exactly because he was born in the Kansai region that his Kansai dialect slipped occasionally.

example_sentences.japanese: あくまでも個人の感想ということだから、そこまで落ち込まなくてもいいと思う。
example_sentences.english: In the end, it is exactly because it is just a personal opinion that I think it is okay not to feel that bad about it.

general_translation: Because, The reason is
formation: Verb + ものだから(1) +  Phrase［い］Adjective + ものだから(1) +  Phrase［な］Adjective + な + ものだから(1) +  PhraseNoun + な + ものだから(1) +  Phrase(1) もので、もんで、もんだから
casual_structure: Verb + ものだから(1) +  Phrase［い］Adjective + ものだから(1) +  Phrase［な］Adjective + な + ものだから(1) +  PhraseNoun + な + ものだから(1) +  Phrase(1) もので、もんで、もんだから
explanation: A somewhat strong expression indicating that (A) being (A) is the reason that a specific thing is expected or resulted.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: 郊外に家を買ったものだから、通勤に２時間もかかる。
example_sentences.english: Because I bought a house in the suburbs, the commute to work takes two hours.

example_sentences.japanese: すみません、今仕事をしているものだから、また後でかけ直します。
example_sentences.english: Sorry, because I am working right now, I will call you back later.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は人が多いものだから、週末に行くのはあまりお勧めしません。
example_sentences.english: I would not recommend going on the weekends, because it is usually crowded on weekends.

example_sentences.japanese: 生の魚は苦手なものだから、寿司は食べられない。
example_sentences.english: I can't eat sushi because I don't like raw fish.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は新人なものだから、まだこの会社のルールをよくわかっていない。
example_sentences.english: Because he is new, he doesn't really understand the rules of this company.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は夕方から娘の発表会があるもので、私はそろそろ帰りますね。
example_sentences.english: Because my daughter has a recital this evening, I am going to go home soon.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近は日本語を話す機会が減ってきているもんで、日本語を忘れてきた感じがする。
example_sentences.english: I feel as if I have forgotten some Japanese, because I have fewer opportunities to speak Japanese these days.

example_sentences.japanese: まあ、安いもんで...
example_sentences.english: Well, because it's cheap…

example_sentences.japanese: 税関に引っかかったものだから、遅くなってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Because I was stopped by the customs officer, I ended up being late.

example_sentences.japanese: 素人が制作したものだから、やっぱりすぐに壊れてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Because it is something created by a novice, as expected, it broke right away.

example_sentences.japanese: 英語が苦手なものだから、海外旅行に行くのは楽しくない。
example_sentences.english: Because I am bad at English, taking trips abroad isn't fun.

example_sentences.japanese: 墨で黒く塗ってしまったものだから、何て書いてあったか分からない。
example_sentences.english: Because it is painted black with ink, I don't know what was written.

example_sentences.japanese: 寸法を測り間違えたものだから、袖が長すぎて困ります。
example_sentences.english: Because the measurement was done incorrectly, I am stuck with sleeves that are too long.

example_sentences.japanese: テレビの番組で宣伝したものだから、次の日お客さんが殺到しました。
example_sentences.english: Because of the publicity from the TV program, customers flooded in the next day.

example_sentences.japanese: 線路で立ち往生したものだから、帰りたくても帰れない状況です。
example_sentences.english: Because the train line came to a standstill, I am in a position where even if I wanted to go home, I couldn't.

example_sentences.japanese: 全速力で走ったものだから、次の日は全身筋肉痛だ。
example_sentences.english: Because I ran at full speed, my whole body was sore the next day.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は何でも率直に言うものだから、ある人たちからは嫌われています。
example_sentences.english: Because he says everything frankly, he is disliked by certain people.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨で登板予定がスライドしたものだから、立ち上がりなかなか調子が出なかった。
example_sentences.english: Because rain changed the batting arrangement, the pitcher isn't doing very well.

example_sentences.japanese: 道が渋滞していたものだから、時間通りに来られませんでした。遅れて来てすみません。
example_sentences.english: Because there was a lot of traffic, I could not come in time. Sorry for being late.

general_translation: Because, My excuse is, My explanation is
formation: Verb + ものですから(1) +  Phrase［い］Adjective + ものですから(1) +  Phrase［な］Adjective + な + ものですから(1) +  PhraseNoun + な + ものですから(1) +  Phrase(1) もので、もんで、もんですから
casual_structure: Verb + ものですから(1) +  Phrase［い］Adjective + ものですから(1) +  Phrase［な］Adjective + な + ものですから(1) +  PhraseNoun + な + ものですから(1) +  Phrase(1) もので、もんで、もんですから
explanation: A strong phrase that indicates the thing which can be determined as (A) as being an excuse or reason for something.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: 売上が良かったものですから、発注しすぎてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Because sales were good, I accidentally over-ordered.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔大工として働いていたものですから、リフォームなら私に任せてください！
example_sentences.english: Because I used to work as a carpenter, if you are renovating, leave it to me!

example_sentences.japanese: この道路は狭いものですから、スピードを落として運転をしてください。
example_sentences.english: Because this road is narrow, please drive slowly.

example_sentences.japanese: 苦いものが苦手なものですから、コーヒーやお茶は飲めません。
example_sentences.english: Because I don't like bitter things, I can't drink things such as coffee and tea.

example_sentences.japanese: この車は中古なものですから、不具合だらけです。
example_sentences.english: Because this car is second hand, it is full of defects.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は日本に住んでいたもので、日本語はまあまあ話せます。
example_sentences.english: Because he lived in Japan, he speaks Japanese fairly well.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は運転をするのが嫌いなもんで、出かけるときにはいつもタクシーと電車を使っている。
example_sentences.english: Because I don't like driving, I always use taxis and trains when I go out.

example_sentences.japanese: いや、危なかったもんで...
example_sentences.english: Well, because it was dangerous…

example_sentences.japanese: 育児は初めてなものですから、いろいろと教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Because it is my first time raising a child, please teach me various things.

example_sentences.japanese: 熊の足跡があったものですから、山に入るのはやめました。
example_sentences.english: Because there were bear tracks, I gave up on going into the mountains.

example_sentences.japanese: アクセントが違ったものですから、地元の方ではないのかと思いました。
example_sentences.english: Because his accent was different, I thought, he isn't from my hometown.

example_sentences.japanese: 明け方まで仕事をしていたものですから、もう眠いです。
example_sentences.english: Because I was doing work until dawn, I am already sleepy.

example_sentences.japanese: 脂ものが苦手なものですから、あの店のラーメンは食べられません。
example_sentences.english: Because I dislike fatty things, I cannot eat that shop's ramen.

example_sentences.japanese: 怪しい格好をしていたものですから、疑ってしまってごめんなさい。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry that I doubted you because you were being suspicious.

example_sentences.japanese: 薄暗かったものですから、家を探すのに時間がかかってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Because it was dim/gloomy, looking for the house unfortunately took a lot of time.

example_sentences.japanese: 銀行の窓口がとても混んでいたものですから、遅くなってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Because the ticket window at the bank was crowded, I was (unfortunately) late.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女に憧れていたものですから、お会い出来るなんて光栄です。
example_sentences.english: Because I have admired her, it is such an honor to be able to meet her.

example_sentences.japanese: 天体観測が趣味なものですから、新しい望遠鏡が欲しいのです。
example_sentences.english: Because my hobby is astronomical observation, I want a new telescope.

example_sentences.japanese: この広場では花火が禁止なものですから、他の場所を探さなければなりません。
example_sentences.english: Because fireworks are prohibited in this plaza, we have to find another place (to set them off).

general_translation: Strong judgement, There is something, Feel strongly that
formation: Verb + ものがある［い］Adjective + ものがある［な］Adjective + な +ものがある
casual_structure: Verb + ものがある［い］Adjective + ものがある［な］Adjective + な +ものがある
polite_structure: Verb + ものがあります［い］Adjective + ものがあります［な］Adjective + な +ものがあります
explanation: A structure showing that (A) is definitely a thing that exists, or felt strongly about.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: モナリザには、神秘的なものがあるよ。
example_sentences.english: I feel strongly that that (the) Mona Lisa is mysterious.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画は人の心を動かすものがある。
example_sentences.english: This film has something that moves people's hearts.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の話には納得いかないものがある。
example_sentences.english: There is something about his story that I don't agree with.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分が好きなことを仕事にできるのは、嬉しいものがある。
example_sentences.english: There is something delightful about being able to do what you love for a living.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供だけで川で遊ばせるのは、危険なものがある。
example_sentences.english: There is something dangerous about letting children play in the river alone.

example_sentences.japanese: 文房具には魅力的なものがある。
example_sentences.english: I feel strongly that stationery is fascinating.

example_sentences.japanese: この絵って、うまく説明できないけどすばらしいものがあるよ。
example_sentences.english: I can't explain well, but this painting gives me a strong feeling of amazement.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の遺した言葉には考えさせられるものがあった。
example_sentences.english: I felt strongly that his last words were inspiring.

example_sentences.japanese: 売店には全然売れないものがある。
example_sentences.english: For a shop, there are things that doesn't sell well at all.

example_sentences.japanese: あの店には、派手好きにはたまらないものがある。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but feel strongly that that store is attention-seeking.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらのお店のメニューには、人を引き付けるものがある。
example_sentences.english: I feel strongly that this restaurant's menu will bring in people.

example_sentences.japanese: 君の俳句にはなんとも言えないものがある。
example_sentences.english: (I feel strongly that) there is something about your haiku that words cannot describe.

example_sentences.japanese: あの商品には、単なる流行とは言えないものがある。
example_sentences.english: I feel strongly that those goods can't be called a simple fad.

example_sentences.japanese: 方言には同じ日本語とは思えないものがある。
example_sentences.english: For a dialect, I feel strongly that one could think that it is not even Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の伝統芸能には、心を動かすものがある。
example_sentences.english: In Japanese traditional art, there is something that really moves your heart.

example_sentences.japanese: 美味しいものを食べるため、寒い中行列に並ぶのはつらいものがある。
example_sentences.english: It is very hard to stand in line in the bitter cold, just to eat something delicious. (strong judgment)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の運動神経の良さは目を見張るものがある。
example_sentences.english: His athleticism is remarkable.

general_translation: Tendency, Trend, Inclination
formation: Verb［る］(1) + 傾向（けいこう）［い］Adjective + 傾向（けいこう）［な］Adjective + な + 傾向（けいこう）Noun + の + 傾向（けいこう）(1) Verb［た］
casual_structure: Verb［る］(1) + 傾向（けいこう）［い］Adjective + 傾向（けいこう）［な］Adjective + な + 傾向（けいこう）Noun + の + 傾向（けいこう）(1) Verb［た］
explanation: A formal phrase highlighting that a trend exists toward (A). (A) is being inclined toward.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: だが、調べたデータによると、そのようなけいこうも見られる。
example_sentences.english: But, according to the research data, trends like that can also be observed.

example_sentences.japanese: この国では首都に近づけば近づくほど物価が上がっていくけいこうがある。
example_sentences.english: In this country, there is a tendency of prices rising as you get closer to the capital.

example_sentences.japanese: 鬱で悩まされている人は気分の浮き沈みが激しいけいこうがある。
example_sentences.english: People suffering from depression are inclined to have severe mood swings.

example_sentences.japanese: あの会社が発売する教科書は使いやすくてユニークなけいこうがあると言われている。
example_sentences.english: It is said that textbooks released by that company have a tendency to be user-friendly and unique.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近は世界中で小家族化のけいこうがある。
example_sentences.english: Recently, there has been a trend toward smaller families around the world.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近ではコンピューターやスマホが文字を自動変換してくれるので、漢字の書き方を忘れてしまうけいこうがみられる。
example_sentences.english: Recently, computers and smartphones automatically convert characters, so people tend to forget how to write kanji characters.

example_sentences.japanese: 年月が経つとともにこのけいこうが見られるようになった。
example_sentences.english: As the years passed, this trend became visible.

example_sentences.japanese: ハイエンドスマホの需要は最近ますます低下のけいこうにある。
example_sentences.english: The demand for high-end smartphones has been in a declining trend recently.

example_sentences.japanese: 健康問題の数量は老化とともに増加するけいこうがある。
example_sentences.english: The amount of health problems (that arise) has the tendency to increase with aging.

example_sentences.japanese: 次に、インフレが加速すると同時に物価も増加するけいこうがある。
example_sentences.english: Then, while inflation accelerates, prices of commodities also have the tendency to increase.

example_sentences.japanese: 人間は無意識に外観で人を判断してしまうけいこうが強い。
example_sentences.english: People have a strong inclination to unconsciously judge others by appearance.

example_sentences.japanese: 普通の時計に代わって、スマートウォッチを使用するけいこうが続いており、２０１９年のスマートウォッチの予測される売上は２億５千万になるだろう。
example_sentences.english: The trend of using smart watches instead of regular watches continues and the forecasted sales of 2019 are as high as 250 million.

example_sentences.japanese: 以下の「昼食と学力の関係」というグラフによると、お腹が空いた子供は成績が悪くなるけいこうにあるようだ。
example_sentences.english: According to the 'Relation of Academic Ability and Lunch' graph below, it seems that hungry children fall into the trend of getting worse grades (than children who are not hungry).

example_sentences.japanese: ほとんどの４０歳以下の人々はカジュアルな話にら抜き言葉を多用するけいこうがあるといえるだろう。
example_sentences.english: It is fair to say that most people younger than 40 years old have a tendency to frequently use 'ra'-removed words in casual conversations.

example_sentences.japanese: より新しいスマホの機種では、電池は取り替えられなくなっているという一般的けいこうが見られる。
example_sentences.english: With newer smartphone models, one could say that there is a general trend of batteries being non-replaceable.

example_sentences.japanese: 大人になると、どうしても他の人より自分の意見の方が正しいと思ってしまうけいこうが見られるのだ。
example_sentences.english: Upon becoming an adult, people have a tendency to think that, no matter what, their opinion is more correct than other people.

example_sentences.japanese: 一方、ＨＤＤはＳＳＤほど効率的ではないけいこうがある。
example_sentences.english: On the other hand, an HDD has the tendency to not be as efficient as an SSD.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は少子化の傾向にある。
example_sentences.english: Japan is experiencing a declining birthrate. (Ongoing trend)

example_sentences.japanese: この研究によると、勤務時間が短いほうが仕事の効率がよくなる傾向にあるようだ。
example_sentences.english: According to this study, shorter work hours tend to improve work efficiency. (Statistics)

general_translation: Be worthy of, Deserving of, Amounts to
formation: Verb + に値（あたい）するNoun +  に値（あたい）するVerb + に値（あたい）する + NounNoun +  に値（あたい）する + Noun
casual_structure: Verb + に値（あたい）するNoun +  に値（あたい）するVerb + に値（あたい）する + NounNoun +  に値（あたい）する + Noun
explanation: An expression used to say that something has value, both positively and negatively.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の行動は、尊敬にあたいする。
example_sentences.english: His actions are worthy of respect.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたは、総理にあたいする人間です。
example_sentences.english: You are a person worthy of being prime minister.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の論文は、十分に出版にあたいする内容だ。
example_sentences.english: Her thesis has sufficient content that is worthy of publication.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの何気なく発した発言が、詐欺罪にあたいするんですよ。
example_sentences.english: Your remarks which you spout off so casually amount to fraud.

example_sentences.japanese: オリンピック選手にあたいする技術を、あなたは持っています。
example_sentences.english: You possess skills worthy of an Olympian.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の髪色は、校則違反にあたいするのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if my hair color amounts to a violation of the school rules.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの作品が、彼の作品にあたいする訳がないじゃん！
example_sentences.english: There is no way that your work amounts to the same level as his!

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の冷静な判断と的確な指示は、リーダーとして信頼にあたいするものだった。
example_sentences.english: His cool judgement and precise instructions were worthy of trust as a leader.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年１年の成績に基づいて、あなたがプロレベルにあたいするかどうかを検討します。
example_sentences.english: Based on this year’s performance, we will consider if you are worthy of being professional level.

example_sentences.japanese: 顧客からの信頼を得るには、それにあたいする行動と誠意が求められます。
example_sentences.english: To gain trust from customers, actions and sincerity worthy of that trust are required.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の寝坊の言い訳、「宇宙人にさらわれたから」は、もはや表彰にあたいするレベルの発想力だと思う。
example_sentences.english: His excuse for oversleeping, that ‘I was abducted by aliens’, is a creative level which is award-worthy.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ、その日の料理の出来栄えがミシュラン三つ星にあたいするとしても、常に一貫した料理の質でなければ、認定されることはない。
example_sentences.english: For example, even if that day’s cooking was worthy of three Michelin stars, it would not be recognized as such unless that standard was consistently maintained.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のこれまでの努力は、間違いなく高い評価にあたいするものであり、私たちはその功績を正当に認めるべきだと思います。
example_sentences.english: His efforts until now are unmistakably worthy of high praise, and I believe that we should duly recognize his achievements.

example_sentences.japanese: 日々の地道な努力と、どんな困難にも屈しない姿勢は、若者たちの模範として称されるにあたいするだろう。
example_sentences.english: Her daily efforts and indomitability in the face of difficulties is worthy of praise as a role model for young people.

example_sentences.japanese: このネックレスは、古代エジプトの遺物にも劣らぬ価値を持ち、博物館での永久保存にあたいする逸品だと言えるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: It could be said that this necklace is a masterpiece worthy of permanent preservation in a museum and of value which would not be inferior to even the relics of Ancient Egypt.

example_sentences.japanese: これは読むに値する論文だ。
example_sentences.english: This paper is worth reading.

example_sentences.japanese: その手法は詐欺に値するから、見直したほうがいいと思いますよ。
example_sentences.english: That method is worthy of being considered as a scam, so I think you should reconsider.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の行動は尊敬に値しない。人として当たり前なことをしたまでだ。
example_sentences.english: His actions are not worthy of respect. He simply did what any normal person would do.

example_sentences.japanese: あの舞台は大根役者の集まりなので、見るに値しない。
example_sentences.english: That play is a gathering of bad actors, so it is not worth watching.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の不動産の価値は滅多に上がらない。
example_sentences.english: The value of real estate in Japan rarely rises.

example_sentences.japanese: 商品に値札をつけるのを忘れた。
example_sentences.english: I forgot to put a price tag on a product.

example_sentences.japanese: 村田さんの作品に値をつけるのはとても難しいと言われている。
example_sentences.english: It is said that it is hard to put worth on Murata-san’s works.

general_translation: Extremely, Very, Really, It can't be helped
formation: Verb ［て］ + しょうがない［い］Adjective［て］+ しょうがない［な］Adjective + で + しょうがない
casual_structure: Verb ［て］ + しょうがない［い］Adjective［て］+ しょうがない［な］Adjective + で + しょうがない
explanation: A common phrase highlighting that there is no way for anything to be done about (A), or that it cannot be helped.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: いつも同じものをわすれてしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but always forget the same thing (again and again).

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語が上手になりたくてしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but want to become good at Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋が暑くてしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: My room is extremely hot.

example_sentences.japanese: スイーツが好きでしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: I love sweets so much that it can't be helped.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は今妊娠をしているが、寿司を食べたくてしかたがない。
example_sentences.english: Although I am pregnant right now, I really want to eat sushi.

example_sentences.japanese: 眠くてしかたがなかったので、少しだけ昼寝をしました。
example_sentences.english: Since I was extremely sleepy, I took a small nap.

example_sentences.japanese: この古いパソコンは不便でしかたがないから捨てることにします。
example_sentences.english: Since this old computer is extremely useless, I will throw it away.

example_sentences.japanese: ゲームがしたくてしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: I want to play video games so bad it can't be helped.

example_sentences.japanese: たのしくてしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: Extremely fun.(So fun it can't be helped)

example_sentences.japanese: あの望遠鏡がほしくてしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: I really want that telescope.(I want that telescope so much that it can't be helped)

example_sentences.japanese: 包帯をしているから、かゆくてしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: Because it is bandaged, it is extremely itchy.(Because I am wearing a bandage, it itches so much that it can't be helped)

example_sentences.japanese: マラソン大会にでたくてしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: I really want to join a long distance race competition.(I want to join the long distance race competition so much that it can't be helped)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はめだちたくてしょうがないのだろう。
example_sentences.english: He really wants to stand out, doesn't he.(He stands out so much that it can't be helped, doesn't he)

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の家の人がやかましくてしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: The neighbors are very noisy.(The neighbors are so noisy that it can't be helped)

example_sentences.japanese: レインコートを着ると、汗をかいてしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: When I wear a raincoat, I really sweat.(I sweat so much that it can't be helped)

example_sentences.japanese: 工事の音がうるさくてしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: The construction noises are very loud.(The construction noises are so loud that it can't be helped)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は早く種をまきたくてしょうがないのだろう。
example_sentences.english: That person really wants to sow seeds early, don't they.(That person wants to sow seeds so much that it can't be helped)

example_sentences.japanese: あの店員さんの喋り方を真似したくてしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but want to imitate that clerk's way of speaking.

general_translation: At least, It's better than..., One should feel grateful for
formation: Verb + だけまし + だ［い］Adjective + だけまし + だ［な］Adjective + な + だけまし + だNoun + である + だけまし + だ
casual_structure: Verb + だけまし + だ［い］Adjective + だけまし + だ［な］Adjective + な + だけまし + だNoun + である + だけまし + だ
polite_structure: Verb + だけまし + です［い］Adjective + だけまし + です［な］Adjective + な + だけまし + ですNoun + である + だけまし + です
explanation: A construction showing that just (A), or only (A) is preferable to possible alternatives, so one should be grateful.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: ご馳走とは言えないが、食べるものがあるだけましだ。
example_sentences.english: I can't say that I feasted, but at least I had something to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気はあまり良くないが、久しぶりに旅行に来れただけましだ。
example_sentences.english: Although the weather isn't the best, I should be grateful that I am able to travel for the first time in a long time.

example_sentences.japanese: このアパートはボロボロだけど、職場に近いだけましだ。
example_sentences.english: This apartment is a wreck, but at least it is close to my work place.

example_sentences.japanese: 味覚はないかもしれないが、元気なだけましだ。
example_sentences.english: Although I can't taste, at least I am feeling well.

example_sentences.japanese: 古い校舎だが、冷房があるだけましだ。
example_sentences.english: The school building is old, but at least it has air conditioning.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな大事故が起きたのだから、命があるだけましだ。
example_sentences.english: Since such a big accident occured, you should be grateful that you are still alive.

example_sentences.japanese: 泥棒に入られたが、金庫が無事なだけましだ。
example_sentences.english: A robber broke in, but I should be grateful that the safe is intact.

example_sentences.japanese: 上手な部員はいなくても、部に後輩がいるだけましです。
example_sentences.english: Even if there are no skilled staff, there are at least some kouhai in the department.

example_sentences.japanese: 料理は微妙でも、裁縫が上手なだけましだ。
example_sentences.english: Even if their cooking is questionable, at least they are good at sewing.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はやり方が強引ですが、暴力を振るわないだけましです。
example_sentences.english: His way of doing it is overbearing, but you should be grateful that he isn't violent.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の旦那は料理もしない。あなたの旦那は料理をしてくれるだけましだ。
example_sentences.english: My husband doesn't even cook. At least your husband cooks for you.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の口実はいいとは言えませんが、嘘をつかないだけましです。
example_sentences.english: It can't be said that her excuses are good, but at least she doesn't lie.

example_sentences.japanese: あの講師の教え方は上手とは言えないが、黒板の字が綺麗なだけましだ。
example_sentences.english: It can't be said that that lecturer's way of teaching is good, but at least the characters they write on the chalkboard are nice.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事は辛いかもしれないけど、公務員は安定しているだけましだ。
example_sentences.english: Your job is probably tough, but a public servant's job is stable at least.

example_sentences.japanese: 少額だとしても、お小遣いをもらえるだけましだ。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is a small amount, you should be grateful you are receiving an allowance.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はいつもより寒いけど、風が吹いていないだけまだましだ。
example_sentences.english: It is colder than usual today, but at least it's not windy.

general_translation: Luckily, Fortunately
formation: 幸（さいわ）い + （、(1)）+ Phrase幸（さいわ）いなことに(2) + Phrase(1)に、にも(2) 幸（さいわ）いだったことに
casual_structure: 幸（さいわ）い + （、(1)）+ Phrase幸（さいわ）いなことに(2) + Phrase(1)に、にも(2) 幸（さいわ）いだったことに
explanation: An expression indicating that (A) is fortunate. To that (A) is a happy thing, (B).
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: さいわいなことに遊ぶ時間が結構ある。
example_sentences.english: Fortunately, I have quite a lot of time to enjoy myself.

example_sentences.japanese: さいわい、ライフジャケットを着ていたので溺れずに済んだ。
example_sentences.english: Fortunately, I had my life jacket on so I did not drown.

example_sentences.japanese: さいわい、留学する前に大親友に会う事ができました。
example_sentences.english: Luckily, I was able to meet my best friend before going abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: さいわいなことに、おじいちゃんの手術は成功しました。
example_sentences.english: Fortunately, my grandpa's surgery was a success.

example_sentences.japanese: さいわいなことに、優しい人に道を教えてもらったので、終電を逃すことなく家に帰る事ができました。
example_sentences.english: Fortunately, a kind person showed me the way and I was able to get home without missing the last train.

example_sentences.japanese: さいわいなことに、船上に医者がいた。
example_sentences.english: Luckily, there was a doctor on board the ship.

example_sentences.japanese: さいわいなことに人を集めることができました。
example_sentences.english: Luckily, I was able to gather people.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はさいわい、エアバッグのおかげで怪我をせずに済んだ。
example_sentences.english: Luckily for him, thanks to the airbag, he got away without injury.

example_sentences.japanese: さいわいなことに元気な赤ちゃんが生まれました。
example_sentences.english: Fortunately, a healthy baby was born.

example_sentences.japanese: さいわい、美術館が閉まる前に入れました。
example_sentences.english: Luckily, I was able to get into the art museum before it closed.

example_sentences.japanese: さいわい、貿易は順調です。何も心配はいりません。
example_sentences.english: Fortunately, (international) trade is doing well. You do not need to worry about anything.

example_sentences.japanese: さいわいなことに、謝ったら許してもらえたので安心しました。
example_sentences.english: Fortunately, when I apologized they forgave me, so I am at ease.

example_sentences.japanese: さいわいなことに案内してもらえたので、無事辿り着けました。
example_sentences.english: I was fortunate enough to have someone tell me the way, so I arrived safely.

example_sentences.japanese: さいわい、部長の機嫌が良かったから助かったよ。
example_sentences.english: Fortunately, the head of the department was in a good mood, so I made it through (the day).

example_sentences.japanese: さいわい、血はすぐに止まったから、選手交代は必要ない。
example_sentences.english: Luckily, the bleeding stopped, so there was no need for a substitution.

example_sentences.japanese: 亡き父からもらった財布が盗まれたが、さいわいなことに、現金を抜かれただけで、財布自体は警察がすぐに見つけてくれた。
example_sentences.english: The wallet I received from my late father was stolen, but fortunately only the money was taken and the wallet itself was recovered quickly by the police.

example_sentences.japanese: 嬉しいことに、小さい頃からずっと行きたかった大学に入れる事ができた。
example_sentences.english: To my delight, I was able to get into the university I had always wanted to go to since I was a little.

example_sentences.japanese: 悲しいことに、おばあちゃんから貰ったネックレスを無くしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Sadly, I lost a necklace that my grandmother gave me.

general_translation: If, If it is true that
formation: Verb + ようでは(2) + (Negative Result)(2) ようじゃ
casual_structure: Verb + ようでは(2) + (Negative Result)(2) ようじゃ
explanation: An expression stating that if something is determined to be the manner of (A), then (B) will also be the case.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: そこまで甘やかすようでは、ろくな大人にならないですよ。
example_sentences.english: If you are spoiled to that extent, you can't become a decent adult. (...it appears that...)

example_sentences.japanese: こんな毎日同じミスをするようでは、いつまで経っても店長にはなれませんよ。
example_sentences.english: If you keep making the same mistake everyday, you will never be able to become a manager.

example_sentences.japanese: これらの文法が分からないようでは、Ｎ２に合格することはできません。
example_sentences.english: If you do not understand these grammar points, you will not be able to pass N2.

example_sentences.japanese: これぐらいの高さで怖がっているようでは消防士にはなれませんよ。
example_sentences.english: You can't become a firefighter if you're afraid of heights like this.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに日時を間違えるようでは、仕事なんてできないよ。
example_sentences.english: If you can make these kinds of mistakes about the time and date, you can't do your job. (...it appears that...)

example_sentences.japanese: こんな問題も解けないようでは、次のテストが思いやられる。
example_sentences.english: If you can't solve a problem like this, I am worried about your next test. (...it appears that...)

example_sentences.japanese: 人の成功を羨んでいるようでは、自分の成功にはつながらない。
example_sentences.english: If you envy other people's achievements, it won't lead to your own achievements. (...it appears that...)

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強の日課を守れないようでは、試験に受からないと思います。
example_sentences.english: If you can't keep up with your daily study routine, I don't think you can pass the test. (...it appears that...)

example_sentences.japanese: この程度で吐き気がするようでは、もっと強い薬は使えない。
example_sentences.english: If you are having this degree of nausea, you cannot use a stronger medicine. (...it appears that...)

example_sentences.japanese: 緊張して実力を発揮できないようでは、この世界では通用しない。
example_sentences.english: If you get nervous and can't demonstrate your true ability, you will not make it in this world. (...it appears that...)

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事と休息のバランスが取れないようでは、体を壊してしまいます。
example_sentences.english: If you cannot balance work and rest, your body will end up breaking down. (...it appears that...)

example_sentences.japanese: 反省する気がないようでは、今後の成長は見込めない。
example_sentences.english: If you do not feel like reflecting on your actions, you cannot anticipate growing any further. (...it appears that...)

example_sentences.japanese: 日当たりが悪いようでは、部屋の借り手はなかなか見つからないと思います。
example_sentences.english: If this place doesn't get enough sun, I don't think you will find a renter for the room. (...it appears that...)

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ん坊のおむつを替えられないようでは、とてもイクメン（子育てする男性）とは呼べない。
example_sentences.english: If he can't change a baby's diapers, he can't be called a man who can raise a child. (...it appears that...)

example_sentences.japanese: この程度の距離で音を上げているようでは、本格的な登山に挑戦することなどできない。
example_sentences.english: If you are going to give up at this distance, you won't be able to take on the challenge of real mountain climbing. (...it appears that...)
