general_translation: as one would expect, only natural, that is just like..., even
formation: さすが + （に）+ Phraseさすが + （の）+ Noun
casual_structure: さすが + （に）+ Phraseさすが + （の）+ Noun
explanation: A short exclamation which often highlights that (A) is just as the speaker had thought, or exactly what was expected.
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: いいカーブだ。さすがダルビッシュ。
example_sentences.english: What a nice curveball. That's just like Darvish.

example_sentences.japanese: すごい！さすが先輩！
example_sentences.english: Wow! That's what I would expect from you senpai!

example_sentences.japanese: さすがに今日は雨が降りすぎだろ...
example_sentences.english: As one would expect, it is raining way too much today.

example_sentences.japanese: さすがの君でもこの問題は難しいだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even for someone like you, this problem is difficult, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: さすがに食いすぎたな。椅子から立てない。
example_sentences.english: As expected, I ate too much. I can't get up from a chair.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなおめでたい席に、さすがにあの格好はない。
example_sentences.english: As one would expect, that is not suitable for this highly auspicious seat.

example_sentences.japanese: 一流のオーケストラの演奏はさすがですね。
example_sentences.english: The performance was as would be expected from a first rate orchestra.

example_sentences.japanese: さすがに落し物が多すぎる。注意しないと。
example_sentences.english: As one would expect, you lose too many things. You need to be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: 指圧のしすぎで、さすがに親指が痛い。
example_sentences.english: I gave too many massages and as would be expected, my thumbs hurt.

example_sentences.japanese: 涙が出るほど夕焼けが綺麗だ。さすが神様だ。
example_sentences.english: The sunset was beautiful enough to elicit tears. As one would expect from the gods.

example_sentences.japanese: さすがの君でも、あれだけ食べればカロリー取り過ぎです。
example_sentences.english: Even as would be expected from you, consuming that many calories is too much.

example_sentences.japanese: 会話が漫才のようだ。さすが関西人。
example_sentences.english: The conversation was like talking with a comedian. That's just like a person from Kansai.

example_sentences.japanese: さすがの神戸牛だ。世界一脂の乗った肉だ。
example_sentences.english: As one would expect from Kobe beef, it has the best marbling in the world.

example_sentences.japanese: さすがの解説者も、今日の試合の結末は予想できなかった。
example_sentences.english: Even (an established) commentator couldn't have predicted the ending of today's match.

example_sentences.japanese: さすがに空手の稽古を積んできただけに、１５ｋｇのダンベルは持てる。
example_sentences.english: As might be expected from a person who trains karate, he can lift 15kg dumbbells.

example_sentences.japanese: さすが田中くん！発注ミスの天才だね！
example_sentences.english: As expected, Tanaka-kun! You are a genius at making order errors!

general_translation: It is true...but, although, but
formation: Verb + ことは + Verb(*) + が(1)［い］Adjective + ことは + ［い］Adjective(*) + が(1)［な］Adjective + なことは + ［な］Adjective(*) + だが(1)Noun + なことは + Noun(*) + だが(1)(1) けど、けども、けれど、けれども(*) The same Adjective, Verb, or Noun
casual_structure: Verb + ことは + Verb(*) + が(1)［い］Adjective + ことは + ［い］Adjective(*) + が(1)［な］Adjective + なことは + ［な］Adjective(*) + だが(1)Noun + なことは + Noun(*) + だが(1)(1) けど、けども、けれど、けれども(*) The same Adjective, Verb, or Noun
explanation: A structure which indicates that that which is (A) is true in general, but (B).
lesson_topic: It Is The Way It Is

example_sentences.japanese: パターンがあることはあるが、なかなか解読できません。
example_sentences.english: It is true that there are patterns, but I can't easily decode them.

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字は読めることは読めるが、簡単な漢字しか読めないです。
example_sentences.english: It is true that I can read kanji, but I can only read easy ones.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい家は広いことは広いけど、家具が多いから狭く見える。
example_sentences.english: It is true that my new house is spacious, but because there is a lot of furniture, it looks small.

example_sentences.japanese: このスマホは便利であることは便利であるけど、本体がデカすぎて片手では操作できない。
example_sentences.english: It is true that this smartphone is useful, but because it is big, I can't use it with just one hand.

example_sentences.japanese: ここは道路なことは道路だけど、狭すぎて車が通れない。
example_sentences.english: It is true that this road is a road, but it is too narrow that a car can't pass through.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨に濡れたことは濡れたが、大したことはなかった。
example_sentences.english: It is true that it got soaked by the rain, but it wasn't a big deal.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱が出たことは出たが、インフルエンザではありませんでした。
example_sentences.english: It is true that I had a fever, but it wasn't the flu.

example_sentences.japanese: 締切を延ばせたことは延ばせたが、余裕ないですよ。
example_sentences.english: It is true that the deadline was extended, but it will still be tight.

example_sentences.japanese: ボルトは外れることは外れたが、これ以上分解できない。
example_sentences.english: It is true that the bolts were able to be removed, but it cannot be dismantled any further.

example_sentences.japanese: カタログを一通り見ることは見たが、欲しいものがない。
example_sentences.english: It is true that I looked at the catalog from start to finish, but there isn't anything I want.

example_sentences.japanese: 一休みすることはしたが、全然疲れが取れません。
example_sentences.english: It is true that I took a break, but I am still really tired.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強を始めたことは始めたが、全然集中していない。
example_sentences.english: It is true that I started studying, but I am not focusing at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 引越しはしたことはしたが、こっちの家も欠陥住宅だった。
example_sentences.english: It is true that I moved, but this house has also turned out to be defective.

example_sentences.japanese: 岩村：「日本語が分かりますか？」 土井：「分かることは分かりますが、簡単な言葉だけです。」
example_sentences.english: Iwamura: 'Do you understand Japanese?' Doi: 'It is true that I understand it, but only simple vocabulary.'

example_sentences.japanese: 藤本：「守口さんって、優しい人らしい。」石川：「優しいことは優しいが、自分の家族に対してだけ。」
example_sentences.english: Fujimoto: 'I have heard that Moriguchi-san is a nice person.' Ishikawa: 'Well, it is true that Moriguchi-san is nice, but only towards her family.'

example_sentences.japanese: 遠藤：「北村さんって、日本に行ったことある？」 北村：「行ったことは行ったけど、東京の空港を見ただけだよ。」
example_sentences.english: Endo: 'Kitamura-san, have you ever been to Japan?' Kitamura: 'It is true that I have been there, but I have only seen Tokyo Airport.'

general_translation: Even more or further, Again, More and more
formation: さらに + Phrase
casual_structure: さらに + Phrase
explanation: A somewhat formal expression indicating that in addition to (A), (B). Often implying a surprising increase in amount or intensity.

example_sentences.japanese: 税金がさらに高くなった。
example_sentences.english: Taxes got higher again. (more and more)

example_sentences.japanese: 電気代がさらに高くなった。
example_sentences.english: The electricity bill has become even more expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: 刺身には刺身専用の醤油をかけると、さらに美味しくなります。
example_sentences.english: Sashimi tastes even better when served with soy sauce specially designed for sashimi.

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンにウイルス対策ソフトを入れたら、パソコンがさらに遅くなった。
example_sentences.english: When I installed antivirus software on my computer, my computer became even slower.

example_sentences.japanese: さらに気を付けてもらわないと困ります。
example_sentences.english: There will be trouble if you aren't more careful. (more and more)

example_sentences.japanese: さらに給与が上がり、とても助かります。
example_sentences.english: My salary has gone up even more and that is very helpful. (more and more)

example_sentences.japanese: さらに乾燥がひどくなり、保湿するのが大変だ。
example_sentences.english: The dry air has become even more terrible and moisturizing is difficult. (more and more)

example_sentences.japanese: 国家からの融資でさらにグラフェンの研究を進める。
example_sentences.english: Financing from the state will push the graphene research further. (more and more)

example_sentences.japanese: 雪解けにつれて川や湖の水のかさがさらに増す一方だ。
example_sentences.english: As the snow thaws, the quantity of water in lakes and rivers keeps on increasing further. (more and more)

example_sentences.japanese: スマホを見る時間がさらに増えた。依存症だな。
example_sentences.english: The time I spend looking at my smartphone has increased even more. I have become dependent on it, haven't I.

example_sentences.japanese: さらに加速がよくなったが、公道では役に立ちません。
example_sentences.english: The acceleration has become even better, but that isn't helpful on public roads. (more and more)

example_sentences.japanese: さらに基準が高くなるらしく、合わせるのが大変です。
example_sentences.english: The standard will apparently become even more expensive, making it difficult to match. (more and more)

example_sentences.japanese: 肉体をさらに強化できれば、来年は優勝も夢ではない。
example_sentences.english: If you can strengthen your body more and more, victory next year won't just be a dream.

example_sentences.japanese: さらに行列が長くなり、お店の人も整理しきれなくなってしまった。
example_sentences.english: As the line grew even more, it became impossible for that store's staff to regulate everyone. (more and more)

example_sentences.japanese: さらにクーラーがきいてきて、風邪をひきそうだ。
example_sentences.english: As the air conditioner runs more and more, I appear to be catching a cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 病院に行き始めてから彼は更に元気になった。
example_sentences.english: Ever since he started going to the hospital, he has gotten even better.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事をクビになって更に生活が苦しくなった。
example_sentences.english: My life became even more difficult after being fired.

general_translation: (At) most , (At) best, No more than, Barely
formation: せいぜい  + Phrase
casual_structure: せいぜい  + Phrase
explanation: A strong construction implying that something is at most, or at best (A). In every essence, (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「３８歳だって？せいぜい３０くらいなものだと思っていたよ。」
example_sentences.english: '38 years old you say? I thought he was around 30 at most!'

example_sentences.japanese: このバッグはせいぜい千円くらいだろう。
example_sentences.english: This bag probably costs 1000 yen at most.

example_sentences.japanese: せいぜい３ヶ月は働いてもらわないと困ります。
example_sentences.english: It would be a problem if you could only work for 3 months at the most.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が作れる料理はせいぜいこんなもんです。
example_sentences.english: This is at best what I can cook.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は今働いているから、勉強できても一日にせいぜい一時間ぐらいしか勉強ができない。
example_sentences.english: Since I am working now, even if I could study, I can only study 1 hour a day at most.

example_sentences.japanese: 「電車が来ないうちに観光出来るのはせいぜい４時間ぐらい。」
example_sentences.english: 'Before the train comes, we can do sightseeing for four hours at most.'

example_sentences.japanese: 証人：「加害者はたぶんせいぜい３０歳ぐらいでしょ。」
example_sentences.english: Witness: 'The assailant is about 30 years old at most.'

example_sentences.japanese: 凄く怒ったファン：「ダーデンはせいぜい二流のコーチだぞ！子供でさえもっと上手くコーチングできるぞ!」
example_sentences.english: Extremely angry fan: 'Durden is a second-rate coach at best! Even a child can coach better than him!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「この車を買うのに彼が支払ったのはせいぜい３万ドルだと思う。」
example_sentences.english: 'I think that in order to buy that car he spent 30 grand at most.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「この選手の動きからすると、せいぜい２、３年空手を習った程度だろう。」
example_sentences.english: 'Judging from this athlete's movements, he has been studying karate for 2-3 years at most.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「手伝いたいけど、救急要員が少ないのでせいぜい５人しか送ってあげられません。」
example_sentences.english: 'I want to help, but because there are few first-aid personnel available, I can only send you five people at most.'

example_sentences.japanese: このプロジェクトに出来るだけ多くの時間を割きたいが、一日に使える時間はせいぜい三時間とかだろう。
example_sentences.english: I want to dedicate as much time as possible to this project, but in a day I probably only have 3 hours of useable time at most.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔の日本人が高い白米を食べれたのは、せいぜい祭りや結婚といったイベントの時だけでした。
example_sentences.english: The Japanese of old used to only eat good quality white rice during events like weddings and festivals at most.

example_sentences.japanese: 店員：「これ、１０００円です。」クライアント：「１０００円だって？この服の品質がそんなに高いとは思えないがね。払えるのはせいぜい５００円でしょ。」
example_sentences.english: Clerk: 'This is 1000 yen.' Client: '1000 yen? I don't think that the quality of these clothes is that high. I can pay 500 yen at most.'

example_sentences.japanese: 平和な田舎ではほとんど鍵なんか使わなくて、使うとしてもせいぜい治安が悪化している時くらいだ。
example_sentences.english: Locks are mostly not used in the peaceful countryside, and even if we assume that they were, it would at most only be in times where the safety worsens.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日現在、テスラＳという電気自動車では一充電あたりせいぜい数百キロ走行分くらいしか蓄えられない電池を載せることしかできないけれども、おそらく近い将来グラフェンという物質によって電池の満充電容量は劇的に増えるのではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: As of today, an electric car called the Tesla S can only carry batteries that store enough energy for a maximum of a few hundred kilometers per charge, but, I think that in the near future, the capacity of batteries will dramatically increase because of the substance known as graphene.

general_translation: Only, Slightly, A little, Barely, Merely
formation: わずかに +  Phrase
casual_structure: わずかに +  Phrase
explanation: A structure implying a very small or slight amount of (A). Compared to what is possible, the amount of (A) is only meager.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女とはわずかに意見が違う。
example_sentences.english: (My) opinion differs slightly from her's.

example_sentences.japanese: この建物は真下からみると、わずかに傾いているように見える。
example_sentences.english: This building appears to tilt slightly when viewed from directly below.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の人のテレビの音がわずかに聞こえる。
example_sentences.english: I can slightly hear the sound of my neighbor's TV.

example_sentences.japanese: 建物と建物の間から富士山がわずかに見えた。
example_sentences.english: Mt. Fuji was slightly visible between the buildings.

example_sentences.japanese: 始めた頃に比べると、わずかに上手になった感じがします。
example_sentences.english: Compared to when I started, I feel I am only slightly better.

example_sentences.japanese: ＬＩＮＵＸのインタフェイスはＷＩＮＤＯＷＳのとわずかに異なる。
example_sentences.english: Linux's interface slightly differs from Windows'.

example_sentences.japanese: 似ているけど、わずかに形が違うような気がした。
example_sentences.english: They look similar, but I had a feeling that their shapes were slightly different.

example_sentences.japanese: わずかに毛が生えてきた。育毛に成功したのかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: My hair is coming in slightly. My hair restoration might just be working.

example_sentences.japanese: 校長先生の怒鳴り声がわずかに聞こえる。
example_sentences.english: I could hear the angry voice of the principal just barely.

example_sentences.japanese: 間違いがわずかに見つかってしまった。やり直しだな。
example_sentences.english: I unfortunately found a slight mistake. Looks like I have to redo it.

example_sentences.japanese: わずかに寝坊した。急げば間に合うかな？
example_sentences.english: I overslept slightly. If I hurry I wonder if I will be able to make it in time.

example_sentences.japanese: 宿題がわずかに残っている。食事の後にやるしかない。
example_sentences.english: I only have a little homework left. I have no choice but to do it after I eat.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の声がわずかに聞こえた。きっと電話の向こうに彼がいる。
example_sentences.english: I could barely hear his voice. He must be far from the phone.

example_sentences.japanese: 怪我をした小鳥がわずかに飛んだ。もう少しで元気になる。
example_sentences.english: The small injured bird flew a little (slightly). It will soon become healthy.

example_sentences.japanese: そのグループの中から準決勝に進出する選手はわずかに４人です。
example_sentences.english: Only four players will advance to the semifinals from this group.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頃、この通りにそって歩いて行くと、子供が遊んでいるのが見えたものだ。賑やかな街だった。今ではわずかに会えるくらいだ。
example_sentences.english: During my childhood, when I went along this street I used to see children playing.It used to be a lively town. Now, I barely see anyone.

example_sentences.japanese: あの提案に賛成した議員はほんのわずかだ。
example_sentences.english: Only a small number of assembly members agreed to that suggestion.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼に残された時間は残りわずかだった。
example_sentences.english: He had very little time left.

general_translation: Just less than
formation: Number + Counter + 弱（じゃく）
casual_structure: Number + Counter + 弱（じゃく）
explanation: A suffix added to a counter that indicates the quantity is less than a specific number.

example_sentences.japanese: １０人じゃくで大縄跳びをしたが、３回も続かなかった。
example_sentences.english: We played group jump rope with a little less than 10 people, but we couldn't even keep it going for three jumps.

example_sentences.japanese: 前を歩いている人のカバンのチャックが５ミリじゃく開いている。
example_sentences.english: The zipper on the bag of the person walking in front of me is open a little less than 5 millimeters.

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒：「熱が３９度じゃくあるので今日は授業をお休みします。」先生：「お大事にしてくださいね。」
example_sentences.english: Student: 'I have a fever of a little less than 39 degrees, so I will take the day off from class today.' Teacher: 'Please take care of yourself.'

example_sentences.japanese: あと５ページじゃくで読み終わるところだった本に牛乳をこぼし、終わりを読めなくなった。
example_sentences.english: I spilled milk on a book that I was going to finish reading in a little less than 5 pages, and I couldn't read the ending.

example_sentences.japanese: 美容師に「髪を１センチじゃく切ってください。」と伝えても、いつも２センチくらいは平気で切られるのは何でだろう。
example_sentences.english: I wonder why even when I tell the hairdresser, 'Please cut just less than 1 centimeter of my hair', they always casually cut off about 2 centimeters.

example_sentences.japanese: あと１分じゃくで目的地に到着するところで、エンジンが壊れて車が動かなくなった。
example_sentences.english: With just less than a minute left before arriving at our destination, the engine broke down and the car stopped moving.

example_sentences.japanese: 客：「リビングはどのくらいの広さですか？」仲介者：「１０畳じゃくですね。」
example_sentences.english: Customer: 'How big is the living room?' Agent: 'It's just less than 10 tatami mats big.'

example_sentences.japanese: 青森市では今年も８メートルじゃくの積雪が観測されました。
example_sentences.english: In Aomori City, a snowfall of just less than 8 meters was observed this year as well.

example_sentences.japanese: この村には５０世帯じゃくしか住んでいないので、１０年以内に無人になると言われている。
example_sentences.english: Because there are just less than 50 households living in this village, it is said that it will become uninhabited within 10 years.

example_sentences.japanese: 海水温度が３０℃じゃくになるとサンゴは色を失い、やがて死滅することもあります。
example_sentences.english: When the seawater temperature reaches just less than 30°C, coral loses its color and can eventually die off.

example_sentences.japanese: 研究によると、世界では年間３億５，０００万トンじゃくのプラスチックごみが出ており、その多くが適切に処理されないまま自然環境に流されているという。
example_sentences.english: According to research, just less than 350 million tons of plastic waste is generated globally each year, and much of it is released into the natural environment without being properly treated.

example_sentences.japanese: 新薬の研究のために実験に参加した姉は２週間じゃく入院し、その間は点滴のみで、食事を摂ることが許されなかったそうだ。
example_sentences.english: My older sister, who participated in an experiment for new drug research, was hospitalized for just less than two weeks, and I heard she was only on an IV drip and wasn't allowed to eat during that time.

example_sentences.japanese: いまだに１０ｋｍ弱を４０分で走った自分が信じられません。
example_sentences.english: I still can't believe I ran just under 10 kilometers in 40 minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: １０人弱しか集まらないようでは、担当を変えざるを得ないな。
example_sentences.english: If only a little less than 10 people gather, we have no choice but to change the person in charge.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人一時間弱で交代して、星の観察をしよう。
example_sentences.english: Let's take turns for just under an hour each and observe the stars. (Could mean 'just over' for some speakers)

general_translation: Just more than
formation: Number + Counter + 強（きょう）
casual_structure: Number + Counter + 強（きょう）
explanation: A suffix added to a counter that indicates the quantity is more than a specific number.

example_sentences.japanese: この荷物は１０キロきょうある。
example_sentences.english: This luggage weighs just more than 10 kilograms.

example_sentences.japanese: 二日酔いのせいで、１２時間きょうも寝続けていた。
example_sentences.english: Because of a hangover, I kept sleeping for a little more than 12 hours.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣町の人口は１，０００人きょうしかいない。
example_sentences.english: The population of the neighboring town is only just more than 1,000 people.

example_sentences.japanese: 相手チームのエースは身長２３０センチきょうもあるそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard the opposing team's ace is just a little more than 230 centimeters tall.

example_sentences.japanese: マネージャー：「この会場のキャパは何人だ？」チーフ：「大体３００人きょうが入ります！」
example_sentences.english: Manager: 'What is the capacity of this venue?' Chief: 'It fits roughly just more than 300 people!'

example_sentences.japanese: この橋の全長は２，０００メートルきょうあり、どうやら日本一の長さらしい。
example_sentences.english: The total length of this bridge is just more than 2,000 meters, and it is apparently the longest in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 両者の話し合いは４時間きょう経った今も尚、続いているそうです。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the discussion between both parties is still continuing even now, after a little more than four hours have passed.

example_sentences.japanese: 部下：「これ以上プロジェクトを進めても赤字になるだけです！中止しましょう！」上司：「何を言っているんだ！既に５００人きょうの参加者が集まっているんだぞ！」
example_sentences.english: Subordinate: 'Continuing this project any further will only result in a deficit! Let's cancel it!' Boss: 'What are you talking about! We already have just more than 500 participants gathered!'

example_sentences.japanese: 新制度が始まり１０年きょう経つが、国民の理解は十分に進んでいない。
example_sentences.english: Just more than 10 years have passed since the new system started, but the public's understanding has not sufficiently progressed.

example_sentences.japanese: この地域では人口の半分きょうが農業に関わっているとされており、そのほとんどが高齢者のため、将来地域を支えていく若者が必要とされている。
example_sentences.english: In this region, it is said that a little more than half of the population is involved in agriculture, and because most of them are elderly, young people are needed to support the region in the future.

example_sentences.japanese: 家から学校までは５ｋｍきょうあります。
example_sentences.english: It is just more than 5 kilometers from my house to the school.

example_sentences.japanese: 小さじ１きょうの小麦粉を入れました。
example_sentences.english: I added just more than one teaspoon of flour.

example_sentences.japanese: スーパーで売られているりんごは、大体１個２００グラム強あるらしい。
example_sentences.english: It seems that apples sold at the supermarket generally weigh just over 200 grams each.

example_sentences.japanese: ファンクラブの会員数が次第に増えていって、今は１万人強もいる。
example_sentences.english: The number of fan club members has gradually increased, and now there are just over 10,000.

example_sentences.japanese: １０年弱この会社で働いているから社長の人柄はよく知っている。
example_sentences.english: I have been working at this company for just under 10 years, so I know the president's personality well. (Could mean 'just over' for some speakers)

example_sentences.japanese: ５ｋｇ強の宝石を手に入れたから、一生楽して生きていける！
example_sentences.english: I got my hands on just over 5 kilograms of jewels, so I can live comfortably for the rest of my life! (Could mean 'a good amount more than' for some speakers)

general_translation: And, As well as
formation: Noun + および
casual_structure: Noun + および
explanation: A formal structure used to convey (A) and (B). Reaching also (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 布団および枕等はございます。
example_sentences.english: There are things like futons and pillows.

example_sentences.japanese: 免許証および印鑑を持ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: Please bring your driver's license and seal.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校説明会に参加されたい方、および体験入学をされたい方は８時から５時の間にこちらの電話番号までお電話をください。
example_sentences.english: If you would like to participate in a school information session and enroll in a trial lesson, please call this number between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.

example_sentences.japanese: 夕食および朝食は別料金になります。
example_sentences.english: Dinner and breakfast are charged separately.

example_sentences.japanese: 帽子およびメガネは外してください。
example_sentences.english: Hats and glasses must be removed.

example_sentences.japanese: 当店の定休日は月曜日および水曜日となっています。
example_sentences.english: We are closed on Mondays as well as Wednesdays.

example_sentences.japanese: 指輪およびネックレス等は外してください。
example_sentences.english: Please remove things like rings and necklaces.

example_sentences.japanese: 受付および入館は８時からです。
example_sentences.english: Reception and entry begins at 8.

example_sentences.japanese: 手帳および日記等を見せてください。
example_sentences.english: Please show me things like your notebook and your diary.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅館およびホテルへの連絡はご遠慮ください。
example_sentences.english: Please refrain from contacting the Ryokan as well as the hotel.

example_sentences.japanese: 帽子および手袋等はご持参ください。
example_sentences.english: Please take things like gloves and a hat.

example_sentences.japanese: 予習および復習は各自でやるように。
example_sentences.english: Lesson preparation and review should be done individually.

example_sentences.japanese: 夕食および夜食はご用意いたします。
example_sentences.english: We will provide an evening meal as well as midnight snack.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長および専務は今大事な会議をしています。
example_sentences.english: The company president and the managing director are having an important meeting now.

example_sentences.japanese: 顧客サポートおよび払戻に関する事項。
example_sentences.english: Matters related to refunds and customer support.

example_sentences.japanese: 憲法から：「国家は良心の自由および信教の自由を保証すること。」
example_sentences.english: From the constitution: 'The state guarantees freedom of conscience and religious liberty.'

example_sentences.japanese: お知らせ：「大学生のための職探し、および起業に関するセミナー。」
example_sentences.english: Notification: 'Seminar about job-hunting and starting a business for university students.'

general_translation: Immediately, Quickly, Suddenly, In a moment or flash
formation: たちまち + Phrase
casual_structure: たちまち + Phrase
explanation: A construction implying that (A) was done immediately, and without thought or control.

example_sentences.japanese: 少し油断したら、ライバルにたちまち追い越された。
example_sentences.english: (I) was only slightly negligent, but (my) rival immediately overtook me.

example_sentences.japanese: あのレコード会社に所属すると、アーティストたちはたちまち有名になる。
example_sentences.english: Artists who belong to that record company quickly become famous.

example_sentences.japanese: 私と田中さんはたちまち仲良くなった。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-san and I immediately became friends.

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫に入れておいたシナモンロールはたちまち妻の胃袋へと消えた。
example_sentences.english: The cinnamon rolls I had put in the fridge quickly disappeared into my wife's stomach.

example_sentences.japanese: 小さな村で噂がたちまち広がるのは当然だよ！
example_sentences.english: It's only natural that rumors would spread in a flash in small villages!

example_sentences.japanese: うちの庭を掘ったら、たちまち温泉が出てきて驚いた。
example_sentences.english: When I dug up my yard, an onsen suddenly sprung up and I was surprised.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの犬は郵便配達員を見るとたちまちフェンスにそって走り始めるのだ。
example_sentences.english: My dog starts to run along the fence immediately when he sees a postman.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに仲が良かったのに、あの事件のせいでたちまち解散だ。
example_sentences.english: Even though they got along that well, because of that one incident they immediately broke up.

example_sentences.japanese: 有名な本は、本棚に並べられたとたんに、たちまち売り切れた。
example_sentences.english: As soon as the famous book hits the shelves, it sold out immediately.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの会社では、いいアイデアを出せばたちまち人気者になれるよ。
example_sentences.english: At my company, if you produce a good idea you will immediately become popular.

example_sentences.japanese: 安易に質を落として値を下げたりすると、たちまち売れなくなる。
example_sentences.english: If (you) simply drop the quality and the price, (you) will quickly become unable to sell it.

example_sentences.japanese: ミスをしたらたちまち意地悪になる上司なんて最悪だ。
example_sentences.english: Bosses that suddenly become ill-tempered the moment you make a mistake are the worst.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は基礎を理解した瞬間、たちまち応用できるすごい人だ。
example_sentences.english: He is someone who can immediately put to practice something that they just learned the basics of.

example_sentences.japanese: 有名な方にほんの少しコツを教えてもらったら、たちまちオルガンが上達した。
example_sentences.english: When I had a famous organist teach me a simple trick, I immediately improved the way I play the organ.

example_sentences.japanese: たった一つの不良品で、たちまち売れ行きがストップしてしまうこともあるので気をつけてください。
example_sentences.english: There is a chance that your sales will immediately cease if you have but one faulty product, so be careful.

general_translation: For no reason, Suddenly, All of a sudden
formation: いきなり + (Action) Phrase
casual_structure: いきなり + (Action) Phrase
explanation: An expression meaning to go and become (A). Often used to mean suddenly, or abruptly, when something uncontrollable happens.

example_sentences.japanese: いきなりの展開に驚きを隠せない。
example_sentences.english: I can't hide my surprise at the sudden development.

example_sentences.japanese: いきなり電話してごめん。ちょっと相談したい事があるんだけど今時間大丈夫？
example_sentences.english: Sorry for calling you suddenly. I need to talk to you about something, but is now a good time for you?

example_sentences.japanese: いきなり雨が降ってきたからびしょびしょだよ。
example_sentences.english: It suddenly started raining and I'm drenched.

example_sentences.japanese: ペットのワンちゃんがいきなり吠え出したからびっくりして起きた。
example_sentences.english: I was startled awake when my pet dog suddenly started barking.

example_sentences.japanese: いきなり電波が切れてしまうのは困る。
example_sentences.english: Suddenly losing phone service gets on my nerves.

example_sentences.japanese: そんないきなり停車したら危ないですよ。
example_sentences.english: Abruptly stopping like that is dangerous!

example_sentences.japanese: いきなり難問に突き当たってしまった。
example_sentences.english: I suddenly, and unfortunately, ran into a hard problem.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は、いきなり手づかみでご飯を食べ始めた。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother suddenly started eating rice with his hands for no reason.

example_sentences.japanese: お婆さんは何も言わず、いきなり私を抱きしめました。
example_sentences.english: Grandma, without saying a word, suddenly hugged me.

example_sentences.japanese: 出会っていきなり結婚を申し込むなんて、何を考えているんだ。
example_sentences.english: What are you thinking, suddenly proposing to someone after running into them.

example_sentences.japanese: いきなりテーマと違う話をするのはやめてください。
example_sentences.english: Please stop abruptly talking about stuff different from the current project for no reason.

example_sentences.japanese: いきなり手続きはできません。書類を揃えてください。
example_sentences.english: I cannot just all of a sudden process it. Please put the documents in order.

example_sentences.japanese: 床屋さんが何も聞かずにいきなり髪を切り始めた。
example_sentences.english: The barber suddenly began cutting my hair without asking anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 散歩の最中に、岩村さんがいきなり「好きな女の子がいるの？」と私に聞いたので、びっくりした。
example_sentences.english: In the middle of our walk, Iwamura-san suddenly asked me 'Do you have a girl you like?', and it surprised me.

example_sentences.japanese: いきなり飛び込んだ店で契約が取れました。
example_sentences.english: I was able to land a contract with the shop that I suddenly showed up to unannounced.

general_translation: Such as, Like, So much as
formation: Noun + といった + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + といった + Noun
explanation: A phrase that which emphasizes things like those which are said to be in category (A), and then explains them.

example_sentences.japanese: 勝敗といったものにこだわるのはやめよう。
example_sentences.english: Let's stop fussing over things such as winning or losing.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の父は、ゲートボールといったスポーツが好きだそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently my father likes sports such as gateball.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの国ではおはぎといった和菓子は売られていますか？
example_sentences.english: Are Japanese sweets such as ohagi sold in your country?

example_sentences.japanese: 旦那は洗濯や料理といった家事は一切しません。
example_sentences.english: My husband does not do any household chores such as laundry or cooking.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は生姜とかパクチーといった香味野菜を使った料理が苦手です。
example_sentences.english: I am not a fan of food that uses pot-herbs such as ginger and cilantro.

example_sentences.japanese: 蕎麦といった麺類があまり好きではありません。
example_sentences.english: I don't really like noodles such as soba.

example_sentences.japanese: 相撲といった日本の文化に興味がある。
example_sentences.english: I have interest in Japanese culture such as sumo.

example_sentences.japanese: 宣伝といったものに振り回されてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You must not be manipulated by things such as advertisements.

example_sentences.japanese: これといった理由もないのに約束を破ってはいけない。
example_sentences.english: Since you don't even have so much as a reason you cannot break your promise.

example_sentences.japanese: 「末っ子だからね」といったレッテルを貼るのはやめてください。
example_sentences.english: Please stop labeling me with such things as 'It is because you are the youngest child'.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は将棋やポーカーといった勝負ごとに強い。
example_sentences.english: He is skilled at match-based games like Shogi and Poker. (such as)

example_sentences.japanese: 総理大臣といった偉い人には簡単には会えません。
example_sentences.english: You cannot simply meet a prominent person such as the Prime Minister.

example_sentences.japanese: 素質といったものは、遺伝的な要素が大きいのかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Genetics are maybe a big factor in things such as one's character.

example_sentences.japanese: 炊事洗濯といった家事もりっぱな仕事だと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think doing housework, such as cooking and washing, is a splendid job.

example_sentences.japanese: 休みの日に何かを習いに行くといった趣味はない。
example_sentences.english: My hobbies don't include things such as going to learn something on my days off.

example_sentences.japanese: 団地といった集合住宅では、近所付き合いが大変な場合がある。
example_sentences.english: There are situations where neighborhood interaction is tough in housing complexes such as multi-unit apartments.

general_translation: Full of, Filled with, With ～
formation: Noun + を込（こ）めて
casual_structure: Noun + を込（こ）めて
explanation: A construction meaning that something is filled with, or jam-packed with (A). Often used in relation to feelings.

example_sentences.japanese: 感謝の気持ちをこめて、プレゼントを贈った。
example_sentences.english: Full of the feeling of gratitude, I gave a present. (filled with feelings of)

example_sentences.japanese: 感謝の気持ちをこめて、１年間お世話になった先生に花束をあげた。
example_sentences.english: Full of the feeling of gratitude, I gave a bouquet of flowers to a teacher who has taken care of me for the past year.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫は毎晩、愛をこめて晩御飯を作ってくれる。
example_sentences.english: My husband cooks dinner filled with love every night.

example_sentences.japanese: 歌うのが下手でも、心をこめて歌えば上手に聞こえる。
example_sentences.english: Even if you are not a good singer, you can sound like a good singer if you sing with all your heart.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が愛をこめて作った弁当を食べたい！
example_sentences.english: I want to eat a bento made full of love by my girlfriend. (filled with feelings of)

example_sentences.japanese: 憧れをこめて伯父さんの背中を見ていた。
example_sentences.english: I watched my uncle from behind, filled with admiration. (filled with feelings of)

example_sentences.japanese: 祈りをこめて書いた詩に涙した。
example_sentences.english: I shed tears at the poem that was written full of prayer. (filled with feelings of)

example_sentences.japanese: 願いをこめてステージで歌う姿にジーンときた。
example_sentences.english: Seeing them sing on stage, full of hope, gave me the chills. (filled with feelings of)

example_sentences.japanese: 敬意をこめて述べたのに、うまく伝わりませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Although my expression was full of respect, I did not communicate it well. (filled with feelings of)

example_sentences.japanese: 「祖父より愛をこめて」といった葉書が届いた。
example_sentences.english: A postcard saying 'From grandpa with love' arrived. (filled with feelings of)

example_sentences.japanese: 希望をこめて、人々は代表チームを応援している！
example_sentences.english: Filled with hope, people cheer for a national team! (filled with feelings of)

example_sentences.japanese: 期待をこめて少し厳しいことを言ってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Full of anticipation, I unfortunately said something a little over the top. (filled with feelings of)

example_sentences.japanese: 素人でも、思いをこめて作った作品には味がある。
example_sentences.english: Even an amateur's eagerly made piece has charm (full of eagerness). (filled with feelings of)

example_sentences.japanese: 皮肉をこめて言ったのに、彼は喜んでいた。
example_sentences.english: Even though what I said was filled with sarcasm, he was delighted. (filled with feelings of)

example_sentences.japanese: 心をこめて作った料理を食べてもらえなかった。
example_sentences.english: I wasn't able to have them eat cuisine made with all of my heart. (full of heart/wholeheartedly・filled with feelings of)

general_translation: Not only...but also, In addition, Not to mention
formation: Noun + に加（くわ）え（て）
casual_structure: Noun + に加（くわ）え（て）
explanation: A formal grammar point expressing that in addition to (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 白髪にくわえてシワまで増えてきた。もう年だな。
example_sentences.english: My gray hair, not to mention my wrinkles, have increased. Boy am I old.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は暑さにくわえて湿度も高くなる恐れがあるので外に出る方は熱中症に気をつけてください。
example_sentences.english: Today, in addition to the heat, there is a threat of high humidity, so please be careful of heat stroke if you are planning to leave the house.

example_sentences.japanese: 今学期から文法にくわえて漢字も教えることになった。
example_sentences.english: Starting this semester, in addition to grammar, I will also be teaching Kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は空手にくわえて、剣道もできるそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that he does kendo in addition to karate.

example_sentences.japanese: 性能にくわえて価格まで負けているようではどうにもならない。
example_sentences.english: Nothing can be done about the inferior value, not to mention ability.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の別荘にはテニスコートにくわえてサッカーコートまであるんですよ。
example_sentences.english: His vacation home not only has a tennis court, but also a soccer pitch.

example_sentences.japanese: 内科にくわえて外科にもかかることになるなんて思いもしなかった。
example_sentences.english: I never thought I’d have to see a surgeon on top of a physician.

example_sentences.japanese: 中指にくわえて薬指まで骨折してしまいました。
example_sentences.english: In addition to the middle finger, I also broke my ring finger.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱にくわえて吐き気まである。多分風邪だな。
example_sentences.english: In addition to a fever, I have nausea. It is most likely a cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 箸にくわえて茶碗まで高級だ。彼は金持ちだ。
example_sentences.english: His chopsticks, not to mention his rice bowls, are high grade. He is rich.

example_sentences.japanese: 女房にくわえて母親まで僕のスピーチを聞きに来て、少し恥ずかしい。
example_sentences.english: My wife, in addition to my mother, have come to listen to my speech. I am a little embarrassed.

example_sentences.japanese: 定休日にくわえて臨時休業が多いから、あの店はいつやっているのかよく分からない。
example_sentences.english: Since there are a lot of temporary business closures in addition to regular holidays, I can never know for sure when that store is open.

example_sentences.japanese: スウェーデンは天然資源の豊かさにくわえて、立派な教育体制によって産業が発達している国でもある。
example_sentences.english: Sweden, in addition to being rich in natural resources, is also a country of developed industries. This is due to their fine educational system.

example_sentences.japanese: スマホという最近の携帯電話は、電話の機能にくわえ、パソコンのように多くの他の用途がある。
example_sentences.english: In addition to having the ability to make phone calls, newer mobile phones (smartphones) have many functions similar to personal computers.

example_sentences.japanese: 人が天才と呼ばれるには物事の詳細な部分を見る能力にくわえ、物事の全体をつかむ能力も必要である。
example_sentences.english: For a person to be called genius, it is necessary for them to have the ability to grasp what they see as a whole, in addition to every little detail.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の母の日には母に花束に加えて心を込めて書いた手紙を渡すつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: This Mother's Day, I plan to give my mother a heartfelt letter in addition to a bouquet of flowers.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年になってから電気代に加えてガス料金までもが高くなった。
example_sentences.english: This year, in addition to the electricity bill, even the gas bill has increased.

grammar_point: 何（なに）から何（なに）まで
general_translation: Everything and anything, From A to Z, From head to toe, Everything
formation: 何（なに）から何（なに）まで + Phrase
casual_structure: 何（なに）から何（なに）まで + Phrase
explanation: An expression indicating anything and everything. From whatever until whatever, (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「本当になにからなにまですみません。」
example_sentences.english: 'I am sorry about everything.' (from A to Z/anything and everything)

example_sentences.japanese: 浜崎さんは釣りのことならなにからなにまで知っているから、何か分からない事があったら浜崎さんに聞きな。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Hamasaki knows everything and anything about fishing, so if you have any questions, ask him.

example_sentences.japanese: なにからなにまですみません。
example_sentences.english: Sorry for everything.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの子は勉強にしろ家事にしろ、なにからなにまでいい加減だから困っちゃうわ。
example_sentences.english: My son does everything halfheartedly, whether it's his studies or chores, so I'm frustrated.

example_sentences.japanese: なにからなにまでありがとうございました。
example_sentences.english: Thank you so much for everything.

example_sentences.japanese: この１年間なにからなにまでお世話になり本当にありがとうございました。
example_sentences.english: Thank you so much for everything you have done for me over the past year.

example_sentences.japanese: サポートスタッフ：「このマニュアルには、なにからなにまで書いてあります。」
example_sentences.english: Support staff: 'Everything is written in the manual.' (from A to Z)

example_sentences.japanese: 刑事、容疑者について：「彼の話はなにからなにまでうそだった！」
example_sentences.english: Detective, about suspect: 'His story was all a lie, from A to Z.' (anything and everything)

example_sentences.japanese: ライトノベル：「しかし、そのルールはなにからなにまで当てはまるわけではない。例外もある。」
example_sentences.english: Light novel: 'However, this rule doesn't apply to anything and everything. There are also exceptions.' (from A to Z)

example_sentences.japanese: 子供について、ご近所さんの話：「エレンはなにからなにまで母親そっくりだ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between neighbors about a child: 'Eren resembles his mother from head to toe.' (anything and everything)

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒、先生に：「オニヅカ先生にはなにからなにまで教えていただき、大変お世話になりました。」
example_sentences.english: Student, to a teacher: 'Mr. Onizuka, thank you very much for everything you have done.' (anything and everything/from A to Z)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の間での話：「じょういちろうさんって料理のことならなにからなにまで知っているそうだ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'I heard that Mr. Jouichirou knows everything and anything when it comes to cooking.' (from A to Z)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達１：「……なにからなにまで、僕が悪い。すいません。」友達２：「構わないさ。それじゃ─」
example_sentences.english: Friend 1: '... Everything was my fault. I'm sorry.'Friend 2: 'It's not a problem. Well then… (shall we go?)'

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩、新入社員について：「あの新人には、なにからなにまで説明しないといけないなぁ。あぁ面倒臭い。」
example_sentences.english: Senpai, about a new employee: 'I have to explain everything to the new guy. What a pain.' (anything and everything/from A to Z)

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行中、ガイド：「 ヴィエリチカ岩塩坑は階段から彫像まで、なにからなにまで塩でできています。」
example_sentences.english: During a trip, guide: 'In the Wieliczka salt mine, anything and everything, from the stairs to the sculptures, is made from salt.' (from A to Z)

example_sentences.japanese: 孫、医師に：「祖父がなにからなにまでお世話になり、ありがとうございます。」
example_sentences.english: Grandchild, to a doctor: 'Thank you very much for everything you did for my grandfather' (anything and everyting/from A to Z)

example_sentences.japanese: 告白、Ａ：「じゃ、私の何が好きなの？」Ｂ：「全てだよ。なにからなにまで全てさ。君の笑顔、強さ、動き方…そういうものが好きなんだ。」
example_sentences.english: Love confession, A: 'So, what do you like about me?'B: 'Everything! Anything and everything. Your smile, your strength, the way you move. I like those things (about you).' (from A to Z)

general_translation: Apart from, (Setting) aside, Whether or, Except for, Save for
formation: Noun + は別（べつ）として + PhraseA(1) + （か）+ B(1) + （か）+ は別（べつ）として + PhraseA(1) + （か）+ (Antonym) A(1) + (か）+ は別（べつ）として + PhraseA(1) + かどうか(2) + は別（べつ）として + PhraseA(1) + A［ない］(1) + は別（べつ）として + Phrase(1) Noun, ［な］Adjective、［い］Adjective、Verb(2) か、か否（いな）か
casual_structure: Noun + は別（べつ）として + PhraseA(1) + （か）+ B(1) + （か）+ は別（べつ）として + PhraseA(1) + （か）+ (Antonym) A(1) + (か）+ は別（べつ）として + PhraseA(1) + かどうか(2) + は別（べつ）として + PhraseA(1) + A［ない］(1) + は別（べつ）として + Phrase(1) Noun, ［な］Adjective、［い］Adjective、Verb(2) か、か否（いな）か
explanation: An expression which says in general, going off (A) being separate, (B). Save for (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 手伝うべきかどうかはべつとしてそもそも現場にはいなかった。
example_sentences.english: Leaving aside whether I should help or not, I wasn't at the scene in the first place.

example_sentences.japanese: この家の外観はべつとして、中は完全にリフォームされているからとても綺麗だ。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside the exterior of this house, the inside is very clean because it has been completely remodeled.

example_sentences.japanese: ホラーはべつとして映画なら基本的になんでも好きです。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside horror, I generally like any movie.

example_sentences.japanese: 給料がいいかどうかはべつとして、自分が楽しいと思える仕事がしたい。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside whether the pay is good or not, I want a job that I will enjoy.

example_sentences.japanese: このハンバーガーは体にいいかどうかはべつとして、とても美味しい。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside whether this burger is good for my body or not, it is very tasty.

example_sentences.japanese: このお茶は美味しい美味しくないはべつとして、健康にいいらしい。
example_sentences.english: I hear this tea is good for your health, whether it tastes good or not.

example_sentences.japanese: 試合で優勝するしないはべつとして、精一杯頑張る事が大切だ。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not you win the match, it is important to do your best.

example_sentences.japanese: それはべつとしてもたぶん遅かれ早かれそのトピックに戻ってくるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if we set it aside, that topic will most likely resurface sooner or later.

example_sentences.japanese: この子犬はかわいい、かわいくないはべつとして確かに動物としては随分賢い。
example_sentences.english: Leaving aside whether this puppy is cute or not, certainly, it is extremely smart for an animal.

example_sentences.japanese: そのジョークを言うのはいいか悪いかはべつとして、自分ではとてもおもしろいと思った！
example_sentences.english: Leaving aside whether saying this joke is good or bad, I thought it was really funny.

example_sentences.japanese: 喰われている餌食自身はべつとして喰っている捕食動物は本当に幸せだ。
example_sentences.english: (Setting) aside the prey that is being eaten, the predator enjoying its meal is surely happy.

example_sentences.japanese: プロジェクトに間に合うか間に合わないかはべつとして問題解決に集中しましょう。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside whether it will be on time for the project or not, let's concentrate on solving the problem.

example_sentences.japanese: 考えられる正当な理由の場合はべつとして警察は国民を調べることはできません。
example_sentences.english: Apart from a particular case of probable cause, police cannot search citizens.

example_sentences.japanese: 速くか遅くかはべつとして適した靴なしにコンクリートの歩道を走るのは危険なこともある。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside whether you are going fast or slow, it is dangerous to run on a concrete sidewalk without suitable shoes.

example_sentences.japanese: 現在の進行状況はべつとしてこれからの展望に関して話しましょう。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside the current progress, let's talk about future prospects.

example_sentences.japanese: 短期間にＸの株が上がるはずか上がらないはずかはべつとして長期的な展望は明るそうに見える。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside whether X's stocks will rise or not in short term, the long-term outlook seems to be bright.

example_sentences.japanese: ユーフォーの証人：「信じるかどうかはべつとして、私は確かにユーフォーを見たのです。」特別代理人マンハイム：「実はね、奥さん、あなたが空で見た閃光はユーフォーではなくて、沼地ガスがヴィーナスの光を反射しただけなんですよ。」
example_sentences.english: UFO witness: 'Setting aside whether or not you believe me, I am certain that I saw a UFO.' Special agent Mannheim: 'In all honesty ma'am, the flash you saw in the sky was not a UFO, but just swamp gas reflecting light from Venus.'

example_sentences.japanese: 実験の結果の良し悪しはべつとして結果を見たい。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside whether the results of the experiment are good or bad, I want to see them.

example_sentences.japanese: 見た目は別にして、あそこの料理はとても美味しい。
example_sentences.english: Aside from the appearance, the food there is very good.

general_translation: As might be expected, Because, All the more because, It's only natural
formation: Verb + だけに［い］Adjective + だけに［な］Adjective + な + だけにNoun + だけに
casual_structure: Verb + だけに［い］Adjective + だけに［な］Adjective + な + だけにNoun + だけに
explanation: A structure that highlights that just with (A), (B) may be expected, or is only natural.

example_sentences.japanese: この車は最新だけに、椅子のヒーターもあります。
example_sentences.english: This is a brand new car and as one might expect, it comes with heated seats.

example_sentences.japanese: トムさんは日本語を８年勉強しているだけに、日本語がペラペラだ。
example_sentences.english: Tom has been studying Japanese for 8 years and as one might expect, he is fluent in Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: このアパートは東京駅に近いだけに、家賃が高い。
example_sentences.english: This apartment is very close to Tokyo station, and as one might expect, the rent is expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: このアプリは便利なだけに、どんどんとユーザーが増えてきています。
example_sentences.english: This application is becoming more and more popular just because it is so useful.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏休みであるだけに、海水浴場には人がたくさんいる。
example_sentences.english: It is summer vacation and as one might expect, there are a lot of people at the beach.

example_sentences.japanese: 合格したと思っていただけに、不合格と知った時はとてもショックだった。
example_sentences.english: I was very shocked when I learned that I had been rejected because I thought I had passed.

example_sentences.japanese: 普段は優しいだけに、彼女が怒っている姿を見た時はびっくりしました。
example_sentences.english: I was surprised to see her angry because she is usually so kind.

example_sentences.japanese: 年を取ってきただけに、出来なくなったことが多い。
example_sentences.english: As one might expect with aging, there are a lot of things you can no longer do.

example_sentences.japanese: 大工だけに、椅子くらいならすぐに作ってくれる。
example_sentences.english: As one might expect from a carpenter, if it is something like a chair, they can quickly make that for you.

example_sentences.japanese: 寿司職人だけに、醤油へのこだわりがすごい。
example_sentences.english: As one might expect from a sushi craftsman, his particularity toward soy sauce is extensive.

example_sentences.japanese: スチュワーデスだけに、身長が高く姿勢もいいですね。
example_sentences.english: As one might expect from a stewardess, she is tall and her posture is good.

example_sentences.japanese: 消防署だけに、火の取り扱いはちゃんとしている。
example_sentences.english: As one might expect from a fire station, they properly handle fires.

example_sentences.japanese: プロ棋士だけに、将棋との向き合い方が半端じゃない。
example_sentences.english: As one might expect from a professional shogi player, the way he approaches the game is not careless.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はスキーの上級者だけに、難しいコースでも難なく滑れる。
example_sentences.english: He is an advanced skier, so as one might expect, he can easily ski difficult courses.

example_sentences.japanese: 賞金が高額なだけに、応募者が殺到しています。
example_sentences.english: As one might expect from the prize money being a large sum, applicants are flooding in.

example_sentences.japanese: 知り合いだけに、あんな事件を起こすなんて残念でならない。
example_sentences.english: She is someone I know, so as one might expect, I can't help feeling disappointment at that she caused such an incident.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は経験が長いだけに、自信を持って演説ができた。
example_sentences.english: As one might expect from his extensive experience, he confidently gave the speech.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は有名な司会者だけに、臨機応変に対応できます。
example_sentences.english: As one might expect from him being a famous moderator, he can adapt himself to deal with it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は子供の頃からそろばんを習っているだけに、暗算がとてもうまい。
example_sentences.english: Just in that he has been learning the abacus since childhood, he is very good at mental math.

general_translation: To do all that one can, As much or many ~ as one could
formation: Verb + だけは + Verb［た］(*)Verb + だけは + Verb［ている］(*)(*) The same Verb has to be repeated
casual_structure: Verb + だけは + Verb［た］(*)Verb + だけは + Verb［ている］(*)(*) The same Verb has to be repeated
explanation: An expression that indicates that the general state of (A) is just as much, or only as much as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べられるだけは食べた。食べ放題だからさ。
example_sentences.english: I ate all that I could. It was an all you can eat after all.

example_sentences.japanese: 飲み放題だったから、飲めるだけは飲んだ。
example_sentences.english: It was all you could drink, so I drank as much as I could.

example_sentences.japanese: トイレットペーパーを買えるだけは買ったが、置く場所がない。
example_sentences.english: I bought as much toilet paper as I could afford, but I have nowhere to put it.

example_sentences.japanese: ピアノのレッスンには通うだけは通っているけど、ピアノにはあまり興味がない。
example_sentences.english: I go to piano lessons as much as I can, but I am not very interested in piano.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日漢字の勉強をするだけはしているが、上達している感じがしない。
example_sentences.english: I do as much as I can to study kanji every day, but I don't feel like I'm making progress.

example_sentences.japanese: このナッツを砕くだけは砕いた。
example_sentences.english: I crushed these nuts as much as I could.

example_sentences.japanese: 儀式だからやるだけはやっているが、さっぱり意味が分からない。
example_sentences.english: Since it is a ceremony, I am doing as much as I can. However, I have no idea what any of it means.

example_sentences.japanese: 感想を書くだけは書いてみたが、まだメールで送っていません。
example_sentences.english: I wrote out my impressions the best I could, but I still haven't sent it out (via email).

example_sentences.japanese: 今日着たい服を乾かすだけは乾かして家を出た。
example_sentences.english: I dried the clothes I want to wear today as much as I could and then left the house.

example_sentences.japanese: 為替を毎日チェックするだけはしているが、イマイチよく分からない。
example_sentences.english: Every day I check the money orders as much as I can, but I still don't quite understand (them).

example_sentences.japanese: 欲しかった楽器を買うだけは買ったが、全然練習していません。
example_sentences.english: Even though I bought as many of the instruments that I wanted as I could, I have not been practicing at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 行列に並ぶだけは並んでいるが、何の行列かは知りません。
example_sentences.english: I did the best I could to line up in a line, but I don't know what the line is for.

example_sentences.japanese: 着替えを持つだけは持ったが、この服で良かったのかどうかはよく分からない。
example_sentences.english: I brought as many changes of clothes as I could, but I am unsure if these clothes are appropriate.

example_sentences.japanese: 組合せを決めるだけは決めてみたが、たぶんみんな文句を言うだろうな。
example_sentences.english: I decided on the combination as best as I could, but everyone will still probably complain.

example_sentences.japanese: 警備会社に連絡するだけはしてみたが、大して何もしてくれなさそうな雰囲気でした。
example_sentences.english: I tried contacting the security firm as much as I could, but I get the feeling that they won't do anything for me.

example_sentences.japanese: 研修に行くだけは行ってみたが、大したことない内容だったな。
example_sentences.english: I went to as many training courses as I could, but the content was all meaningless.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強だけはしたが、全然頭に情報が入ってこなかった。
example_sentences.english: I studied as much as I could, but I didn't get any information in my head.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩には何回も連絡だけはしているが、全然返事をしてくれない。
example_sentences.english: I have been trying to contact my senpai as much as I could, but he won't respond at all.

general_translation: Is only natural, …Being the case, Because, As might be expected
formation: Verb + だけ（のことは）あって［い］Adjective + だけ（のことは）あって［な］Adjective + な + だけ（のことは）あってNoun + だけ（のことは）あって
casual_structure: Verb + だけ（のことは）あって［い］Adjective + だけ（のことは）あって［な］Adjective + な + だけ（のことは）あってNoun + だけ（のことは）あって
explanation: An expression that indicates that just the existence of (A) leads to (B) being expected or natural.

example_sentences.japanese: 茶道を習っているだけあって、礼儀が正しい。
example_sentences.english: As one might expect, since she is learning tea ceremony, she is polite.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は１０年間日本に住んでいただけあって、日本語を日本人のように話せる。
example_sentences.english: As one might expect, he can speak Japanese like a Japanese person because he lived in Japan for 10 years.

example_sentences.japanese: あのホテルは高いだけあって、サービスがとてもいい。
example_sentences.english: As one might expect, that hotel has great service because it is expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: 浅草は有名なだけあって、平日でも観光客で賑わっている。
example_sentences.english: As might be expected with how popular Asakusa is, it is crowded with tourists even on weekdays.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中先生は習字の先生だけあって、漢字を書くのが上手です。
example_sentences.english: As expected, Tanaka-sensei is good at writing kanji because she is a calligraphy teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 昼寝しただけあって、午後から眠くなることはなかった。
example_sentences.english: (As might be expected) because I took a nap, I didn't become tired in the afternoon.

example_sentences.japanese: あの二人は仲良しなだけあって、いつも一緒にいるよね。
example_sentences.english: As might be expected with how close those two are, they are always together.

example_sentences.japanese: 揚げ物を控えただけあって、私は３キロも痩せた。
example_sentences.english: As might be expected, I avoided eating fried food and I lost three kilograms.

example_sentences.japanese: アナウンサーだけあって、早口言葉が得意だ。
example_sentences.english: As might be expected from an announcer, tongue twisters are his strong point.

example_sentences.japanese: 判事だけあって、普段から真面目な生活をしているんですね。
example_sentences.english: As might be expected from a judge, he habitually leads an honest life.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強時間を増やしただけあって、どんどん上達している。
example_sentences.english: As might be expected from increasing my study hours, I am rapidly seeing improvement.

example_sentences.japanese: 専門家だけあって、彼はいつも中身の濃い提案をしてくれる。
example_sentences.english: As might be expected from a specialist, he always gives us proposals with dense content.

example_sentences.japanese: 国語の先生だけあって、俳句を詠むのが上手ですね。
example_sentences.english: As might be expected of a Japanese teacher, she is good at reciting haikus.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は列車の運転士だけあって、この路線の駅名を全て暗記している。
example_sentences.english: As expected from a train driver, he remembers all the station names along the route.

example_sentences.japanese: 頑張って勉強しただけあって、妹はいい大学に入学できた。
example_sentences.english: As expected, my little sister studied hard, and got into a good college.

example_sentences.japanese: とても幼いころから空手を学んでいただけあって、１３歳なのに黒帯も持っているし、トーナメントにも多数優勝した。
example_sentences.english: As expected from someone who has learned Karate from a very young age, despite being 13 she has a black belt and has won numerous tournaments.

example_sentences.japanese: 幼い頃からアイススケートを習っていただけあって、将来はオリンピック選手になるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: As expected from someone who has been learning ice skating from a young age, she will probably be an Olympic athlete in the future. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日一生懸命勉強しただけあって、彼は試験に合格するだろう。
example_sentences.english: As expected, he studied hard everyday, and would probably do well on his exams. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Be glad, Be relieved, Most, Best, Above all else, More than anything
formation: 何（なに）より + （も）+ Phrase何（なに）より + の + Noun
casual_structure: 何（なに）より + （も）+ Phrase何（なに）より + の + Noun
explanation: A structure often used to show relief about (A), or that (A) is the best. More than whatever else, (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「ありがとうございます。」「お役に立てれば、なによりの幸せです。」
example_sentences.english: 'Thank you very much.''More than anything it is a blessing to be able to help.' (above all else・more than anything)

example_sentences.japanese: なにより驚いたのは、あの中田くんが医者になったことだ。
example_sentences.english: The most surprising thing is that Nakata-kun became a doctor.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中様のお役に立ててなによりです。
example_sentences.english: We are glad to be of service to you, Tanaka-sama.

example_sentences.japanese: なによりも大切なのは、何でも諦めずに頑張ってやることだ。
example_sentences.english: The most important thing is to not give up and to do your best in anything you do.

example_sentences.japanese: 休みの日に妻とドライブに行くのがなによりの楽しみです。
example_sentences.english: I love going on drives with my wife on weekends more than anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達：「互いに助け合うことがなにより大事なのよ。」
example_sentences.english: Friend: 'Helping one another is the most important thing.' (above all else・more than anything)

example_sentences.japanese: 久しぶりに挨拶する時：「お元気そうでなによりです。」
example_sentences.english: When greeting someone we haven't seen for a long time: 'I am really glad that you seem to be doing well.' (above all else・more than anything)

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「両親にとって自分の子供の健康がなにより大切です。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'For parents, there is nothing more important than the health of their children.' (above all else・more than anything)

example_sentences.japanese: らくさん：「あなたにもらった本、わたしの息子がとても気に入っています。」おのでらさん：「それはなによりです。」
example_sentences.english: Raku: 'My child loved the book he received from you.'Onodera: 'I am really glad.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「見つけた時、すべて折半だよ。」「どっちにしろ、そのためには、なによりまず見つけないと話にならん。」
example_sentences.english: 'When we find it, we split everything equally.''Either way, for that, above all else, if we can't find it first, we won't get anywhere.'

example_sentences.japanese: プレゼントなどにたいして感謝を述べる時：「なによりのプレゼントをありがとう。」
example_sentences.english: When saying thanks for presents and the like: 'Thank you for the most wonderful gift!' (above all else・more than anything)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「わたしは本を読むことがなにより好きだ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'What I like the most is reading books.' (above all else・more than anything)

example_sentences.japanese: メグニンさん：「お店を爆発させちゃってすみませんでした。」ウィスさん：「問題ないし無事でなによりよ。」
example_sentences.english: Megunin: 'I am sorry for blowing up your shop.'Vis: 'No problem, I am glad that you are safe.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「そしてなにより驚くべきことは、セガが日本で設立されなかったということだ。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'And the most surprising thing is that SEGA was not founded in Japan.' (above all else・more than anything)

example_sentences.japanese: 久しぶりに目上に挨拶する時：「お元気になられてなによりです。」
example_sentences.english: When greeting a superior they haven't seen for a long time: 'I am glad that you are in good health.'

example_sentences.japanese: 部長：「お子さんが生まれたのですね。」部下：「はい。長女が無事に誕生いたしました。」部長：「そうですか。それはなによりです。」
example_sentences.english: Department chief: 'You had a baby, right?'Subordinate: 'Yes. My first daughter was born, without any problems.'Department chief: 'Is that so? I am really glad.'

general_translation: By any account, All the same, No doubt
formation: 何（なん）といっても + Phrase
casual_structure: 何（なん）といっても + Phrase
explanation: An expression stating that no matter what is said, the result or truth of (B) remains unchanged.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の長所は、なんといっても朗らかなところだ。
example_sentences.english: His strong point is, by any account, his cheerfulness.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の日本語の先生は厳しいけど、なんといっても日本語を教えるのがものすごく上手だ。
example_sentences.english: My Japanese teacher is strict, but she is very good at teaching Japanese without a doubt.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の悪いところは、なんといってもすぐに嘘をつくことだ。
example_sentences.english: The bad thing about him is, by any account, that he is quick to lie.

example_sentences.japanese: あのカフェはなんといってもコーヒーとアイスクリームが安いからとても人気がある。
example_sentences.english: Without a doubt, they have cheap coffee and ice cream at that cafe, so it is very popular.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は正直者だし、話しやすい。しかし、なんといっても誰に対しても優しいからみんなに好かれている。
example_sentences.english: He is honest and easy to talk to. But, by any account, he is nice to anyone, so he is well liked by everyone.

example_sentences.japanese: この地域の見所は、なんといっても紅葉だ。
example_sentences.english: The highlight of this area is no doubt the fall colors.

example_sentences.japanese: このマンションのセールスポイントは、なんといっても駅から近いことです。
example_sentences.english: By any account, this apartment's selling point is that it is close to the station.

example_sentences.japanese: あの牧場のおすすめは、なんといっても自家製のアイスクリームだ。
example_sentences.english: My recommendation for that farm, is no doubt, their home-made ice cream.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの会社のいいところは、なんといってもボーナスがたくさんもらえることです。
example_sentences.english: A good point about our company is, by any account, that we get lots of bonuses.

example_sentences.japanese: あの店のおすすめのメニューは、なんといっても煮込みハンバーグだ。
example_sentences.english: By any account, that restaurant's recommended menu is the braised Hamburg steak.

example_sentences.japanese: あのスーパーはなんといっても冷凍食品が安いから人気がある。
example_sentences.english: Without a doubt, that supermarket's frozen foods are cheap, so it is popular.

example_sentences.japanese: あの遊園地のアトラクションは色々ありますが、なんといってもジェットコースターがおすすめです。
example_sentences.english: This amusement park has various attractions, but I recommend the roller coaster without a doubt.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はとても無口な漁師だが、なんといっても腕がいい。
example_sentences.english: He is a very restrained fisherman, but without a doubt, he is skilled.

example_sentences.japanese: この電車は新しくて綺麗だ。しかし、なんといっても客席のすわり心地が最高だ。
example_sentences.english: This train is new and clean. There's no doubt that the seats are extremely comfortable.

example_sentences.japanese: 別府は空気や雰囲気がいい。なんといってもいろんな温泉を楽しめる。
example_sentences.english: Beppu is a place with clear air and a wonderful atmosphere. All the same, you can enjoy its various hot springs.

example_sentences.japanese: ここの回転寿司は、ネタが新鮮で美味しい。しかし、なんといっても安いからおすすめだ。
example_sentences.english: The toppings at this kaiten-zushi restaurant are fresh and delicious. But, by any account, it's very cheap so I recommend it.

general_translation: Or something, Or something like that
formation: Noun + か何（なに）か
casual_structure: Noun + か何（なに）か
explanation: A casual phrase which expresses whether it is (A), or whatever it is, the speaker is not sure.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校かなにかに通ってるみたいだけど。
example_sentences.english: He seems to go to school or something.

example_sentences.japanese: すみません、お茶かなにかありませんか？
example_sentences.english: Excuse me, do you have tea or something?

example_sentences.japanese: お巡りさん！あそこにナイフかなにかを持った怪しい人がいました。
example_sentences.english: Officer! There was a suspicious person over there holding a knife or something.

example_sentences.japanese: 何でもいいんで、水かなにかをください。
example_sentences.english: Please give me water or something. Anything would be fine.

example_sentences.japanese: 紅茶かなにか飲みませんか？
example_sentences.english: Do you want to drink tea or something?

example_sentences.japanese: 「仕事でいやなことがあったかなにか？機嫌が悪そうね。」
example_sentences.english: 'Did something happen at work or something? You seem to be in a bad mood.'

example_sentences.japanese: バーテンダーのひとみさん：「お飲み物はいかが？」顧客のにったさん：「ビールかなにかがほしいな。」
example_sentences.english: Hitomi, the bartender: 'How about a drink?'.Nitta, the customer: 'I'd like a beer or something'.

example_sentences.japanese: 奥さん：「コーヒーかなにか飲みませんか？」お客さん：「結構です。」
example_sentences.english: Wife: 'Would you like coffee or something to drink?'Guest: 'No, I'm fine.'

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官：「泥棒はバールかなにかを使って、窓を開けたと思います。」
example_sentences.english: Policeman: 'I think that the thief opened the window using a crowbar or something.'

example_sentences.japanese: 子供：「母さん、ご飯できたの？」お母さん：「まだよ。おなかがすいてたら、ケーキかなにか食べてもいいよ。」
example_sentences.english: Child: 'Mom, is the food ready?'Mother: 'Not yet. If you are hungry, you can eat cake or something.'

example_sentences.japanese: 郵便配達人：「ここに署名していただけますか。」小包をもらう人、誰かへ話している：「鉛筆かなにかを貸してくれる？」
example_sentences.english: Postman: 'Could you sign here?'The person who is getting the package talking to someone: 'Would you lend me a pencil or something?'

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼は体調が悪くて寝ている。昨日食べた肉かなにかがよくなかったみたい。」
example_sentences.english: 'He was feeling unwell and went to sleep. Apparently the meat he ate yesterday was not good or something. '

example_sentences.japanese: 友達１：「コーラかなにか飲みたい。。。」 友達２：「喉が渇いたわけだね。暑いから。」
example_sentences.english: Friend1: 'I want to drink a coke or something.'Friend2: 'No wonder you are thirsty. It's hot.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「彼はどうしたの？３時間も遅れるなんて...」Ｂ：「バスで来るはずだから、交通渋滞かなにかのような気がする。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Where could he be? He's like three hours late now…'B: 'He should be coming by bus, so I have a feeling that he is stuck in traffic or something.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「これ、手品じゃなくて、魔法だよ！」スケプティクさん：「そうは思わないね。本当に科学かなにかでこのことは説明できるでしょう。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'This is not a magic trick, it is MAGIC!'Mr. Skeptic: 'I don't think so. You probably can explain it with science or something.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達１：「どうしたの？まるで幽霊かなにかを見たような青白い顔をしているよ！」幸運に恵まれている友達２：「あのね、たった今宝くじが当たったの。１００万ドルをもらうのよ！」
example_sentences.english: Friend 1: 'What happened? Your face is almost as pale as if you had seen a ghost or something.'A friend blessed with good luck 2: 'Well the thing is, I actually just won the lottery. I'm going to get a million dollars!'

general_translation: Very, Extremely, Can't help but do
formation: Verb［て］+ ならない［い］Adjective［て］+ ならない［な］Adjective + で + ならない
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ ならない［い］Adjective［て］+ ならない［な］Adjective + で + ならない
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ ならない［い］Adjective［て］+ なりません［な］Adjective + で + なりません
explanation: A phrase often used in relation to feelings, exclaiming that not becoming that way is unavoidable.

example_sentences.japanese: 詐欺にあったきがしてならない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but feel it was a scam.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は徹夜して勉強してたから、眠くてならない。
example_sentences.english: I was up all night studying yesterday, so I'm extremely sleepy.

example_sentences.japanese: 愛知県の夏は暑くてならない。
example_sentences.english: Summer in Aichi prefecture is extremely hot.

example_sentences.japanese: ここ五年間娘と連絡がつかないから、心配でならない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but to feel worried because I haven't heard from my daughter in 5 years.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなコレクションは無駄におもえてならない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot help but think that that collection is worthless.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年あなたと見た紅葉がおもいだされてならない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but remember the fall colors I saw with you last year.

example_sentences.japanese: この毛皮はあつくてならない。
example_sentences.english: This fur is extremely warm. (I can't help but feel...)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の見学が楽しみでならない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but look forward to tomorrow's field trip.

example_sentences.japanese: 血圧が高すぎて不安でならない。
example_sentences.english: I am extremely worried about my blood pressure being too high. (I can't help but feel...)

example_sentences.japanese: サイレンが鳴り止まないから、心配でならない。
example_sentences.english: I am extremely worried because that siren won't stop ringing. (I can't help but feel...)

example_sentences.japanese: オリンピックで転んでしまった選手がかわいそうでならない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but feel sorry for the athlete who fell during the Olympics.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に来てから、家族に会えず、さびしくてならない。
example_sentences.english: Since coming to Japan, I haven't been able to see my family and can't help but feel lonely.

example_sentences.japanese: あのサークルが今や大人気だなんて、不思議でならない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but marvel at how popular that (sports) circle is now.

example_sentences.japanese: 壁に小指をぶつけるなんて災難だ。いたくてならない。
example_sentences.english: Banging your pinky (toe) into the wall is terrible. It is extremely painful. (I can't help but feel...)

example_sentences.japanese: 今週末の同窓会に行けないので、残念でならない。
example_sentences.english: Since I can't go to my class reunion this weekend I can't help but feel disappointed.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はいつも僕に嘘をつくからむかついてならない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but be extremely mad at her because she lies to me all the time. (Continuing feeling, natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: この漫画はつまらなくてならない。
example_sentences.english: This manga is extremely boring. (Momentary feeling, unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Only (formal)
formation: Noun + のみNoun + Particle + のみVerb + のみ［な］Adjective + である + のみ［い］Adjective + のみ
casual_structure: Noun + のみNoun + Particle + のみVerb + のみ［な］Adjective + である + のみ［い］Adjective + のみ
polite_structure: Noun + のみ + ですNoun + Particle + のみ + ですVerb + のみ + です［な］Adjective + である + のみ + です［い］Adjective + のみ + です
explanation: A formal adverbial particle used to emphasize or restrict a single state or instance.

example_sentences.japanese: 掲示板：「本日は、当日券のみ販売しております。」
example_sentences.english: Notice Board: 'Today, we are selling same-day tickets only .'

example_sentences.japanese: あの新入社員は成績が良いのみで、責任感は１ミリもないんだ。
example_sentences.english: That new employee only gets good results; they don't have a shred of responsibility.

example_sentences.japanese: 客：「ドリンクのみでもいいですか？」店員：「はい。アルコール以外にも多数ご用意しております！」
example_sentences.english: Customer: 'Is it okay if we only order drinks?' Staff: 'Yes. We have a wide variety available besides alcohol too!'

example_sentences.japanese: それは便利であるのみで、必ずしも安全とは言えない。
example_sentences.english: It is only convenient, not necessarily safe.

example_sentences.japanese: モデルオーディションの面接官：「この子は見た目がいいのみ、性格は暗そうだな。」
example_sentences.english: Model audition judge: 'This girl only has good looks; her personality seems gloomy.'

example_sentences.japanese: 得点に加算されるのはあそこの赤い線を超えた球のみです。
example_sentences.english: Only the balls that cross that red line over there will be added to the score.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はいつも悩み事を姉に相談する。なぜなら彼女は私の話を聞くのみで、私を決して責めないからだ。
example_sentences.english: I always consult my older sister about my worries, because she only listens to me, never blaming me.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は医者から癌と伝えられると、静かに黙ってうなずくのみ、何も言葉を発さなかった。
example_sentences.english: When the doctor told my father he had cancer, he only nodded quietly in silence and didn't utter a single word.

example_sentences.japanese: この問題については多くの議論がされてきたが、現時点では結論を急がず、慎重に検討を続けるのみである。
example_sentences.english: There has been much discussion regarding this issue, but at this point, we can only continue to carefully examine it without rushing to a conclusion.

example_sentences.japanese: あとは結果を待つのみだ。
example_sentences.english: Now, we only have to wait for the results.

example_sentences.japanese: ここの図書館は市民のみが利用できます。
example_sentences.english: Only residents can use this library.

example_sentences.japanese: 私に今できることは、彼の無事を祈るのみだ。
example_sentences.english: I can only pray for his safety now.

example_sentences.japanese: この割引は、学生のみが使えます。
example_sentences.english: This discount can be used by students only.

example_sentences.japanese: 皆様はご覧になるのみで結構です。
example_sentences.english: It is fine if you only look.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらは、優勝者にのみ与えられる金のカエルです！
example_sentences.english: This is the golden frog given only to the winner!

example_sentences.japanese: 探せるだけ探したけど、ネックレスは見つからなかった。
example_sentences.english: I searched as much as I could, but I couldn't find the necklace.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋は静かであるのみで、外部からの音は一切聞こえない。
example_sentences.english: This room is only quiet, absolutely no sounds from the outside can be heard.

example_sentences.japanese: 料金が高いのみで、サービスは普通だ。
example_sentences.english: The fee is only expensive, the service is ordinary.

general_translation: Not only...but, Not just...but, What is more
formation: Verb + のみならず［い］Adjective + のみならず［な］Adjective + である + のみならずNoun +（である）+ のみならずPhrase。 のみならず + Phrase
casual_structure: Verb + のみならず［い］Adjective + のみならず［な］Adjective + である + のみならずNoun +（である）+ のみならずPhrase。 のみならず + Phrase
explanation: A formal grammar point which indicates that not only (A), but (B) too. Literally, without only becoming (A), (B) too.

example_sentences.japanese: 炭素繊維は極めて丈夫であるのみならず非常に軽いらしい。
example_sentences.english: Apparently, carbon fiber is not only extremely durable, but also very light.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は仕事に遅刻したのみならず、帰りの終電も逃してしまった。
example_sentences.english: Today I was not only late for work, but also missed the last train home.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の夏は暑いのみならず湿気が高いから熱中症になりやすい。
example_sentences.english: Japanese summers are not only hot, but also humid, making it easy to suffer heat stroke.

example_sentences.japanese: あのパソコンは便利であるのみならず、安いので他のと比べてたくさん売れています。
example_sentences.english: That computer is not only convenient but also inexpensive, so it sells a lot more compared to the others.

example_sentences.japanese: この漫画は子供のみならず大人の間でも人気があります。
example_sentences.english: This manga is popular not only among children, but also among adults.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんは私の先輩だ。のみならず、命の恩人でもある。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-san is my senpai. Furthermore, he is the person that saved my life.

example_sentences.japanese: 高橋さんはサッカーの専門家だ。のみならず野球にも詳しい。
example_sentences.english: Takahashi-san is an expert on soccer. Moreover, he is also very knowledgeable about baseball.

example_sentences.japanese: この大統領候補は、豊富な知識があるのみならず経験の深い人でもある。
example_sentences.english: This presidential nominee is not only a person with abundant knowledge, but also is a person with vast experience.

example_sentences.japanese: 現代人は健康のために健康食品を食べるのみならず、運動もするべきである。
example_sentences.english: Modern people should not only eat healthy food for the sake of their health, but they should also exercise.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は年が経つに伴って英語のみならず中国語も流麗に話せるようになった。
example_sentences.english: As he grew older, he became able to speak fluently not only in English, but also in Chinese.

example_sentences.japanese: 発光ダイオードは蛍光灯よりずっと安いのみならず環境への影響も細小である。
example_sentences.english: Light emitting diodes are not only much cheaper than fluorescent lights, but also their impact on the environment is miniscule.

example_sentences.japanese: アニメや漫画は日本の国内のみならず国際的に絶大な人気を持つようになった。
example_sentences.english: Anime and manga have gained enormous popularity not only in Japan, but all over the world.

example_sentences.japanese: 喫煙は喫煙者のみならず周りにいる者、特に子供、お年寄りなどを肺がんにする可能性がある。
example_sentences.english: Smoking has the potential to cause lung cancer not only for smokers, but also for those around them, especially children and the elderly.

example_sentences.japanese: ボストン・ダイナミクスの新たなロボットは、速く走れるのみならず、ジャンプしたり、押されればバランスを取れたりする素晴らしい機械である。
example_sentences.english: The new Boston Dynamics robot is a fantastic device that can not only run quickly, but is also able to do things like jump and regain balance if pushed.

example_sentences.japanese: 韓国の化粧品のブランドは若者の間ではアジアのみならずヨーロッパやアメリカでも親しまれている。
example_sentences.english: Korean cosmetic brands are popular among young people not only in Asia, but also in Europe and the United States.

example_sentences.japanese: ある研究によると、植物はＶＯＣという化学物質を通してお互いに伝えるのみならず、地下で共生している菌類を用いるということだ。
example_sentences.english: According to a certain study, plants do not only communicate with one another through a chemical substance called VOC, but also use symbiotic fungi underground.

example_sentences.japanese: 良い兵士は命令に従うべきであるのみならず国際法律も尊重するべきである。
example_sentences.english: Good soldiers should not only obey orders, but also should respect international law.

example_sentences.japanese: ポキマンについてのゲームは、小学生のみならず大人たちの中でも人気である。
example_sentences.english: Games about Pokiman are not only popular among elementary schoolers, but also among adults.

general_translation: And yet, Despite this
formation: Phrase。それなのに  + Phrase
casual_structure: Phrase。それなのに  + Phrase
explanation: A sentence starter indicating that even despite that which was previously said, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 新品を買った。それなのにもう壊れた。
example_sentences.english: I bought it brand new. Despite this, it is already broken.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻は今、風邪をひいて寝込んでいる。それなのに、いきなり動物園に行きたいと言ってきた。
example_sentences.english: My wife is currently in bed with a cold. And yet, she suddenly told me that she wants to go to the zoo.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日３時間日本語の勉強をしている。それなのに全然上達している感じがしない。
example_sentences.english: I study Japanese for three hours every day. And yet I don't feel like I'm improving at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 早起きするために早く寝た。それなのに寝坊した。
example_sentences.english: In order to wake up early, I went to bed early. And yet, I overslept.

example_sentences.japanese: アンテナを新しくした。それなのにテレビの映りが悪い。
example_sentences.english: I got a new antenna. Despite this, the quality of the TV picture is bad.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は遠足だ。それなのに夜更かししている。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I have an outing. Despite this I am staying up late.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は努力していると思う。それなのにうまくいかないのか。
example_sentences.english: I think I am putting in effort and yet, why isn't it going well?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は一流のアスリートだ。それなのにかなり腰が低い。
example_sentences.english: He is a first class athlete. And yet, he is rather humble.

example_sentences.japanese: もう薄暗い。それなのにライトをつけていない車がいて危ない。
example_sentences.english: It is already dim. And yet there are cars without their lights on and it is dangerous.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は移転してきたばかりだ。それなのに道に迷わないなんてすごい。
example_sentences.english: He just transferred here. Despite this, it is amazing that he doesn't get lost.

example_sentences.japanese: 一生懸命育児をしている。それなのに夫は手伝ってくれない。
example_sentences.english: I am giving it my all to raise my child. And yet, my husband doesn't help me.

example_sentences.japanese: 衣食住がちゃんと揃っています。それなのに感謝しないのはよくないと思います。
example_sentences.english: They have all the necessities of life. Despite this, the fact that they don't give thanks is bad, I think.

example_sentences.japanese: みんな応援してくれた。それなのに結果を出せずに申し訳ありません。
example_sentences.english: Everyone cheered me on. And yet, it is inexcusable that I wasn't able to get (good) results.
