example_sentences.japanese: 落し物を拾った。それなのに警察に届けないなんて泥棒です。
example_sentences.english: They picked up the lost property. Despite this, not handing it over to the police makes them a thief.

general_translation: What is called, So-called, Generally known
formation: いわゆる + Noun
casual_structure: いわゆる + Noun
explanation: An old-fashioned grammar point expressing that something is commonly called or generally known as (A).

example_sentences.japanese: それはいわゆる神話というやつです。信用してはいけません。
example_sentences.english: That’s what you’d call a myth. You shouldn’t believe it.

example_sentences.japanese: ハンバーガーやフライドポテトはいわゆるジャンクフードだ。
example_sentences.english: Hamburgers and French fries are so-called junk food.

example_sentences.japanese: それはいわゆる陰謀論というものですね？
example_sentences.english: That is what is called a conspiracy theory, right?

example_sentences.japanese: これはいわゆる和製英語というものです。
example_sentences.english: This is what is called a Japan-made pseudo-English word.

example_sentences.japanese: これはいわゆる宣伝ですので、ご理解ください。
example_sentences.english: Since this is a so-called advertisement, please understand.

example_sentences.japanese: これはいわゆる葬式ではありませんので、悲しまないでください。
example_sentences.english: This is not what you would call a funeral, so do not be sad.

example_sentences.japanese: これはいわゆる総理案件というやつでは？
example_sentences.english: Isn't this what is called a matter related to the prime minister?

example_sentences.japanese: いわゆる送料ですが、無料でやらせてもらっています。
example_sentences.english: This is generally known as (having) postage, but for you there is no charge.

example_sentences.japanese: いわゆる速達でも多分間に合わないと思いますよ。
example_sentences.english: I think the so-called express delivery will probably not make it in time.

example_sentences.japanese: 「素質がない」と言ったが、いわゆる力不足だ。
example_sentences.english: (They) said '(he) doesn't have the qualities,' but it is what is called a lack of power.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい麺を開発したそうだが、これはいわゆる蕎麦だね。
example_sentences.english: I heard that a new noodle was developed, but this is commonly known as soba.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいわゆるゴールドラッシュのおかげで大金を稼いだ。
example_sentences.english: He has earned his fortune thanks to the so-called gold rush.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼を犯罪者扱いするのはやめてください。いわゆる推定無罪ということです。
example_sentences.english: Please stop treating him as a criminal. (He) is what we call presumed innocent.

example_sentences.japanese: 他の言語から取り入れた言葉、いわゆる借用語は日本語の中によくみられる。
example_sentences.english: Words introduced from other languages, so-called loanwords, can often be seen in Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 本物のように見えるが薬効成分のない薬、いわゆる偽薬が場合によって医者から処方されているかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Medicine that looks like the real thing, but does not have an active ingredient (what is called a placebo), might be prescribed by a doctor in some cases.

general_translation: No more than, Just, Merely
formation: Verb +（だけ）にすぎない［い］Adjective +（だけ）にすぎない［な］Adjective +（なだけ）にすぎないNoun +（だけ）にすぎない
casual_structure: Verb +（だけ）にすぎない［い］Adjective +（だけ）にすぎない［な］Adjective +（なだけ）にすぎないNoun +（だけ）にすぎない
polite_structure: Verb +（だけ）にすぎません［い］Adjective +（だけ）にすぎません［な］Adjective +（なだけ）にすぎませんNoun +（だけ）にすぎません
explanation: A grammar point that indicates that (A) is no more than that, or not too much of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 君は学生にすぎない。
example_sentences.english: You are nothing more than a student.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はお金が欲しかったから、あなたを助けたにすぎない。
example_sentences.english: I helped you just because I wanted money.

example_sentences.japanese: どんだけ勉強していても、ちゃんと集中して勉強をしないと時間を無駄にしているにすぎない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much you study, if you don't focus on your studies properly, you are just wasting your time.

example_sentences.japanese: あの建物は古いだけにすぎない。
example_sentences.english: That building is nothing more than old.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんはハンサムなだけにすぎない。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-san is nothing more than handsome.

example_sentences.japanese: 藤田さん、君は子供にすぎない。
example_sentences.english: Fujita-san, you are nothing more than a child.

example_sentences.japanese: この納豆はただくさいだけにすぎない。
example_sentences.english: This natto just smells.

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎はただ不便なだけにすぎない。
example_sentences.english: The countryside is nothing more than inconvenient.

example_sentences.japanese: 行動しなかったら、口だけにすぎない。
example_sentences.english: If you don't act, then that is nothing more than talk.

example_sentences.japanese: 運が悪いだけにすぎない。
example_sentences.english: It is just bad luck. (nothing more than)

example_sentences.japanese: 利害関係があるから、親切にしているにすぎない。
example_sentences.english: Since I have an interest/stake in it, I am merely being kind. (nothing more than)

example_sentences.japanese: 「いつか飲みましょう」って言ったけど、あれは社交辞令にすぎない。
example_sentences.english: I said, 'Let's drink sometime,' but that is no more than social etiquette.

example_sentences.japanese: あの行事は儀式にすぎない。みんなやりたくてやっているわけではない。
example_sentences.english: That event is no more than a ceremony. It doesn't mean that everyone is doing it because they want to.

example_sentences.japanese: あの悔しがり方は芝居にすぎない。騙されてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: That way of resent/regretting is no more than an act. You shouldn't be fooled.

example_sentences.japanese: あの謙虚な態度はまやかしにすぎません。本当はふてぶてしい人です。
example_sentences.english: That humble attitude is no more than a deception. He is really a shameless person.

example_sentences.japanese: その線は目安にすぎません。多少越えても大丈夫です。
example_sentences.english: That line is no more than an estimate. It is okay to go a little over it.

example_sentences.japanese: 北枕がよくないというのは、迷信にすぎない。
example_sentences.english: It is said that laying down with one's head to the north is bad for you. That is no more than superstition.

example_sentences.japanese: あの国王は飾りにすぎない。牛耳っているのは国王の妻だ。
example_sentences.english: That king is no more than a decoration. The person in control is the king's wife.

example_sentences.japanese: この喜びは束の間にすぎない。明日からはまた厳しい練習が待っているのだ。
example_sentences.english: This happiness is no more than a brief moment. We still have hard practices waiting for us from tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: これは氷山の一角にすぎないとおもう...
example_sentences.english: I think that this is just the tip of the iceberg…

general_translation: …And…, Both ... and ..., ... And ... as well
formation: Noun (A)も + Verb［ば］+ Noun (B)もNoun (A)も + ［い］Adjective［ば］+ Noun (B)もNoun (A)も + ［な］Adjective + なら + Noun (B)もNoun (A)も + Noun + なら + Noun (B)も
casual_structure: Noun (A)も + Verb［ば］+ Noun (B)もNoun (A)も + ［い］Adjective［ば］+ Noun (B)もNoun (A)も + ［な］Adjective + なら + Noun (B)もNoun (A)も + Noun + なら + Noun (B)も
explanation: A hypothetical expression that points out that in addition to the surprising (A), the surprising (B) is also true.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は地位もなければお金もない。
example_sentences.english: She has neither status nor money.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんはイタリア語も出来れば、スペイン語も話せる。
example_sentences.english: My father can speak Italian and Spanish.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の冬は湿度も低ければ、温度も低いから外で火を使う時は気をつけないといけない。
example_sentences.english: Winter in Japan is cold and dry, so you have to be careful when using fire outside.

example_sentences.japanese: このギターの音も好きなら柄も好きなので、一生手放したくありません。
example_sentences.english: I like the sound and the design of this guitar, so I never want to let it go.

example_sentences.japanese: マルチ商法の話を聞くたびに、騙す方も騙す方なら、騙される方も騙される方だといつも思う。
example_sentences.english: Whenever I hear about pyramid schemes, I always think that if the scammers are scammers, then the scammed are scammed. (I always think that the scammers and the scammed are both at fault.)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は、実力もあれば、努力もする。
example_sentences.english: That person has capabilities and puts forth effort.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は撮影もできれば、ナレーションもできる。
example_sentences.english: He can do photography and also narration.

example_sentences.japanese: 「うまくいっている」という実感もなければ、兆候もない。
example_sentences.english: There is not any feeling of 'it is going well,' nor is there any indication.

example_sentences.japanese: 総理大臣は、経済も見直せれば、人権問題も解決できます。
example_sentences.english: The Prime Minister can reform the economy and resolve human rights issues.

example_sentences.japanese: あの曲芸師は、茶碗も回せれば、座布団も回せる。
example_sentences.english: That acrobat can spin a tea cup and spin a cushion.

example_sentences.japanese: あの子は、算数もできなければ国語もできないから、将来が不安です。
example_sentences.english: That child cannot do math, and cannot do Japanese, so I am anxious about their future.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は、スポーツも上手にできれば、仕事も効率よくできる。
example_sentences.english: He can play sports well and does his job efficiently.

example_sentences.japanese: あのバスは、指定席もなければ予約もできないから、行ってみないと乗れるか分からない。
example_sentences.english: Since that bus does not have assigned seating and you cannot reserve a seat, if you do not go and check, you won't know if you can ride or not.

example_sentences.japanese: あの候補者は、地盤もなければ知名度もないから、たぶん受からないと思います。
example_sentences.english: Since that candidate does not have a base and does not have popularity, I think perhaps he will not win.

example_sentences.japanese: 人は皆、短所もあれば弱さもある。だからこそ、助け合って生きるのです。
example_sentences.english: Everyone has disadvantages and weaknesses. For that reason, live to help each other.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は、習字もできれば、ピアノだって弾けるし、スポーツも万能だ。
example_sentences.english: He can write well, as well as play the piano, and he is versatile in sports.

example_sentences.japanese: あの居酒屋のスタッフの態度もよければ、値段も高いから人気がある。
example_sentences.english: The attitude of the staff at that izakaya is good and it is expensive, which is why they are so popular. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Merely, Nothing but, No more than
formation: Noun + でしかない
casual_structure: Noun + でしかない
polite_structure: Noun + でしかありません
explanation: A phrase that determines that (A) is nothing more than (A), or just (A).

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は見栄の塊でしかない。
example_sentences.english: That person is nothing but the embodiment of vanity.

example_sentences.japanese: それは言い訳でしかない。
example_sentences.english: That is nothing but an excuse.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩は愛のムチだと言っているが、暴言でしかない。
example_sentences.english: My senpai says that he is saying this out of love, but it's nothing more than abusive language.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子にとっては宝物かもしれないが、私にとってはゴミでしかない。
example_sentences.english: To my son, it is something precious, but to me it is nothing but garbage.

example_sentences.japanese: 聞こえはいいが、安易な言い訳でしかない。
example_sentences.english: That sounds good, however it is merely a simple excuse.

example_sentences.japanese: 「訓練だ」と言っているが、あんなの意地悪でしかない。
example_sentences.english: They are saying it is 'discipline', but it is merely bullying.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女から秘密を教えてもらったが、ウソでしかなかった。
example_sentences.english: She shared some secrets with me, but they were nothing more than lies.

example_sentences.japanese: アイデアは悪くないが、机上の空論でしかない。
example_sentences.english: The idea is not bad, but it is merely academic gossip.

example_sentences.japanese: 君の言うことはもっともだが、飽くまで理想でしかない。
example_sentences.english: What you are saying is plausible, but after all, it is merely an ideal.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は憧れでしかない。きっと友達になんてなれないだろう…
example_sentences.english: I merely long for that person. Surely, I could never be friends (with them)...

example_sentences.japanese: あの発言は甘えでしかない。厳しく対応する必要があると思う。
example_sentences.english: That remark is merely to be agreeable. I think it is necessary to respond strictly.

example_sentences.japanese: プロの野球選手になる事は夢でしかない。たぶんなれないと思う。
example_sentences.english: Becoming a professional baseball player is merely a dream. I think that it probably cannot be done.

example_sentences.japanese: 賞味期限は目安でしかない。多少過ぎても気にしない。
example_sentences.english: The best by date is merely an estimate. I don't worry if it is a little past the date.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに成長しても、親から見ると息子は子供でしかない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much he grows up, the parents will always see their son as nothing more than a child.

example_sentences.japanese: 事故を起こしたとしても、あなたが無事なら全部大丈夫。車は車でしかないよ。
example_sentences.english: Even if you did cause an accident, so long as you're fine, everything's okay. The car is nothing but a car.

general_translation: Can't help but want to, Very, Extremely
formation: Can't help but want to...Verb［たい］［て］ + たまらないVery・Extremely［い］Adjective［て］+ たまらない［な］Adjective + で + たまらない
casual_structure: Can't help but want to...Verb［たい］［て］ + たまらないVery・Extremely［い］Adjective［て］+ たまらない［な］Adjective + で + たまらない
polite_structure: Can't help but want to...Verb［たい］［て］+ たまりませんVery・Extremely［い］Adjective［て］+ たまりません［な］Adjective + で + たまりません
explanation: A phrase which expresses not doing (A) as being intolerable, or unbearable.

example_sentences.japanese: サイレンの音がうるさくてたまらない。
example_sentences.english: The sound of the siren is extremely loud. (I can't stand it)

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は３時間しか寝てないから、眠たくてたまらない。
example_sentences.english: I only slept for 3 hours last night, so I'm extremely sleepy.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月公開される映画が見たくてたまらない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but want to watch the movie that is going to be released next month.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘をお使いに行かせたが、ちゃんと一人で行って帰ってこれるかが心配でたまらない。
example_sentences.english: I sent my daughter on an errand, but I'm extremely worried about whether she would be able to go and come back by herself.

example_sentences.japanese: 蚊に刺されてかゆくてたまらない。
example_sentences.english: I was bitten by a mosquito and it is extremely itchy. (I can't stand it・I can't help but itch)

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の子供のことがしんぱいでたまらない。
example_sentences.english: I am extremely worried about my own kids.

example_sentences.japanese: あつくてたまらない。だからクーラーをつけた。
example_sentences.english: It is extremely hot. So, I turned on the air conditioner. (I can't stand it・I can't help but be hot)

example_sentences.japanese: あのコーラスグループのコンサートがみたくてたまらない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but want to see that chorus group's concert.

example_sentences.japanese: 胡椒をかけたら、くしゃみがひどくてたまらない。
example_sentences.english: If you put pepper on it, I can't help but sneeze a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のコレクションの中の一つがほしくてたまらない。
example_sentences.english: I really want one of the things in his collection. (extremely)

example_sentences.japanese: 梅雨の季節は湿気がひどくてたまらない。
example_sentences.english: The humidity in the rainy season is extremely awful. (I can't stand it)

example_sentences.japanese: 納豆の嫌いなところは、くさくてたまらないところだ。
example_sentences.english: What I don't like about natto is that it smells very bad. (I can't stand it)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の家はいつも散らかっている。きたなくてたまらない。
example_sentences.english: His house is always in a state of disorder. It is extremely dirty. (I can't stand it)

example_sentences.japanese: あの工場から出る匂い、焦げくさくてたまらない。
example_sentences.english: The smell coming from that factory is extremely stinky like something is burning. (I can't stand it)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はたくさん仕事をしたので、ねむくてたまらない。
example_sentences.english: Because I did a lot of work today, I am extremely tired. (I can't help but feel tired)

general_translation: Even if, Even though, No matter, Whether… or
formation: Verb + にしろ(1) + Phrase［い］Adjective + にしろ(1) + Phrase［な］Adjective + (である）+ にしろ(1) + PhraseNoun + （である）+ にしろ(1) + Phrase(1) にせよ
casual_structure: Verb + にしろ(1) + Phrase［い］Adjective + にしろ(1) + Phrase［な］Adjective + (である）+ にしろ(1) + PhraseNoun + （である）+ にしろ(1) + Phrase(1) にせよ
explanation: A strong, imperative phrase, highlighting that regardless of (A), (B) is still true.

example_sentences.japanese: 違いがあるにせよ、わずかな差だ。
example_sentences.english: Even if there is a difference, it is minimal.

example_sentences.japanese: 飲み会に参加しないにせよ、参加費は明日までに持ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: Even if you are not going to attend the drinking party, please bring your entrance fee by tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 怖いにしろ、私の仕事なのでやらなくてはならない。
example_sentences.english: Even though it scares me, I have to do it because it's my job.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに不便であるにせよ、私は自然が豊かな田舎に住みたいです。
example_sentences.english: Even if it would be very inconvenient, I would prefer to live in the countryside where nature is abundant.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は相手が子供にしろ、一切手加減はしない。
example_sentences.english: That person does not take it easy at all, even if the opponent is a child.

example_sentences.japanese: それは難しいにしろ、するしかない。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is hard, I have no choice but to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 飲まないにしろ、居酒屋に行こう。
example_sentences.english: Even if we don't drink, let's go to an Izakaya.

example_sentences.japanese: いずれにせよ、この決定は変わりません。
example_sentences.english: At any rate, this decision will stand.

example_sentences.japanese: それが上司の命令にせよ、わたしは従えません。
example_sentences.english: Even if that is an order from the boss, I will not follow it.

example_sentences.japanese: この状態では何にせよ、誰かに助けてもらうしかないよ。
example_sentences.english: In this situation, no matter what we do we need to get someone to help us.

example_sentences.japanese: 悪い結果にしろ、いつかハードワークが報われる時が来るでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Even if the results are bad, eventually hard work will pay off.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長に頼まれたにせよ、今回は断るしかない。
example_sentences.english: Even if the company chief asked me, I would have to refuse.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえこちらが正当であるにせよ、いま抗議するのはタイミングが悪い。
example_sentences.english: Even if we are right, this is not the time to protest.

example_sentences.japanese: わが社の提案は一目見てお分りいただけるにしろ、そちらに納得いただけるかどうかは保証できません。
example_sentences.english: Even if they can understand our offer instantly, I cannot guarantee that they will be satisfied with it. (even though)

example_sentences.japanese: どんな事情があったにしろ、締め切りは先週だった。もう少し締め切りよりも早く書類を提出してもよかった。
example_sentences.english: No matter the circumstances, the deadline was a week ago. It would have been better to have submitted the documents before the deadline.

example_sentences.japanese: 詩人：「私が死亡するにせよ青銅の記念碑より詩で永続する記憶が存在するだろう。」
example_sentences.english: Poet: 'Even if I die, with my poems, I have created a legacy that will last longer than any bronze monument.'

general_translation: No wonder, After all, In fact, Because, At any rate
formation: 何（なに）しろ + Phrase
casual_structure: 何（なに）しろ + Phrase
explanation: A strong imperative phrase, showing that whatever the case may be, (A) is the underlying cause or truth.

example_sentences.japanese: なにしろ暑いからね。食欲も出ないよ。
example_sentences.english: Because it is so hot. It's no wonder that I have lost my appetite.

example_sentences.japanese: なにしろ彼はまだ始めたばかりなので大目に見てやってください。
example_sentences.english: After all, he is new, so please cut him some slack.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はできて当たり前だよ。なにしろ彼はプロなんだから。
example_sentences.english: It's no wonder he can do it. After all, he is a professional.

example_sentences.japanese: なにしろ今日は普段より暑かったからクタクタだよ。
example_sentences.english: After all, it was hotter than usual today, so I'm exhausted.

example_sentences.japanese: なにしろこの商品は不便すぎるので、どれだけ値下げをしても売れないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: After all, this product is too inconvenient and will not sell no matter how low the price goes.

example_sentences.japanese: なにしろ期限が迫っている。急いでくれないか。
example_sentences.english: At any rate, the deadline is drawing near. Won't you hurry up?

example_sentences.japanese: なにしろ基礎ができていないから、彼に数学を教えるのは大変だ。
example_sentences.english: At any rate, since his math foundation is not up to par, it is difficult to teach him math.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこの会社はなにしろ規律が厳しい。あれじゃあまるで軍隊だ。
example_sentences.english: At any rate, that company has strict rules. It is pretty much the equivalent of being in the military.

example_sentences.japanese: あの社長はなにしろ強引だから、それで会社を辞めた人もたくさんいます。
example_sentences.english: At any rate, that CEO is overbearing, so therefore, the company has a lot of people quitting.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の父はなにしろ合理的で、無駄なことを一切しません。
example_sentences.english: At any rate, my father is rational and would never do anything pointless.

example_sentences.japanese: 奢ってあげたいけど、なにしろお小遣いが少なくてね。お金がないんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I want to treat you, but at any rate, my allowance is small. I don't have any money.

example_sentences.japanese: なにしろ言葉遣いがなってないから、面接受かるはずないよ。
example_sentences.english: At any rate, since his choice of words is unacceptable, there is a good chance (he) won't pass the interview.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はなにしろ教養がないから、接客していても微妙なことばかり言ってしまう。
example_sentences.english: After all, since he has no culture, he constantly says insensitive things while serving customers.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「トムちゃんはやっと寝付いたね？」Ｂ：「なにしろ、一日中遊んで疲れたからね。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Little Tommy finally fell asleep, right?' B:' No wonder, it's because he got tired from playing all day.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はなにしろ謙虚だ。あれだけの成績を収めても、決して天狗にならない。
example_sentences.english: After all, he is modest. Even if he gets results to that degree, he is certain not to brag about it.

example_sentences.japanese: 文法ちゃん：「どうしてそんなに悲しそうにしてるの？」 メガネくん：「悲しいのも当然だろ。なにしろガールフレンドにフラれたんだから。」
example_sentences.english: Bunpou-chan: 'Why the long face?' Glasses-kun: 'Isn't it obvious why I am sad? After all, my girlfriend dumped me.'

general_translation: Whether… or
formation: Verb + にしろ(1) + Verb + にしろ(1)［い］Adjective + にしろ(1) + ［い］Adjective + にしろ(1)［な］Adjective +  (である) + にしろ(1) ［な］Adjective +  (である) + にしろ(1)Noun +  (である) + にしろ(1) + Noun +  (である) + にしろ(1)(1) にせよ
casual_structure: Verb + にしろ(1) + Verb + にしろ(1)［い］Adjective + にしろ(1) + ［い］Adjective + にしろ(1)［な］Adjective +  (である) + にしろ(1) ［な］Adjective +  (である) + にしろ(1)Noun +  (である) + にしろ(1) + Noun +  (である) + にしろ(1)(1) にせよ
explanation: A strong, imperative phrase, expressing that regardless of whether it is (A) or (B), the result will not change. Often used with antonyms.

example_sentences.japanese: 好きにしろ嫌いにしろ、このワクチンは義務づけられている。
example_sentences.english: Whether you like it or hate it, the vaccine is obligatory.

example_sentences.japanese: このイベントに参加するにせよしないにせよ、私に連絡をください。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not you plan to attend this event, please contact me.

example_sentences.japanese: 給料が多いにしろ少ないにしろ、給料をもらっている以上ちゃんと働かないといけない。
example_sentences.english: As long as you are getting paid, you must properly do your job whether you get paid well or not.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強が好きにせよ嫌いにせよ、子供である以上、勉強はしなくてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: Whether you like studying or not, as long as you are a child, you have to study.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長にしろアルバイトにしろ、工場内での喫煙は禁止されている。
example_sentences.english: Whether you are the president or a part-time worker, smoking is prohibited in the factory.

example_sentences.japanese: 公務にしろプライベートにしろ、ルールはちゃんと守ってください。
example_sentences.english: Whether it is public or private, please properly obey the rules.

example_sentences.japanese: 古典にしろ新作にしろ、とにかく彼の落語が好きだ。
example_sentences.english: Whether it is his old stuff or a new, in any case, I like his rakugo.

example_sentences.japanese: 言葉遣いにしろ態度にしろ、彼の印象はとにかく悪い。
example_sentences.english: Whether in speech or attitude, I have a really bad impression of him.

example_sentences.japanese: 寿司にしろ刺身にしろ、とにかく生の魚が好きなんです。
example_sentences.english: Whether it is sushi or sashimi, in any case, I like raw fish.

example_sentences.japanese: 下書きするにしろしないにしろ、ちゃんと完成させてくれたらそれでいい。
example_sentences.english: Whether you made a rough draft or not, it would be good if you properly finished it.

example_sentences.japanese: 実用化されるにしろされないにしろ、僕はこのアイデアを形にしたい。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not you implement it, I want to make this idea take form.

example_sentences.japanese: 国語にしろ算数にしろ、勉強というものはすべて苦手だ。
example_sentences.english: Whether it is Japanese or math, I am bad at studying everything.

example_sentences.japanese: 作者にしろ編集者にしろ、こんな本を出版しようと思うなんてどうかしている。
example_sentences.english: Whether it was the writer or the editor, what were they thinking planning on publishing such a book.

example_sentences.japanese: 勝ったにしろ、勝てなかったにしろ、去年の優勝者に対して善戦した。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether they won or lost, they put up a good fight against last year's champion.

example_sentences.japanese: 村にせよ大都市にせよ、近代では下水は絶対必要だ。
example_sentences.english: Whether it is a village or a big city, the sewage system is absolutely necessary in modern times.

example_sentences.japanese: 平凡な住人にしろ大統領にしろ、この辺りでは喫煙は禁じられている。
example_sentences.english: Whether you are an ordinary inhabitant or the president, smoking is forbidden in this area.

example_sentences.japanese: このレストランは、料理にせよ接客態度にしろ、全てが最悪だ。
example_sentences.english: Everything about this restaurant, whether it be the food or the customer service attitude, is terrible. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 浅い川にしろ深い川にしろ、子供にはライフジャケット着させないといけない。
example_sentences.english: Whether the river is deep or shallow, children must wear life jackets.

general_translation: Setting aside, Apart from
formation: Noun + は + ともかく（として）
casual_structure: Noun + は + ともかく（として）
explanation: An expression used to change topic, by alluding to or hinting at there being other important things to discuss or do.

example_sentences.japanese: 冗談はともかく、そろそろビジネスの話だ。
example_sentences.english: All jokes aside, let's get down to business.

example_sentences.japanese: この料理の見た目はともかく、味はとてもいい。
example_sentences.english: Apart from the appearance of this dish, it is very delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: 家賃が高いか安いかはともかく、東京駅の近くに住みたい。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside whether the rent is expensive or cheap, I want to live near Tokyo station.

example_sentences.japanese: 給料はともかく、やりがいのある仕事がしたい。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside the pay, I want a worthwhile job.

example_sentences.japanese: 家屋はともかくとしてもだ、せめてアルバムだけでも持って逃げたい。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside the house, I at least want to take the album and run.

example_sentences.japanese: カタカナはともかく、平仮名は読めないと困ります。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside katakana, you will be in trouble if you can't read hiragana.

example_sentences.japanese: 楽器はともかく、せめて歌だけでも歌いましょうよ。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside instruments, let's at least sing a song.

example_sentences.japanese: 関東はともかく、関西でだけでもいいから売れたい。
example_sentences.english: Apart from Kanto, even if it is just Kansai that's fine, I just want to sell it.

example_sentences.japanese: 看病はともかく、買い物だけでもしてもらえると助かります。
example_sentences.english: Putting aside the caregiving, if you could at least do the shopping (for me), it would be a big help.

example_sentences.japanese: 行事はともかく、授業にはちゃんと出席してください。
example_sentences.english: Apart from the event, please also properly attend class.

example_sentences.japanese: このスマホの形はともかく、性能は一線級だと思ってる。
example_sentences.english: Apart from the shape of this smartphone, I think its performance is top-notch.

example_sentences.japanese: この実験、方法はともかくとして、結果は予想外に素晴らしい。
example_sentences.english: This experiment, setting methods aside, has unexpectedly amazing results.

example_sentences.japanese: 怒った妻：「どうしてこんな夜遅くに帰ってきたの？それはともかく、あなたの服、どこなの？」
example_sentences.english: An angry wife: 'Why are you coming home so late? Apart from that, your clothes, where are they?'

example_sentences.japanese: 外部の人間はともかく、内部の人間にはちゃんと機密を守ってもらいます。
example_sentences.english: Apart from the outsiders, the insiders will properly protect the secret.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語能力試験に合格したかはともかく、過去半年間にたくさんのことを学んだ。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside whether I passed the JLPT or not, I have learned a lot over the last six months.

example_sentences.japanese: 美人か美人じゃないかはともかく、優しくて料理が上手な人と結婚をしたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to marry someone who is kind and a good cook, whether she is beautiful or not is neither here nor there.

general_translation: Whether or, Things like, And … so on
formation: A(1) + やら + B(1) + やら(1) Verb［る］、Noun、［い］Adjective
casual_structure: A(1) + やら + B(1) + やら(1) Verb［る］、Noun、［い］Adjective
explanation: A structure used to express things from within a list when the speaker is uncertain about determining any one thing as the main part.

example_sentences.japanese: 嬉しいやら恥ずかしいやらで、どんな顔をしていればいいのか、わからなかった。
example_sentences.english: I didn't know whether I should react with happiness or shyness.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日子供の世話をするやら家事をするやらで忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: I am busy everyday with things such as taking care of my child and doing house chores.

example_sentences.japanese: 先週は身体中が痛いやら、体調が悪いやらで大変でした。
example_sentences.english: Last week I had a tough week because my whole body was aching, wasn't feeling well and so on.

example_sentences.japanese: あのニュースを聞いてから不安やら怒りやら、色々な感情が溢れ出てきた。
example_sentences.english: After hearing that news, I was flooded with feelings such as anxiety, anger, and many other emotions.

example_sentences.japanese: 文法だけではなく漢字やら単語やらも勉強した方がいい。
example_sentences.english: You should study not only grammar but also things such as kanji and vocabulary.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼に褒めてもらうとうれしいやら恥ずかしいやら、とにかく気持ちがよかったわ。
example_sentences.english: When I was praised by him, I don't know whether I felt happiness or shyness. Anyway, it felt great.

example_sentences.japanese: 髭やら頭髪やらの身だしなみのチェックが厳しくて困る。
example_sentences.english: Checking personal grooming such as beard and hair and so on, is so strict that I am bothered.

example_sentences.japanese: 悪口やら皮肉やら、彼はとにかく口が悪いから、あまり付き合いたくない。
example_sentences.english: Whether it is insults or sarcasm, he has a dirty mouth, so I don't really want to spend time with him.

example_sentences.japanese: 小数やら分数やらの問題を教えて欲しいと言われても、算数が苦手なもので...
example_sentences.english: Even if someone says they want me to teach them about decimals and fractions and such problems, I am no good at math...

example_sentences.japanese: マスクやら手洗い・うがいやら、他にも万全の風邪対策をしている。
example_sentences.english: I wear a mask and wash my hands and gargle and so on in addition to taking perfect countermeasures against catching a cold.

example_sentences.japanese: この時期には、マフラーやら手袋やらの忘れ物がかなりの数に上ります。
example_sentences.english: In this season, the number of lost property like scarves, gloves and so on increases.

example_sentences.japanese: あの映画は、戦闘シーンやら冒険シーン等があるから、君も見てみたらいいよ。
example_sentences.english: In that movie, there are many scenes of battles, adventures and so on, you should watch it.

example_sentences.japanese: 歯磨きやら化粧やらでバタバタとしていたら、家を出るのが遅くなってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Hurriedly brushing my teeth and doing my makeup and so on, I ended up leaving the house late.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供は母に叱られたあと、泣くやら、鼻が出ているやらで、ひどい騒ぎだった。
example_sentences.english: When a child was scolded by her mother, she ended up crying, having a runny nose and so on. It was quite the scene.

example_sentences.japanese: さまらさん：「明日パーティーやるんだけど、来る？男の子もいっぱいくるよ。」さだこさん：「パーティー？仕事やら大学やらいろいろあるから遠慮しておくわ。」
example_sentences.english: Samara: 'I am having a party tomorrow, are you coming? There will be a lot of boys!' Sadako: 'Party? I have things like work and college, so I have to refuse.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「ＧＰＳを買うか買わないかわからん...でも、ＧＰＳがどうしてもほしい。」Ｂ：「どうせＧＰＳを買いたいと思ってるなら 、最近の携帯電話はカメラやらＧＰＳやらついているからただのＧＰＳよりスマホを買ったらいい。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I don't know whether to buy a GPS or not… But I want one so much.' B: 'If you want to buy a GPS anyway, modern mobile phones have cameras, GPS and so on. So rather than buying an ordinary GPS, it's better to get a smartphone.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は大学に行くのやら行かないのやらはっきりしない。
example_sentences.english: It is not clear whether she is going to college or not.

example_sentences.japanese: あの歌手は上手なのやら下手なのやら、私にはさっぱりわかりません。
example_sentences.english: I have no idea if that person is a good singer or not.

general_translation: However, Nevertheless, But
formation: Phrase。 しかしながら + Phrase
casual_structure: Phrase。 しかしながら + Phrase
explanation: A formal phrase expressing nevertheless. While in unison with (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「多くの喫煙者は喫煙が癌の原因の一つであることを知っている。しかしながら、気にせずに未だタバコを吸い続けている。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Many smokers know that smoking is one of the causes of cancer. However, they don't care and continue to smoke.'

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は安全な国だと言われている。しかしながら１００％安全というわけでもない。
example_sentences.english: Japan is said to be a safe country. However, it is not 100% safe.

example_sentences.japanese: 精一杯頑張れば夢が叶うと言われている。しかしながら、人生はそう甘くない。
example_sentences.english: It is said that if you work as hard as you can, your dreams will come true. However, life is not so easy.

example_sentences.japanese: そのアイデアはいいと思います。しかしながら、我々の予算だとそのプランを実行することはできないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: I think the idea is good. However, our budget will not allow us to implement that plan.

example_sentences.japanese: ある電気自動車は自動的に運転することができる。しかしながら運転者はまだハンドルの上に手を置く必要がある。
example_sentences.english: 'Certain electric cars can steer automatically. However, the driver still has to keep their hands on the steering wheel.'

example_sentences.japanese: オンラインの安全性の記事：「オンラインショッピングは安全だと考えられている。しかしながら詐欺に遭う可能性が０であるわけではない。」
example_sentences.english: Article about online safety: 'Online shopping is considered safe. However, it doesn't mean that the likelihood of falling victim to a scam is 0.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「オゾンホールの問題は９０年代には解決できるとは思われていなかった。しかしながら、国際協力により、オゾン層は２００５年ごろから回復が進んでいる。」
example_sentences.english: 'The ozone hole problem didn't seem solvable in the 90s. However, thanks to international cooperation, the ozone layer has been recovering since around 2005.'

example_sentences.japanese: アニメーション評価：「『ジェイクとビーモ』というアニメーションは子供向けである。しかしながら、子供たちだけでなく大人向きでもある。」
example_sentences.english: Animation review: 'The animated cartoon "Jake and Beemo" is targeted at children. However, it is suitable not only for children, but for adults as well.'

example_sentences.japanese: 大学を卒業したなら簡単に就職できると考えられている。しかしながら今の就職難の現状からみて、実際は、そのように簡単ではない。
example_sentences.english: It is considered easy to get a job if one graduates from a university. However, judging from the current scarcity of employment, this does not seem to be the case.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「国Ａの政府と国Ｂの政府の関係は悪化しています。しかしながら、一般市民達の関係は依然として良い状態です。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'The relations between the governments of country A and country B are getting worse. However, the relations between ordinary citizens are still in a good state.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「親は自分の子供を客観視しにくいというのは事実である。しかしながら、必要がある場合は、脇から見ることもできるのではないだろうか。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'It is a fact that parents have a hard time looking at their children objectively. However, should the need arise, I think they are also able to look at them without any presumptions.'

example_sentences.japanese: 経済についての記事：「好景気により日本から海外への輸出はこのところ増加を続けている。しかしながら、多くの専門家はそれが一時的な傾向かもしれないので、不景気ための準備しておく必要があると政府や実業家に訴えてる。」
example_sentences.english: Article about the economy: 'Thanks to the booming economy, Japanese exports have been growing lately. However, many experts appeal to the government and business people that preparations for a recession are necessary, since it may be a temporary trend.'

example_sentences.japanese: オンラインの安全性の記事：「Ｇｍａｉｌは添付ファイルをアンチウイルスソフトでスキャンしています。それによって安全に開くことが出来ると思っている人が多いです。しかしながら、十分な安全性を保証することは出来ないので、気をつけて下さい。」
example_sentences.english: Article about online safety: 'Many people think that they can open attachments in Gmail safely due to them scanning the files with antivirus software. However, it is still not completely safe, so please be careful.'

example_sentences.japanese: ＡＩについての記事：「とあるスポーツ用品の製造を行う会社はコスト削減のために全自動の工場を建設した。しかしながら、人力より生産の柔軟性が低いことが明らかになった。そのため、閉鎖した。」
example_sentences.english: Article about AI: 'A certain company that manufactures sports articles had built a fully automatic factory to decrease costs. However, it turned out that production flexibility was lower than with human labor. Because of that, it has been closed.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「人の筋肉は、通常、わずかな自分の力のみを使用しています。しかしながら、例外があります。もし命が脅かされている場合、脳が制限を取っ払うことができます。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Human muscles usually use only a fraction of their power. However, there are exceptions. If one's life is in danger, the brain can strip away restrictions.'

general_translation: Just because… doesn't mean…
formation: Phrase + からといって + Phrase + ことにはならないPhrase［ても］ + ことにはならない
casual_structure: Phrase + からといって + Phrase + ことにはならないPhrase［ても］ + ことにはならない
polite_structure: Phrase + からといって + Phrase + ことにはなりませんPhrase［ても］ + ことにはなりません
explanation: An expression indicating that which is (A) will not generally become (B), or doesn't mean that it will become (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 錆びているからといって、ガラクタだということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because it is rusty doesn't mean it is junk.

example_sentences.japanese: 殴られたからと言って、殴り返してもいいということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because someone hits you doesn't mean it's okay to hit back.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなが簡単にできたからと言って、君にも簡単にできるということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because it was easy for everyone else doesn't mean it will be easy for you.

example_sentences.japanese: いくら上司でも、仕事を全部部下たちに押し付けてもいいことにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because you are the boss doesn't mean that you can force all your work onto your subordinates.

example_sentences.japanese: ５分ノートを見直しただけでは、勉強したことにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because you reviewed your notes for five minutes doesn't mean that you have studied.

example_sentences.japanese: サンプルだからといって、乱暴に扱ってもいいということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because it is a sample doesn't mean that it is okay to handle it carelessly.

example_sentences.japanese: 祝日だからといって、いつまで寝ていてもいいということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because it is a holiday doesn't mean it is okay to sleep until anytime you please.

example_sentences.japanese: 実力があるからといって、威張ってもいいということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because you have some real ability doesn't mean it is okay to be proud/boastful about it.

example_sentences.japanese: ジャーナリストだからといって、事実を何でも公表してもいいということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because you are a journalist doesn't mean it is okay to publicize any fact you like.

example_sentences.japanese: 集金だからといって、どんなに遅い時間に訪問してもいいということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because you are collecting money doesn't mean it is okay to come knocking at any late hour you please.

example_sentences.japanese: 出張だからといって、羽を伸ばしてもいいということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because it is a business trip doesn't mean it is okay to have a good time.

example_sentences.japanese: お金を払うからといって、いくらでもお酒を飲んでいいということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because I am paying doesn't mean that it is okay to drink as much as you like.

example_sentences.japanese: サンタさんが太っているからと言って、煙突から入れないということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because Santa is fat, that doesn't mean that he can't come in through the chimney.

example_sentences.japanese: 撮影だからといって、近所の人に迷惑をかけてもいいということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because it is photography, doesn't mean that it is okay to create a nuisance for your neighbors.

example_sentences.japanese: いいホテルに泊まろうと言ったとしても、必ず一流ホテルに泊まるということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because I said let's stay at a nice hotel, that doesn't necessarily mean that we will stay at a five star hotel.

example_sentences.japanese: 母親が美しいと言われていても、その娘が成長したら美人になるということにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Just because it is said that a mother is beautiful, it does not necessarily mean that her daughter will be beautiful when she grows up.

general_translation: No wonder, Not surprising that, As expected
formation: Verb + だけのことはある［い］Adjective + だけのことはあるNoun +（だった）+ だけのことはある［な］Adjective + な(1) + だけのことはある(1) だった
casual_structure: Verb + だけのことはある［い］Adjective + だけのことはあるNoun +（だった）+ だけのことはある［な］Adjective + な(1) + だけのことはある(1) だった
polite_structure: Verb + だけのことはあります［い］Adjective + だけのことはありますNoun +（だった）+ だけのことはあります［な］Adjective + な(1) + だけのことはあります(1) だった
explanation: A positive structure highlighting that just with that which is (A), in general (B) existing could have been expected, or is not surprising.

example_sentences.japanese: かなりの実力だ。誘いを蹴っただけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: (He) is quite competent. As expected from refusing temptation.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘が空手の大会で優勝した。さすがに一年間毎日稽古に行っていただけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: My daughter won a karate competition. As expected, she has been going to practice every day for a year.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中くんは体力もあるし動きもテキパキしている。やっぱり若いだけのことはあるな。
example_sentences.english: As expected from someone as young as Tanaka-kun, he is physically strong and moves quickly.

example_sentences.japanese: あのホテルのサービスはとても良かったし、朝食と夕食もものすごく美味しかった。やっぱり有名なだけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: The service at that hotel was very good and the breakfast and dinner were extremely delicious. As expected from how famous that place is.

example_sentences.japanese: 高橋先生が書く漢字はものすごく綺麗だ。さすが習字の先生だけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: Takahashi-sensei's kanji writing is extremely beautiful. As expected from a calligraphy teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: あの政治家はとても信頼されている。さすが昔から正直だっただけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: As expected from a politician that has been honest for years, he is very trusted.

example_sentences.japanese: 鈴木さんは６０歳なのにムキムキだ。昔ボクサーだっただけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: As expected from someone who used to be a boxer, Suzuki-san is very muscular even though he is 60 years old.

example_sentences.japanese: すごいことを思いついた。苦心しただけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: I hit upon something great. As expected from the hard work I did.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕上がりが完璧だ。彼にお願いしただけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: The finished product is perfect. As expected having made the request to him.

example_sentences.japanese: 利益が上がってきた。経費を削っただけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: Profits have begun to rise. As expected from cutting down on expenses.

example_sentences.japanese: いい芝居だった。一生懸命稽古しただけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: It was a good play. As expected from the practicing with all of one's heart.

example_sentences.japanese: しっかり休養しただけのことはある。かなり元気になった。
example_sentences.english: As expected from taking a solid break, I have become considerably more energetic.

example_sentences.japanese: 開幕から８連勝だ。戦力を強化しただけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: From the opening, he has had 8 straight victories. As expected from reinforcing his fighting ability.

example_sentences.japanese: わざわざ担当を交替させただけのことはある。状況がかなり改善された。
example_sentences.english: As expected from specifically changing the person in charge, the conditions have improved considerably.

example_sentences.japanese: 公表しただけのことはある。続々と問い合わせがある。
example_sentences.english: As expected from making an official announcement, inquiries have come one after another.

example_sentences.japanese: メアリーさんはカーリングで金メダルを取った。やはり子供のころから練習していただけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: Mary won a gold medal in Curling. No wonder, she has been practicing from childhood.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は昨日、試験の結果発表があり合格した。さすがに二か月勉強しているだけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: The exam results were announced yesterday and my son passed. As expected considering he studied for two months.

example_sentences.japanese: 片岡さんは英語でペラペラ話している。数年間もアメリカで留学してきただけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: Kataoka-san is speaking English fluently. No wonder, he studied abroad in the United States for several years.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は試験に合格できなかった。馬鹿なだけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: As expected from an idiot, my daughter failed the exam. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Must not, Cannot, Should not
formation: Verb［て］+ はならない
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ はならない
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ はなりません
explanation: A strong expression indicating that one must not do (A). It cannot become that (A) occurs.

example_sentences.japanese: くれぐれもこの戸をあけてはならない。
example_sentences.english: You must not open this door under any circumstances.

example_sentences.japanese: この池では泳いではならない。
example_sentences.english: You must not swim in this lake.

example_sentences.japanese: お酒を飲んで運転してはならない。
example_sentences.english: You must not drink and drive.

example_sentences.japanese: 妊娠している間はタバコを吸ってはならない。
example_sentences.english: You must not smoke while you are pregnant.

example_sentences.japanese: 十代はお酒をのんではならない。
example_sentences.english: Teenagers must not drink any alcohol.

example_sentences.japanese: 市民病院ではタバコをすってはならない。
example_sentences.english: You must not smoke in the municipal hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: 安易に規律をやぶってはならない。
example_sentences.english: You must not simply break rules.

example_sentences.japanese: 何事も限度をこえてはならない。
example_sentences.english: You must not push the limits of anything and everything.

example_sentences.japanese: 機密情報を公表してはならない。
example_sentences.english: You must not publicize confidential information.

example_sentences.japanese: 顕微鏡を乱暴にあつかってはならない。
example_sentences.english: You must not treat the microscope carelessly.

example_sentences.japanese: 強引に勧誘してはならない。逆効果だ。
example_sentences.english: You must not invite forcefully. That has the opposite effect.

example_sentences.japanese: このセーターは縮むから、自分であらってはならない。
example_sentences.english: Because this sweater will shrink, you must not wash it yourself.

example_sentences.japanese: 他人の姿は決してわらってはならない。
example_sentences.english: You absolutely must not laugh at other people's appearances.

example_sentences.japanese: その文章はけずってはならない。意味が分かりにくくなる。
example_sentences.english: You must not remove that sentence. The meaning will become difficult to understand.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの会社は「敬語をつかってはならない」という変なルールがある。
example_sentences.english: My company has this strange rule of 'You must not use keigo'.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなことで泣いていてはだめだ！
example_sentences.english: You shouldn't cry over something like this.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議中に携帯を使ってはいけない。
example_sentences.english: You must not use your cellphone during the meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: ここから先は関係者以外、入ってはならない。
example_sentences.english: You must not enter from this point forward if you are not an authorized personnel.

general_translation: Not well or properly, Not much or enough, Barely, Hardly
formation: ろくに + (Negative) Phrase
casual_structure: ろくに + (Negative) Phrase
explanation: A grammar point highlighting that something is not satisfactorily, or hardly (A). (A) doesn't even reach ground level.

example_sentences.japanese: ろくに準備もしていないのに、ショップをオープンさせた。
example_sentences.english: Even though we had barely prepared, I had them open the shop. (hardly・not well/properly)

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は英語をろくに話せないのに、アメリカにひとりで行くそうだ。大丈夫かな。
example_sentences.english: Apparently my son is going to the States, even though he can barely speak English. I hope he will be okay.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はろくに仕事も出来ないのに、偉そうな態度をとるから会社中で嫌われている。
example_sentences.english: He is disliked by everyone in the company because he has an arrogant attitude even though he can barely do his job.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が忙しすぎて、ここ最近、ろくに友達にも会えていない。
example_sentences.english: Because I am so busy, I barely have time to see my friends.

example_sentences.japanese: 近所のワンちゃんが朝までずっと吠えていたから、昨晩はろくに寝れなかった。
example_sentences.english: A dog in my neighborhood was barking until this morning so I barely got any sleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 豆なんてろくに食べないのに、うちには豆の缶詰がいっぱいある。
example_sentences.english: I have a lot of canned beans at home even though I hardly eat them.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はケーキを焼くどころか、シンプルな料理さえろくにできない。
example_sentences.english: Far from baking a cake, he can't even cook a simple meal properly. (hardly・not well)

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日、うちの猫に起こされるせいでろくにねられない。
example_sentences.english: Every day I am woken up by my cat, so I can't sleep well. (hardly・not properly)

example_sentences.japanese: ろくに演技もできないのに、テレビドラマのオファーがきた。
example_sentences.english: I can hardly do a stage play, and yet I was offered a part in a television drama. (hardly/barely・not well)

example_sentences.japanese: ろくに掃除もしないのに、なぜか洗剤をたくさん持っている。
example_sentences.english: Even though I barely clean, I have tons of detergent for some reason. (hardly・not well/properly)

example_sentences.japanese: ろくに宣伝もせず店を始めたから、誰も来てくれない。
example_sentences.english: Since we opened our business without properly advertising, no one came. (hardly/barely・not well)

example_sentences.japanese: ろくに稽古もせずステージに出て、悲惨なことになった。
example_sentences.english: I went on stage, not having properly prepared, and it was a disaster. (hardly/barely・not well)

example_sentences.japanese: ろくに修行もせずに始めた蕎麦屋がなぜか大人気だ。
example_sentences.english: The soba restaurant that was started without proper training is somehow really popular. (hardly/barely・not well)

example_sentences.japanese: ろくに知識もないのに田んぼに挑戦したが、やっぱり失敗した。
example_sentences.english: Even though I barely had any knowledge, I tried rice planting and inevitably failed. (hardly・not well/properly)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はろくに勉強もしていないのに、なぜか大学院にまで行けた。
example_sentences.english: Even though he hardly studies, he managed to make it into grad school somehow. (barely・not well/properly)

example_sentences.japanese: ろくに体操もせず運動したから怪我をしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Since I did not properly warm-up, I got injured when I exercised. (hardly/barely・not well)

example_sentences.japanese: 英語をろくにしらないのに父が外国人のカップルに道を教えようとした。
example_sentences.english: Despite barely knowing any English, dad tried to give directions to a foreign couple. (hardly・not well/properly)

general_translation: Can't afford to, Unable to
formation: Verb［て］+ はいられない［い］Adjective［て］+ はいられない［な］Adjective + では(1) + いられないNoun + では(1) + いられない(1) じゃ
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ はいられない［い］Adjective［て］+ はいられない［な］Adjective + では(1) + いられないNoun + では(1) + いられない(1) じゃ
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ はいられません［い］Adjective［て］+ はいられません［な］Adjective + では(1) + いられませんNoun + では(1) + いられません(1) じゃ
explanation: A phrase used to express that one cannot afford to do (A), by literally indicating that they cannot live with it.

example_sentences.japanese: 時間がない。下書きしてはいられない。
example_sentences.english: There is no time. I can't afford to make a rough draft.

example_sentences.japanese: もうこんな会社の社員ではいられない。
example_sentences.english: I can no longer be an employee of this company.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日までに提出しないといけないレポートがあるから、遊んではいられない。
example_sentences.english: I have an essay I need to submit by tomorrow, so I can't afford to hangout.

example_sentences.japanese: あと３０分で家を出ないといけないので、のんびりご飯を食べてはいられない。
example_sentences.english: I have to leave the house in 30 minutes, so I am unable to relax and eat my food.

example_sentences.japanese: 午後までに終わらせるように先輩に頼まれたから、休んではいられない。
example_sentences.english: My senpai asked me to finish by this afternoon, so I can't afford to take a break.

example_sentences.japanese: 次の大会で勝つには、こんな遅くてはいられない。
example_sentences.english: We can't afford to be this slow if we want to win the next tournament.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんもいつまでも元気ではいられないんだから、そろそろ健康に気をつけな。
example_sentences.english: Dad, you can't stay healthy forever, so you should start taking better care of yourself.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は実績を上げています。まけてはいられません。
example_sentences.english: He is achieving results. He can't afford to lose.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒すぎて写生してはいられません。
example_sentences.english: It is too cold. I am unable to do drawings from nature.

example_sentences.japanese: もう働くしかない。受験してはいられない。
example_sentences.english: I have no choice but to work. I can't afford to take an exam.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなひどい商品、宣伝してはいられません。
example_sentences.english: Such a terrible product, we can't afford to advertise it.

example_sentences.japanese: 髭をそってはいられない。緊急事態だ。
example_sentences.english: I can't afford to shave. It is a state of emergency.

example_sentences.japanese: あまりにも量が多すぎて、番号をそろえてはいられない。
example_sentences.english: There are way too many. I cannot afford to gather the numbers.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は一日たりとも日本語の勉強なしではいられない。
example_sentences.english: I can't afford to even go a day without learning Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 待ち合わせに間に合わないから、シャッターをしめてはいられない。
example_sentences.english: Since (it would mean that) I would not be on time for my appointment, I can't afford to close the shutter.

example_sentences.japanese: 対立してはいられない。協力しないと大変なことになります。
example_sentences.english: I cannot afford to confront them. If we do not cooperate, there will be hell to pay.

example_sentences.japanese: 小野：「カラオケに行こう！」岩本：「ごめん、明日の朝までに数学の宿題をしなくちゃいけないから、カラオケしてはいられないんだ。」
example_sentences.english: Ono: 'Let's go to karaoke!' Iwamoto: 'Sorry, I have math homework to finish by tomorrow morning, so I can't afford to go to karaoke.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に自身の仕事の愚痴を漏らす：「また週末上司に仕事をさせられた。このままじゃいられない。転職するつもりだよ。」
example_sentences.english: Spilling your personal complaints about work to a friend: 'I have been forced to work on the weekend again by the boss. It cannot be like this. I plan to change jobs.'

general_translation: Moreover, Furthermore
formation: Phrase (A) + しかも + Phrase (B)
casual_structure: Phrase (A) + しかも + Phrase (B)
explanation: A somewhat formal expression that indicates that furthermore to the surprising (A), (B) is also in unison, and should be considered together.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の鼻はとても大きく、しかも曲がっている。
example_sentences.english: My nose is big and what's more, it is crooked.

example_sentences.japanese: このテレビは画質がめちゃくちゃいい。しかも、受信機がついていないから受信料を払わなくてもいい。
example_sentences.english: This TV has a very good resolution, and what's more, it doesn't have a receiver, so you don't have to pay a TV reception fee.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はとても頭がいいし性格もいい。しかも、美人だからもてないわけがない。
example_sentences.english: She is very smart and has a great personality. Moreover, she is beautiful, so there is no way that she is not popular.

example_sentences.japanese: あの店は古いし汚い。しかも品揃えもよくないから、そのうち潰れるだろう。
example_sentences.english: That store is old and dirty. Moreover, they don't have a good selection of goods, so they will probably go out of business soon.

example_sentences.japanese: あのスーパーの肉は安い。しかも、脂がのっている。
example_sentences.english: That supermarket's meat is cheap. Moreover, it is marbled (good quality).

example_sentences.japanese: プレーは一流。しかも、ファンに優しい。
example_sentences.english: The play is first rate. Moreover, they are fan friendly.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は常識を知らない。しかも、厚かましい。
example_sentences.english: That person does not have common sense. Moreover, he is brazen.

example_sentences.japanese: しかも、舞台の途中に足が絡んで、転けた。
example_sentences.english: Furthermore, while on stage, he tripped and fell.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は日本語が上手。しかも、漢字が綺麗に書ける。
example_sentences.english: He is good at Japanese and furthermore, he can write kanji beautifully.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は全然仕事をしない。しかも、威張っている。
example_sentences.english: That person doesn't do their job at all. Moreover, they are boastful about it.

example_sentences.japanese: あの部屋は狭い。しかも薄暗いから、借り手がつかない。
example_sentences.english: That room is confining. Moreover, since it is dim, it can't hold down a tenant.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は裏口入学したらしい。しかも、全然学校に来ない。
example_sentences.english: That person apparently paid someone to take their entrance exam. Moreover, they don't come to school at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 友人は大きな家に住んでいる。しかも、お手伝いさんまでいるらしい。
example_sentences.english: My friend lives in a big house. Moreover, he apparently even has a maid.

example_sentences.japanese: 高級マンションに引っ越しました。しかも、温泉つきです。
example_sentences.english: I moved to a high class apartment. Moreover, it comes with an onsen/spa.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は超一流のシンガーだ。しかも、ほとんどの楽器が弾けるらしい。
example_sentences.english: He is a super first-rate singer. Moreover, he can apparently play most instruments.

general_translation: Even if I have to, By any or all means, No matter what
formation: Verb［て］+ でも
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ でも
explanation: A very casual, hypothetical phrase, highlighting that even if the action of (A) has to be persisted, it will be no matter what.

example_sentences.japanese: どんな事をしてでも、海賊王になりたいぞ！
example_sentences.english: No matter what it takes, I want to become a pirate king!

example_sentences.japanese: あの最新のノートパソコンは高いお金を払ってでも手に入れたい。
example_sentences.english: I want that laptop, even if I have to pay a lot of money for it.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒い中並んででもあそこのラーメンを食べてみたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to eat their ramen, even if I have to line up in the cold.

example_sentences.japanese: このレポートは徹夜してでも終わらせなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: I need to finish this essay, even if it means that I need to stay up all night.

example_sentences.japanese: グループを解散してでも守りたい秘密がある。
example_sentences.english: There are secrets I want to protect even if the group must break up.

example_sentences.japanese: あらそってでもいいから、あの契約を取ってこい！
example_sentences.english: It's fine even if you have to fight for it, so go and get that contract!

example_sentences.japanese: それはまたあらためてでもいいので、必ず持ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: Since it is fine even if you need to revise it again, please make sure to bring it.

example_sentences.japanese: 意地悪とおもわれてでも、説得するしかない。
example_sentences.english: Even if you have to be thought of as malicious, there is no choice but to persuade them.

example_sentences.japanese: 手間と時間をかけてでも、日本語がぺらぺらになりたい。
example_sentences.english: Even if I have to spend time and effort, I want to become fluent in Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: こうなったらおどろかしてでもいいから、彼に言葉を発してもらうんだ。
example_sentences.english: If it has come to this, even if it means we have to frighten him, we will get him to talk.

example_sentences.japanese: 時間を延長してでもこの話し合いの結論を出さなければなりません。
example_sentences.english: We have to come to a conclusion for this discussion even if we need a time extension.

example_sentences.japanese: 未払い残業してでも、この会社で働こうと思う。
example_sentences.english: Even if I have to work unpaid overtime, I am going to work for this company.

example_sentences.japanese: くたくたに疲れてるけど、失神してでも、最後までこの試合をやりぬく。
example_sentences.english: I am exhausted, but even if I faint, by any means, I will play this match till the end.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月末までずっと安いラーメンを食べる事になってでも、このゲームがほしい。
example_sentences.english: Even if it becomes so that I have to eat nothing but cheap ramen until the end of the month, I want this game.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ん坊をだいてでも行列に並びたいほどあの店のパンは美味しい。
example_sentences.english: That store's bread is so good that I want to line up even if I have to hold a baby (while I wait).

general_translation: Even if, No matter
formation: Verb［おう］ + ともVerb［なくて］ + とも［な］Adjective + であろう + とも［い］Adjective［く］(1) + とも(1) ［い］Adjective［かろう］
casual_structure: Verb［おう］ + ともVerb［なくて］ + とも［な］Adjective + であろう + とも［い］Adjective［く］(1) + とも(1) ［い］Adjective［かろう］
explanation: A grammar point which quotes the previous statement and declares that even if that is the case, (B) is still also true. No matter if (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: どんなことになろうとも、国家が破産するのはまずありえない。
example_sentences.english: No matter what (becomes of it) , it is impossible for a country to go bankrupt.

example_sentences.japanese: いくら下手であろうとも、毎日練習をしていればそのうち上手になれる。
example_sentences.english: No matter how bad you are at it, if you practice every day, you will eventually get good at it.

example_sentences.japanese: 親が何と言おうとも、私は彼と結婚するつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: No matter what my parents say, I intend on marrying him.

example_sentences.japanese: 魚がどんなに暴れようとも、この糸は絶対に切れません。
example_sentences.english: No matter how violent the fish thrashes around, this line will never break.

example_sentences.japanese: 人生がいくら辛くとも、諦めてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how hard life is, you must not give up.

example_sentences.japanese: 頂点にはとどかなくとも、行けるところまで行ってみよう。
example_sentences.english: Even if we don't reach the summit, let's try to go as far as we can.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに生意気になろうとも、わたしの息子であることに変わりはない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how cheeky he  becomes, he's still my son.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰ににくまれようとも、使命を果たさないわけにはいきません。
example_sentences.english: Even if everyone hates it, it is an obligation we must fulfill.

example_sentences.japanese: ため息がでようとも、仕事はやり遂げなければなりません。
example_sentences.english: Even if you sigh, you must get some work done.

example_sentences.japanese: 狙いがはずれようとも、何度でも釣り糸を垂らす。
example_sentences.english: Even if my aim is off, I will cast a fishing line many times.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなにタバコが好きであろうとも、赤ちゃんができたら吸うわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much you like cigarettes, if you get pregnant you can't smoke.

example_sentences.japanese: どんな新人が登場しようとも、まだまだ勝つ自信があります。
example_sentences.english: No matter what type of new person enters, I believe I can still win.

example_sentences.japanese: 南極にいこうとも、寒さに強い彼には大したことはないらしい。
example_sentences.english: Even if he goes to Antarctica, it seems like it won't be a problem for someone who can resist the cold like him.

example_sentences.japanese: 調味料がかぎられようとも、彼女はあるもので美味しい料理が作れる。
example_sentences.english: Even if the spices are limited, she can make delicious food with what she has.

example_sentences.japanese: 試験直前になろうとも、平常心でいられるよう普通に過ごそう。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is right before the test, let's spend our time like we normally would with a calm mind.

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒が授業に出席しなくとも、教師はきちんと授業を進めていくべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Even if students do not attend, the teacher should proceed with the lesson.

grammar_point: ない訳（わけ）にはいかない
general_translation: Can't not, No way to avoid
formation: Verb［ない］+ わけにはいかない
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ わけにはいかない
polite_structure: Verb［ない］+ わけにはいきません
explanation: A strong expression highlighting that not doing (A) cannot be so, or will not go.

example_sentences.japanese: 訳あって、白髪をそめないわけにはいかないんです。
example_sentences.english: For some reason, he cannot avoid dyeing his gray hair.

example_sentences.japanese: いつもお世話になっている先輩の結婚式だから、行きたくなくても行かないわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: It's the wedding of a senior who has always been a great help to me, so even if I didn't want to go, I can't not go.

example_sentences.japanese: ダイエット中だからといって、何も食べないわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Just because I am on a diet doesn't mean that I can avoid eating food.

example_sentences.japanese: めんどくさいからと言って、宿題をしないわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Just because it's a hassle doesn't mean that you don't do your homework.

example_sentences.japanese: ベテランの職人でも、トレーニングをしないわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Even a veteran worker cannot avoid training.

example_sentences.japanese: 面倒だからといって、打ち合わせをしないわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Even though it is troublesome, there is no way to avoid having a meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: 締切前だからといって、まったくねないわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is just before the deadline, you can't not sleep at all. (no way to avoid)

example_sentences.japanese: 慣れたメニューだとはいえ、味見しないわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Although it is a menu I am used to, there is no way to avoid taste testing.

example_sentences.japanese: 初級問題だとはいえ、何度か見直しをしないわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Although it is a beginner problem, there is no way to avoid revising it several times.

example_sentences.japanese: 帰りが深夜になってしまったが、化粧をおとさないわけにはいきません。
example_sentences.english: My return home unfortunately became late, but there is no way to avoid having to take off my makeup.

example_sentences.japanese: 疲れたからといって、勉強をしないわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Just because you are tired, you can't not study. (no way to avoid)

example_sentences.japanese: 好き嫌いが激しいからといって、出されたものをたべないわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Just because you are very particular about your likes and dislikes, you can't not eat the food that was put out. (no way to avoid)

example_sentences.japanese: 苦手だからといって、家事をしないわけにはいきません。
example_sentences.english: Just because you are bad at it, you can't avoid doing housework.

example_sentences.japanese: ケンカが気まずいからといって、彼女の誕生日パーティにいかないわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Just because it is awkward after a fight, there's no way to avoid going to her birthday party.

example_sentences.japanese: 受験生だからといって、アルバイトをしないわけにはいかない事情がある。
example_sentences.english: While I may be a student preparing for exams, I have a situation where I cannot avoid having a part time job.

grammar_point: と言（い）う訳（わけ）ではない
general_translation: It is not that, It doesn't mean that, It is not always the case
formation: Verb + という + わけでは(1)ない［い］Adjective + という + わけでは(1)ない［な］Adjective +（だ）+ という + わけでは(1)ない Noun +（だ）+ という + わけでは(1)ない(1) じゃ
casual_structure: Verb + という + わけでは(1)ない［い］Adjective + という + わけでは(1)ない［な］Adjective +（だ）+ という + わけでは(1)ない Noun +（だ）+ という + わけでは(1)ない(1) じゃ
polite_structure: Verb + という + わけでは(1)ありません［い］Adjective + という + わけでは(1)ありません(2)［な］Adjective +（だ）+ という + わけでは(1)ありません(2) Noun +（だ）+ という + わけでは(1)ありません(2)(1) じゃ(2) ないです
explanation: A phrase used when expressing that it is not so that (A) is being said. (A) is not always the case.

example_sentences.japanese: 苦情というわけではなく、提案です。
example_sentences.english: It is not (that it is) a complaint, it is a suggestion. (not the reason)

example_sentences.japanese: 数学が嫌いというわけではない、ただ苦手なだけだ。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I don't like math, I'm just not good at it.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に２年間住んでいたからと言って、日本語を話せるというわけではない。
example_sentences.english: Just because I lived in Japan for two years does not mean I speak Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: いつもニコニコしているからって、親切だというわけではない。
example_sentences.english: Just because they are always smiling doesn't mean they are nice.

example_sentences.japanese: 離婚というわけではないが、しばらく別居することになった。
example_sentences.english: It was not a divorce, but we had to live separately for a while.

example_sentences.japanese: 全てのキノコが毒を持っているというわけではない。
example_sentences.english: It is not the case that all mushrooms are poisonous. (not the reason)

example_sentences.japanese: 儀式というわけではないけど、あれはもはや儀式に近い。
example_sentences.english: It's not to say that it's a ritual, but at this point it's close enough to being a ritual. (not the case)

example_sentences.japanese: 正式な基準というわけではないですが、参考にしてください。
example_sentences.english: It is not that it is officially the norm, but please take note. (not the reason)

example_sentences.japanese: 警備というわけではないが、近くにいてもらえるとありがたいです。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't mean that (I need) security, but I would be grateful if you stayed near me. (not the reason)

example_sentences.japanese: 見学というわけではないが、工場の中を見せてくれた。
example_sentences.english: It is not that it was an inspection, but they let me see the inside of the factory. (not the reason)

example_sentences.japanese: 謙遜というわけではないが、あなたからいろいろ学びたいことがある。
example_sentences.english: It is not that I am being modest, I want to learn a number of things from you. (not the reason)

example_sentences.japanese: 突拍子もない発想に見えるが、空想というわけではない。
example_sentences.english: It may look like an astounding concept, but it doesn't mean that it is a fantasy. (not the reason)

example_sentences.japanese: このパソコンは一番速いというわけではないのに、多くの人に買われた。いったい何なんだ？
example_sentences.english: This computer, despite not being the fastest, many people bought it. What the heck? (not the case/reason)

example_sentences.japanese: 休業というわけではないのだが、お客さんが来ないから休業みたいなものだ。
example_sentences.english: It is not that it is a business holiday, but since customers don't come in, it is like a business holiday. (not the reason)

example_sentences.japanese: 月給というわけではないが、毎月収入が得られる仕事の依頼があった。
example_sentences.english: It is not that I got a monthly salary, but I was on a commision job where I would receive income each month. (not the reason)

example_sentences.japanese: 母：「何でこれを食べないの？あたしの料理、嫌いなの？」 息子：「嫌いだというわけではないけど、単に今は食べたくない。」
example_sentences.english: Mother: 'Why aren't you eating? Do you hate my cooking?' Son: 'It is not the case that I hate it, I am simply not hungry at the moment.' (not the reason)

example_sentences.japanese: ということは、彼女は彼を助けるために、彼を押し倒したという訳だ。
example_sentences.english: So that means that she pushed him in order to save him.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼がこの国に入国できないのは、以前この国で犯罪を犯したからというわけだ。
example_sentences.english: So the reason why he cannot enter this country is because he has committed crimes in this country in the past.

general_translation: May well, Have or has good reason for, No wonder, … Is only natural
formation: Verb + のも(1) + もっとも + だ［い］Adjective + のも(1) + もっとも + だ ［な］Adjective + なのも(1) + もっとも + だ Noun + も(2) + もっともだ(1) のは(2) は
casual_structure: Verb + のも(1) + もっとも + だ［い］Adjective + のも(1) + もっとも + だ ［な］Adjective + なのも(1) + もっとも + だ Noun + も(2) + もっともだ(1) のは(2) は
polite_structure: Verb + のも(1) + もっとも + です［い］Adjective + のも(1) + もっとも + です ［な］Adjective + なのも(1) + もっとも + です Noun + も(2) + もっともだ(1) のは(2) は
explanation: A grammar point expressing that (A) is natural. Even that which is (A) is reasonable.

example_sentences.japanese: 状況からして、彼らがそう考えたのももっともだ。
example_sentences.english: Given the situation, no wonder they thought so.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなことを彼女に言ったのか？彼女が怒るのももっともだ。
example_sentences.english: You said something like that to your girlfriend? She has every right to be angry.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも夜遅くまで残業をしているから、いつも眠いのももっともだ。
example_sentences.english: He always works late at night, so it's no wonder he's always sleepy.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は高校生の頃から毎日日本語を勉強をしてきた。上手なのももっともだ。
example_sentences.english: He has studied Japanese every day since high school. It is no wonder he is so good at it.

example_sentences.japanese: 親の反対ももっともだが、俺はもう俺のやり方でやると決めたから親の意見に合わすつもりはない。
example_sentences.english: My parents have a good reason to object, but I've already decided to do things my way, so I'm not going to conform to my parents' views.

example_sentences.japanese: あの本がいつも貸し出し中なのももっともだ。大ベストセラーだから。
example_sentences.english: There is good reason that that book is always unavailable (for rent). It is a huge best seller.

example_sentences.japanese: ＳＮＳの投稿回数を減らしたのももっともだ。彼女は忙しすぎる。
example_sentences.english: It is only natural that number of SNS messages she sends has decreased. She is much too busy.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社の規約を改正するのももっともだ。あの規約は古すぎる。
example_sentences.english: No wonder the company is revising their code of conduct. Those rules are too old.

example_sentences.japanese: 解説者が言っているのももっともだ。かなり的確な意見だと思います。
example_sentences.english: There is good reason that the commentator is saying (those things). It is quite an appropriate viewpoint.

example_sentences.japanese: 二人の意見が食い違うのももっともだ。性格が違いすぎる。
example_sentences.english: No wonder their opinions clash. Those two have very different personalities.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が自信過剰になるのももっともだ。実力がずば抜けている。
example_sentences.english: It is only natural that he is presumptuous. He has outstanding ability.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の怒りはもっともだ。オレがお気に入りの花瓶を壊しちゃったから。
example_sentences.english: There is good reason for her anger. It is because I broke her favorite vase.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が海水浴が嫌いなのももっともだ。昔海で溺れかけたことがあるから。
example_sentences.english: There is good reason for him to hate swimming in the ocean. He nearly drowned some time ago.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が活躍するのももっともだ。才能があり、しかも誰よりも努力をしている。
example_sentences.english: No wonder she is flourishing. She is a genius. What's more she puts forth more effort than anyone else.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの学校の生徒の学力が下がったのももっともだ。環境が悪すぎる。
example_sentences.english: No wonder my school's students' literary ability has decreased. The surroundings are absolutely terrible.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の作った料理が美味しいのももっともだ。十歳から一人で料理をしてきたやつだけのことはある。
example_sentences.english: It is only natural that the dish he made is tasty. This can be expected from a guy who has been cooking by himself since he was 10.

general_translation: Even if, Even though, No matter how
formation: Verb［た］+ ってVerb［なくて］ + たって［い］Adjective［く］+ たって［い］Adjective［なくて］ + たって［な］Adjective + だって［な］Adjective + じゃなくたってNoun + だってNoun + じゃなくたって
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ ってVerb［なくて］ + たって［い］Adjective［く］+ たって［い］Adjective［なくて］ + たって［な］Adjective + だって［な］Adjective + じゃなくたってNoun + だってNoun + じゃなくたって
explanation: A very casual expression which indicates that even if (A), (B), or no matter how (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: パーティーにはピザじゃなくたってかまわないよね。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is not a pizza party, I don't mind.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女に謝ったってどうせ許してくれないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if I apologized to her, she wouldn't forgive me anyway.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生に聞いたって、何も教えてくれないからインターネットで調べる。
example_sentences.english: Even if I ask the teacher, they won't tell me anything, so I am going to look it up on the internet.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに欲しくたって、万引きをしてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much you want something, you must not shoplift.

example_sentences.japanese: 稽古がどんなに楽しくなくたって、稽古中には欠伸をしてはならない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how boring the lesson might be, you must not yawn during a lesson.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな簡単な問題馬鹿だってわかるよ！
example_sentences.english: Even an idiot can figure out a simple problem like this!

example_sentences.japanese: 友達だって喧嘩をすることがある。
example_sentences.english: Even friends can get into fights.

example_sentences.japanese: ブロッコリーが健康によくたって、もう食べたくない！
example_sentences.english: Even if broccoli is good for your health, I still don't want to eat it.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなにおしたくたって、この赤いボタンを押してはダメ。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much you want to press it, you must not press the red button.

example_sentences.japanese: 海水浴にいったって僕は泳げないからつまらない。
example_sentences.english: Even if I went to the beach, since I can't swim, it would be boring.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ彼がどこにいるか知っているとしたって、それでもお前には教えない。
example_sentences.english: Even if (we assume that) I did know where he is, I still would not tell you!

example_sentences.japanese: この試合にかったって、準々決勝には進めないよ。
example_sentences.english: Even if I win the match I won't proceed to the quarterfinals!

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ家がおおきくなくたって、オレンジ色の屋根があればそれでいい。
example_sentences.english: Even if a house is not large, I will be fine if the roof is orange.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに改造したってエンジンが古すぎるから無駄だと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: Even if we did that much remodeling, the engine is too old, so it would be a waste I think.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語が上手にできなくたって、それでも日本旅行を楽しめるよね。
example_sentences.english: Even if you are not capable in Japanese, you can still enjoy your time in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 真剣に告白したって、彼女は冗談だと思うかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Even if I confess (my love) in all seriousness, she might think it is a joke.

example_sentences.japanese: まさか、また宿題忘れたの？あたしの友達だって、いちいち写させることができないわ。もっとしっかりしなさい！
example_sentences.english: No way, you forgot the homework again?! Even if you are my friend, I can't let you copy it every single time! Get a grip!

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「バンジージャンプをしてみるのはどうだろう？やらずに後悔するよりやって後悔したほうがいい。」Ｂ：「カッコよくいったってダメ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'What about trying bungee jumping? It is better to regret doing something than to regret not doing it.' B: 'Even if you say it in a cool way, I will not allow it.'

general_translation: If it's (A), sure, but (B), Putting aside (A), (B)
formation: Verb + ならともかく［い］Adjective + ならともかく［な］Adjective + ならともかくNoun + ならともかく
casual_structure: Verb + ならともかく［い］Adjective + ならともかく［な］Adjective + ならともかくNoun + ならともかく
explanation: A phrase which concedes the hypothetical point (A) only to dismiss it, setting it aside.

example_sentences.japanese: 生魚ならともかく、納豆は食べられません。
example_sentences.english: If it's raw fish, sure, but I can't eat natto.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の妹ならともかく、俺はそんなことしねぇ〜よ。
example_sentences.english: If it's my little sister, sure, but I would never do such a thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 丈夫で何回も使えるものならともかく、なんでわざわざ高くて使い捨てみたいなもんを買うんですか。
example_sentences.english: If it is tough and can be used multiple times, sure, but why would you go out of your way to buy something that is expensive and basically disposable.

example_sentences.japanese: 新人ならともかく、君みたいなベテランがわからないようじゃ困ったもんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I understand if a newbie didn't know, but it is a problem if a long time worker like you didn't know.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜ならともかく、夏は日中は外に出られない。
example_sentences.english: If it's night, sure, but you can't go outside during the day in summer.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ん坊ならともかく、子供には叱る事も必要だ。
example_sentences.english: If it's a baby, sure, but it's necessary to scold kids.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長ならともかく、平社員に決定権はありません。
example_sentences.english: If it's the president, sure, but a rank-and-file staff member has no right to make decisions.

example_sentences.japanese: イケメンならともかく、そうでない人はナンパで成功しないだろう。
example_sentences.english: If it's a hottie, sure, but a person that isn't would surely not succeed at picking someone up.

example_sentences.japanese: 得意な科目ならともかく、そうでないならテスト勉強が必要だ。
example_sentences.english: If it's a subject I'm good at, sure, but if it's not, test study will be necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: 試合に勝ったのならともかく、負けたのだから反省しなさい。
example_sentences.english: If you won the contest, sure, but since you lost, learn from it.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカならともかく、日本では露出度の高い服は着られない。
example_sentences.english: If it was America, sure, but in Japan, you can't wear something with that much exposure.

example_sentences.japanese: 男性の方が女性よりも偉い？昭和ならともかく、今は令和だ。
example_sentences.english: Men are higher status than women? If it was Showa, sure, but it's Reiwa now.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本ならともかく、フランスで自分の荷物から目を離したら荷物がなくなるだろう。
example_sentences.english: If it was Japan, sure, but if you take your eyes off your luggage in France, it will probably disappear.

example_sentences.japanese: お金持ちならともかく、そうでない人は飛行機のビジネスクラスには乗れない。
example_sentences.english: If you're a rich person, sure, but for people that aren't, you can't ride in business class on a plane.

example_sentences.japanese: ただ思うだけならともかく、差別的な発言をするのは許されません。
example_sentences.english: If it's nothing more than a thought, sure, but it is unforgivable if you blurt out a discriminatory statement.
